PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Computational Prediction of Protein Interactions in Single Cells by Proximity Sequencing
Source Link  : https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011915
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011915
Journal      : PLoS Computational Biology, 2024, Vol. 20(3), Article e1011915
Authors      : Junjie Xia, Hoang Van Phan, Luke Vistain, Mengjie Chen, Aly A. Khan, Savaş Tay
Platform     : Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq) combined with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq), a method for simultaneous quantification
of mRNA, surface protein expression, and protein complexes (dimers) at the single-cell level.
Prox-seq uses a proximity ligation assay (PLA) with DNA-conjugated antibody probes (Probe A and
Probe B) targeting surface proteins of interest. Ligation of the oligos on Probe A and Probe B
occurs only when the two probes are within 50-70 nm of each other — i.e., when their respective
target protein molecules are co-localised or physically interacting. The resulting ligated PLA
products are barcoded, counted by unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) after sequencing, and
provide direct single-cell readout of protein complex formation.

By combining Prox-seq with scRNA-seq, PLA product libraries are sequenced alongside complementary
DNA (cDNA) libraries, yielding multi-omic single-cell data: gene expression, protein abundance,
and protein complex expression simultaneously from the same cell.

The paper introduces a physical simulation model of Prox-seq data and computationally benchmarks
three methods for removing proximity noise (random ligation background) and quantifying true
protein complexes: the iterative method, the linear regression (LR) method, and a new ensemble
method combining both. The ensemble method is demonstrated to be the most accurate and robust
across diverse biological scenarios.

Two cell line arms are encoded:
  ARM 1: Jurkat T cells — known complexes: CD3:CD3 and CD28:CD28 (homodimers)
  ARM 2: Raji B cells  — known complex: ICAM1:ICAM1 (homodimer on cell surface)

Code repository : https://github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq_computation
Data repository : NCBI GEO accession GSE196130


METHOD DESIGN
-------------
Probe Design:
  Each target protein is stained with TWO DNA-conjugated antibodies:
    - Probe A: antibody conjugated to oligo A (contains barcode for protein i)
    - Probe B: antibody conjugated to oligo B (contains barcode for protein j)
  Ligation of oligo A to oligo B occurs only if Euclidean distance between
  the two probes <= ligation distance (50-70 nm; set to 50 nm in simulation model).
  Result: a PLA product barcode encoding the protein pair i:j.

  Importantly, unligated probes do NOT contribute to PLA signal because both library
  preparation and sequence alignment require barcodes from both the A and B probe.
  UMI counting of PLA products after sequencing gives the number of protein complexes
  per cell per protein pair.

Free Oligo Modification:
  An experimentally modified Prox-seq procedure adds FreeOligoA and FreeOligoB
  (non-antibody-conjugated oligos) alongside the probe panel. These generate PLA products:
    - Protein_X : free_oligo_B  ->  measures non-proximal (unligated) Probe A count
    - free_oligo_A : Protein_Y  ->  measures non-proximal (unligated) Probe B count
  These non-proximal counts serve as explanatory variables in the linear regression (LR)
  method and ensemble method for per-cell proximity noise estimation.

Proximity Noise:
  Random co-localisation of non-interacting proteins produces "proximity noise": ligation
  events between Probe A and Probe B from unrelated proteins that happen to be nearby.
  Theoretical expected proximity noise:
    E(X_ij) = (d_ligation^2 / 4R^2) * A_i * B_j
  where d_ligation = 50 nm, R = cell radius = 5 um, A_i = Probe A count for protein i,
  B_j = Probe B count for protein j.
  Proximity noise scales quadratically with both protein abundance and ligation distance
  (Fig 2e). Identifying and removing proximity noise is essential for accurate complex
  quantification, especially for highly expressed proteins.

Isotype Control:
  Isotype control antibodies with oligonucleotide conjugation are included in both Probe A
  and Probe B panels. This allows direct estimation of nonspecific antibody binding
  probability from observed PLA data. For extracellular Prox-seq assays, nonspecific
  binding constitutes <1% of both-specific PLA counts (e.g. CD147:CD147 in Jurkat cells,
  S4 Fig), and is much less important than proximity noise.


PROBE PANEL
-----------
Targets : CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7
Control : Isotype control antibody (oligo-conjugated) in both Probe A and Probe B panels
Reference: Same panel as Vistain et al. Nat Methods 2022 (Ref [4])

Jurkat T cells express  : CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1
  Known complexes       : CD3:CD3 (homodimer, Ref [12]); CD28:CD28 (homodimer, Ref [13])

Raji B cells express    : ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7, CD147
  Known complex         : ICAM1:ICAM1 (homodimer on cell surface, Ref [14])
  Specificity check     : Raji cells do not express CD3 or PD1; PLA counts for those
                          targets are near zero, validating probe panel specificity


COMPUTATIONAL METHODS
---------------------

Iterative Method:
  Mechanism   : Solve quadratic equations iteratively for all possible protein dimers.
                Protein complex count = observed PLA count minus expected random PLA count.
                Expected count calculated from protein abundance estimates derived from
                summing PLA product counts per protein.
  Equation    : Y_ij^(m+1) = X_ij - [(sum_A_i - sum_Y_i^m) * (sum_B_j - sum_Y_j^m)] /
                              (total_PLA_sum - sum_Y^m)
  Strengths   : Performs well at high signal-to-noise; no additional experiment required.
  Limitations : Unstable with multiple protein dimers or overabundant proteins;
                sensitive to initialisation (default: all-zeroes matrix).
                Consistently underestimates true complex count (Fig 3c, 3e).
  Best for    : Simpler scenarios with only homodimers or only heterodimers.

Linear Regression (LR) Method:
  Mechanism   : Weighted least squares regression of observed PLA count (X_ij) onto
                product of non-proximal Probe A count (A_i') and Probe B count (B_j').
                Slope beta_1 estimates proximity noise; intercept beta_0 detects complex.
                Protein complex count Y_ij = X_ij - beta_1 * A_i' * B_j'.
  Equation    : X_ij ~ beta_0 + beta_1 * A_i' * B_j'  (weighted by 1 / (A_i' * B_j'))
  Requirement : Free oligo modification experiment required to measure non-proximal counts.
  Strengths   : More accurate than iterative method; performs well in low signal-to-noise
                and multi-dimer scenarios; greater robustness for complex biological cases.
  Limitations : Unstable when non-proximal probe counts are near zero;
                not optimal for high signal-to-noise homodimer/heterodimer-only scenarios.
                Suffers false positives when noise is very low (Fig 4c).
  Best for    : Low signal-to-noise and scenarios with multiple protein dimers or
                overabundant proteins.

Ensemble Method (recommended):
  Mechanism   : Apply LR method first; use LR output (protein complex matrix) as
                initialisation for iterative method instead of all-zeroes matrix.
                Bridges weaknesses of both methods.
  Requirement : Free oligo modification experimental procedure required.
  Strengths   : Robust and consistent across all 8 biological scenario types and both
                high and low signal-to-noise cases (800 randomised tests).
                Highest average prediction score; lowest variance; fewest false positives.
                Most accurate quantification of true-positive complex abundance in single
                cells (Fig 4d).
  Best for    : Recommended default when true biological conditions are uncertain.

Fisher's Exact Test:
  Mechanism   : One-sided Fisher's exact test on 2x2 PLA product contingency table per cell.
                Benjamini-Hochberg correction applied. Identifies enriched protein complexes.
  Use         : Statistical validation of complex enrichment; complementary to quantification.

Prediction Score:
  Formula     : Score = 0.5 * SumPearson - 0.4 * SumMeanDeviation - 0.1 * SumFPrate
  Result      : Ensemble method scores highest and shows lowest variance across all scenarios
                (S10d Fig, S2 Table).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

--- ARM 1: JURKAT T CELLS ---

Step 1 | Cell Suspension Preparation (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : JurkatCells, PBS
  Operation   : Resuspend Jurkat T cells in PBS at appropriate concentration for staining
  Duration    : 5 min (mix)
  BioScript   : jurkatSuspension = mix jurkatCells with cellPBS for 5m

Step 2 | Nonspecific Binding Block (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatSuspension, BlockingBuffer
  Operation   : Mix with blocking buffer; incubate 10 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 10 min at 4 C
  Purpose     : Reduces nonspecific antibody binding background
  Notes       : Nonspecific binding <1% of both-specific PLA counts for extracellular
                assays (CD147:CD147 in Jurkat cells, S4 Fig)
  BioScript   : blockedCells = mix jurkatSuspension with blockingBuf for 10m
                heat blockedCells at 4c for 10m

Step 3 | Probe A Staining with Isotype Control (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : blockedCells, ProxSeqProbeA, IsotypeControlAntibody
  Operation   : Mix isotype control into Probe A panel; stain cells 30 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 30 min at 4 C
  Probe A panel: CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7 + isotype control
  BioScript   : probeAWithControl = mix probeAStain with isotypeControl for 5s
                probeAStained = mix blockedCells with probeAWithControl for 30m
                heat probeAStained at 4c for 30m

Step 4 | Wash Unbound Probe A (Jurkat, 3x)
  Reagents    : probeAStained, WashBuffer (x3)
  Operation   : 3 sequential PBS washes, 2 min each
  Duration    : 3 x 2 min
  Notes       : Unligated probes do not contribute to PLA signal (dual-barcode requirement)
  BioScript   : washedA1 = mix probeAStained with wash1A for 2m
                washedA2 = mix washedA1 with wash2A for 2m
                jurkatProbeAReady = mix washedA2 with wash3A for 2m

Step 5 | Probe B Staining (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatProbeAReady, ProxSeqProbeB
  Operation   : Stain cells with Probe B panel 30 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 30 min at 4 C
  Notes       : After this step, cells carry both Probe A and Probe B on surface proteins
  BioScript   : probeBStained = mix jurkatProbeAReady with probeBStain for 30m
                heat probeBStained at 4c for 30m

Step 6 | Wash Unbound Probe B (Jurkat, 3x)
  Reagents    : probeBStained, WashBuffer (x3)
  Operation   : 3 sequential PBS washes, 2 min each
  BioScript   : washedB1 = mix probeBStained with wash1B for 2m
                washedB2 = mix washedB1 with wash2B for 2m
                jurkatDualStained = mix washedB2 with wash3B for 2m

Step 7 | Free Oligo Addition (Jurkat, non-proximal probe measurement)
  Reagents    : jurkatDualStained, FreeOligoA, FreeOligoB
  Operation   : Mix free oligos together; add to dual-stained cells; incubate 10 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 10 min at 4 C
  Purpose     : FreeOligoA generates PLA products Protein_X:free_oligo_B (non-proximal Probe A)
                FreeOligoB generates PLA products free_oligo_A:Protein_Y (non-proximal Probe B)
                Non-proximal counts required for LR method: Y_ij = X_ij - beta_1 * A_i' * B_j'
                (Methods: LR method; Ref [4] Vistain et al. Nat Methods 2022)
  BioScript   : freeOligoMix = mix freeOligoADrop with freeOligoBDrop for 5s
                jurkatWithFreeOligos = mix jurkatDualStained with freeOligoMix for 10m
                heat jurkatWithFreeOligos at 4c for 10m

Step 8 | Proximity Ligation Reaction (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatWithFreeOligos, LigationBuffer, Ligase (T4 DNA Ligase)
  Operation   : Mix ligation buffer with ligase; add to cells; incubate 30 min at 25 C
  Duration    : 30 min at 25 C
  Ligation distance: 50-70 nm (50 nm threshold in simulation model)
  Proximity noise: E(X_ij) = (d_ligation^2 / 4R^2) * A_i * B_j
                   (R = 5 um, d_ligation = 50 nm; Methods: Theoretical calculation)
  BioScript   : ligationReagents = mix ligBuf with ligase for 5s
                jurkatLigated = mix jurkatWithFreeOligos with ligationReagents for 30m
                heat jurkatLigated at 25c for 30m

Step 9 | Ligation Stop and Wash (Jurkat, 3x)
  Reagents    : jurkatLigated, StopSolution, WashBuffer (x3)
  Operation   : Add stop solution (5 min mix); 3x PBS wash, 2 min each
  Duration    : 5 min (stop) + 3 x 2 min (washes)
  BioScript   : jurkatStopped = mix jurkatLigated with stopSol for 5m
                jurkatLigatedReady = (3x wash chain, 2m each)

Step 10 | Single-Cell Encapsulation and Library Preparation (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatLigatedReady, DNALibraryBuffer, SequencingReagent
  Operation   : Encapsulate cells in individual droplets; lyse; capture mRNA (poly-dT)
                and PLA products (barcoded sequences); prepare combined cDNA + PLA library
  Duration    : 30 min at 37 C (library prep) + 10 min (sequencing reagent addition)
  Output      : Combined scRNA-seq + Prox-seq sequencing library
  BioScript   : jurkatLibPrep = mix jurkatLigatedReady with dnaLibBuf for 30m
                heat jurkatLibPrep at 37c for 30m
                jurkatSeqReady = mix jurkatLibPrep with seqReagentJ for 10m

Step 11 | Jurkat Library QC and Branching Gate
  Reagents    : jurkatSeqReady
  Operation   : detect seqLibraryQC on jurkatSeqReady for 30s
  Detection   : Abstracts fluorometric/electrophoretic QC (Bioanalyzer, Qubit)
                Checks fragment size, library complexity, UMI diversity
  Branch Pass : jurkatLibSignal > 0  ->  dispose(jurkatSeqReady)  ->  proceed to Raji arm
  Branch Fail : jurkatLibSignal <= 0 ->  drain(jurkatSeqReady)    ->  proceed to Raji arm

--- ARM 2: RAJI B CELLS ---
  Steps 12-22 are structurally identical to Jurkat steps 1-11.
  Key differences:
    - RajiCells instead of JurkatCells
    - Raji cells express ICAM1:ICAM1 homodimer (confirmed by all 3 methods, Fig 5d-f)
    - Raji cells do not express CD3 or PD1 (near-zero PLA counts for those pairs)
    - Non-proximal Raji probe counts used to calibrate proximity noise for Raji arm
    - Final QC gate on rajiLibSignal; terminal block disposes rajiLibSignal

Step 12 | Cell Suspension Preparation (Raji)        -- same as Step 1 for Raji
Step 13 | Nonspecific Binding Block (Raji)           -- same as Step 2 for Raji
Step 14 | Probe A Staining with Isotype Control (Raji) -- same as Step 3 for Raji
Step 15 | Wash Unbound Probe A (Raji, 3x)            -- same as Step 4 for Raji
Step 16 | Probe B Staining (Raji)                    -- same as Step 5 for Raji
Step 17 | Wash Unbound Probe B (Raji, 3x)            -- same as Step 6 for Raji
Step 18 | Free Oligo Addition (Raji)                 -- same as Step 7 for Raji
Step 19 | Proximity Ligation Reaction (Raji)         -- same as Step 8 for Raji
Step 20 | Ligation Stop and Wash (Raji, 3x)          -- same as Step 9 for Raji
Step 21 | Single-Cell Encapsulation and Library Preparation (Raji) -- same as Step 10 for Raji
Step 22 | Raji Library QC and Branching Gate
  Branch Pass : rajiLibSignal > 0  ->  dispose(rajiSeqReady)  ->  terminal (BB7)
  Branch Fail : rajiLibSignal <= 0 ->  drain(rajiSeqReady)    ->  terminal (BB7)

Terminal     : dispose(rajiLibSignal)
               Experiment ends. Sequencing data submitted to computational pipeline.
               Code: https://github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq_computation
               Data: GEO GSE196130


SIMULATION MODEL
----------------
Physical model of PLA product formation per single cell:
  - Non-interacting Probe A points generated as random points on sphere (radius R = 5 um)
  - Non-interacting Probe B points generated as random points on sphere
  - Protein complex points generated as random points; added to both Probe A and Probe B sets
  - Pairwise Euclidean distances computed between all Probe A and Probe B points
  - Pairs within ligation distance threshold (50 nm) are ligated; each probe ligated at most once
  - Non-ligated points returned as non-proximal probe count (measured by free oligo modification)

Variance model:
  - Simulated counts without variance follow Poisson distribution
  - Real data shows overdispersion; negative binomial (NB) variance added: n_NB = 1.5
  - NB formulation: A_i^(t) ~ NegativeBinomial(n_NB, p_NB); p_NB = (1 + A_i/n_NB)^-1
  - NB variance captures positive correlation between PLA product count and non-proximal
    probe count in real data (S1b-S1g Fig)

Calibration:
  - Posterior predictive checks (PPCs): Mann-Whitney U statistic and coefficient of variation
    compared between replicated simulated data and real Jurkat/Raji data (S3a, S3b Fig)
  - n_NB = 1.5 chosen as mean of best-fit n_NB values across all PLA products (S3c Fig)
  - Simulation faithfully captures key aspects of real Prox-seq data


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : xia_proxseq_computational_prediction.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 sequential if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file        : xia_proxseq_computational_prediction_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : All durations in s (seconds) or m (minutes); h token not supported by compiler
Duration conversions:
  5m   ->  300.0 SECOND
  10m  ->  600.0 SECOND
  30m  -> 1800.0 SECOND
  2m   ->  120.0 SECOND
  30s  ->   30.0 SECOND
Modules declared  : proxSeqDetection, viabilityDetection, plaDetection, seqLibraryQC
Active QC module  : seqLibraryQC (used in detect statements for both Jurkat and Raji gates)
Manifests (15)    : JurkatCells, RajiCells, PBS, ProxSeqProbeA, ProxSeqProbeB,
                    FreeOligoA, FreeOligoB, LigationBuffer, Ligase, BlockingBuffer,
                    WashBuffer, DNALibraryBuffer, SequencingReagent,
                    IsotypeControlAntibody, StopSolution
Compiler note     : lilott8/BioScript maps both dispose and drain to a unified disposal
                    IR operation (both appear as dispose in IR output). This is expected
                    compiler behaviour and does not affect correctness.
                    Observed in bsbbif_3_f (Jurkat fail path) and bsbbif_6_f (Raji fail path).
CFG arms          : Two sequential arms. ARM 1 (Jurkat) runs in BB1 main. ARM 2 (Raji) runs
                    in BB4 jurkatLibJoin after Jurkat QC gate converges. Both arms share the
                    same 11-step structure: blocking -> Probe A -> wash x3 -> Probe B ->
                    wash x3 -> free oligo addition -> ligation -> stop+wash x3 ->
                    library prep -> QC detect -> branch gate.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Computer Vision Reveals Hidden Variables Underlying NF-kB Activation in Single Cells
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/epdf/10.1126/sciadv.abg4135
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abg4135
Journal      : Science Advances, 2021, Vol. 7, Article eabg4135
Platform     : High-throughput microfluidic live-cell imaging (PDMS chip) + image-based SVM machine learning


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic live-cell imaging approach to uncover hidden molecular
variables controlling heterogeneous NF-kB (nuclear factor kappa B) activation in single
mammalian cells. The core experiment uses automated PDMS microfluidic chambers to culture
and stimulate NIH 3T3 mouse fibroblasts expressing dual fluorescent reporters (p65-dsRed
for NF-kB dynamics, H2B-GFP as a nuclear marker), combined with a custom image-based support
vector machine (SVM) pipeline that predicts which individual cells will activate NF-kB from
their prestimulation images alone.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Microfluidic device preparation: fibronectin coating and cell seeding
  2. Live-cell imaging: 1.5 h unperturbed prestimulation imaging followed by TNF-alpha
     stimulation (0.1 ng/mL) and 6 h post-stimulation tracking of p65 nuclear translocation
  3. Image-based machine learning: SVM classifier trained on 236 hand-crafted features
     per cell; predicts activation with 79.4% accuracy from prestimulation images alone
  4. Fixed-cell immunofluorescence: validates the IkB-alpha/NF-kB ratio as the primary
     molecular determinant of heterogeneous single-cell activation probability

Key finding: cell-to-cell variability in NF-kB activation is largely explained by a
preexisting difference in the IkB/NF-kB ratio. Cells with a low IkB/NF-kB ratio show
minute "leaky" nuclear p65 localization at rest and are significantly more sensitive to
TNF stimulation. Activated cells show on average a 5-fold higher leaky nuclear p65 level
before stimulation than non-responding cells (P = 1.35e-13). Resting cells dynamically
transition between molecular states but maintain their overall activation probability
(autocorrelation r = 0.78 at 35 min before stimulation, n = 1109 cells).


DEVICE AND IMAGING SETUP
-------------------------
Device material  : PDMS microfluidic chambers
Surface coating  : Fibronectin (FC010-10MG), overnight at room temperature
Cell density     : ~20,000 cells/cm2; cells taken at 100% confluence via 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA
                   (25200-056) for 5 min and cultured 5 h before stimulation
Culture          : 37 C, 5% CO2; standard cell culture conditions maintained during imaging
                   using an on-stage incubation chamber
Microscope       : Nikon Eclipse Ti2
Camera           : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V3 Digital CMOS (C13440)
Magnification    : 20x
Imaging interval : 5 min per field of view
Stimulus delivery: TNF-alpha vials pressurized at 5 psi; connected to chip via PEEK microbore
                   tubing (VICI)
Image analysis   : Custom MATLAB scripts; NF-kB quantified as mean nuclear fluorescence
                   intensity after background correction; peak analysis via MATLAB smooth +
                   z-score normalization + peak detection


CELL LINE
---------
Parental         : p65(-/-) knockout NIH 3T3 mouse fibroblasts
Reporters        :
  p65-dsRed      : NF-kB transcription factor p65 fused to dsRed, expressed under native
                   p65 promotor; minimum fluorescence clone selected to represent endogenous
                   NF-kB pathway dynamics
  H2B-GFP        : Histone 2B fused to GFP, expressed from ubiquitin promotor; serves as
                   nuclear marker for segmentation and cell tracking

In activated cells, cytoplasmic p65-dsRed rapidly translocates to the nucleus in a digital
(switch-like) fashion within ~40 min of TNF stimulation. Non-responding cells show no
translocation and no NF-kB target gene expression.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Chamber Coating
  Reagent  : Fibronectin (FC010-10MG)
  Duration : Overnight (~720 min) at room temperature
  Purpose  : Promotes cell adhesion to PDMS chamber surface prior to loading

Step 2 | PBS Wash of Coated Chamber
  Reagent  : PBS
  Duration : 1 min
  Purpose  : Removes unbound fibronectin before cell seeding

Step 3 | Cell Seeding and Pre-stimulation Culture
  Cell line: NIH 3T3 p65-dsRed / H2B-GFP
  Density  : ~20,000 cells/cm2
  Process  : Cells harvested at 100% confluence with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA (25200-056) for
             5 min, loaded into coated chamber
  Culture  : 5 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 300 min) before stimulation; allows cell adhesion and
             equilibration to endogenous reporter expression levels

Step 4 | Prestimulation Live-Cell Imaging (t = -90 min to t = 0)
  Duration  : 1.5 h = 90 min; image every 5 min (18 time points)
  Channels  : p65-dsRed (red), H2B-GFP (green), phase contrast
  Output    : 236 hand-crafted features per cell per time point, including:
                - Mean nuclear p65-dsRed fluorescence (top predictor, r = 0.62)
                - SD of nuclear p65-dsRed
                - Nuclear phase entropy
                - Nuclear pixel correlation (information measure)
                - Otsu dimension
                - SFTA (Segmentation-based Fractal Texture Analysis)
                - Major axis length
                - H2B-GFP channel morphology features
  Purpose   : Provides the unperturbed cell image input for the SVM activation classifier.
              Cells are not chemically stimulated during this window.
  Note      : mix step in BioScript abstracts the repeated imaging acquisition loop;
              no reagent mixing occurs at this step.

Step 5 | TNF-alpha Stimulation (t = 0)
  Reagent          : TNF-alpha (PMC3014_3671982503)
  Diluent          : FluoroBrite DMEM (A1896701) + 2x GlutaMAX (35050061) +
                     penicillin/streptomycin (15140-122) + FBS (16140071)
  Concentration    : 0.1 ng/mL (main dataset, n = 2113 cells)
                     Multi-dose: 0.005, 0.05, 0.5, 5 ng/mL (n = 3456 cells combined)
  Delivery         : Pressurized vial at 5 psi; PEEK microbore tubing (VICI); chip inlet
  Time zero        : Stimulation marks t = 0 for all single-cell NF-kB trace analyses

Step 6 | Post-Stimulation Live-Cell Imaging (t = 0 to t = +360 min)
  Duration      : 6 h = 360 min at 37 C, 5% CO2; image every 5 min (72 time points)
  Readout       : Nuclear NF-kB (p65-dsRed) tracked per cell over 6 h
  Activation    : Responding cells show complete cytoplasm-to-nucleus translocation
                  (digital / switch-like behavior); non-responding cells show no change
  Labeling      : Binary threshold on (nuclear p65_peak - nuclear p65_(t=0)) > 500
                  (MATLAB: smooth + z-score normalization, peak detection; Fig. S4A)
  Datasets      : Main: 0.1 ng/mL TNF, n = 2113 cells (independent validation set)
                  Multi-dose: 0.005-5 ng/mL, n = 3456 cells (SVM training set)

Step 7 | NF-kB Activation Detection (QC Gate)
  Module   : nfkbActivationDetection
  Duration : 30 s (image analysis classification)
  Gate     :
    Pass (activationSignal > 0)  -> activated cell; proceed to fixed-cell IF (Step 8-13)
    Fail (activationSignal <= 0) -> non-responding cell; drain

Step 8 | PBS Rinse (pass branch only)
  Reagent  : PBS
  Duration : 1 min
  Purpose  : Removes culture medium before fixation; matches Materials and Methods protocol

Step 9 | Paraformaldehyde Fixation (pass branch only)
  Reagent     : 4% PFA in PBS (ParaformaldehydeFixative)
  Duration    : 10 min at room temperature (25 C)
  Imaging note: Cell image taken at t = -5 min (immediately preceding fixation) used to
                align fixed-cell IF data with live imaging UMAP space (Fig. 5A-B)

------------
1. Prestimulation p65 nuclear leakiness is the primary predictor of single-cell NF-kB

   significant inverse correlation (rho = -0.256, P = 2.7e-11) confirmed by IF (Fig. 5C).
3. Activated cells show on average 5-fold higher leaky nuclear p65 before stimulation than
   non-responding cells (P = 1.35e-13; Fig. 4E). Leakiness represents ~12% of total fluorescence.
4. Unstimulated cells dynamically transition between molecular states but maintain stable
   activation probability (autocorrelation r = 0.78 at 35 min before stimulation, n = 1109).
5. 73.71% of state transitions remain within or adjacent to the same activation-probability
   cluster; TNF sensitivity is stable across the observed prestimulation time window.
6. Counterintuitively, cells with high initial IkB require a smaller TNF dose to achieve
   NF-kB activation, because probability depends on the IkB/NF-kB ratio, not absolute IkB.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidic Device for Measuring Cell Migration Towards Substrate-Bound and Soluble Chemokine Gradients
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/srep36440
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/srep36440
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2016, Vol. 6, Article 36440
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidic device with LAPAP photo-patterning and flow-free diffusion gradient generation


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic approach for simultaneously generating surface-immobilized
haptotactic chemokine gradients and diffusion-based soluble chemotactic gradients within the same
migration chamber, enabling quantitative single-cell tracking of dendritic cell (DC) migration in
combined and competing chemokine gradient fields.

The device integrates three functional capabilities:
  1. LAPAP (Laser-Assisted Protein Adsorption by Photobleaching) photo-patterning of
     arbitrarily shaped, graded surface-immobilized chemokine patterns (CCL21 24-98 bio)
     with ~0.7 um lateral resolution and ~100:1 dynamic range.
  2. Flow-free diffusion-based soluble chemokine gradients (CCL19) via source-sink
     flow-switching, independently controllable in steepness, mean concentration, and duration.
  3. Precise positioning of immune cells on haptotactic gradients, with simultaneous
     superimposition of opposing or co-directional soluble gradients.

The protocol is divided into three experimental arms:
  ARM 1. Haptotaxis arm: DC migration on immobilized CCL21 gradient (no soluble gradient)
  ARM 2. Chemotaxis arm: DC migration in soluble CCL19 diffusion gradient (no immobilized chemokine)
  ARM 3. Competing gradients arm: DC migration simultaneously exposed to opposing immobilized
         CCL21 (haptotactic) and soluble CCL19 (chemotactic) gradients

Key finding: haptotactic CCL21 gradients dominate at low soluble CCL19 (~0-1 ug/mL), while
increasing CCL19 concentrations (~0-1.2 ug/mL) override the immobilized CCL21 signal and
redirect DC migration along the soluble gradient.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : PDMS flow layer; 6 migration chambers (l=1100 um, w=200 um, h_max=28 um).
            Each chamber has one side port at the midpoint of the long axis and two ports at
            the short ends connected to source and sink support channels.
Layer ii  : PDMS control layer; independently controllable PDMS membrane valves on all ports.
            Optimal closing pressure determined per chip by incrementing control channel
            pressure in 0.5 bar steps.
Layer iii : Glass substrate; coated with human plasma fibronectin (250 ug/mL, Millipore)
            for beta2-integrin-mediated DC adhesion and 2D migration.

Inlets  : 9 reagent inlets, 1 cell loading inlet
Outlets : 3 waste outlets

Support channels connect reagent inlets with migration chambers. Flow lines pressurised
at 0.2-0.4 bar. All ports equipped with independently controllable PDMS membrane valves.


CELL TYPE
---------
Bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (DCs) from C57BL/6J mice (C57BL6 strain).
Cultured: GM-CSF hybridoma cell line supernatant (granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating
factor) in non-adhesive petri dish. Bone marrow extracted from femur and tibia; 4500 rpm
spin distally capped bones. 2 x 10^6 cells/10 mL R10 medium per dish.
  - Day 0: seed bone marrow
  - Day 4: add 10 mL R10 + 2 mL GM-CSF supernatant
  - Day 7: replace 10 mL with fresh R10 + 2 mL GM-CSF supernatant
  - Day 8-10: harvest; mature overnight with LPS (200 ng/mL)
Cell culture medium (R10): RPMI 1640 + 10% fetal calf serum + L-Glucose +
Penicillin/Streptomycin (all from Life Sciences, Austria).


REAGENTS
--------
Buffer               : PBS (phosphate-buffered saline)
Surface coating      : Human plasma fibronectin, 250 ug/mL (Millipore, Austria)
LAPAP anchor         : Biotin-4-fluorescein (B4F), 150 ug/mL (Sigma Aldrich, US)
Streptavidin adapter : Streptavidin-Cy3 (SA-Cy3), 10 ug/mL in PBS + 3% BSA (Sigma Aldrich, US)
Immobilized chemokine: CCL21 24-98 bio (biotinylated truncated murine CCL21, aa 24-98;
                       custom synthesized by ALMAC, Craigavon, UK); 250 ng/mL in PBS;
                       stock 25 ug/mL in PBS; stored at -20 C.
                       Truncated to remove basic C-terminal extension (aa 99-134) which causes
                       unspecific binding via heparan sulfate. Max surface density: 157+/-33
                       molecules/um2 (quantified by fluorescence intensity standard curve).
Soluble chemokine    : Murine CCL19 (R&D Systems, USA); 2.5 ug/mL in R10; stock 25 ug/mL in PBS.
Gradient tracer      : FITC-dextran 10 kDa, 200 ug/mL (Sigma Aldrich, US);
                       hydrodynamic radius 2.3 nm (comparable to CCL19: 1.7+/-0.4 nm,
                       CCL21: 1.9+/-0.4 nm).
Cell culture medium  : R10 (RPMI 1640 + 10% FCS + L-Glucose + Pen/Strep)
DC maturation        : LPS, 200 ng/mL


LAPAP SYSTEM
------------
Full name            : Laser-Assisted Protein Adsorption by Photobleaching
Laser                : 355 nm pulsed UV, steerable; pulse frequency 1 kHz
Objective            : Zeiss LD Plan Neo 20x/0.4 (long working distance)
Scanning             : High-speed galvanometric mirror pair; spot spacing ~half focus diameter
                       for continuous pattern; total light dose split into multiple pulses per
                       spot to average pulse-to-pulse power variability
Lateral resolution   : ~0.7 um
Dynamic range        : ~100:1
Pattern specification: Image file; pixel intensity values determine local light dose (bleaching dose)
Calibration          : Compensates for off-center numerical aperture drop and geometric
                       distortions from scan mirrors into objective back aperture
Pattern types        : Uniform patch (haptokinesis control), linear gradient (haptotaxis)
Reference            : Behrndt et al., Science 338, 257 (2012) for hardware description


GRADIENT GENERATION
-------------------
Soluble method       : Flow-free diffusion; source-sink flow-switching strategy
                       (Frank & Tay, Lab Chip 13, 1273, 2013;
                        Mehling et al., Lab Chip 15, 1276, 2015)
Source channel       : Sequentially refilled with R10 + CCL19 (2.5 ug/mL) + FITC-dextran
                       10 kDa (200 ug/mL) via short-end port
Sink channel         : Sequentially refilled with fresh R10 via opposite short-end port
Gradient build time  : ~2.5 h to reach peak CCL19 ~1.8 ug/mL (~190 nM)
CCR7/CCL19 Kd       : 10-100 nM (concentrations in gradient cover dissociation constant range
                       and are sufficient for G-protein loading and downstream signalling)
CCL19 regimes tested :
  CCL19_low    : 0-1.2 ug/mL -> chemokinesis (increased speed, undirected)
  CCL19_medium : 0-1.3 ug/mL -> directed chemotaxis (significantly increased directionality)
  CCL19_high   : 0-1.7 ug/mL -> highly directional chemotaxis (further augmented directionality)
Gradient monitoring  : FITC-dextran fluorescence; spatially averaged over centered
                       longitudinal section of chamber (Fig. 1d in paper)

STATISTICAL ANALYSIS

Directionality metric : <cos(Theta)>; Theta = angle between gradient direction and current
                        cell direction. Determined every 3 min (cells move ~1 cell diameter).

Bootstrapping         : 200 resamplings with original sample size
Error bars            : Standard deviation of <cos(Theta)> from bootstrapping

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Digital Microfluidic Platform for Human Plasma Protein Depletion
Source Link  : https://collectionscanada.gc.ca/obj/thesescanada/vol2/OKQ/TC-OKQ-12209.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac5022198
Journal      : M.Sc. Thesis, Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario, Canada, May 2014
               Supervisors: Dr. Richard D. Oleschuk & Dr. Aaron A. Wheeler
Platform     : Two-plate digital microfluidics (DMF) on glass chip with automated
               motor-controlled magnetic separation and custom Microdrop software


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated DMF-based method for depleting high-abundance
human plasma proteins -- human serum albumin (HSA) and immunoglobulin G (IgG) --
which together constitute approximately 80% of total plasma protein content and severely
mask low-abundance analytes in proteomic studies. The approach uses paramagnetic beads
functionalized with Protein A/G (for IgG capture) and anti-HSA (for HSA capture),
actuated and mixed on a two-plate glass DMF device under an automated controller system.

The protocol depletes IgG and HSA simultaneously with up to 98% efficiency in 10 minutes
across four samples processed in parallel. Depleted samples show an approximately 3-fold
increase in MALDI-MS signal-to-noise ratio and are compatible with downstream LC-MS/MS
proteomic analysis. Successful tryptic in-solution digestion of cytochrome C from depleted
samples yielded 89% sequence coverage (11 peptides, MALDI score 225).

The protocol consists of two encoded phases:
  1. Core on-chip protein depletion: eight-step bead-based immunocapture workflow
  2. Fluorescence kinetics characterisation: FITC-IgG and FITC-HSA depletion efficiency
     probed at 30-second intervals over 10 minutes total using a PHERAstar plate reader


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Format     : Two-plate glass DMF chip
Fabrication: University of Toronto Nanofabrication Centre (TNFC) clean room
Bottom plate: Patterned electrode array on glass
Top plate   : ITO-coated glass (ground plate)
Coatings    : Parylene-C dielectric (vapor deposition) + Teflon-AF hydrophobic layer (spin-coat)

Actuation   : 100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz sine wave
Droplet vol : 4 uL unit droplets; four droplets merged per depletion run
Incubation  : Figure-8 pattern across 4 electrodes for continuous droplet/bead mixing

Magnetic separation:
  Motor-controlled magnetic lens assembly (~600 uN force; minimum threshold 470 uN)
  Magnet position automated via custom Microdrop software + Pogo-pin interface
  Microcapture USB camera for real-time video monitoring

Controller system: National Instruments PXI chassis (MIP), custom Microdrop software
                   NI PXI-4130 (DC power), NI PXI-5422 (AC function generator)


REAGENTS
--------
Plasma proteins:
  HSA          : 0.5 mg/mL in PBS (66,437 Da; lyophilized, Life Technologies)
  IgG          : 2.0 mg/mL in PBS (150,000 Da; diluted from 4.7 mg/mL stock)
  FITC-IgG     : 0.5 mg/mL (GenScript USA Inc., Piscataway, NJ) -- kinetics only
  FITC-HSA     : 1.0 mg/mL (Abcam, Cambridge, MA) -- kinetics only
  Hemopexin    : 0.1 mg/mL in PBS (57,000 Da; low-abundance marker)

Paramagnetic beads (Millipore, Billerica, MA; 10 um diameter):
  Protein A/G Beads : PureProteome Protein A/G Mix Magnetic Beads (LSKMAGAG02)
                      Diluted 1:4 from stock in PBS; captures IgG
  Anti-HSA Beads    : PureProteome Albumin Magnetic Beads (LSKMAGL02)
                      Diluted 1:2 from stock in PBS; captures HSA

Buffer      : Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS)
Surfactant  : Pluronic F-68 at 0.05% in PBS
              Selection rationale: Pluronic F-127 and L64 inhibited Protein A/G bead
              binding (Chapter 3 screening). Pluronics L92, F68, and F88 did not interfere
              with binding; F-68 produced optimal droplet movement on DMF chip.

Waste removal: KimWipes (Kimberly-Clark) wicking from device surface


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Reagent Preparation and Device Loading
  Reagents  : ProteinAG_Beads, AntiHSA_Beads, PlasmaProteinSample, PBS_Buffer, PluronicF68
  Operation : Off-chip bead dilution; pipette-load into device reservoirs
  Notes     : Bead types combined into single mixed-bead suspension on-chip (5s mix).
              Protein sample (IgG + HSA + hemopexin + 0.05% F-68 in PBS) prepared fresh.
              4 uL droplets. Four samples processed simultaneously in parallel.

Step 2 | Bead Actuation onto Device Array
  Reagents  : mixedBeads, PBS_Buffer
  Operation : DMF electrode actuation (100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz)
  Notes     : Mixed bead droplet moved from reservoir into active array. Beads remain
              suspended during electrode-to-electrode transfer.

Step 3 | First Magnet Engagement -- Bead Immobilization
  Operation : heat at 25c for 30s (BioScript abstraction for magnet dwell)
  Duration  : 30 s
  Notes     : Motor-controlled magnet (~600 uN) lowered below chip. Paramagnetic beads
              pelleted onto device surface. heat at 25c is a BioScript-level abstraction

Step 4 | Supernatant Removal and PBS Wash
  Reagents  : PBS_Buffer
  Operation : mix beadDroplet + washBuffer for 5s; heat at 25c for 30s
  Notes     : Bead storage buffer actuated to waste and wicked off with KimWipes. PBS
              wash droplet added; magnet re-engaged (30s) to re-pellet beads before
              sample merging.

Step 5 | Protein Sample Merge with Bead Pellet
  Reagents  : beadWash1, samplePlusMix
  Operation : mix for 10s
  Notes     : Sample droplet actuated over immobilized beads; magnet disengaged to
              resuspend beads into protein sample. Merged droplet contains IgG, HSA,
              hemopexin, 0.05% F-68, Protein A/G beads, and anti-HSA beads.

Step 6 | Active Incubation -- Figure-8 Mixing
  Operation : heat at 37c for 10m
  Temperature: 37 C
  Duration  : 10 min (600 s)
  Pattern   : Figure-8 across 4 electrodes; 100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz
  Results   : IgG depletion efficiency up to 98%; HSA depletion efficiency up to 98%
              (FITC-labeled fluorescence assay, N=3-4 per condition)
  Notes     : Continuous movement maximizes bead-protein contact. All four samples
              run concurrently on the same device.

Step 7 | Bead Re-Immobilization and Supernatant Separation
  Operation : heat at 25c for 30s
  Duration  : 30 s
  Notes     : Magnet re-engaged; beads (now carrying captured IgG and HSA) pelleted.

================================================================================
PROTOCOL: LENGEN - Lentiviral Generation, Packaging, and Transduction
         on a Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform
================================================================================

SOURCE LINK : https://40332f11-eff8-4959-967a-6c98c26063bd.filesusr.com/ugd/447feb_13f855ea4ef54fee80498ee6773b93b0.pdf
PAPER DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05227
PUBLISHED   : Analytical Chemistry, 2022, Vol. 94, pp. 4039-4047

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

LENGEN is the first microfluidic method that integrates lentiviral generation,
packaging, and transduction on a single digital microfluidic (DMF) platform.
It produces viral titers between 6.5 x 10^6 and 1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL (comparable
to macroscale) and achieves high transduction efficiency for hard-to-transfect
cell lines. The total protocol runs in approximately 2 days vs. ~2 weeks at
macroscale, with 100-fold volume savings and no ultracentrifugation or manual
purification.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVICE SPECIFICATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Platform                  : Digital Microfluidic (DMF), two-plate system
  Bottom plate electrodes   : 80 per set (2 sets total = 160 electrodes)
  Production site           : 1.6 mm diameter hydrophilic spot (x1 per set)
  Transduction sites        : ~1.2 mm diameter hydrophilic spots (x6 per set)
  Multiplexing              : 12-plex simultaneous transduction analysis
  Production droplet volume : ~3 uL (split into ~1 uL unit droplets)
  Actuation voltage         : ~500 V total, 15 kHz
  Electrode design          : Overlapping "prong" electrodes bussed via 2 wired
                              connections (22 electrodes per connection)
  Highway track             : One-directional delivery to 6 transduction sites

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS AND MATERIALS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CELLS
  - HEK293T            : Producer/packaging cell line
  - Target cell lines  : MCF-7, T47DKB-Luc, H1299 (breast cancer / lung)

  PLASMIDS (Core - Steps 1-8)
  - pMDLg/pRRE         : 0.75 ug  | Packaging plasmid
  - pRSV-Rev           : 0.75 ug  | Packaging plasmid
  - pMD2.G             : 1.5 ug   | Envelope plasmid
  - Transfer plasmid   : 3.0 ug   | e.g. pLv-mCherry (~4 kb)

  PLASMIDS (Optional Applications)
  - MISSION shRNA      : TRCN00000003300 | ESR1 knockdown (Step 9)
  - pLentiCRISPR-mCherry-NeoRv2 (LCMNv2) : ~15 kb | ESR1 knockout (Step 10)

  TRANSFECTION REAGENTS
  - Lipofectamine 3000 : 12.5 uL
  - P3000 Reagent      : 12.0 uL
  - Opti-MEM           : Total volume 500 uL
  - Pluronics F-127    : 0.05% w/v (added to all droplets for DMF actuation)

  CULTURE AND PROCESSING
  - Complete medium    : DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS
  - DMEM + Polybrene   : 8 ug/mL polybrene + 0.05% Pluronics F-127 (diluent)
  - Trypsin-EDTA       : 0.25% w/v, 2 uL per well (cell detachment)
  - PBS                : 5 uL per well (wash buffer prior to trypsinization)
  - Puromycin          : 1 ug/mL (selection, Step 9 only)

  DETECTION
  - Fluorescence microscope : Olympus IX73 inverted
    Excitation / Emission   : 585 nm / 608 nm (mCherry)
  - Hoechst 33342           : Nuclear stain (total cell count)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 - SEED HEK293T PRODUCER CELLS
--------------------------------------
  1a. Grow HEK293T cells in 100 mm Petri dishes, wash with PBS, trypsinize
      with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA, and resuspend in complete medium.
  1b. Count cells and prepare suspension at ~2.5-3.0 x 10^6 cells/mL.
  1c. Supplement cell suspension with 0.05% w/v Pluronics F-127.
  1d. Pipette 1.5 uL of cell suspension onto the bottom plate at the edge
      of the top plate. Apply driving potentials (~500 V, 15 kHz) to
      dispense and actuate droplet across the 1.6 mm hydrophilic production
      site (passive dispensing). ~1.5 uL adheres to the site.
  1e. Remove excess liquid to a waste reservoir with a KimWipe.
  1f. Incubate at 37 C until cells reach 50-70% confluency (~2500 cells).
      Duration: 24h

  NOTE: Cells can also be seeded onto the ~1.2 mm transduction sites in
  parallel at densities of 1.0-1.5 x 10^6 cells/mL (Step 5 may be done
  concurrently with Steps 2-4).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 2 - PREPARE LIPOFECTAMINE-DNA MASTERMIX
---------------------------------------------
  2a. Prepare plasmid mix in Opti-MEM:
        - 0.75 ug pMDLg/pRRE
        - 0.75 ug pRSV-Rev
        - 1.5 ug  pMD2.G
        - 3.0 ug  transfer plasmid (pLv-mCherry or equivalent)
      Mix each addition for 5s on the DMF device using the four-electrode
      linear array.

  2b. Prepare lipofection reagent mix:
        - 12.5 uL Lipofectamine 3000
        - 12.0 uL P3000 Reagent
      Mix for 5s.

  2c. Combine plasmid mix with lipofection reagent mix. Mix for 5s.

  2d. Add Opti-MEM to reach a total volume of 500 uL. Mix for 5s.

  2e. Add 0.05% w/v Pluronics F-127 for DMF actuation compatibility.
      Mix for 20m.

  2f. Incubate at room temperature (25 C) for 20 min to allow
      DNA-liposomal complex formation.

  NOTE: For shRNA knockdown (Step 9), replace transfer plasmid with
  MISSION shRNA plasmid (TRCN00000003300). For CRISPR knockout (Step 10),
  replace with LCMNv2 all-in-one Cas9/sgRNA plasmid (~15 kb).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 3 - TRANSFECT HEK293T CELLS
----------------------------------
  3a. Actuate the lipofectamine mastermix droplet (1.5 uL) toward the
      seeded HEK293T cells at the production site.
  3b. Circulate the merged droplet continuously around the four-prong
      electrode production area for 1 min (3 circulations) to ensure
      uniform mixing and replicate the reverse transfection procedure.
  3c. The formulation (3 uL total) is mixed in a circular fashion by
      actuating adjacent electrodes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 4 - LENTIVIRAL PARTICLE PRODUCTION AND SUPERNATANT HARVEST
-----------------------------------------------------------------
  4a. Incubate the transfected HEK293T cells at 37 C for 24h (or 48h for
      higher titer).
  4b. Lentiviral particles accumulate in the cell supernatant. Cells remain
      adhered to the hydrophilic production spot; supernatant is collected
      by electrode actuation for downstream dilution.

  Expected output:
    - 24h: ~1.56 TU/cell | Titer ~6.5 x 10^6 TU/mL
    - 48h: ~2.65 TU/cell | Titer ~1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL
    - Comparable to macroscale benchtop: ~2.80 TU/cell after 5 days

  NOTE: The 24h timepoint is sufficient for downstream gene silencing and
  editing assays. No ultracentrifugation or purification is required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 5 - SEED TARGET CELLS
----------------------------
  5a. Prepare target cell suspension (MCF-7, T47DKB-Luc, or H1299) at
      1.0-1.5 x 10^6 cells/mL in complete medium + 0.05% Pluronics F-127.
  5b. Dispense four independent target cell droplets (one per dilution) onto
      four separate 1.2 mm hydrophilic transduction sites via highway track
      passive dispensing. ~1.0 uL adheres to each site. Two additional sites
      are available for controls (complete medium +/- polybrene, no virus).
  5c. Remove excess liquid to waste reservoir.
  5d. Incubate at 37 C for 24h before transduction.

  Cell viability on device:
    - MCF-7      : 83.7% (48h), 85.7% (72h)
    - T47DKB-Luc : 98.4% (48h), 88.6% (72h)

  NOTE: Four independent target cell droplets are dispensed separately in
  the BioScript implementation to satisfy the use-once type system (each
  droplet variable can only be consumed once).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 6 - SERIAL DILUTION OF VIRAL SUPERNATANT
-----------------------------------------------
  6a. After production incubation (Step 4), generate four serial dilutions
      of the lentiviral supernatant using highway track electrode actuation
      (~98% actuation accuracy):

      Diluent: DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + 8 ug/mL polybrene
               + 0.05% Pluronics F-127

      Dilution series:
        1:3  - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 2 uL viral supernatant (5s mix)
        1:6  - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 1 uL of 1:3 product  (5s mix)
        1:12 - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 1 uL of 1:6 product  (5s mix)
        1:24 - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 1 uL of 1:12 product (5s mix)

  6b. Two control spots are prepared:
        - Control 1: Complete medium + 8 ug/mL polybrene (no virus)
        - Control 2: Complete medium only (no polybrene, no virus)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 7 - TRANSDUCE TARGET CELLS
---------------------------------
  7a. Actuate each dilution (1 uL) to its dedicated target cell site via the
      highway track one-directional electrode path. Each dilution is merged
      with its own independent target cell droplet. The transduction
      incubation is encoded directly in the mix operation (24h duration).
  7b. Flip the DMF device upside down and incubate overnight at 37 C to
      maximize lentiviral contact with target cells.
      Duration: 24h (sufficient) or 48h (for improved efficiency)

  Transduction efficiency (T47DKB-Luc):
    - 48h post-transduction : ~43%
    - 96h post-transduction : ~60%

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 8 - MCHERRY FLUORESCENCE DETECTION AND VIRAL TITER CALCULATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  8a. After incubation, image each transduction site using an Olympus IX73
      inverted fluorescence microscope.
        Excitation filter : 585 nm
        Emission filter   : 608 nm

  8b. Imaging pipeline (ImageJ):
        i.   Split Hoechst (nuclear) and mCherry channels
        ii.  Apply threshold to each channel independently
        iii. Count total Hoechst-stained nuclei (cell counter)
        iv.  Count mCherry-positive cells
        v.   Calculate: % Fluorescence = (mCherry+ cells / Hoechst nuclei) x 100

  8c. Calculate viral titer:
        TU/mL = (# cells transduced x % fluorescent x dilution factor)
                / transduction volume (mL)

  8d. QC gate (BioScript CFG):
        - Detect mCherry signal on all four transduction droplets (30s each).
        - If signal at 1:3 dilution > 0 : dispose transduction droplets (pass)
        - If signal at 1:3 dilution <= 0 : drain transduction droplets (fail)
        - All signal droplets are disposed unconditionally at the join block.

  Expected results:
    - Optimal dilution    : 1:3
    - Titer range         : 6.5 x 10^6 to 1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL
    - Functional titer    : ~1 x 10^7 TU/mL (on-device, 24h or 48h)
    - Macroscale benchtop : ~1 x 10^7 TU/mL (for comparison)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 9 - shRNA KNOCKDOWN ASSAY [OPTIONAL]
------------------------------------------
  Target gene : ESR1 (Estrogen Receptor alpha)
  Plasmid     : MISSION shRNA (TRCN00000003300, nontargeting shRNA as control)

  9a. Repeat Steps 2-8 substituting the transfer plasmid with the MISSION
      shRNA plasmid targeting ESR1. Fresh independent producer cell and
      target cell droplets are dispensed for this branch.
  9b. After 24h transduction, retrieve transduced cells from the device:
        i.   Bring device to biosafety cabinet and separate top from bottom plate.
        ii.  Pipette 5 uL PBS onto each microwell; aspirate with Pasteur pipette
             (leaves only adhered cells).
        iii. Add 2 uL Trypsin-EDTA (0.25% w/v); replace top plate; incubate
             2 min at 37 C with 5% CO2.
        iv.  Pool 2 microwells of the same dilution by resuspending each in
             10 uL complete medium; transfer to 100 uL complete medium in a
             96-well plate (~2800 cells total).
  9c. Next day, refresh medium with complete medium + 1 ug/mL puromycin.
  9d. After 7 days outgrowth, collect cell lysate for qRT-PCR analysis.
        Method          : delta-delta-Cq (DDCq)
        Reference gene  : ACTB (beta-actin)
        Target gene     : ESR1

  9e. QC gate (BioScript CFG):
        - Detect geneKnockdownDetection signal on shrnaCells (30s).
        - If shrnaSignal > 0 : dispose shrnaCells (pass)
        - If shrnaSignal <= 0 : drain shrnaCells (fail)
        - shrnaSignal disposed unconditionally at join block.

  Expected mRNA transcript reduction (MCF-7 cells, LENGEN):
    Dilution 1:3  -> 89% knockdown
    Dilution 1:6  -> 79% knockdown
    Dilution 1:12 -> 48% knockdown
    Dilution 1:24 -> 18% knockdown

  NOTE: Results are consistent with well-plate (macroscale) controls at
  equivalent MOIs (MOI 5 = 89% knockdown in well plate).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 10 - CRISPR-Cas9 KNOCKOUT ASSAY [OPTIONAL]
-------------------------------------------------
  Target gene : ESR1 (Estrogen Receptor alpha)
  Plasmid     : pLentiCRISPR-mCherry-NeoRv2 (LCMNv2), ~15 kb all-in-one
                Cas9 + sgRNA (available on Addgene)

  10a. Repeat Steps 2-8 substituting the transfer plasmid with LCMNv2.
       Fresh independent producer cell and target cell droplets are dispensed
       for this branch. Note: Larger payload (~15 kb vs ~4 kb) will reduce
       transduction efficiency; optimize MOI/dilution accordingly.
  10b. Retrieve transduced MCF-7 cells from device as described in Step 9b.
       No antibiotic selection required for CRISPR experiments.
  10c. Pool 1:3 dilution transduced cells (~2800 cells) into a 96-well plate
       for outgrowth and single-clone isolation.
  10d. After 7 days post-transduction, collect cell lysate and perform
       genomic cleavage assay (T7 endonuclease or equivalent):
         Parental band  : 409 bp  (blue arrow on gel)
         Cleavage bands : 235 bp and 174 bp (red arrows on gel)
         % Cleavage calculated from band intensity ratios.

  10e. Confirm mCherry fluorescence to verify transduction before cleavage
       assay (mCherry co-expressed with Cas9 in LCMNv2).

  10f. QC gate (BioScript CFG):
        - Detect mCherryDetection signal on crisprCells (30s).
        - If crisprMCherry > 0 : dispose crisprCells (pass)
        - If crisprMCherry <= 0 : drain crisprCells (fail)
        - crisprMCherry disposed unconditionally at terminal join block (BB10).

  Expected knockout cleavage efficiency:
    LENGEN (1:3 dilution) : ~6.9%
    Well plate MOI 0.5    : ~5.8%
    Well plate MOI 1      : ~6.2%
    Well plate MOI 2      : ~6.4%
    Well plate MOI 5      : ~9.4%

  NOTE: For H1299 cells with integrated eGFP, gene cleavage efficiency
  of 16.1% was observed using the same LENGEN workflow.

  Volume savings        : 100-fold reduction vs. macroscale

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidic DNA Library Preparation Platform for Next-Generation Sequencing
Source Link  : https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0068988&type=printable
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0068988
Journal      : PLoS ONE, 2013, Vol. 8, Issue 7, Article e68988
Platform     : DMF hub with peripheral capillary-based modules (digital microfluidics +
               continuous-flow off-chip sample preparation modules)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a fully integrated and automated microfluidic system for preparing
Illumina sequencer-ready NGS libraries from nanogram-scale genomic DNA samples. The platform
combines a central digital microfluidic (DMF) hub -- a planar, Teflon-AF-coated ITO electrode
array that actuates discrete droplets via electrowetting -- with peripheral continuous-flow
capillary-based modules that perform each of the four unit operations in the Nextera library
preparation workflow: DNA tagmentation, magnetic bead-based clean-up, limited-cycle PCR, and
two-stage size selection.

The DMF hub serves as a "fluidic router": it meters reagents, routes droplets between
peripheral modules via in-plane fused-silica capillaries, and integrates all sample
preparation steps into a single, hands-free, programmable protocol. Off-DMF modules are
individually optimised for their respective unit operations, allowing reliable thermocycling,
magnetic bead manipulation, and precise size selection that would be difficult to implement
on the DMF surface alone.

The platform was validated with human genomic DNA, Escherichia coli MG1655 gDNA (5 ng input),
and Klebsiella pneumoniae BAA-2146 (KpnNDM) gDNA. E. coli libraries yielded >99% alignment
to the reference genome, even genome coverage, and mean depth of 168-320X across three
replicates. De novo assembly of KpnNDM revealed at least five beta-lactamase genes including
NDM-1. The protocol reduces hands-on time to ~5 min and total preparation time to ~1 h,
using ~30 uL total reagent volume (vs. 80-650 uL conventional).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Hub type : Central DMF hub; two gap configurations:
             185 um gap (human gDNA; 1-2 uL droplet volumes)
             400 um gap (bacterial gDNA; 2X volumes)

Bottom plate : ITO-patterned glass (photolithography + etching); coated with 4 um Parylene-C
               + 50 nm Teflon-AF (spin-coated 1% wt/wt Fluorinert FC-40, 2000 rpm, 60 s;
               post-baked at 160 C, 10 min). 48 actuation electrodes: 44 rectangular
               (~2.5 x 2.5 mm and ~6.3 x 9.5 mm), 4 pentagon-shaped (~4.5 x 7.5 x 6.3 mm);
               inter-electrode gap 20 um.
Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO glass; 50 nm Teflon-AF.
Manifold     : Custom-engineered polymer manifold frame with metal compression frames;
               spring-loaded pogo-pin electrical contacts; CapTite fittings.

Capillary interface:
  14 side ports; fused-silica capillaries (Polymicro) coated in-house with Teflon-AF.
  185 um gap:  160/100 um OD/ID capillaries (Part TSU100170); tip ~250 um from
               2.5 x 2.5 mm receiving electrodes.
  400 um gap:  360/100 um OD/ID capillaries (Part TSU100375); directly inserted.
  Module tubing: 750/562 um OD/ID polycarbonate (Part CT562-750-5, Paradigm Optics).
  Short coupling tubes: 500/167 um OD/ID (Part CT250-500-5); glued with optical cement.
  Pumping:     8-port valve manifold syringe pump (Part 59943-01, Hamilton, Reno NV);
               positive displacement; 10 uL/min flow rate. 1-2 uL air gap separates
               reagent bolus from pumping water.

Peripheral modules:
  Tagmentation   : Thermal module; 750 um OD tubing in ~850 x 800 um (D x W) groove in
                   custom-machined Al block; module recessed ~100 um below block surface
                   for temperature match within ~5 C. Closed-loop PID TEC.
  Limited-cycle PCR : Same Al block configuration; OpenPCR benchtop cycler (Saratoga CA).
  Clean-up       : Capillary tube module; external neodymium magnet (3 mm dia x 3 mm,
                   K&J Magnetics, Jamison PA); positive pressure-driven syringe pump for
                   near-complete supernatant removal; bolus shuttle resuspension.
  Size selection : Same magnet/pump configuration as clean-up; two-stage bead:DNA ratio
                   protocol (2.2 uL and 0.45 uL SPRI beads for Stages 1 and 2).
  Waste          : Dedicated waste capillary and reservoir.

Actuation: 80-90 V_rms at 15 kHz generated by function generator (Trek, Medina NY) amplified
           by Digi-Key Corporation (Thief River Falls MN). Computer-controlled electronic
           interface via manual keystrokes or preprogrammed scripts. Droplets visualised with
           MVX10 microscope (Olympus) + QIClick camera (Qimaging); Streampix5 (Norpix) for
           video capture.


REAGENTS
--------
Carrier fluid      : Fluorinert FC-40 (Sigma Chemical, St. Louis MO)
Pluronic additive  : Pluronic F127 (Sigma Chemical); 0.1% w/v in all DNA and reagent solutions.
                     Added to prevent biofouling (protein/enzyme adsorption to Teflon-AF).
                     Validated not to affect Nextera tagmentation efficiency (Fig S1, paper).
Buffer             : 1X Tris-EDTA (TE) pH 8.0 (Sigma Chemical)
Nextera enzyme mix : Nextera DNA Sample Preparation Kit (Illumina, San Diego CA)
                     On-chip mixture: 2 uL High Molecular Weight + 0.5 uL enzyme mix + 0.1% F127
PCR mixture        : 12.5 uL 2X PCR buffer + 0.5 uL primer cocktail + 0.5 uL PCR enzyme
                     + 0.5 uL 50X Adapter 2 (Nextera kit); scaled to 2.8 uL on-chip volume
SPRI beads         : Solid Phase Reversible Immobilisation beads (Beckman Coulter, Danvers MA)
Wash solvent       : Ethanol (HPLC-grade organic solvent)
Elution buffer     : Water + 0.1% Pluronic F127 w/v
Decontamination    : 10% v/v bleach then deionized water rinse between library runs


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | gDNA Sample Dispensing and Nextera Enzyme Mixing
  Reagents        : GenomicDNA (1.8 uL at 5 ng/uL in TE + 0.1% F127); NexteraEnzymeMix (0.6 uL)
  Operation       : Dispense both droplets from pre-loaded capillaries onto 185 um-gap DMF hub;
                    actuate together; mix by continuous aspiration in and out of capillary for 30 s
                    at room temperature (80-90 V_rms, 15 kHz)
  Duration        : 30 s mixing
  Notes           : Bacterial gDNA runs use 400 um-gap hub with 2X volumes of all reagents.

Step 2 | Tagmentation
  Reagents        : tagmentationMix
  Operation       : Aspirate into tagmentation thermal module; incubate at 55 C for 5 min
  Temperature     : 55 C
  Duration        : 5 min (300 s)
  Module          : Tagmentation Al block (closed-loop PID TEC; temperature match within ~5 C)
  Product         : Adapter-tagged DNA fragments; broad 150-1000 bp distribution (Fig 4b);
                    adapter dimers ~45 bp also generated; removed in Step 3
  Notes           : Transposase simultaneously fragments and tags gDNA (Nextera transposition
                    reaction). No mechanical fragmentation or end-repair required.

Step 3 | Magnetic Bead Clean-up -- Capture and Supernatant Removal
  Reagents        : tagmentedProduct; MagneticBeads_SPRI (4.5 uL)
  Operation       : Merge on DMF hub (30 s); aspirate combined droplet into clean-up module;
                    apply external neodymium magnet; immobilise bead pellet on inner tube wall;
                    positive pressure-driven flow removes supernatant; supernatant returned to
                    DMF hub and actuated to waste capillary
  Duration        : 30 s mixing
  Supernatant removed: Excess enzyme, adapter dimers, small DNA fragments
  Notes           : Near-complete supernatant removal achieved by positive pressure-driven syringe
                    pump flow (vs. conventional DMF magnet actuation). Bead pellet not on DMF
                    surface -- preserves Teflon-AF coating (Fig 3, paper).

Step 4 | Ethanol Wash of Bead Pellet (x3)
  Reagents        : EthanolWash (3.0 uL per cycle)
  Operation       : Dispense fresh ethanol droplet onto DMF hub; aspirate into clean-up module;
                    shuttle bolus back-and-forth across immobilised bead pellet for 30 s;
                    return ethanol to DMF hub; actuate to waste module; aspirate off-chip.
                    Repeat for 3 wash cycles total
  Duration        : 30 s per wash cycle; 3 cycles
  Notes           : Chaotic back-and-forth mixing enhances contaminant removal. Each wash
                    uses a fresh 3 uL ethanol droplet dispensed independently.

Step 5 | Elution of Purified Tagmented DNA
  Reagents        : ElutionBuffer (2.2 uL)
  Operation       : Dispense elution buffer onto DMF hub; aspirate into clean-up module;
                    remove external magnet; shuttle bolus for 30 s to resuspend bead pellet;
                    re-apply magnet to immobilise beads; return DNA-containing eluate to DMF hub;
                    actuate to PCR inlet electrode
  Duration        : 30 s resuspension
  Temperature     : Room temperature
  Product         : 2.2 uL purified adapter-tagged DNA fragments (excess enzyme and adapter
                    dimers removed)

Step 6 | PCR Mixture Dispensing and Merging with Eluate
  Reagents        : cleanedDNA (2.2 uL); PCRMixture (2.8 uL)
  Operation       : Dispense PCR Mixture from capillary onto DMF hub; merge with eluate (30 s);
                    aspirate 2.8 uL combined droplet into PCR thermal module inlet;
                    remaining 2.2 uL actuated to waste
  Duration        : 30 s mixing

Step 7 | Limited-Cycle PCR -- Adapter Addition and Library Enrichment
  Reagents        : prePCRDroplet (2.8 uL in PCR module)
  Operation       : Thermocycling in PCR module (Al block, OpenPCR cycler, closed-loop PID TEC)
  PCR conditions  :
    Initial extension  : 72 C for 3 min
    Denaturation       : 95 C for 30 s
    10 cycles          :
      Denaturation     : 95 C for 10 s
      Annealing        : 62 C for 30 s
      Extension        : 72 C for 3 min
    Note: 9 cycles for bacterial gDNA (400 um gap hub)
  Product         : Enriched library ~200-10000 bp; Illumina-specific dual-indexed sequencing
                    adapters incorporated; primer dimers ~55 bp present (removed by size selection)
                    (Fig 4c)
  Notes           : PCR reaction mixture (2.8 uL) cycled in module. After completion, product
                    dispensed back onto DMF hub for size selection.

Step 8 | Size Selection Stage 1 -- Removal of Fragments <200 bp
  Reagents        : prePCRDroplet; MagneticBeads_SPRI (2.2 uL)
  Operation       : Merge PCR product with SPRI beads on DMF hub (30 s); aspirate into
                    size-selection module; apply magnet; immobilise beads;
                    return supernatant to DMF hub
  Bead ratio      : High bead:DNA ratio (binds all DNA fragments including primer dimers
                    and small fragments <200 bp onto beads)
  Supernatant     : Contains desired 200-400 bp library fragments in solution at this ratio
  Notes           : The supernatant -- not the bead-bound fraction -- carries the size-selected
                    library at Stage 1. Bead pellet (small DNA, primer dimers) disposed.

Step 9 | Size Selection Stage 2 -- Removal of Fragments >400 bp
  Reagents        : librarySuper; MagneticBeads_SPRI (0.45 uL); EthanolWash; ElutionBuffer
  Operation       : Merge Stage 1 supernatant with low-volume SPRI beads (30 s); aspirate into
                    size-selection module; apply magnet; immobilise beads containing 200-400 bp
                    library; ethanol wash bead pellet; elute final library (3 uL EB; 5 uL for
                    bacterial gDNA); return eluate to DMF hub as final sequencer-ready library
  Bead ratio      : Low bead:DNA ratio (captures only large fragments >400 bp; desired
                    200-400 bp library bound to pellet after Stage 1 supernatant binds)
  Product         : Final sequencer-ready DNA library; target size distribution 200-400 bp
                    (Fig 4d); small broad hump at high MW indicates trace single-stranded products
  Notes           : At Stage 2 the desired 200-400 bp library IS bead-bound; large fragments
                    remain in solution and are disposed. Final library eluted into 3 uL (human)
                    or 5 uL (bacterial) elution buffer and dispensed to DMF hub.

Step 10 | Library QC Detection and Off-chip Sequencing
  Reagents        : dnaLibrary (3 uL)
  Operation       : detect libraryQC on dnaLibrary for 30 s
  Detection module: libraryQC (abstracts Bioanalyzer size distribution check + Kapa quant)
  Off-chip QC     :
    Size distribution : Bioanalyzer (Agilent); target peak 200-400 bp (Fig 4d)
    Quantitation      : Kapa Library Quantification Kit (KAPA Biosystems, Woburn MA)
    Loading conc.     : 8 pM on MiSeq; primary variability source is ~1000X dilution step
    Sequencing kit    : 300-cycle paired-end 150 bp MiSeq kit (Illumina)
    Read archive      : NCBI SRA accession SAMN02152539 (E. coli); APNN00000000.1 (K. pneumoniae)
  Branch          :
    Pass (BB2)    : librarySignal > 0 -> valid 200-400 bp library at sequencer-compatible
                    concentration; dispose for off-chip MiSeq loading
    Fail (BB3)    : librarySignal <= 0 -> failed library preparation; drain


SEQUENCING RESULTS (E. coli MG1655, 3 replicates)
--------------------------------------------------
Instrument      : Illumina MiSeq (in-house); 300-cycle paired-end 150 bp kit; 8 pM loading
Total bases     : 1.1 GB, 0.7 GB, 1.3 GB

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform for Complete Mammalian Cell Culture — Adherent Cell Seeding, Growth, Media Exchange, Subculture, and On-Demand Transfection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Fibronectin (ECM protein, dispensed and dried to form an "adhesion pad" on the Teflon-AF electrode surface)
  - Cell Suspension (CHO-K1, HeLa, NIH-3T3, or INS-1 cells, 20-100 cells seeded per 150 nL droplet)
  - Growth Media (DMEM, F-12/DMEM, or RPMI 1640, supplemented with 10% FBS)
  - Fresh Media (used for daily passive-dispensing media exchange, three source droplets per exchange)
  - Trypsin/EDTA (0.25% vol/vol trypsin, 1 mM EDTA, used to detach cells from the adhesion pad)
  - Harvest Media (1 uL droplet passed over the primary pad to collect detached cells and deliver them to the secondary pad; ~2-3% of cells transferred per pass, four passes per subculture)
  - Transfection Mix (pCAG-GFP plasmid DNA complexed with Dreamfect cationic lipid, diluted in culture media)

STEPS:
1. Adhesion pad preparation: Dispense a droplet of fibronectin onto the electrode and allow it to dry, forming an ECM-coated adhesion pad on the hydrophobic Teflon-AF surface.
2. Cell seeding: Dispense a 150 nL droplet of cell suspension (20-100 cells) onto the primary (1 deg) adhesion pad and mix with growth media.
3. Growth incubation: Incubate the seeded droplet at 37 C (5% CO2 humidified chamber) for 24 h, allowing cells to shift from round to spread morphology.
4. Daily media exchange (passive dispensing): Every 24 h, drive three successive 1 uL source droplets of fresh media across the adhesion pad; each passing droplet sweeps away old media and leaves a fresh ~150 nL droplet behind (<3% carryover after one exchange, background level after three). Repeat this daily exchange/incubation cycle across the culture period.
5. Confluency check: Monitor cell density; once cells reach the second half of exponential growth (high density, e.g. 200-300 cells on the pad), proceed to subculture.
6. Cell detachment: Passively exchange the old media on the primary pad with a 150 nL droplet of trypsin/EDTA (three source-droplet exchanges) and allow cells to dissociate for 3-5 min.
7. Harvest and delivery to secondary pad: Translate a 1 uL droplet of fresh media over the primary pad to collect dissociated cells (blocking further trypsin activity), then drive the droplet to the secondary (2 deg) adhesion pad, where a passive-dispensing step deposits some of the cells. Repeat four times (collect + deliver) so that ~10% of the primary-pad cells are transferred to the secondary pad, then discard the depleted primary-pad droplet.
8. Secondary-pad growth: Incubate the newly seeded secondary pad at 37 C for 72 h, with daily passive-dispensing media exchange as in step 4, before subculturing again onto a subsequent generation.
9. On-demand transfection: Passively exchange the media on a subcultured (2 deg) pad with a 150 nL droplet of transfection mix (pCAG-GFP plasmid + Dreamfect lipid, ~5 ng DNA/~20 nL lipid per droplet) and incubate 3 h at 37 C.
10. Post-transfection recovery: Passively exchange the transfection solution for fresh media (three source droplets) and incubate overnight (24 h) at 37 C to allow GFP expression.
11. Detection: Image/quantify GFP fluorescence on the droplet to determine transfection efficiency, then discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful implementation of complete on-chip mammalian cell culture is confirmed by growth/proliferation rates and morphology in droplets comparable to conventional multiwell-plate culture across multiple cell lines and subculture generations, and by transfection efficiencies (~20% GFP-positive cells) comparable to macro-scale transfection, supporting the DMF platform as an automated, miniaturized alternative to conventional mammalian cell seeding, feeding, passaging, and on-demand genetic transformation.
