This protocol describes an ultra-high-throughput, label-free method for the enrichment of
circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from peripheral blood of cancer patients using a multiplexed
spiral microfluidic biochip. The device exploits inertial focusing and Dean drag forces within
rectangular-cross-section spiral microchannels to achieve size-based separation of CTCs from
hematological cells without the need for antibody labelling or immunomagnetic steps.

The protocol is divided into three independent functional experiments:
  1. MCF-7 spiked recovery efficiency experiment -- validates device recovery and purity
     using a breast adenocarcinoma cell line (MCF-7) spiked into healthy donor blood.
  2. T24 cell viability experiment -- independently validates that neither the RBC lysis
     buffer nor the spiral shear forces compromise cell viability, using a bladder
     carcinoma cell line (T24) spiked into a separate healthy donor blood sample.
  3. Clinical CTC enrichment from patient blood -- isolates and identifies CTCs from
     7.5 mL blood samples of Stage IV metastatic breast cancer and NSCLC patients, with
     downstream immunofluorescence (IF) identification and HER2 FISH analysis.

The complete sample-to-CTC workflow (lysis to collection) takes approximately 10 minutes
for 7.5 mL of blood, compared to 30 minutes for the previous integrated biochip design.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type         : Multiplexed spiral microfluidic biochip
Configuration: 3 stacked single-layer PDMS spiral chips bonded together; 2 inlets, 2 outlets
Fabrication  : SU-8 silicon molds by standard photolithography; silanized with trichloro
               (1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane (Sigma Aldrich, USA) to render hydrophobic.
               PDMS prepolymer mixed 1:10 (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning, USA), degassed, poured
               onto SU-8 mold, cured at 80 C for 1-2 h. Four fluidic access holes punched.
               Three spiral chips bonded using oxygen plasma and manual alignment.
               Whole assembly bonded to microscopic glass slide by air plasma machine.

Channel      : Rectangular cross-section spiral microchannels
Separation   : Inertial focusing + Dean drag forces
               - Centrifugal forces in radial direction form two counter-rotating Dean vortices
               - CTCs (>15 um): equilibrate near inner microchannel wall (CTC outlet)
               - WBCs, RBCs, platelets (<20 um): migrate to outer wall (waste outlet)
Enrichment   : ~10^4-fold from RBC-depleted nucleated cell fraction

Inlets       : I1 (sample: nucleated cell fraction), I2 (sheath: PBS at 750 uL/min)
Outlets      : Inner wall (CTC collection), Outer wall (WBC/waste)


CELL LINES
----------
- MCF-7 (human breast adenocarcinoma, HTB-22, ATCC, ~20 um diameter):
  Used for recovery efficiency characterisation (Protocol 1).
  Cultured in high-glucose DMEM (Invitrogen) + 10% FBS (Invitrogen) + 1% penicillin-
  streptomycin (Invitrogen), 37 C, 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere, until 80% confluence.
  Sub-cultivated 1:3 twice weekly (BD Bioscience 6-well plates); media replaced every 48 h.
  Dissociated with 0.01% trypsin + 5.3 mM EDTA (Lonza, Switzerland).
  Resuspended in PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA (Miltenyi Biotec, Germany).

- T24 (human bladder carcinoma, HTB-4, ATCC, ~30 um diameter):
  Used for cell viability characterisation (Protocol 2). Independent experiment from MCF-7.
  Same culture conditions as MCF-7.


CLINICAL SAMPLES
----------------
- 10 patients: 5 metastatic breast cancer (Stage IV), 5 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC, Stage IV)
- 5 healthy donor controls
- 7.5 mL whole blood per sample, collected in Vacutainer EDTA tubes (Becton-Dickinson, NJ, USA)
- Processed within 2-4 h to prevent blood coagulation
- IRB-approved protocol (Institutional Review Board, Singapore)
- Collected in collaboration with National Cancer Centre Singapore and
  National University Hospital, Singapore


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

===========================================================
PROTOCOL 1: MCF-7 Spiked Recovery Efficiency Experiment
===========================================================

Step 1 | MCF-7 Cell Culture and Preparation
  Cell line    : MCF-7 (breast adenocarcinoma, ~20 um)
  Media        : High-glucose DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen-strep, 37 C, 5% CO2
  Duration     : 48 h representative culture period (172800 s; BioScript: heat at 37c for 2880m)
  Dissociation : 0.01% trypsin + 5.3 mM EDTA
  Resuspension : PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA (EDTA_BSA_Buffer)
  Note         : MCF-7 and T24 are spiked in separate, fully independent experiments.

Step 2 | Healthy Donor Blood Collection and RBC Lysis (MCF-7 arm)
  Volume       : 7.5 mL whole blood, Vacutainer EDTA tubes
  Lysis        : Ammonium chloride RBC lysis buffer (Bioscience, USA), 5 min at RT,
                 continuous gentle mixing
  Centrifugation: 1000xg, 5 min (BioScript: heat at 25c for 5m)
  Resuspension : PBS; concentrated to 3.75 mL (2x concentration = ~14e6 WBCs)
  Effect       : RBC lysis removes contaminants; no significant cancer cell loss
                 (98% T24 recovery vs whole blood, p=0.82; no morphology change, p=0.2)

Step 3 | MCF-7 Spike into Nucleated Cell Fraction
  Concentration: 500 MCF-7 cells per 7.5 mL whole blood (clinically relevant level)
  Buffer       : PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA
  Operation    : mix, 1 min

Step 4 | On-Chip CTC Separation -- MCF-7 Spiked Sample
  Device       : Multiplexed spiral biochip (3 stacked chips)
  Sample inlet : 350 uL/min; Sheath inlet: 750 uL/min PBS
  Duration     : ~10 min for 7.5 mL blood (BioScript: mix for 10m)
  Physics      : Dean vortex + inertial lift; CTCs to inner wall, WBCs to outer wall
  Detection    : ctcDetection module, 30 s
  Results      : 87.6% MCF-7 recovery efficiency; 76.4% T24 recovery efficiency
                 (500 cells/7.5 mL, n=3, Anova single factor, P < 0.05)
  QC Branch    : ctcSignal > 0  -> dispose (pass, BB2)
                 ctcSignal <= 0 -> drain   (fail, BB3)
                 Both converge at BB4 (mcf7Join)

===========================================================
PROTOCOL 2: T24 Cell Viability Experiment (Independent)
===========================================================

Step 5 | T24 Cell Culture and Preparation
  Cell line    : T24 (bladder carcinoma, ~30 um)
  Media        : High-glucose DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen-strep, 37 C, 5% CO2
  Duration     : 48 h (172800 s; BioScript: heat at 37c for 2880m)
  Note         : Completely independent from Protocol 1; own blood sample prepared separately.

Step 6 | Healthy Donor Blood Collection and RBC Lysis (T24 arm)
  Volume       : 7.5 mL whole blood (independent from Protocol 1 blood sample)
  Lysis        : Same ammonium chloride lysis protocol; 5 min RT
  Centrifugation: 1000xg, 5 min (heat at 25c for 5m)
  Note         : T24 cells spiked before lysis; before/after counts compared (Fig. 3A)

Step 7 | T24 Spike and On-Chip Separation
  Spike        : 500 T24 cells per 7.5 mL; resuspended in EDTA_BSA_Buffer
  Separation   : 350 uL/min sample, 750 uL/min sheath, 10 min
  Operation    : mix (BioScript abstraction of spiral chip separation)

Step 8 | PFA Fixation (Viability Arm)
  Reagent      : 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 10 min at RT (25 C)
  Operation    : mix + heat at 25c for 10m

Step 9 | Triton X-100 Permeabilization (Viability Arm)
  Reagent      : 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 5 min
  Operation    : mix, 5 min

Step 10 | Cell Viability Staining -- PI + Pan-CK/CD45 Panel
  Panel        : pan-CK FITC (1:100) + APC-CD45 (1:100) + Hoechst + Propidium Iodide
                 Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific, Singapore; Hoechst dye in PBS buffer
  PI           : ex 488 nm / em 617 nm; labels dead cells
  Pan-CK       : confirms recovered cells are cancer cells (not WBC contamination)
  Incubation   : 30 min on ice (4 C) (BioScript: heat at 4c for 30m)
  Quantification: BD Accuri C6 flow cytometer; gated on FSC/SSC and fluorescence
  Detection    : viabilityDetection module, 30 s
  Results      : <10% PI+ cells (>90% viable); high shear in spiral microchannels
                 has no adverse effect on cell viability (Fig. 4B)
  QC Branch    : viabilitySignal > 0  -> dispose (pass, BB6)
                 viabilitySignal <= 0 -> drain   (fail, BB7)
                 Both converge at BB8 (viabJoin)

===========================================================
PROTOCOL 3: Clinical CTC Enrichment from Patient Blood
===========================================================

Step 11 | Clinical Blood Collection and RBC Lysis
  Samples      : 10 patient samples (5 breast, 5 NSCLC; Stage IV); 5 healthy controls
  Volume       : 7.5 mL per sample, Vacutainer EDTA tubes, within 2-4 h
  Lysis        : Ammonium chloride, 5 min RT; centrifuge 1000xg 5 min; resuspend in PBS
  Concentration: 3.75 mL (2x); ~14e6 WBCs (optimal for purity per Fig. 2B)
  Input velocity: 350 uL/min

Step 12 | On-Chip Separation of Clinical Sample
  Device       : Multiplexed spiral biochip, same parameters as Protocol 1
  Duration     : ~10 min for 7.5 mL blood
  WBC depletion: ~99.99% (from ~7e6 input nucleated cells)
  Robustness   : 900-1200 WBCs / 5 min uniformly across 0-30 min window (Fig. 2C)

Step 13 | PFA Fixation (Clinical IF Arm)
  Reagent      : 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 10 min at RT (25 C)
  Operation    : mix + heat at 25c for 10m
  Note         : Required for intracellular pan-cytokeratin antibody staining

Step 14 | Triton X-100 Permeabilization (Clinical IF Arm)
  Reagent      : 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 5 min
  Operation    : mix, 5 min

Step 15 | Immunofluorescence (IF) Staining for CTC Identification
  Panel        : pan-CK FITC (1:100) + APC-CD45 (1:100) + Hoechst
                 Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific, Singapore
  CTC criteria : Hoechst+ / Pan-CK+ / CD45-
  Incubation   : 30 min on ice (4 C)
  Imaging      : Epi-fluorescence microscopy + BD Accuri C6 flow cytometry
  Detection    : ctcDetection module, 30 s
  Results      :
    Breast cancer   : 20-67 CTCs/mL (n=5; 100% detection)
    NSCLC           : 33-135 CTCs/mL (n=5; 100% detection)
    Healthy control : 1-4 CK+ cells/mL (background threshold)
    CTC diameter    : 15-25 um (lung); 20-35 um (breast)
    CTC morphology  : Intrapatient pleomorphism observed; eccentric, bi-lobed,
                      kidney-shaped nuclei; microemboli (clusters) in some samples
    Stem cell markers: CD166+/CD133+ sub-population identified (~1 in 135 cells)
  QC Branch    : clinicalSignal > 0  -> HER2 FISH (BB10)
                 clinicalSignal <= 0 -> drain(stainedClinical) (BB11)
                 Both converge at BB12 (finalCleanup)

Step 16 | HER2 FISH Analysis on Isolated CTCs (pass branch only)
  Patient subset: HER2+ breast cancer patients (n=5)
  HER2 criterion: HER2/CEP17 ratio > 2 in single nuclei = amplified

  (a) Cytospin        : Cells spun onto slides (Cytospin, Thermo Scientific, USA);
                        600 rpm, 6 min.
  (b) PFA fixation    : 4% PFA, 10 min RT.
  (c) Dehydration     : Ethanol series 80%, 90%, 100%.
                        BioScript: combined with fixation as heat at 25c for 10m.
  (d) RNase treatment : 4 mg/mL RNase (Sigma, USA) in PBS/0.2% Tween 20;
                        40 min at 37 C. Removes RNA for clean probe hybridization.
                        BioScript: mix + heat at 37c for 40m (2400s).
  (e) Denaturation    : 70% formamide/2xSSC, 80 C, 10 min.
                        Opens dsDNA for probe access.
                        BioScript: mix + heat at 80c for 10m.
  (f) Probe hybridization: HER-2/neu gene locus (red) + CEP17 (green);
                        applied at 42 C, overnight, dark and humid conditions.
                        BioScript: heat at 42c for 600m (10h approximation; s/m limit).
  (g) Post-hyb washes : Wash 1: 50% formamide/2xSSC, 45 C, shaking, 5 min.
                        Wash 2: 2xSSC, 45 C, shaking, 5 min.
                        BioScript: two sequential heat at 45c for 5m steps.
  (h) DAPI counterstain: DAPI (4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole); coverslipped (50x50 mm,
                        Fisher Scientific, USA).

  Detection    : her2FISHDetection module, 30 s
  Results      : 3 of 5 HER2+ breast cancer patients showed HER2-negative CTCs
                 (HER2/CEP17 < 2), indicating heterogeneity between primary tumor
                 and disseminated circulating cells (Fig. 5C).

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Discovery of New States of Immunomodulation for Vaccine Adjuvants via High
               Throughput Screening: Expanding Innate Responses to PRRs
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/acscentsci.2c01351?ref=article_openPDF
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/acscentsci.2c01351
Journal      : ACS Central Science, 2023, Vol. 9, pp. 427-439
Platform     : High-throughput robotic liquid handling (384-well plate, pin-drop dispenser,
               plate reader, AlphaLISA); in vivo murine vaccination model (C57/B6 mice)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput screening (HTS) pipeline to discover small-molecule
"immunomodulators" that alter the activity of two key innate immune signalling pathways:
the NF-kB pathway (nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B-cells) and the
IRF pathway (interferon regulatory factors). Immunomodulators act on the signalling network
downstream of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) rather than binding to the PRR itself,
enabling fine-tuned customisation of innate immune responses.

The pipeline is divided into three sequential phases:
  1. Primary Screen: NF-kB and IRF transcription factor activity in RAW-Dual macrophages
     (murine reporter cell line) across 13 PRR agonists and ~3,147 modulators at 10 uM;
     384-well format; pin-drop robotic dispensing; 24 h readout.
  2. Secondary Screen: Six-plex AlphaLISA cytokine panel in THP-1 monocytes (human);
     720 downselected modulators x 7 PRR agonists; cytokines: IL-1beta, IL-12p40,
     IP-10 (CXCL10), CCL4, TNF-alpha, IFN-beta; quantitative vaccine score computed.
  3. In Vivo Validation: Lead modulators tested in murine prime-boost vaccination model
     (OVA subunit + commercial Fluzone 2021-2022 and Typhim-Vi vaccines); endpoints are
     antigen-specific serum IgG at Day 49 and systemic TNF-alpha at 1 h post-injection.

Key findings:
  - Modulators inhibit and enhance NF-kB and IRF independently by >100-fold.
  - Some modulators are "generalists" (active across nearly all 13 PRR agonists);
    others are "specialists" (active against 1 or a small subset of receptors).
  - Lead antibody-enhancing modulator PME-564 (Lyn kinase / tyrosine kinase inhibitor)
    produces a ~4-fold log AUC increase in anti-HA IgG when combined with Fluzone.
  - Lead cytokine-reducing modulators (PME-1226, PME-397) significantly decrease
    systemic TNF-alpha when combined with CpG (TLR9) agonist.
  - In vivo success rate: ~10-20% of lead candidates validated in murine model.


SCREENING LIBRARY
-----------------
Primary library    : 3,147 compounds total
  Composition      : 246 NF-kB/IRF inhibitors + 2,895 pathway-specific inhibitors
  Many compounds   : Previously studied or FDA-approved in other indications
Compound dose      : 10 uM final concentration (<0.05% DMSO v/v)
Addition method    : Pin-drop (robotic; ~23 nL of 10 mM DMSO stock per 230 uL well)
Downselection      : PCA on 16 variables (NF-kB + IRF activity across 8 high-Z-factor
                     agonists); compounds outside radius 1.75 retained -> 720 compounds
                     for secondary library (SI Appendix Figures S4, Table S3)


PRR AGONISTS
------------
Primary screen : 13 agonists (majority TLRs; SI Appendix Table S2)
  Pam3CSK4     (TLR2/1)      Pam2CSK4    (TLR2/6)
  Poly I:C     (TLR3)        LPS         (TLR4)
  MPLA         (TLR4)        Flagellin   (TLR5)
  Imiquimod    (TLR7)        TL8-506     (TLR8)
  ODN 1826     (TLR9)        3'3'-cGAMP  (STING)
  Tri-DAP      (NOD1)        MDP         (NOD2)
  mIFN-B       (IFNAR1/2)

Agonist concentration : EC50 per agonist (SI Appendix Table S2); occasionally adjusted
                        if modulatory range exceeded dynamic limit

Secondary screen : 7 agonist subset (Pam3CSK4, Pam2CSK4, Poly I:C, LPS, Flagellin,
                   R848 TLR7/8, 3'3'-cGAMP STING)

In vivo subunit model : R848 (TLR7/8), Flagellin (TLR5), CpG 1826 (TLR9)


CELL LINES
----------
- RAW-Dual macrophages (murine): dual NF-kB SEAP / IRF luciferase reporter system;
  both pathways measured in parallel from the same well.
  Primary screen only; cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2.

- THP-1 monocytes (human): secondary screen; selected because human AlphaLISA reagents
  provide higher cytokine multiplexing capacity than murine reagents.
  Cultured in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2.

- BMDC (murine bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells): off-chip validation of lead compounds
  for cytokine production and cell surface marker expression before in vivo dosing
  (SI Appendix Figure S10).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Primary Screen -- Cell Seeding
  Cell line    : RAW-Dual macrophages
  Plate format : 384-well
  Operation    : Robotic seeding at optimised cell density
  Incubation   : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 for cell adherence before compound addition
  Purpose      : Establish monolayer with consistent NF-kB/IRF dynamic range
  Reference    : SI Appendix Figure S1

Step 2 | Primary Screen -- Immunomodulator Pin-Drop Addition
  Library size : ~3,147 compounds
  Method       : Pin-drop dispense; ~23 nL of 10 mM DMSO stock -> 10 uM final
  DMSO         : <0.05% v/v final
  Pre-incubation: 1 h at 37 C before agonist addition (equilibration/uptake)
  Notes        : Modulator added before agonist; not co-added

Step 3 | Primary Screen -- PRR Agonist Addition
  Agonists     : 13 PRR agonists at EC50; one agonist per well per modulator
  Method       : Robotic dispense from pre-prepared agonist stocks
  Notes        : Wide range covers TLR, NLR, STING, and IFNAR families; allows detection
                 of generalist vs specialist modulator activity

Step 4 | Primary Screen -- 24 h Co-incubation
  Temperature  : 37 C, 5% CO2
  Duration     : 24 h (= 1440 min; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  Outcome      : Transcription factor activity develops; supernatant drawn after incubation

Step 5 | Primary Screen -- Cell Viability QC
  Method       : Live-cell imaging + digital confluency mask (SI Appendix Figure S3)
  Purpose      : Identify and exclude toxic modulator/agonist combinations
  Outcome      : Compounds that reduce confluency below threshold are flagged and removed
                 before TF readout; <1% of library showed inherent pathway activation

Step 6 | Primary Screen -- Dual NF-kB / IRF Transcription Factor Readout
  NF-kB method : SEAP reporter; QUANTI-Blue reagent; absorbance 620 nm
  IRF method   : Luciferase reporter; QUANTI-Luc reagent; luminescence
  Both measured simultaneously from same supernatant well
  Report       : Fold change vs agonist-alone control
  Dynamic range: Inhibition and enhancement observed up to >100-fold in both directions
  Observation  : NF-kB and IRF modulation are largely independent (R2 = 0.0409 for LPS)
  PCA gate     : PC1+PC2 account for 49% of variance; retain outside radius 1.75;
                 3,147 -> 720 compounds advanced to secondary library

Step 7 | Secondary Screen -- THP-1 Cell Seeding
  Cell line    : THP-1 monocytes (human)
  Rationale    : Human AlphaLISA reagents; higher multiplexing than murine RAW-Dual
  Plate format : 384-well; identical robotic workflow to primary screen
  Incubation   : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 for equilibration

Step 8 | Secondary Screen -- Re-apply Lead Modulator
  Compounds    : 720 downselected modulators
  Method       : Same pin-drop protocol; 10 uM final; <0.05% DMSO
  Pre-incubation: 1 h at 37 C before agonist addition
  Scale        : 720 modulators x 7 agonists = 5,040 wells per cytokine

Step 9 | Secondary Screen -- PRR Agonist Addition and 24 h Incubation
  Agonists     : 7-agonist subset of primary screen
  Incubation   : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2
  Supernatant  : Collected for AlphaLISA multiplexed measurement

Step 10 | Secondary Screen -- AlphaLISA Six-Plex Cytokine Detection
  Platform     : AlphaLISA (PerkinElmer); no-wash, multiplexed bead assay
  Excitation   : 680 nm; emission 615 nm (channel-switched per bead pair)
  Cytokines    : IL-1beta, IL-12p40, IP-10 (CXCL10), CCL4, TNF-alpha, IFN-beta
  Rationale per cytokine:
    TNF-alpha  : Baseline generalised inflammation; endogenous pyrogen
    IL-1beta   : Partially outside direct NF-kB regulation; enables pathway differentiation
    IFN-beta   : Strong IRF pathway correlate; antiviral type I interferon
    IL-12p40   : Activates NK cells; Th1/Th17 polarisation; adaptive immunity bridge
    IP-10      : Early adjuvant signal; T cell and DC chemoattractant; tolerability correlate
    CCL4       : Monocyte and NK cell chemoattractant; tolerability correlate
  Replicates   : Triplicate duplexed measurements per well
  Standard curves: Per cytokine per agonist (SI Appendix Table S5)
  Normalisation : Fold change vs agonist-alone; transformed to [-1,1] for vaccine score
  Crosstalk    : Corrected per SI Appendix Figure S5D

Step 11 | Secondary Screen -- Vaccine Score Computation and Downselection
  Method       : Weighted normalised cytokine score per modulator/agonist combination;
                 summed across agonists to produce generalist vaccine score
  Weights      : Positive for IFN-beta, IP-10, CCL4, IL-12; negative for TNF-alpha, IL-1beta
  Score range  : -20 (most negative; PME-2988) to +10 (most positive)
  Top generalist threshold: score >= 6 (approximately 20 compounds from 720 pool)
  Reference    : SI Appendix Figure S9

Step 12 | BMDC Validation (off-chip; lead compounds only)
  Cells        : Murine bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDC)
  Purpose      : Confirm cytokine production and cell surface markers in primary DCs
  Agonists     : Multiple (from primary screen subset)
  Reference    : SI Appendix Figure S10

Step 13 | In Vivo -- Prime Injection (Day 0)
  Model        : C57/B6 mice; i.m. injection
  Modulator dose: 1.5 umol in DMSO:Addavax 1:1 v/v
  Arms         :
    Arm A (Fluzone): Fluzone 2021-2022 (inactivated quadrivalent flu) + modulator
                     Endpoint: anti-HA IgG at Day 49 (log AUC)
    Arm B (Typhim): Typhim-Vi (carbohydrate typhoid vaccine) + modulator
                     Endpoint: systemic TNF-alpha at 1 h post-injection (pg/mL)
    Arm C (OVA):   OVA + R848/Flagellin/CpG1826 + modulator
                     Endpoint: anti-OVA IgG at Day 35 and Day 49 (n=4)
  Early cytokine: Serum collected at 1 h post-injection for TNF-alpha readout

Step 14 | In Vivo -- Boost Injection (Day 21)
  Schedule     : Day 21 post-prime
  Formulation  : Identical to prime; same modulator dose and vehicle
  Interval     : 21 days from prime (= 30240 min; IR: 1814400.0 SECOND)

Step 15 | In Vivo -- Antibody Titer Readout (Day 35 and Day 49)
  Method       : ELISA; antigen-specific serum IgG; log AUC reported
  Fluzone targets: A/Victoria/2570/2019 (HA); B/Phuket/3073/2013 (HA)
  OVA target   : Anti-OVA IgG D49 antibody level
  Timepoints   : Day 35 (14 days post-boost) and Day 49 (28 days post-boost; primary endpoint)
  Interval     : Day 21 to Day 49 = 28 days (= 40320 min; IR: 2419200.0 SECOND)
  Key result   : PME-564 + Fluzone -> ~4-fold log AUC increase vs Fluzone alone (****P<0.0001)
                 PME-564 + OVA subunit -> 2-6x IgG increase across all adjuvants tested
                 PME-1226 + PME-397 + CpG -> significant TNF-alpha reduction (Typhim model)
  n per group  : 4-5 mice


LEAD MODULATORS
---------------
PME-564   : Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (Lyn/Src-family kinase); top generalist vaccine score
            (~8-10). Enhances IP-10, IFN-beta, IL-12 across most agonists; suppresses TNF-alpha
            notably for Pam3CSK4 and R848. In vivo: ~4-fold log AUC IgG increase with Fluzone.
            Clinical precedent: used in myelogenous leukaemia treatment.

Title        : An Automated Single-Cell Droplet-Digital Microfluidic Platform for Monoclonal Antibody Discovery
Source Link  : https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/smll.202308950
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.202308950
Journal      : Small, 2024, Vol. 20, Article 2308950
Authors      : Fatemeh Ahmadi, Hao Tran, Natasha Letourneau, Samuel R. Little,
               Annie Fortin, Anna N. Moraitis, Steve C. C. Shih
Platform     : Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidics (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel
               microfluidics) on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidic platform for automated monoclonal
antibody (mAb) discovery. The platform integrates a bottom digital microfluidic (DMF) electrode
layer (chromium co-planar electrodes on glass + 7 um SU-8 dielectric) with three stacked
PDMS-based microchannel devices, enabling individual electrode-addressable control of droplets
flowing inside microfluidic channels -- a configuration combining "droplet-in-flow" techniques
with digital microfluidics for on-demand droplet generation and manipulation.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. Target cell encapsulation and single-cell sorting (Devices 2 and 3)
  2. Hybridoma cell staining and hydrodynamic single-cell trapping (Device 1)
  3. In situ deterministic co-encapsulation by phase change and electrode-actuated merge
  4. On-chip incubation, droplet disruption, and PBS/Alexa Fluor 647 wash (Device 1)
  5. Fluorescence-based antibody binding detection and positive hybridoma recovery

The complete workflow from trapping to recovery processes 100 doublets in ~60 min, achieving
co-encapsulation efficiency of 95 +/- 3.2% -- the highest reported without preliminary sorting
of both cell types or microvalve-based capture systems. This surpasses the Poisson-based
nondeterministic co-encapsulation efficiency of ~16%, which is the limit of conventional
flow-focusing droplet microfluidic approaches.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass; co-planar ground and actuation electrodes.
Layer ii  : SU-8 dielectric, 7 um thick; spin-coated and hard-baked.
Layer iii : Three stacked PDMS-based microchannel devices adhered to the dielectric layer.

Device 1 -- Trapping array:
  100 traps total (50 per serpentine side); channel height 20 um, channel width 50-75 um;
  7 um constriction per trap; 2 actuation electrodes + 1 ground electrode per trap;
  sets of 5 traps bussed together to one potential circuit to reduce electrode density
  and operational complexity.

Device 2 -- Flow-focusing droplet generator:
  Generates ~30 pL monodisperse droplets at ~3 kHz throughput;
  used for target cell encapsulation following Poisson distribution.

Device 3 -- Co-planar binary electrode sorter:
  Selects single-target-cell droplets by CFSE fluorescence (ex 470 nm / em 520 nm);
  PMT photon-counting head triggers electrode actuation to sort droplets above single-cell
  fluorescence threshold and below two-cell threshold.

Inlets  : Inlet 1 (HFE7500 oil, main channel), Inlet 2 (PBS / Alexa647 Ab / target droplets),
          Inlet 3 (hybridoma cell suspension in IMDM)
Outlets : Outlet 1 (sample recovery via reverse oil flow, 4 nL/s)

Actuation: 15 kHz AC; 32 Vrms for encapsulation/merge; 64 Vrms for droplet disruption/wash.
           Electrode actuation controlled through in-house Python-based GUI automation software
           (open-source: https://bitbucket.org/shihmicrolab/f_ahmadi_2023_uflowcontrol).


CELL LINES
----------
- Hybridoma cells (confidential line, provided by NRC Canada):
  Produces monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) that bind to specific membrane-bound antigens on target
  cells. Cultured in IMDM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + mouse IL-6 (1 ng/mL) + pen/strep;
  37 C, 5% CO2. Passaged every 3 days at 8e6 cells/mL. Loaded at 1e6 cells/mL in IMDM
  (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic). Stained with CellTrace Calcein Red-Orange AM
  (ex 577 nm / em 590 nm) prior to chip loading.

- Target cells (confidential line, provided by NRC Canada):
  Express membrane-bound antigens recognised by the desired antigen-specific mAbs.
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + G418 (0.4 mg/mL); 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Passaged every 3 days at 3e6 cells/mL. Loaded at 1e6 cells/mL in IMDM
  (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic). Stained with CellTrace CFSE (ex 470 nm / em 520 nm)
  prior to chip loading for Device 3 sorting.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents  : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronics F-127
  Mix       : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Flow rate : 50 nL/s from inlet 3 for 5 min (outlet 1 closed); then reduced to 1 nL/s
              and outlet 1 opened
  Duration  : 5 min (300 s)
  Purpose   : Reduces non-specific hybridoma cell adhesion to PDMS channel walls.

Step 2 | Target Cell Staining and Encapsulation (Device 2)
  Cell line      : Target cells
  Stain          : CellTrace CFSE (5 uM, 1e6 cells/mL in PBS, Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Stain time     : 20 min at 37 C; wash with PBS to remove excess dye
  Resuspension   : IMDM (10% FBS + mouse IL-6 1 ng/mL, no antibiotic, 1e6 cells/mL)
  Operation      : Flow-focusing encapsulation (Poisson distribution)
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant
  Droplet size   : ~30 pL monodisperse
  Throughput     : ~3 kHz
  Purpose        : Encapsulate target cells in small droplets for downstream sorting (Device 3).

Step 3 | Single Target-Cell Droplet Sorting (Device 3)
  Detection      : CFSE fluorescence (ex 470 nm / em 520 nm) via PMT photon-counting head
  Sorting gate   : Fluorescence counts above single-cell threshold and below two-cell threshold
  Action (pass)  : Single-target-cell droplet collected into gas-tight glass syringe with HFE7500
  Action (fail)  : Empty or multi-cell droplets sent to waste channel
  Transfer       : Collected droplets bridged to Device 1 inlet 2 via 0.014" OD / 0.006" ID tubing
  Purpose        : Ensure only droplets with exactly one target cell are used for co-encapsulation.

Step 4 | Hybridoma Cell Staining and Hydrodynamic Trapping (Device 1)
  Cell line      : Hybridoma cells
  Stain          : CellTrace Calcein Red-Orange AM (1e6 cells/mL, 20 min at 37 C; PBS wash)
  Resuspension   : IMDM (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic, 1e6 cells/mL)
  Flow rate      : 1-5 nL/s; optimal 1 nL/s
  Trapping eff.  : 98 +/- 3.92% at 1 nL/s (N=5 repeats, n=10 replicates per flow rate)
  Trap design    : 7 um constriction (smaller than hybridoma cell diameter); hydrodynamic
                   confinement by fluidic resistance. Open trap Rtrap < Rbypass; when occupied
                   Rtrap increases, directing flow to next open trap.
  Trap count     : 100 traps (50 per serpentine side per device)
  Occupancy check: singleCellTrapDetection module; fluorescence threshold gates single occupancy
  Purpose        : Isolate single hybridoma cells in addressable traps for deterministic
                   co-encapsulation and individual droplet-level screening.

Step 5 | In Situ Droplet Generation (Device 1)
  Method         : Phase change from single-phase aqueous (IMDM) to two-phase (water-in-oil)
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant, 1 nL/s from inlet 1
  Electrode      : 32 Vrms, 15 kHz; electrodes below traps actuated to shear aqueous phase
  Droplet volume : 40-150 pL (varies with oil flow rate)
  Success rate   : >95% at 1 nL/s
  Frame sequence : Oil enters main channel while trap electrode holds aqueous phase.
                   Oil shears aqueous at both trap ends; cell remains inside.
                   Droplet pinches off; oil continues to next trap.
  Purpose        : Deterministic encapsulation of single hybridoma cell per trap.
                   No Poisson statistics. No preliminary sorting of hybridoma cells required.

Step 6 | Deterministic Co-Encapsulation (Droplet Merge, Device 1)
  Operation      : On-demand electrode-actuated droplet merge
  Re-injection   : Sorted single-target-cell droplets re-injected from inlet 2 at 5 nL/s
  Oil spacer     : HFE7500 from a separate inlet at 1 nL/s (spaces droplets entering traps)
  Electrode      : 32 Vrms, 15 kHz; actuated when target-cell droplet reaches trap proximity
  Efficiency     : 95 +/- 3.2% co-encapsulation at 5 nL/s re-injection flow rate
                   (N=5 repeats, n=10 replicates; highest reported without microvalves)
  Time for 100   : 60 min for 100 two-cell doublets with automated system
  Notes          : Two separate inlets avoid merging of sequential target-cell droplets.
                   Electrode actuation pattern detailed in Figure S6 of paper.
                   Failure mode at >10 nL/s: target droplet coalesces with empty trap droplet.

Step 7 | On-Chip Co-Incubation
  Temperature    : 25 C (room temperature; no external heating element)
  Duration       : 30 min (1800 s)
  Events         : Hybridoma cells secrete mAbs into confined droplet volume.
                   Antigen-specific mAbs diffuse and bind to membrane-bound antigens on
                   co-encapsulated target cell surface.
                   Non-specific mAbs remain free in droplet volume.

Step 8 | Droplet Disruption and PBS / Alexa Fluor 647 Wash (Device 1)
  Wash solution  : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated goat anti-mouse
                   IgG (H+L) secondary antibody; loaded from inlet 2 at 1-5 nL/s
  Electrode      : 64 Vrms, 15 kHz; field intensity 2-4 x 10^5 V/m; electrodes below traps
  Duration       : ~5 min to wash all 50 traps
  Mechanism      : Electrostatic force perpendicular to droplet interface (Figure S7 of paper)
                   disrupts IMDM droplet; non-specific mAbs washed out through 7 um constriction.
                   Hybridoma + target cell retained in trap (antigen-Ab bond maintains target cell;
                   hybridoma remains by hydrodynamic confinement).
  Wash efficiency: 96.8% reduction in normalised fluorescence intensity after 1 wash step
                   (N=15 replicates; Figure 4C of paper)
  Cell retention : 96 +/- 9.6% at 1-5 nL/s (N=5 repeats, n=10 replicates; Figure 4D)
  Re-formation   : PBS/Alexa647 flow reduced to 0.1 nL/s; HFE7500 oil flow increased to
                   5 nL/s to re-form PBS droplet around both cells in situ.
  Advantage      : Individual droplet disruption by electrostatic forces avoids chemical
                   demulsifiers (which compromise cell viability) and acoustic/magnetic methods
                   (which have device material limitations).

Step 9 | Fluorescence Detection and Antibody Binding Screening
  Channel        : Alexa Fluor 647 (ex 627 nm / em 665 nm); 300 ms exposure
  Camera         : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash 4.0 (Township, NJ, USA)
  Detection      : antibodyBindingDetection module gates on mean fluorescence of cell >
                   mean fluorescence of surrounding droplet (SNR threshold)
  Result (pass)  : Localised red fluorescent signal around target cell membrane =
                   antigen-specific mAb detected; hybridoma is a positive producer
  Result (fail)  : No localised signal = non-specific mAb producer; droplet drained
  SNR            : Significant improvement post-wash for antigen-specific vs non-specific
                   hybridomas (P < 0.05); without washing both types have similar SNR (P > 0.05)
  Selection rate : 94.00 +/- 1.41% at 100:0 ratio (100% desired); 1.60% at 1:50 ratio
                   (platform detects rare-cell populations at biologically relevant concentrations
                   of ~2% antigen-specific B cells from immunised donors)
  Purpose        : Distinguish antigen-specific from non-specific mAb-producing hybridomas
                   at the single-cell level without requiring pre-sorting or bulk assays.

Step 10 | Positive Hybridoma Recovery
  Condition      : antibodySignal > 0 only (antigen-specific mAb detected)
  Recovery steps :
    1. Positive droplet released by reverse oil flow at 4 nL/s from outlet 1
       (inlet 3 briefly opened to remove previously accumulated droplets in that channel)
    2. Droplet collected into glass capillary pre-filled with HFE7500 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant
    3. Capillary contents expelled onto 10-20 uL IMDM complete medium placed on hydrophobic
       PTFE membrane (0.22 um, Thomas Scientific) secured in custom 3D-printed holder
    4. ~1 mL Fluorinert FC-40 oil added; FC-40 disrupts surfactant-stabilised emulsion
       and PTFE membrane absorbs HFE7500 and surfactant
    5. Aqueous cell droplet released into IMDM complete medium
    6. Merged droplet transferred to well-plate (e.g. 96-well) using pipette for downstream
       antibody characterisation (sequencing, ELISA, binding kinetics, SPR, etc.)
  Downstream     : Antibody characterisation assays (off-chip; not encoded in BioScript).

1. Bead binding: mix the mid-log-phase E. coli culture with WGA-lectin-coated magnetic beads and rotate/incubate for 15 minutes to bind cells to beads (approximately one bead per cell).
2. Bead blocking: mix the bead-bound cells with fat-free powdered milk blocking agent for 1 minute to prevent bead-cell aggregation and promote uniform dispersion.
3. Media exchange: pull bound cells out of suspension with a magnet, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the bead-bound cells in growth medium.
4. Heat-shock induction: incubate the resuspended, bead-bound cells at 42 C for 15 minutes to induce expression of the lambda-Red recombination proteins (Exo, Beta, Gam).
5. Electrocompetence washes: for each of 3 wash cycles, magnetically pellet the bound cells, remove the supernatant, and replace it with DI water (with 0.05% Tween 20) without resuspension, to render the cells electrocompetent.
6. Oligo loading: suspend the washed, bead-bound cells in DI water, add the single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide, and incubate briefly (about 30 seconds) to allow oligo uptake.
7. 8. Recovery: immediately merge the pulsed sample with recovery growth medium and incubate at 30 C for 2.5 hours to allow the cells to recover and express any successfully incorporated genetic changes.
9. Transformation frequency readout: plate (or otherwise assay) the recovered cell sample on selective and non-selective media to determine the transformation frequency as the ratio of colony-forming units on the selective condition to the total colony-forming units.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Input Dose Differentiation by NF-kB
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/752394v1.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/752394
Journal      : bioRxiv preprint, September 4, 2019 (bioRxiv 752394)
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidic chip (64 independent chambers, >500 cells/chamber)
               with automated Matlab GUI valve control and live-cell fluorescence imaging


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic live-cell analysis pipeline used to investigate how the
NF-kB signalling pathway in single mammalian cells responds to dynamically varying cytokine
concentrations. Using a multiplexed PDMS microfluidic chip, cells expressing p65-DsRed (NF-kB
reporter) and H2B-GFP (nuclear marker) are exposed to TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, or Pam2CSK4 in
precisely controlled temporal profiles: instant step increase, linear ramp, exponential ramp,
and random fluctuating order. Nuclear NF-kB localization is tracked in real time by time-lapse
fluorescence microscopy. Downstream, cells are retrieved from the chip for RT-qPCR measurement
of NF-kB target gene expression.

The central finding is that NF-kB acts as a dose differentiator: its nuclear localization
amplitude (peak height and AUC) is proportional to the logarithm of the change in cytokine
concentration, not the absolute concentration itself. This behaviour is analogous to an
electronic differentiator circuit and is described by:

    NF-kB ~ log(delta_cytokine + 1)   [for delta_cytokine > 0]

A20 and IkBa negative feedbacks are identified as the molecular mechanism providing short-term
memory of prior cytokine level, continuously resetting IKK cycling and receptor sensitivity.
The protocol also includes an A20 CRISPR/Cas9 knockout arm that experimentally confirms A20's
role, and RT-qPCR measurements showing that distinct cytokine input dynamics drive distinct
subsets of NF-kB target gene expression.

The complete experimental workflow covers device fabrication, chip priming, cell loading,
multi-arm cytokine stimulation, live-cell imaging, mathematical modelling inputs, A20 KO
cell generation, and downstream gene expression analysis.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Two-layer PDMS microfluidic chip fabricated by multilayer soft lithography:

Flow layer  : AZ40XT positive photoresist (25 um, 3400 RPM; rounded cross-section by hard-bake)
              + SU-8 3025 negative photoresist (30 um, 3000 RPM) on 4-inch silicon wafer.
Control layer: SU-8 3025 (25 um, 3500 RPM) on 4-inch silicon wafer.
Lithography : Heidelberg MLA150 maskless aligner; 375 nm laser; 280 mJ/cm2 dose.

PDMS layers:
  Flow layer  : RTV-615 (Momentive), 66 g, 10:1 monomer:catalyst; ~2 cm thick slab;
                cured 80 C >5 h; flow pattern grooved on bottom face.
  Control layer: RTV-615, 10 g; spun at 2200 RPM (~50 um thin film); cured 80 C >=1 h.

Assembly:
  1. Flow layer inputs punched.
  2. Both layers treated with oxygen plasma (Harrick PDC-001).
  3. Layers aligned under custom stereomicroscope; cured 80 C overnight for bonding.
  4. Control layer holes punched; chip bonded to 75 x 25 x 1 mm glass slide by plasma + bake.

Chamber specifications:
  - 64 independent sample chambers per chip
  - Chamber size: 3.5 x 0.8 mm
  - >500 cells per chamber
  - Minimum feature spacing: 150 um (robust bonding and alignment)

Actuation:
  - Control layer: pneumatic solenoid valves at 25-30 psi
  - Input media: pressurized at 3-4 psi through PEEK tubing (VICI, TPK.505) to prevent
    shear stress on cells during feeding
  - Automation: custom Matlab GUI; experiment scripts define feeding timing and medium
    type per chamber; greatly improves accuracy, throughput, and reproducibility

Surface coating:
  - 1:3 fibronectin (1 mg/mL) in sterile PBS; loaded into chambers overnight at room
    temperature before experiment day


CELL LINES
----------
Primary experimental cell line:
  - p65-/- 3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) expressing p65-DsRed and H2B-GFP
    Cultured: DMEM (Gibco 11965092) + 10% fetal bovine calf serum (HyClone) +
              1% GlutaMax (Gibco) + 1x penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco)
    Passaging: Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco); ~1:10 dilution every 2-3 days before 100% confluency
    Conditions: 37 C, 5% CO2
    Imaging media: FluoroBrite DMEM (Gibco A1896702) + same supplements; used during
                   experiments to reduce background fluorescence

A20 knockout cell line:

-----------
Differentiator equation:
  NF-kB ~ log(delta_cytokine + 1)   for positive changes in cytokine concentration

Linear ramp  : Constant NF-kB AUC at each step (NF-kB responds to constant rate of change)

Random input : AUC-vs-delta_TNF correlation ~0.91 for increases; sharp drop for decreases
Pam2CSK4    : No dose differentiation (TLR2 pathway); differentiator is receptor-specific

  Random input     : AUC correlation reduced to ~0.76; NF-kB remains nuclear after dose decrease

  Ramp-following                  : A20, Ccl2 -- mirror NF-kB peak height during ramp;

ASSAY TYPE: Competitive ELISA for benzodiazepine-class drugs (including diazepam) in urine or
blood, using a pre-coated antibody microplate. This version of the workflow has been adapted
to run as a sequence of droplet operations on a digital microfluidic biochip (DMFB) instead
of a standard 96-well plate.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Urine sample (diluted specimen)
  - Benzodiazepine-enzyme conjugate (drug labeled with horseradish peroxidase)
  - Distilled water (wash diluent)
  - TMB substrate (3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine)
  - Stop solution (dilute acid)

STEPS:

1. Combine 10 units of the diluted urine sample with 100 units of the benzodiazepine-enzyme
   conjugate. Mix for 60 seconds.

2. Incubate the combined mixture at 23C (room temperature) for 60 minutes. During this time,
   any free benzodiazepine in the sample competes with the enzyme-labeled conjugate for a
   limited number of antibody binding sites — this competition is the basis of the test.

3. Wash the reaction six times: each wash cycle combines 350 units of distilled water with the
   reaction droplet, mixes for 45 seconds, and removes unbound material before moving to
   detection.

4. Add 100 units of TMB substrate to the washed reaction and mix for 60 seconds. Incubate at
   23C for 30 minutes to allow the color reaction to develop.

5. Add 100 units of stop solution and mix for 60 seconds to halt color development and shift
   the color from blue to yellow.

6. Measure the resulting absorbance signal to obtain the reading. Discard the sample
   afterward.

INTERPRETATION: This is a one-step competitive immunoassay. Free benzodiazepine in the sample
and the enzyme-labeled conjugate compete for a fixed number of antibody binding sites on the
plate. After washing away anything unbound, the remaining bound conjugate is revealed by the
TMB color reaction. Less color development means more drug was present in the sample
(competing more successfully for binding sites); more color development means less or no drug
was present. A result is typically called positive if the sample's absorbance reading is at or
below the reading from a positive reference standard, and negative if it is above.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is an exact numeric match to the cited source across every value: sample volume (10
units), conjugate volume (100 units), first incubation time (60 minutes), wash count and
volume (6 times, 350 units), substrate volume (100 units), second incubation time (30
minutes), and stop solution volume (100 units) all match the source exactly. The only
difference is that the droplet program records the result using the generic "fluorescence"
detect type, since BioScript has no dedicated absorbance-reading instruction, whereas the
real procedure reads absorbance at a dual wavelength (450 nm and 650 nm). This is a known
expressiveness gap in the droplet language, not a deviation from the real procedure.

One caveat on scope: this kit is raised against and validated for benzodiazepines as a drug
class (the antiserum is directed against Oxazepam, with cross-reactivity across the
benzodiazepine group, which includes diazepam), rather than being diazepam-exclusive. This
does not affect the validity of the step-by-step procedure above, which applies identically
regardless of which specific benzodiazepine is being screened for.

An earlier version of this protocol's droplet program included a second, separate
antibody/enzyme incubation-and-wash stage (resembling a two-step "sandwich" ELISA). No real
benzodiazepine or other small-molecule drug immunoassay kit was found using that structure: a
two-step format requires the target molecule to be large enough for two antibodies to bind it
simultaneously, which a small drug molecule (a "hapten") is not large enough to support. Every
real urine drug-screening kit checked (morphine, fentanyl, oxycodone, benzodiazepines) uses
the one-step competitive format reflected in the steps above. The two-step version is treated
as a non-representative artifact of the original test file, not a valid alternative protocol.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Lab-on-a-Chip Integrated Aerosol Particle Sample Collection, Pre-Concentration, and Colorimetric Analysis (Quasi-Real-Time Cascade-Impactor-Coupled Sampling)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Aerosol Impaction Surface (collection surface of the electrowetting chip onto which airborne particles are impacted directly, representing deposited aerosol constituents such as sulfate, nitrate, and ammonium)
  - Ultra-Pure Solvent (micro-droplet digitally directed across the impaction surface to wash and dissolve aerosol constituents)
  - Colorimetric Reagent (reagent that reacts with the extracted aerosol constituents to produce colored complexes for LED/photodiode absorbance detection)

STEPS:
1. Particle collection: Impact airborne aerosol particles directly onto the exposed collection surface of the electrowetting chip during a brief collection phase, with the air stream uninterrupted.
2. Extraction/washing: Interrupt the air stream, dispense a micro-droplet of ultra-pure solvent, and digitally scan/actuate it across the impaction surface (approx. 1 min sampling time) to dissolve and pre-concentrate the aerosol constituents into the droplet.
3. Reagent merge and mix: Dispense a colorimetric reagent droplet, merge it with the extraction droplet by applying voltages to the appropriate electrodes, and mix by shuttling the merged droplet across electrodes for approximately 5 seconds at an actuation voltage of about 50 V to form a colored reaction product.
4. Detection: Measure the absorbance of the colored complex at the target wavelength at room temperature using the on-chip LED (light emitting diode)/photodiode setup.
5. Disposal and cycle repeat: Dispose of the analyzed droplet; repeat the collection-extraction-mix-detect cycle so that sampling can continue in quasi-real time.

INTERPRETATION: Successful integrated sample collection and analysis is confirmed by achieving a time resolution of 1 minute per measurement (roughly two orders of magnitude faster than conventional manual cascade impactor methods), with the very small extraction-droplet volume producing a relatively concentrated solution that allows detection limits in air on the order of tens of ng/m3 (attogram-level analyte mass), supporting quasi real-time, fully automated on-chip quantification of major inorganic aerosol constituents (sulfate, nitrate, ammonium) as well as future extension to airborne bioagent detection.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Deciphering Microbial Interactions in Synthetic Human Gut Microbiome Communities
Source Link  : https://link.springer.com/article/10.15252/msb.20178157
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20178157
Journal      : Molecular Systems Biology (2018), Vol. 14, Article e8157
Platform     : Automated liquid-handling robotic platform (Biomek) + 96-well deep-well microplate
               array; Tecan Infinite F200 Pro plate reader; Illumina MiSeq 16S amplicon sequencing


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a systematic model-guided experimental framework to dissect microbial
interactions governing the assembly and stability of a 12-member synthetic human gut microbiome
community. The community spans four major phyla: Bacteroidetes (BT, BO, BU, BV), Firmicutes
(BH, CH, ER, FP), Actinobacteria (CA, EL), and Proteobacteria (DP), plus Prevotella copri (PC).

Time-resolved measurements of monospecies and pairwise assemblages are used to parameterise a
generalised Lotka-Volterra (gLV) ODE model of community dynamics. The parameterised model is
validated against full 12-member and 11-member single-species dropout communities, and
exo-metabolomics profiling of all monospecies is performed to illuminate metabolic capabilities
and potential molecular bases of microbial interactions.

The protocol is divided into five experimental phases:
  1. Monospecies growth characterisation (M dataset, 12 conditions)
  2. Pairwise co-cultures, 1:1 initial ratio (PW1 dataset, 66 combinations)
  3. Pairwise co-cultures, asymmetric initial ratio (PW2 dataset, 15 conditions, 95:5 and 5:95)
  4. Multi-species community validation (full 12-member + 12 single-species dropout communities)
  5. Exo-metabolomics profiling (11 monospecies; DP excluded; 97 metabolites by LC-MS/MS)


SPECIES COMMUNITY
-----------------
Slow-growth species (inoculated 41 h before experiment):
  BH = Blautia hydrogenotrophica (DSM 10507)
  FP = Faecalibacterium prausnitzii (DSM 17677)
  CA = Collinsella aerofaciens (DSM 3979)
  PC = Prevotella copri (DSM 18205)
  ER = Eubacterium rectale (ATCC 33656)
  DP = Desulfovibrio piger (ATCC 29098)

Fast-growth species (inoculated 16 h before experiment):
  BU = Bacteroides uniformis (DSM 6597)
  BV = Bacteroides vulgatus (ATCC 8482)
  BT = Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (ATCC 29148)
  BO = Bacteroides ovatus (ATCC 8483)
  CH = Clostridium hiranonis (DSM 13275)
  EL = Eggerthella lenta (DSM 2243)


GROWTH CONDITIONS
-----------------
Atmosphere   : Anaerobic (85% N2, 5% H2, 10% CO2); Coy Lab Products anaerobic chamber
Temperature  : 37 C, no shaking
Media        : Anaerobic Basal Broth (ABB, Oxoid) — rich media supporting all 12 species
Plate format : 96-well deep-well plates covered with gas-permeable Breathe Easy seal
Robot        : Biomek liquid-handling robot (community arraying and serial transfer)
OD600        : Tecan Infinite F200 Pro (384-well absorbance plate); 30 min intervals
16S sampling : ~12 h intervals; V3-V4 region, Illumina MiSeq 300 bp paired-end,
               dual-indexed primers (64 forward x 8 bp reverse; 1536 samples/run)
               Processed: PEAR v0.9.0 (merge) + USEARCH v8.0 (align, 97.5% threshold)
Serial transfer: 1:20 dilution into fresh ABB every 24 h; total experiment duration 72 h (3 transfers)
Inoculation  : Each species at 0.01 OD600 from 25% glycerol stock starter cultures


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Starter Culture Preparation
  Slow-growth species (BH, FP, CA, PC, ER, DP):
    Inoculate 200 uL glycerol stock into 15 mL ABB; 37 C, no shaking; 41 h (2460 min).
    IR duration: 147600.0 SECOND
  Fast-growth species (BU, BV, BT, BO, CH, EL):
    Inoculate 200 uL glycerol stock into 15 mL ABB; 37 C, no shaking; 16 h (960 min).
    IR duration: 57600.0 SECOND
  Purpose: ensures all species reach comparable growth phase at t=0 of each community experiment.

Step 2 | Phase 1 — Monospecies Growth Characterisation (M dataset)
  Conditions   : 12 monocultures (one per species); each at 0.01 OD600 in fresh ABB
  Sampling     : OD600 every 30 min; 16S rRNA at ~12 h (detect duration: 43200.0 SECOND in IR)
  Transfer     : 1:20 dilution (1 unit community + 19 units fresh ABB) every 24 h; 3 transfers
  Duration     : 72 h total
  BioScript    : BT, FP, EL encoded as representative monospecies; all 12 follow identical pattern
  Key findings :
    - BT, BV (Bacteroides): lowest CV; fitness least altered by co-species
    - FP: bimodal CV; receives 5 positive incoming interactions in gLV model (ecologically responsive)
    - EL: low monospecies fitness but highest ecological impact; 6 positive outgoing interactions
    - Training on M alone: median Pearson r = 0.53 (T1); monospecies growth does not predict
      multi-species community structure

Step 3 | Monospecies QC Gate
  Module       : monospeciesGrowthDetection
  Branch       : monoQCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2, bsbbif_2_t)
                 monoQCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB3, bsbbif_3_f)
  Join         : BB4 (bsbbif_4_j); PW1 branch begins

Step 4 | Phase 2 — Pairwise Co-cultures, 1:1 Ratio (PW1 dataset)
  Conditions   : 66 combinations (C(12,2)); each species at 0.01 OD600; total OD600 = 0.02
  Sampling     : OD600 every 30 min; 16S rRNA at ~12 h
  Transfer     : 1:20 dilution every 24 h; 3 transfers; 72 h total
  BioScript    : 3 representative pairs encoded (BT+FP, CH+ER, EL+BH)
  Representative pairs:
    BT + FP  : BT inhibits FP (negative outgoing); FP receives 5 positive interactions in full
               community. BT dominance expected.
    CH + ER  : +/- topology (CH inhibits ER; ER stimulates CH). Exemplar of robust coexistence
               motif (Fig 4B, 4C). Converges to ~1:1 from distinct initial conditions.
               Negative feedback loop balances disparate monospecies fitness levels.
    EL + BH  : Mutualism (+/+). Highest pairwise productivity enhancement vs null model.
  Community behaviours at 72 h (across all 51 pairs in PW2 design):
    ~50% single-species dominance
    ~24% stable coexistence
    ~12% history dependence
  Training on M+PW1: median Pearson r = 0.79 (T2); pairwise interactions are major drivers

Step 5 | PW1 QC Gate
  Module       : communityCompositionDetection
  Branch       : pw1QCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB5, bsbbif_5_t)
                 pw1QCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB6, bsbbif_6_f)
  Join         : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j); PW2 branch begins

Step 6 | Phase 3 — Pairwise Co-cultures, Asymmetric Ratio (PW2 dataset)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Method for Protein Extraction by Precipitation
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/precipitation.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac8021554
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2009, Vol. 81, No. 1, pp. 330-335
Authors      : Mais J. Jebrail, Aaron R. Wheeler
Platform     : Digital Microfluidics (DMF) on Parylene-C / Teflon-AF coated glass


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first microfluidic method for extracting proteins from
heterogeneous fluids by precipitation. The approach uses digital microfluidics (DMF)
to implement an automated, fully on-chip sequence of protein precipitation, rinsing,
and resolubilization -- without centrifugation. Protein precipitates settle rapidly
in DMF droplets (~0.1 mm path length vs. several mm in centrifuge tubes) and adhere
strongly to the Teflon-AF device surface, enabling clean separation of the liquid
supernatant from the solid precipitate by droplet actuation alone. The overall
extraction time is approximately 15 min, roughly half that of the conventional
macroscale equivalent (~30 min).

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. Qualitative extraction -- Mb/PC model system evaluated by ESI-MS (Fig. 2)
  2. Quantitative extraction -- protein standards (BSA, Mb, Fb) evaluated by
     fluorescamine assay (Fig. 3); >80% recovery for all three proteins
  3. Complex mixture extraction -- fetal bovine serum (FBS) and Jurkat T-cell
     lysate (CL) evaluated by fluorescamine assay (Fig. 4);
     FBS: 84.0 +/- 7.8%; CL: 82.4 +/- 11.5%

The method is compatible with proteins spanning a wide range of molecular weights
(17-340 kDa) and isoelectric points (pI 4.7-7.3), as well as with complex biological
matrices. Performance is comparable to conventional macroscale precipitation techniques,
with the advantages of automation, reduced reagent/sample consumption, no centrifugation,
and shorter processing time.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Geometry    : Double-T (double cross) electrode layout
Substrate   : Glass wafer
Electrodes  : Chromium (250 nm) patterned by photolithography
              Actuation electrodes: 1x1 mm and 1.5x1.5 mm
              Reservoir electrodes: 2.5x2.5 mm and 3.0x3.0 mm
              Interelectrode gap: 40 um
Dielectric  : Parylene-C, 2.5 um (vapor deposition)
Hydrophobic : Teflon-AF, 50 nm (spin-coated, 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40,
              2000 rpm / 60 s; post-baked 160 C / 10 min)
Top plate   : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass + Teflon-AF (50 nm)
Spacer      : 1-2 layers double-sided tape (70 um or 140 um interplate spacing)
Actuation   : 70-100 Vrms at 18 kHz (function generator + amplifier)
Key feature : Extraction electrode -- surface above this electrode is where
              precipitation, rinsing, and resolubilization all occur

Reservoirs (4 reagent + 1 waste):
  - Precipitant reservoir
  - Rinse solution reservoir
  - Resolubilizing buffer reservoir
  - Sample reservoir
  - Waste reservoir

----------------------

Precipitants (Table 1):
  Mb, Fb           : Acetonitrile (ACN) -- primary; no secondary
  Mb/PC mixture    : ACN (primary) + saturated ammonium sulfate (secondary)
  BSA, FBS         : 20% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) in DI water
  Cell lysate (CL) : 20% TCA in DI water

Rinse solutions (Table 1):
  Mb, Fb, Mb/PC, BSA : 70/30 v/v chloroform/ACN
  FBS                : Acetone
  Cell lysate        : 60/40 v/v chloroform/acetone
  Note: neat chloroform is not directly actuatable at low driving potentials;
  chloroform/ACN (70/30 v/v) mixtures are readily movable on DMF devices.
  Neat acetone dissolves some CL precipitate; chloroform/acetone (60/40) avoids this.

Resolubilization buffers (Table 1):
  Mb, Fb, Mb/PC, BSA : 10 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5) + 1% SDS
  FBS, CL            : 100 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5) + 10% SDS

Working solutions:
  All protein solutions prepared in 10 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5) + 0.08% Pluronics F127 (w/v)
  Carrier fluid: Fluorinert FC-40

Key reagents (Sigma, unless noted):
  Acetone, ACN, chloroform, methanol, boric acid, 50% formic acid, Fluorinert FC-40,

  BSA, fibrinogen (Fb), myoglobin (Mb)
  PBS, FBS: Invitrogen Canada
  1,2-Dibutyroyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (PC): Avanti Polar Lipids

Fluorescence assay:
  Reagent  : Fluorescamine (5 mg/mL in acetone)
  Platform : Pherastar plate reader (BMG Labtech); 384-well low-volume microplate

  Reaction : Immediate; fluorescamine non-fluorescent until it reacts with

  Controls : Unextracted protein droplets processed identically through device

Mb  (myoglobin)            : MW 17 kDa, pI 7.3, 30 mg/mL; precipitant = ACN
Fb  (fibrinogen)           : MW 340 kDa, pI 5.5, 20 mg/mL; precipitant = ACN

Title        : Purification of High Salinity Brine by Multi-Stage Ion Concentration Polarization Desalination
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/srep31850
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/srep31850
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2016, Vol. 6, Article 31850
Authors      : Bumjoo Kim, Rhokyun Kwak, Hyukjin J. Kwon, Van Sang Pham, Minseok Kim,
               Bader Al-Anzi, Geunbae Lim, Jongyoon Han
Platform     : PDMS-based microfluidic ICP (Ion Concentration Polarization) desalination device
               with cation exchange membranes (CEMs) only — unipolar conduction


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a multi-stage Ion Concentration Polarization (ICP) electrical desalination
method for treating high-salinity brine (>35,000 ppm TDS), including produced water from shale
oil/gas development and brine concentrate from seawater desalination plants. ICP desalination
utilises two cation exchange membranes (CEMs) of the same polarity for unipolar ion conduction,
unlike conventional electrodialysis (ED) which uses both AEM and CEM in bipolar configuration.

The protocol is divided into three characterisation branches:
  1. Multi-stage trifurcated ICP desalination — 3 sequential ICP stages with intermediate
     stream recirculation; salt removal QC by conductivity and ICP-AES measurement
  2. Suspended solids removal — simultaneous TDS and TSS reduction from brine containing
     E. coli bacteria and crude oil emulsions; visualised by fluorescence microscopy
  3. Divalent cation removal — quantitative Na+ and Ca2+ removal confirmed by ICP-AES;
     relevant for produced water recycling and scaling prevention in wellbores

Key advantages of ICP over conventional technologies:
  - Treats brine up to 100,000 ppm TDS with salt rejection up to 70%
  - Removes both dissolved salts and suspended solids simultaneously (no pretreatment)
  - Less susceptible to membrane fouling/scaling (no AEM; pH shift occurs near AEM not CEM)
  - Partial desalination (50-75%) sufficient for EOR recycling and discharge
  - Cost < $1/bbl for source water up to 70,000 mg/L TDS; competitive with MSF and MVR


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication   : PDMS (Polydimethylsiloxane)-based microfluidic model system
                (for visualisation and concentration distribution tracing)
Membrane gap  : 1.5-2.0 mm
Channel depth : 0.2-0.6 mm
Channel length: 10-100 mm

CEMs          : Fumasep FTCM-E (FuMA-Tech GmbH, Germany)
                Area resistance: ~13.3 Ohm.cm2
                Note: High-resistance membrane used; significant improvement expected with
                lower-resistance membranes (power consumption strongly dependent on resistance)
AEM           : Fumasep FTCM-A (used in electrodialysis comparison experiments only)
Electrodes    : Carbon paper (Fuel Cell Store, Inc., Boulder, CO)
Ref electrodes: Ag/AgCl (A-M Systems, WA); penetrate channels vertically; measure
                membrane voltage drop per cell only (excludes electrode/reaction overpotential)

Plastic scale-up device: Assembled from CEMs, AEMs (ED only), carbon electrodes, and
                          laser-cut plastic components; channel depth 3 mm.

Output streams (trifurcated):
  Concentrate  : Top stream — ion-enriched; receives negatively charged suspended particles
  Intermediate : Middle stream — concentration ~C0; majority fluid; re-fed to next ICP stage
  Diluate      : Bottom stream — ion-depleted; final treated water product


REAGENTS
--------
Feed solutions:
  NaCl brine             : 0.1-1.7 M NaCl (5,800-100,000 mg/L TDS)
  Natural seawater       : Revere Beach, MA; general precipitation only, no prefiltration
                           (used for fouling/scaling durability experiments)

Electrode rinse          : Na2SO4 at same normality as feed NaCl solution
                           Purpose: Exclude electrode/reaction overpotential from
                           cell voltage measurement

Fluorescent tracers:
  ICP zone visualisation : Alexa Fluor 488, 1.5 uM (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA)
  Fluid tracing          : Fluorescent color coding red dye (Kingscote Chemicals, Inc., OH);
                           1:1000 volumetric ratio
  pH visualisation       : pH indicator dye (Micro Essential Laboratory, Inc., NY); 5 wt%

Bacterial model:
  Strain                 : E. coli K-12 MG1655
  Reporter               : Constitutively expressed GFP
  Purpose                : Visualise bacterial removal from diluate (Fig 7b)

Oil emulsion model:
  Oil                    : Crude oil (Greene, Co., PA)
  Buffer                 : 0.1 M NaCl
  Ratio                  : 1:50 (oil:buffer), sonicated 2 h
  Tracer                 : Fluorescent red dye 1:1000
  Purpose                : Visualise crude oil removal from diluate (Fig 7c)

Demineralised water      : CEM pre-conditioning soak (minimum 48 h before experiments)


EFFICIENCY METRICS
------------------
Current Utilization (CU):
  Formula : CU = zFQ_diluate(C0 - C_diluate) / NI
  Meaning : Fraction of applied current used for salt reduction in diluate flow
            (Ideally unity in ED with no current loss)
  ICP note: CU > 1 achievable with NaCl feed due to diffusivity difference
            DNa+ = 1.33e-9 m2/s; DCl- = 2.03e-9 m2/s; ICP with CEMs enhances
            salt removal ratio up to 20% compared to ED under same current

Energy per Ion Removal (EPIR):
  Formula : EPIR = (IV/Q_diluate) / (zk_BT(C0 - C_diluate)) proportional to V/CU
  Meaning : Specific energy consumed to remove one ion; proportional to voltage/CU
  Key finding: EPIR linearly proportional to salt removal ratio regardless of
               current density, flow velocity, or membrane length (Fig 3c)
               -> Optimal energy efficiency at minimum incremental salt removal ratio
               -> Drives multi-stage (batch) design philosophy


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | CEM Membrane Pre-Conditioning
  Reagents    : Demineralised water
  Operation   : Passive soak (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Duration    : Minimum 48 h at room temperature (25 C) = 2880m = 172800 s
  Purpose     : Equilibrate Fumasep FTCM-E CEMs before experiments
  BioScript   : mix cem_membrane with demineralizedWaterPrep for 2880m

Step 2 | Brine Feed Dispense
  Reagent     : NaCl brine, 0.1-1.7 M (5,800-100,000 ppm TDS)
  Flow rate   : ~20 uL/min via syringe pump (Harvard Apparatus PHD 2200), negative pressure
  Note        : Na2SO4 electrode rinse dispensed per-stage at point of use to avoid
                dead-code tokens in BioScript IR (rinse1, rinse2, rinse3)

Step 3 | Stage 1 — ICP Desalination (First Pass)
  Inputs      : Brine feed + conditioned CEM + Na2SO4 rinse (rinse1)
  ICP mix     : 10 s (flow-through separation abstraction)
  Actuation   : 25 C, 60 min = 3600 s (constant-current electrical actuation abstraction)
  Current     : 125-375 A/m2 constant; Keithley 236 source measurement unit
  Mechanism   : Ion depletion zone adjacent to CEMs; Na+ and Cl- separated into
                concentrate (top, enriched) and diluate (bottom, depleted)
  Trifurcated : Small diluate + majority intermediate (~C0) + small concentrate
  Salt removal: 5-20% per stage (optimal EPIR regime; Fig 3c)
  Rinse mix   : 10 s; stage1WithRinse fed to Stage 2
  Monitoring  : Conductivity probe (Microelectrode Inc.); Ag/AgCl reference electrodes

Step 4 | Stage 2 — ICP Desalination (Second Pass)
  Inputs      : stage1WithRinse (intermediate stream ~C0) + conditioned CEM + rinse2
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 60 min = 3600 s
  Current     : Adjusted per dilute production ratio p (506-1175 A/m2; Fig 5a table)
  Key feature : Feed concentration constant at ~C0 at every stage; system always in
                economically favourable high-salinity low-EPIR regime
                (unlike multi-stage ED where concentration drops stage-to-stage)
  Output      : stage2WithRinse fed to Stage 3

Step 5 | Stage 3 — ICP Desalination (Third Pass)
  Inputs      : stage2WithRinse (intermediate stream ~C0) + conditioned CEM + rinse3
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 60 min = 3600 s
  Output      : treatedDiluate (cumulative 50-75% TDS reduction)
  Overall     : System recovery fixed at 50% for cost comparison (SI-section 3.2.1)
  Justification: 3 stages is representative optimised configuration for high-salinity feed;
                 saltier feedwater requires more stages (SI-section 3.2.3)

Step 6 | Salt Removal QC Detection
  Input       : treatedDiluate
  Module      : saltRemovalDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Methods     : Flow-through conductivity probe (Microelectrode Inc., NH) for bulk TDS;
                CCD-based ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba, Ltd., Japan) for cation quantification
  Pass (BB2)  : saltSignal > 0 -> TDS reduced 50-75%; dispose treatedDiluate
  Fail (BB3)  : saltSignal <= 0 -> TDS target not met; drain treatedDiluate
  Join (BB4)  : dispose saltSignal; proceed to TSS branch

Step 7 | Suspended Solids Removal Characterisation
  Inputs      : E. coli K-12 MG1655 (GFP-expressing) + crude oil emulsion (1:50, sonicated)
                + fresh NaCl brine + demineralised water
  Contaminant mix : 2 s each (sequential)
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 30 min = 1800 s
  Mechanism   : Negatively charged particles (negative zeta potential) migrate en bloc to
                concentrate stream (anode direction) by electrophoretic force + electroconvection
                Diluate exits particle- and salt-free simultaneously
  Module      : suspendedSolidsDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Detection   : Fluorescence microscopy (Olympus IX-71)
  Pass (BB5)  : solidsSignal > 0 -> TSS cleared from diluate; dispose tssSeparation
  Fail (BB6)  : solidsSignal <= 0 -> particles remain; drain tssSeparation
  Join (BB7)  : dispose solidsSignal; proceed to divalent cation branch
  Note        : Majority of bio-contaminants and colloidal particles in natural water carry
                negative zeta potentials; simultaneous TDS+TSS removal is key ICP advantage
                over conventional ED (requires separate pretreatment steps for TSS)

Step 8 | Divalent Cation Removal Characterisation
  Inputs      : Fresh NaCl brine + Na2SO4 rinse (rinseDivalent) + demineralised water
  Feed mix    : 5 s
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 30 min = 1800 s
  Target      : Na+ (monovalent) and Ca2+ (divalent) quantified in diluate
  Module      : divalentCationDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Method      : CCD-based ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba, Ltd., Japan)
  Result      : Divalent cations removed proportionally or in excess of monovalent cations
                (SI-section 8); consistent with electrodialysis literature (refs 41-43)
  Significance: Prevents Ca2+/Mg2+/Ba2+/Sr2+ carbonate/sulfate precipitation in wellbore
                during produced water recycling for hydraulic fracturing reuse
  Pass (BB8)  : divalentSignal > 0 -> Na+/Ca2+ removal confirmed; dispose divalentSeparation
  Fail (BB9)  : divalentSignal <= 0 -> residual divalent ions above threshold; drain
  Terminal (BB10): dispose divalentSignal; NOP


MEMBRANE FOULING AND SCALING
-----------------------------
ICP advantage : Operates without AEMs; pH shift and scale formation (calcium deposits)
                occur near AEM due to water splitting (H+ and OH- production) not near CEM.
                ICP voltage largely constant over extended operation (natural seawater, 3 h,
                500 A/m2, no prefiltration) while ED voltage increases due to organic fouling.
ED comparison : CU reduction ratio higher in ED than ICP (Fig 8e); membrane fouling
                disrupts counter-ion transport and raises resistance.
pH observation: Significant acidification in dilute stream and basification in concentrate
                stream observed near AEM in ED (Fig 8a/b); not observed near CEM in ICP.
Test conditions: Natural seawater (Revere Beach, MA); no prefiltration or chemical
                 precipitation; constant current 500 A/m2; 3-channel stacked devices.


COST ANALYSIS
-------------
ICP target cost : < $1/bbl for source water up to 70,000 mg/L TDS at 70% salt removal;
                  linear dependence of overall cost on feed water salinity (Fig 6)
Capital cost    : Sum of membrane/equipment expenses and maintenance cost
                  (dominated by membrane area; ref 17, 25)
Operating cost  : Power consumption (other minor costs neglected; refs 17, 27, 28)
Optimal staging : More stages -> lower energy cost but higher capital cost;
                  optimum total cost at limit of many stages (incremental desalination)
                  Saltier feedwater -> more stages required (SI-section 3.2.3)

Competitor comparison (Fig 6):
  RO  : Practical limit ~45,000 ppm TDS; not viable for brine; pretreatment > $1/bbl
  MSF : Significant infrastructure; not competitive for partial desalination
  MVR : $3.50-6.25/bbl ($22-39/m3) total; $2-3/bbl operating only; complete desalination
  ICP : Cost (green zone, Fig 6) compares favourably over MSF and MVR for partial
        desalination target (50-75% salt removal)

REAGENTS USED:

  - Methanol (extraction solvent)
  - Deionized Water
