PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single Cells (DISC)
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms8513
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms8513
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2015, Vol. 6, Article 7513
Platform     : Digital Microfluidics (DMF) -- two-plate electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD)


OVERVIEW
--------
DISC is a DMF-based method that automates all steps required to analyse signalling events in
adherent cells in situ: cell culture, serum starvation, sub-second ligand stimulation, chemical
fixation, and full immunocytochemistry (ICC) for quantitative single-cell phosphorylation profiling.

The platform overcomes two key limitations of existing approaches:
  1. Flow-based microfluidics require high flow rates for fast stimulus switching, producing
     shear stresses (>1 dyn/cm2) that activate unwanted mechanosensitive signalling pathways.
     DISC operates at ~0.5 dyn/cm2 with no moving parts.
  2. Conventional bulk methods (western blot, mass spectrometry) require cell disaggregation
     and cannot resolve single-cell heterogeneity or achieve time resolution below minutes.
     DISC achieves ~1 s reagent exchange and probes individual adherent cells in situ.

The protocol is demonstrated on the well-characterised PDGFR/PI3K/Akt signalling pathway
in NIH-3T3 fibroblasts and extended to breast cancer cell heterogeneity (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231).
Key finding: a 10 s pulse of PDGF-BB (3.125 ng/mL) is sufficient to commit >32% of cells to
Akt activation -- kinetics far faster than any previously reported method could resolve.

The complete protocol encodes two sequential ICC arms:
  Arm 1 (PDGFR arm): 2 min stimulation; probes PDGFR Y857 / Y1021 phosphorylation.
  Arm 2 (Akt arm):   5 min stimulation; probes Akt S473 phosphorylation.
Both arms run the identical 11-step ICC pipeline with arm-specific antibody panels.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration: Two parallel plates separated by a ~180 um double-sided tape spacer.

Bottom plate:
  Material    : Chromium electrodes on glass (200 x 300 x 1.1 mm, Telic Co.)
  Electrodes  : 80 actuation electrodes, 2.2 x 2.2 mm each; interdigitated borders
                (140 um sinusoidal pattern); inter-electrode gap 30-80 um.
                Reservoir electrodes for reagent loading and waste removal.
  Dielectric  : Parylene C, ~7 um (vapour deposition with A174 silane adhesion primer).
  Hydrophobic : Teflon-AF, ~200 nm (spin-coat 1% w/w in FC-40, 2000 rpm, 60 s; 165 C bake).

Top plate:
  Material    : ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd, 300 x 100 mm).
  VM sites    : 8 circular hydrophilic ITO spots (1.75 mm diameter, 4.4 mm pitch) created by
                Teflon-AF lift-off using S1811 photoresist patterning.
  Function    : Cells adhere to the ITO spots; Teflon-AF surrounds spots to confine droplets.

Virtual Microwells (VMs):
  Volume      : ~400 nL per VM (2.4 mm2 footprint).
  Formation   : Passive dispensing -- when a source droplet (~900 nL unit droplet or larger)
                is swept across a vacant ITO spot, a sub-droplet spontaneously forms by
                hydrophobic-hydrophilic interaction (Supplementary Fig. 1).
  Capacity    : 150-300 cells per VM at 500,000 cells/mL seeding density.
  Exchange    : One passive dispense displaces ~93% of VM contents.
                Two successive exchanges displace >99% (Fig. 2b-d).
  Exchange time: ~1 s between successive droplet deliveries (Fig. 2a).

Actuation:
  Waveform    : Sine wave, 80-100 V_rms, 10 kHz.
  Interface   : 90-pin Pogo pin connector.
  Control     : DropBot open-source DMF automation system (http://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/dropbot).
  Orientation : Standard (top plate up) for droplet manipulation; inverted (top plate down)
                for all incubation steps so cells settle onto ITO spots by gravity.


CELL LINES
----------
- NIH-3T3 (mouse embryonic fibroblasts):
  Primary model for PDGFR/PI3K/Akt pathway validation (Figs. 3, 5, 6).
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% calf serum (CS) + 100 U/mL pen G + 100 ug/mL strep, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Seeded at 500,000 cells/mL; yields ~150-300 cells per VM.

- MCF-7 (human breast cancer):
  Used for Akt single-cell heterogeneity experiments, 0-5 min stimulation
  (Supplementary Figs. 9-11). Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS + antibiotics.

- MDA-MB-231 (human breast cancer, triple-negative):
  Used for hyperactive-responder single-cell morphology analysis (Fig. 4).
  Higher levels of Akt activation vs MCF-7 after 5 min (Supplementary Fig. 9a).
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS + antibiotics.


PROTOCOL STEPS -- 11-STEP ICC PIPELINE
---------------------------------------
All reagents contain 0.05% v/v Pluronic F-68 (on-chip) to prevent biofouling.
All incubation steps performed at room temperature (25 C) unless otherwise noted.
Device inverted (top plate down) for all incubation steps.

Step 0 | Cell Seeding and Adhesion
  Reagent  : CultureMedia (DMEM + 10% serum + 0.05% F-68 + antibiotics)
  Cells    : NIH-3T3 at 500,000 cells/mL
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL passively dispensed per VM spot
  Duration : 24 h at 37 C in humidified chamber (= 1440 min = 86400 s)
  Notes    : Device inverted after seeding. Cells settle by gravity; adhere to ITO spots.
             10^5-10^6 cells/mL confirmed sufficient for analysis (Supplementary Fig. 4).

Step 1 | Serum Starvation
  Reagent  : StarvedMedia (DMEM + 0.5% serum + 0.05% F-68 + antibiotics)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL
  Duration : 24 h at 37 C (= 1440 min = 86400 s)
  Notes    : Reduces basal PDGFR and Akt phosphorylation to unstimulated baseline.

Step 2 | Serum-Free Rinse
  Reagent  : SerumFreeMedia (DMEM + 0.05% F-68 + antibiotics)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL
  Duration : Immediate (passive dispense; ~1 s per exchange)
  Notes    : Two successive exchanges remove >99% of starving media (Fig. 2b-d).

Step 3 | PDGF-BB Ligand Stimulation
  Reagent  : PDGF-BB in SerumFreeMedia (Sigma-Aldrich human recombinant)
  Volume   : 2 x 900 nL = 1.8 uL
  Duration : 2 min for PDGFR arm; 5 min for Akt arm (encoded separately in BioScript)
  Dose     : 0-200 ng/mL (dose-response); 50 ng/mL (time-series); 3.125 ng/mL (pulse)
  Shear    : ~0.5 dyn/cm2 -- below 1 dyn/cm2 threshold for mechanosensitive signalling.
             Validated: 75 continuous back-and-forth movements, P=0.7188, no Akt effect.
  Variants :
    Single bolus  : Continuous PDGF-BB; fix at t = 30-120 s (Fig. 5a)
    Double bolus  : PDGF-BB at t=0 s + second PDGF-BB or vehicle at t=90 s (Fig. 5b)
    Pulse washaway: PDGF-BB for 3-40 s, then SerumFreeMedia wash, then fix at 2-5 min (Fig. 6a/b/c)

Step 4 | Fixation
  Reagent  : 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) + 0.05% F-68 in DPBS
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 10 min (= 600 s)
  Notes    : Applied within ~1 s of stimulation termination. Arrests signalling at exact
             time point. In time-series experiments, fixation staggered across VMs so
             all VMs are fixed simultaneously.

Step 5 | Post-Fixation Wash
  Reagent  : WashBuffer1 (0.05% v/v F-68 in DPBS)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL

Step 6 | Permeabilisation
  Reagent  : 0.2% v/v Tween-20 in DPBS
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 10 min (= 600 s)
  Notes    : Required for intracellular antibody access; essential for pAkt S473 detection.

Step 7 | Post-Permeabilisation Wash
  Reagent  : WashBuffer2 (0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS)
  Volume   : 9 x 900 nL = 8.1 uL
  Notes    : Extended wash volume to fully remove Tween-20 before blocking.

Step 8 | Blocking
  Reagent  : 1% bovine non-fat dried milk + 0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 60 min (= 3600 s)

Step 9 | Primary Antibody Incubation
  PDGFR arm:
    pan-PDGFR-b : Mouse mAb 1:50, CST sc-19995             [total protein; Cy5 channel]
    p-PDGFR Y857: Rabbit pAb 1:200, SCB sc-12907-R         [phospho; Cy3 channel]
    p-PDGFR Y1021: Rabbit pAb 1:200, SCB sc-12909-R        [phospho; Cy3 channel]
  Akt arm:
    pan-Akt     : Mouse mAb 1:50, CST 2920S                 [total protein; Cy5 channel]
    p-Akt S473  : Rabbit mAb 1:200, CST 4060P               [phospho; Cy3 channel]
  Diluent  : Blocking solution (BS); pre-mixed off-chip before DMF reservoir loading
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : Overnight at 4 C (= 720 min = 43200 s)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Accurate Processing of Ultra-Short Immune Signals by Single Macrophages
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.26.684377v1.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.26.684377
Journal      : bioRxiv preprint, posted October 26, 2025
Platform     : Multilayer PDMS microfluidic live-cell stimulation device with pneumatic valve control


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol investigates the temporal limits of immune signal detection by individual primary
macrophages. Primary bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) from mVenus-RelA (RelA^V/V)
C57BL/6J transgenic mice -- which express an endogenously tagged fluorescent NF-kB p65/RelA
reporter -- are isolated, differentiated, and seeded into multilayer PDMS microfluidic culture
chambers. The cells are then exposed to ultra-short (1-second) chemical pulses of five NF-kB
ligands covering cytokine and pathogen-derived signaling modalities: TNF alpha, Lipid A,
Pam2CSK4, R848 (Resiquimod), and CpG ODN 1668. NF-kB nuclear translocation dynamics of
the mVenus-RelA reporter are tracked by time-lapse epifluorescence microscopy over 6 hours
at single-cell resolution.

Key findings encoded in this protocol:
  - Single macrophages detect and respond to 1-second ligand pulses with high specificity
  - Short-pulse channel capacity (CC_max = 0.82) is comparable to persistent stimulation
    (CC_max = 0.92), demonstrating robust signal discrimination at the 1-second timescale
  - Three macrophage subpopulations emerge: early responders, late responders, non-responders
  - Pam2CSK4 produces the strongest response under 1-second pulse; Lipid A is most potent
    only under persistent stimulation -- stimulus duration alters the ranking of ligand potency
  - Macrophages employ two sensing modes: sensitivity to cytokine duration (TNF) vs. pathogen
    amplitude/dose (Pam2CSK4, R848)
  - Mathematical modeling identifies Hill coefficient (receptor cooperativity) as the primary
    determinant of the three NF-kB activation modes


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Microfluidic chip: Multilayer PDMS fabricated from silicon wafer master molds (10:1 PDMS
monomer:catalyst, Momentive). Control layer and fluid layer spin-coated separately, bonded
by oxygen plasma, overnight-baked. Control and flow inlets punched; glass-bonded.

Flow control:
  - Pneumatic valves electronically controlled via custom MATLAB GUI
  - PEEK tubing (VICI) at 4 psi input pressure
  - Pulse timing CV = 0.06 (6% variability across all analyzed cells)
  - Pulse as short as 1 second reliably delivered to live cells

Environmental control:
  - In-situ microbiome box maintains 37 C, humidity, and CO2 throughout imaging
  - Cells exhibit no photobleaching or phototoxicity under 6-hour imaging protocol


MOUSE MODEL
-----------
Strain     : mVenus-RelA (RelA^V/V) C57BL/6J
Reporter   : mVenus fluorescently tagged p65/RelA NF-kB subunit (endogenous knock-in)
Age/Sex    : 6-12 weeks; male and female
Housing    : Specific pathogen-free, University of Chicago Animal Resources Center
Ethics     : NIH Guide for Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; University of Chicago IACUC
Gift from  : Alex Hoffmann laboratory


REAGENTS
--------
m-CSF                 : Murine m-CSF (Peprotech); reconstituted in ultrapure water;
                        aliquoted and stored at -80 C; 20 ng/mL in complete RPMI
Cell culture media    : Complete phenol red-free RPMI (Gibco)
Fibronectin           : 0.2 mg/mL fibronectin solution (Sigma-Aldrich) in PBS
Nuclear stain         : Hoechst 33342 (Invitrogen), 1 uM in phenol red-free RPMI
Ligands (all stored at -80 C; thawed on ice and diluted in complete RPMI before use):
  TNF alpha           : Murine TNFalpha (R&D Systems),     10 ng/mL
  Lipid A             : Ultrapure Lipid A from E. coli O111:B4 (Invivogen), 10 ng/mL
  Pam2CSK4           : PAM2CSK4 (Invivogen),               3 ng/mL
  R848 Resiquimod     : R848 Resiquimod (Invivogen),       300 ng/mL
  CpG ODN 1668        : ODN 1668 (Invivogen),              300 nM


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | BMDM Isolation and Differentiation
  Tissue source  : Tibias and femurs of 6-12-week-old male and female RelA^V/V C57BL/6J mice
  Isolation      : Bone marrow cells flushed and resuspended in complete RPMI supplemented
                   with 20 ng/mL murine m-CSF (Peprotech)
  Differentiation: 7-9 days at 37 C / 5% CO2 (encoded as 9 days = 12960 min = 777600 s)
  Harvest        : BMDMs harvested on days 7-9; loaded into microfluidic culture chips
  Reference      : Wang et al., Cell Syst 2025 (PMID protocol source)

Step 2 | Microfluidic Device Fibronectin Priming
  Reagents       : 0.2 mg/mL fibronectin (Sigma-Aldrich) in PBS
  Duration       : 5 min (encoded as 300 s)
  Purpose        : Pre-incubation of PDMS culture chambers to promote BMDM adhesion
  Notes          : mix abstracts the channel-flow fibronectin coating step

Step 3 | BMDM Seeding and Equilibration
  Density        : 10^6 cells/mL in complete phenol red-free RPMI
  Duration       : 4-6 h undisturbed (encoded as 6 h = 360 min = 21600 s at 37 C)
  Purpose        : Cells attach and equilibrate in microfluidic chambers before stimulation

Step 4 | Nuclear Tracking Stain
  Reagent        : 1 uM Hoechst 33342 (Invitrogen) in phenol red-free RPMI
  Duration       : ~5 min (per producer instructions)
  Purpose        : Enables nuclear segmentation (395 nm channel) and single-cell tracking
                   throughout the 6-hour time-lapse imaging run

Step 5a | TNF Alpha 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : Murine TNFalpha (R&D Systems), 10 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi (PEEK tubing, VICI)
  Receptor       : TNFR1 (CD120a); cytokine intercellular signaling pathway
  Key result     : Weakest response under 1-second pulse; non-monotonic dose-duration
                   relationship; 100-second pulse doubles NF-kB amplitude vs 1-second pulse;
                   macrophages respond to cytokine duration, not amplitude

Step 5b | Lipid A 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : Ultrapure Lipid A from E. coli O111:B4 (Invivogen), 10 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR4; extracellular bacterial PAMP sensing
  Key result     : Largest late responder fraction (~30%); longest time to peak (>50 min);
                   most potent ligand under persistent stimulation but not under 1-second pulse;
                   reversal of potency ranking demonstrates duration-dependent ligand identity

Step 5c | Pam2CSK4 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : PAM2CSK4 (Invivogen), 3 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR2/TLR6 heterodimer; bacterial lipopeptide sensing via MyD88/TIRAP
  Key result     : Strongest response under 1-second pulse (highest early AUC, amplitude,
                   speed, duration); lowest late responder fraction (~3%); CC_max = 0.82;
                   Pam-vs-control MI with features = 0.87; used as QC reference condition

Step 5d | R848 (Resiquimod) 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : R848 Resiquimod (Invivogen), 300 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR7 (endosomal); viral RNA mimic sensing via MyD88
  Key result     : All-or-nothing activation dynamic (similar to fibroblast/cancer cells);
                   largest channel capacity under dose-duration tradeoff; lower dose (longer
                   pulse) elicits minimal to null response; strong dose (short pulse) gives
                   robust activation

Step 5e | CpG ODN 1668 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : ODN 1668 CpG (Invivogen), 300 nM
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR9 (endosomal); foreign/pathogenic DNA sensing
  Key result     : CpG and TNF induce highest oscillatory frequencies under short pulses;
                   pairwise mutual information CpG vs TNF = 0 at 1-second pulse (cells
                   cannot distinguish these two ligands at 1-second duration)

Step 6 | Time-Lapse NF-kB Live-Cell Imaging and QC Detection
  Microscope     : Nikon Ti2 epifluorescence; 20x magnification
  Camera         : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2
  Channels       : mVenus-RelA (508 nm, NF-kB nuclear translocation); Hoechst (395 nm, nuclei)
  Frame interval : 6 minutes
  Total duration : 6 hours = 360 min = 21600 s (encoded as heat 37 C + detect 360 min)
  Cells per cond : >200 individual cells analyzed per stimulation condition
  Activation threshold: 2 standard deviations above mean nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of
                   unstimulated cells; first passage time defines activation time
  Analysis software: Custom MATLAB 2024a; nuclear segmentation via Hoechst images;
                   nuclear/cytoplasmic mVenus-RelA ratio per cell per frame; dead cells,
                   dividing cells, and out-of-focus cells removed (>99% tracking accuracy)
  QC module      : nfkbTranslocationDetection; positive signal (nfkbSignal > 0) confirms
                   NF-kB nuclear translocation above threshold in at least one cell

  Branch pass    : nfkbSignal > 0 -> dispose(imagingPool_all)   [BB2]
  Branch fail    : nfkbSignal <= 0 -> drain(imagingPool_all)    [BB3]
  Terminal       : dispose(nfkbSignal); experiment ends          [BB4]


SINGLE-CELL SUBPOPULATION ANALYSIS
-----------------------------------
Method         : k-means clustering (MATLAB; 10 random centroid replicates; Euclidean distance)
                 applied to activation time and amplitude from all NF-kB traces
Subpopulations :
  Early Responders (ER)  -- fast response < 25 min, high amplitude
  Late Responders (LR)   -- response onset > 20 min, low amplitude
  Non-Responders (NR)    -- never exceed activation threshold
Late responder fractions:
  Pam2CSK4    ~3%  (lowest; predominantly early responders)
  Lipid A     ~30% (highest; cells activate up to 1 hour post-stimulation)
  TNF         intermediate; non-responder fraction dominates at low doses
  R848        switch from early responders to non-responders as dose decreases
  CpG         intermediate; broader activation time range than TNF or R848
Paracrine check: No correlation between late responder activation time and distance to
                 nearest early responder (r^2 ~ 0); late response is cell-intrinsic


INFORMATION THEORY ANALYSIS
----------------------------
Mutual Information (MI): Quantifies NF-kB trace distinguishability between two ligands
  (1 bit = perfect distinguishability; 0 = indistinguishable)
Channel Capacity (CC_max, 1-second pulse): 0.82 bits at ~21 min
  Comparison to persistent stimulation CC_max: 0.92 bits
  Conclusion: short-pulse specificity nearly equivalent to persistent stimulation
Pairwise MI highlights:
  Highest: Pam2CSK4 vs TNF
  Lowest:  CpG vs TNF (MI = 0; indistinguishable at 1-second)
  Pam2CSK4 vs control (with dynamic features): MI = 0.87 (near-perfect distinguishability)
Most informative dynamic features: Early AUC, amplitude at t_max, activation speed, duration


MATHEMATICAL MODEL SUMMARY
---------------------------
Type         : Minimal ODE model; ligand-receptor interaction + NF-kB signal transduction
               downstream IKK module; Hill function summarizes upstream IKK interactions
Receptor pathways fit: TNFR (TNFalpha), TLR2 (Pam2CSK4), TLR7 (R848)
Three activation modes predicted:
  m1: Monotonic increase  -- NF-kB amplitude increases with pulse duration (high activation rate)
  m2: Non-monotonic       -- intermediate; peak varies non-monotonically with duration
  m3: Monotonic decrease  -- NF-kB amplitude decreases with pulse duration (high-dose filter)
Key predictor: Hill coefficient n (cooperativity); highest MRMR importance score
  TNFR: n = 1.21 (low cooperativity; border between m1 and m2)
  TLR2: n = 1.83 (moderate cooperativity; m2/m3 boundary)
  TLR7: n = 10   (very high cooperativity; operates as high-dose filter; m3)
Noise sources:
  Extrinsic: receptor expression variability (Gamma-distributed)
    TNFR: Gamma(4.32, 1035); TLR2: Gamma(2.23, 4914); TLR7: Gamma(4.80, 4404)
  Intrinsic: stochastic kinetic rate fluctuations
    TNF -> kc variability; Pam -> Hill coefficient n variability; R848 -> K variability

ASSAY TYPE:
Enzymatic activity assay of 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (NADH-Dependent Oxidoreductase Activity).

REAGENTS USED:
- Reaction Buffer (contains acetoacetyl-CoA substrate, 30 uM final)
- NADH Solution (10 mM)
- Purified OsAIM1 Enzyme (0.5 ug)
- Purified GST Protein (0.5 ug, negative control)

STEPS:
1. Primary Preparation (Sample): Dispense 100 units of the reaction buffer containing the acetoacetyl-CoA substrate at 25 degrees C. Dispense 1 unit of the 10 mM NADH solution to obtain a final NADH concentration of 0.1 mM. Mix thoroughly to ensure homogenization.
2. Enzymatic Reaction (Sample): Initiate the reaction by dispensing 1 unit of the purified OsAIM1 protein. Mix immediately to ensure uniform distribution of the enzyme in the reaction solution.
3. Detection (Sample): Measure the absorbance at 340 nm, corresponding to the characteristic absorption peak of NADH. Record absorbance values every 15 seconds in a 4-cycle loop (60 seconds) to monitor continuous oxidation. Discard the droplet.
4. Control Branch: Dispense 100 units of reaction buffer and 1 unit of NADH solution, then mix. Dispense 1 unit of purified GST protein as a negative control to account for non-enzymatic NADH oxidation. Mix and measure absorbance every 15 seconds for 4 cycles, then discard.

INTERPRETATION:
The enzymatic reaction rate is determined from the linear decrease in absorbance at 340 nm over time, reflecting NADH oxidation during the reaction. This accompanies the reversible NADH-dependent reduction of acetoacetyl-CoA to 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA.

The extraction efficiency is quantitatively evaluated using the fluorescamine assay, which reacts with primary amines at the N-terminus of proteins to produce fluorescence. High fluorescence indicates high protein recovery compared to the control.

====================

Title        : High-throughput Isolation and Sorting of Gut Microbes Reduce Biases of Traditional Cultivation Strategies
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2019/09/06/759969.1.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/759969
Journal      : bioRxiv preprint, September 6, 2019

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput end-to-end microfluidic platform for anaerobic
isolation, cultivation, and sorting of gut-associated bacteria in picoliter droplets. The
system enables stochastic single-cell encapsulation in 65-115 pL aqueous droplets suspended
in oil, clonal growth without interspecies competition, and automated image-based sorting of
slow-growing colonies based on an optical density proxy (Wavelet OD). The platform is operated
entirely inside a vinyl anaerobic chamber (Coy Laboratory Products) under strictly anaerobic
conditions (O2 < 1 ppm, H2 1.5-2.5%) to support cultivation of extremely oxygen-sensitive gut
anaerobes.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. ASF model community validation -- 8-species Altered Schaedler's Flora (mouse gut) used
     to confirm all species grow in droplets, including extremely oxygen-sensitive strains,
     and that droplets prevent competitive overgrowth of fast-growing over slow-growing species.
  2. Human stool cultivation across 3 rich media -- BHIS, GMM, and YCFA droplets cultured in
     parallel and compared to conventional agar plates using 16S rRNA amplicon profiling.
     Community richness increases 37% (BHIS) to 410% (YCFA) in droplets over plates.
  3. Wavelet OD-based slow-grower sorting -- image-based sorting at ~30 Hz retains droplets
     with sparse colonies (Wavelet OD 0.3-0.7), further amplifying rare taxa from <1% to >1%
     relative abundance (avg. 6.5 ASVs unsorted vs. 12.5 ASVs sorted, out of 158 total).
  4. Viability confirmation -- sorted droplets streaked onto BHIS agar plates; Sanger
     sequencing of 24 randomly picked colonies confirms viability and taxa identity
     (Hafnia 12/24, Enterococcus 8/24, Bacteroides 4/24).

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Nanoelectrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry (DMF-nESI-MS) for Dried Blood Spot (DBS) Succinylacetone (SA) Quantification

  - Dried Blood Spot Punch (3.2 mm diameter filter-paper punch bearing dried whole blood, fortified with 13C5-SA internal standard)
  - Methanol (neat MeOH, pre-extraction solvent, 15 uL droplets)
  - SA Extraction/Derivatization/MS Reagent (6.5 mM hydrazine and 15 uM 13C5-SA in 80:20 acetonitrile:DI water with 0.1% v/v formic acid, 15 uL droplets)

1-2. Pre-extraction wash 1: Load a 15 uL methanol droplet, actuate onto the DBS punch, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then actuate the droplet away from the punch to a waste reservoir.

5-6. Pre-extraction wash 3: Repeat the load/incubate/waste-removal cycle a third time.
7. First Derivatization Step: Load a fresh 15 uL droplet of the hydrazine/13C5-SA/acetonitrile:water solvent, actuate onto the residual (methanol-washed) DBS punch, and incubate 15 min at 37 C on a hot-plate until the droplet evaporates.
8. Second Derivatization Step: Load a second fresh 15 uL droplet of the same hydrazine reagent, deliver it to the residual blood spot, and incubate for 1 min at room temperature (with circular actuation around the punch).
9. Detection: Actuate the derivatized droplet to the inlet of a pulled-glass capillary nanoESI emitter positioned near the mass spectrometer orifice; apply a DC potential to generate a stable nanoelectrospray and acquire MS/MS spectra, quantifying succinylacetone from the m/z 155->137 (SA) product-ion intensity relative to the m/z 160->142 (13C5-SA internal standard) product-ion intensity; then discard the analyzed droplet.

Title        : An Automated Induction Microfluidics System for Synthetic Biology
Source Link  : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_dff8587cf80c488aa25077207e571507.pdf
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.8b00025
Journal      : ACS Synthetic Biology, 2018, Vol. 7, pp. 933-944
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with integrated 600 nm LED absorbance reader,
               TSL2561 lux sensor, Arduino Uno controller, and MATLAB-based GUI automation


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the Automated Induction Microfluidics System (AIMS), a digital
microfluidic platform for automating bacterial cell culture, OD-triggered IPTG induction,
and on-chip protein expression analysis without manual intervention. The system integrates:
  (1) A DMF device for droplet-based cell culture, induction, and enzymatic assays
  (2) A 600 nm LED + TSL2561 lux sensor for real-time OD monitoring at 280 um gap height
  (3) An Arduino Uno + MATLAB GUI for automated droplet movement and induction triggering
  (4) CLARIOStar plate reader for end-point fluorescence detection (off-chip)

Three protocols are encoded sequentially in the BioScript file:
  P1 - Growth Curve: Semicontinuous mixing of E. coli mother culture with OD monitoring
       until the induction threshold (OD = 0.4) is reached.
  P2 - Inducer Concentration Optimisation: On-chip 2:1 serial dilution of IPTG to generate
       a dose-response curve for RFP expression using a pET16b-RFP reporter construct.
  P3A - BGL Single-Point Screening: Three thermophilic beta-glucosidases (BGL1: T. roseum,
        BGL2: T. terrenum, BGL3: R. marinus) screened for MUG hydrolysis activity after
        4 h induction; time-course fluorescence assay (0, 15, 30, 45, 60 min).
  P3B - BGL3 Multi-Point Optimisation: BGL3 (highest activity, >=6x BGL1/BGL2) optimised
        across five post-induction incubation times (0, 2, 3, 5, 6 h); fixed 30 min MUG
        assay per time point.

Volume reduction: 10,000x in culture (15 uL vs 150 mL); 40x in assay (5 uL vs 200 uL).
Hands-on time at 5-plex: 18 min (AIMS) vs 35 min (bench-top).
IPTG cost at 5-plex: $0.01 reagents (AIMS) vs $2.52 reagents (bench-top).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------

OD MEASUREMENT
--------------
Formula      : A = log(I0 / I) / 0.028
               A  = absorbance (OD units)
               I0 = blank lux intensity (LB media, no cells)
               I  = sample lux intensity
               0.028 = path length correction factor for 280 um gap height
Threshold    : OD = 0.4 (triggers IPTG induction)
LOD          : 0.035 OD units (at 280 um gap height)
Mixing cycle : one actuation every 45 s; 700 ms actuation time; horizontal + vertical
               4-step sequence; prevents biofouling while maintaining cell homogeneity
Re-check     : If OD < 0.4, continue mixing for 10 min before next OD measurement
Doubling time: AIMS: 72.88 +/- 2.30 min; bench-top: 36.80 +/- 0.36 min
               (two-tailed paired t-test; P = 0.018)
               Difference attributed to semicontinuous vs continuous mixing efficiency
               and shorter path length (280 um vs 1 cm)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Automated Microfluidic System for Dynamic Stimulation and Tracking of Single Cells
Source Link  : https://taylab.uchicago.edu/uploads/9/1/8/0/91804060/2018_anal_chem.pdf
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.8b00312
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2018, XXXX, XXX-XXX (ACS Publications)
Platform     : Large-scale integrated microfluidics (LSIM); two-layer PDMS valve-based chip


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a programmable, valve-controlled microfluidic system designed for
long-term culture, dynamic cytokine stimulation, and continuous single-cell time-lapse imaging
of nonadherent hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) and adherent murine embryonic
stem cells (muESCs) without displacing or losing track of individual cells.

The system overcomes a key limitation of existing LSIM devices: most rely on direct media
flow over cells, which physically displaces nonadherent cells during each media exchange.
Here, media exchange occurs exclusively by diffusion through 50-um-wide ports connecting
flanking media reservoirs to the cell culture area. Valves alternate reservoir filling
between left and right sides to prevent cross-chamber pressure-driven flow (flow-switching
strategy). No flow crosses the cell culture area at any point during culture or stimulation.

The protocol is divided into two independent experimental arms encoded in sequence:

  Protocol 1: Long-term GMP differentiation assay
    - Murine LysM-GFP granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GMPs) seeded into 48 chambers
    - 48 h baseline culture in permissive SCF/IL3/IL6 Stem-Span SFEM
    - Switch to 20 ng/mL M-CSF for 48 h; LysM-GFP expression tracked every 30 min
    - In-culture continuous anti-F4/80-APC antibody staining for macrophage commitment
    - Result: 77% of M-CSF colonies vs. 54% of control colonies upregulated LysM-GFP
      within 96 h (p=0.001636, two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test)

  Protocol 2: Dynamic FGF1 stimulation of muESC ERKKTR reporter line
    - Line R1 muESCs expressing ERK kinase translocation reporter (ERKKTR)
    - 2-day self-renewing culture (DMEM + 10% FCS + 1000 U/mL Lif)
    - 16 h starvation (0.5% FCS DMEM without Lif) to synchronise ERK baseline
    - Oscillating FGF1 stimulation: 5 s FGF1 pulse / 32 min incubation / 2 s wash /
      15 min incubation; three complete cycles encoded
    - ERK activity imaged every 3 min (ERKKTR nuclear-to-cytoplasmic C/N ratio)
    - 93% of cells adjacent to reservoir respond within 3 min; all within 10 min


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i  : Flow layer -- PDMS, channel height 25 um; fabricated by photolithography on
           SU-8 3025 master (4-in. silicon wafer); 40 kdpi photomask (Fine Line Imaging).
Layer ii : Control layer -- PDMS, channel height 25 um; AZ-50XT deposited at valve
           positions to produce parabolic valve surfaces for tight closure.
Layer iii: Coverslip bonded to underside of flow layer after O2 plasma treatment.

Fabrication:
  - PDMS ratio: 10:1 polymer:catalyst (RTV 615, Momentive Performance Materials)
  - Cast at 80 C for 45 min on wafer
  - O2 plasma treatment, layer alignment, bonding
  - 2 h thermal bonding at 80 C; additional 12 h cure after full assembly at 80 C

Chip architecture:
  - 48 independently addressable cell culture chambers (1000 um x 350 um x 25 um)
  - 16 independent inputs (left side); 2 outlets / harvesting ports (right side)
  - Four-valve on-chip peristaltic pump for fluid manipulation and cell deposition
  - 2 media reservoirs per chamber; connected via 50-um-wide diffusion ports
  - Valve control: solenoid manifold (1.7-2.5 bar closing; 0.5 bar flow layer)
  - MATLAB GUI for experimental scripting and valve actuation control

Chip validation (bead displacement test):
  - 10 um polystyrene beads (Spherotech) pre-treated with 0.1% Triton-X
  - Bead translocation in culture chamber: <2 um after 15 s reservoir flushing
  - Confirms absence of direct flow in culture area during media exchange
  - 40 kDa rhodamine-dextran (300 uM) used for diffusion rate calibration
    (comparable in size to cytokines; reaches steady state within 10 min)

- Murine LysM-GFP GMPs (granulocyte-macrophage progenitors):
    Source: C57BL/6J male mice, 12-14 weeks old, Lysozyme M gene locus (LysM-GFP)
    Immunophenotype: lin-/Sca1-/c-Kit+/CD34+/CD16/32+
    Isolation: Bone marrow dissected, pulverized (4 C mortar), 40 um nylon mesh strainer

Step 1 | Chip Priming

  Operation : Dispense PBS; force through all channels under pressure while outlet

  Purpose   : Fully wets all surfaces before functionalization. Required step before
              any biological use of the chip.

Step 2 | Surface Functionalization

  Operation : Flow fibronectin through all channels for 3 h at 25 C (or overnight).

  Duration  : 180 m (= 3 h) at 25 C; IR: 10800.0 SECOND
  Purpose   : Promotes hematopoietic progenitor retention and muESC adhesion;
              prevents non-specific cell-to-PDMS binding.

FLOW-SWITCHING STRATEGY
------------------------
The key innovation enabling nonadherent cell culture is the alternating reservoir fill:

  1. Left reservoir filled:  left-side inlet valves open; right-side valves closed.
     Fresh media or stimulant flows into left reservoir channel only.
  2. Right reservoir filled: right-side inlet valves open; left-side valves closed.
     Mirrors left fill. Completes one exchange cycle.
  3. Seeding valves:         always closed during culture phases.

This sequential approach eliminates pressure differentials that would drive flow across
the culture chamber. Reagents exchange into the culture area by diffusion only (Fick's
Law through 50 um port). Steady state reached within 10 min per reservoir fill cycle.
Oscillation periods of 20 min and 40 min were validated with rhodamine-dextran (Fig. 2B).
Chemical gradients across the chamber last a maximum of 20 min per exchange.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (Electrowetting) Colorimetric Enzyme-Kinetic Glucose Assay on Human Physiological Fluids (Serum, Plasma, Urine, Saliva)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Calibrant (100 mg dL-1 glucose standard solution, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Glucose Reagent (6 U mL-1 glucose oxidase, 6 U mL-1 peroxidase, 6 mM 4-aminoantipyrine, 6 mM TOPS, in 0.1 M phosphate buffered saline pH 7.0, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Plasma Sample (1.5 uL droplets)
  - Serum Sample (1.5 uL droplets)
  - Saliva Sample (spiked with glucose, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Urine Sample (spiked with glucose, 1.5 uL droplets; subject to uric acid interference with the Trinder reaction)

STEPS:
1. Calibration run: Dispense a 1.5 uL calibrant droplet (100 mg/dL glucose standard) and a 1.5 uL glucose reagent droplet onto adjacent electrodes (electrode pitch 1.5 mm, spacer height 500 um).
2. Merge and mix the calibrant/reagent droplet by shuttling across multiple electrodes for 15 s.
3. Measure absorbance continuously for at least 30 s using the LED-photodiode setup (545 nm green LED, TSL257 photodiode) and compute RateCALIB from the slope of the absorbance-vs-time curve.
4. Plasma assay: Dispense a 1.5 uL plasma droplet and a 1.5 uL glucose reagent droplet, merge/mix for 15 s, and measure absorbance for at least 30 s to obtain RatePLASMA.
5. Serum assay: Repeat the same dispense/merge-mix/absorbance-read cycle using serum in place of plasma to obtain RateSERUM.
6. Saliva assay: Repeat the same cycle using (glucose-spiked) saliva to obtain RateSALIVA.
7. Urine assay: Repeat the same cycle using (glucose-spiked) urine to obtain RateURINE.
8. Concentration calculation: For each sample, compute CSAMPLE = (RateSAMPLE / RateCALIB) x 100 mg dL-1.
9. Reference comparison: Compare each on-chip concentration against a reference value obtained on a bench-top spectrophotometer (Gensys 20) using a conventional 100-fold dilution; note that the urine result shows a significant deviation from the reference value, attributed to interference by uric acid reacting with hydrogen peroxide in the Trinder reaction (interference that the 100-fold dilution in the reference method suppresses but the digital-microfluidic chip's 2-fold dilution does not).

INTERPRETATION: Successful glucose quantification is confirmed by close agreement between the on-chip and reference concentrations for plasma, serum, and saliva (total error 3, 8, and 3 mg dL-1 respectively), demonstrating basic feasibility of colorimetric enzyme-kinetic bioassays on real physiological samples using an electrowetting-based digital microfluidic lab-on-a-chip; the larger urine discrepancy (16 mg dL-1) highlights a matrix-specific interference (uric acid) that must be addressed (e.g., via additional sample dilution/wash) for that fluid type.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Characterizing Deformability and Electrical Properties of Breast Cancer Cells
               Using a Microfluidic Device Combining Electrical Impedance Sensing and
               Mechanical Constriction
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/ancham/article/90/1/912/818332/Characterizing-Deformability-and-Electrical
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.7b03859
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2018, Vol. 90 (1), pp. 912–919
Authors      : Ying Zhou, Dahou Yang, Yinning Zhou, Bee Luan Khoo, Jongyoon Han, Ye Ai
Affiliations : BioSyM IRG, SMART Centre, Singapore; SUTD Singapore; MIT Cambridge MA
Platform     : Pressure-driven PDMS microfluidic device with integrated coplanar gold electrodes
               in differential impedance configuration; Fluigent MFCS-EZ pressure controller


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes simultaneous characterisation of single-cell mechanical deformability
and electrical properties as cells transit a narrow PDMS constriction under applied pressure.
Four cell populations are compared: untreated MCF-7 (live breast cancer cells), PMA-modified
MCF-7 (modMCF-7, pharmacologically softened), formaldehyde-fixed MCF-7 (stiffened reference),
and red blood cells (RBCs, highly deformable positive reference).

The key innovation is a differential four-electrode-pair impedance configuration that
simultaneously measures:
  (1) Z_undeformed: electrical impedance of the intact cell before entering the constriction,
      captured by two outer electrode pairs positioned upstream/downstream of the constriction.
      This reflects cell size and membrane capacitance.
  (2) Z_deformed: electrical impedance of the fully deformed cell inside the constriction,
      captured by two inner electrode pairs inside the narrow channel. This is dominated by
      cell membrane electrical properties.

This is the first reported device to measure both Z_undeformed and Z_deformed in a single
transit event. Three mechanical timing parameters are also extracted per cell:
  - Passage time : total time from first contact with constriction to full exit
  - Entry time   : time for cell to enter and fully deform into the constriction
  - Transit time : time spent transiting the interior of the constriction

The differential configuration automatically rejects multi-cell transit events (identified
by successive same-sign impedance peaks) and is insensitive to environmental drift, unlike
conventional non-differential two-electrode approaches.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Channel fabrication:
  Photoresist : SU-8 2015 (MicroChem); spin-coated at 2000 rpm; thickness ~20 um
  Soft bake   : 65 C 1 min + 95 C 3 min
  UV exposure : 155 mJ/cm2
  Post bake   : 65 C 1 min + 95 C 3 min
  Developer   : SU-8 developer solution, room temperature
  Mold treat  : trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane, vapor deposition (hydrophobic)
  PDMS        : Sylgard 184 (Dow Corning); base:curing agent 10:1; degas; pour on mold;
                cure 60 C ≥3 h; peel; punch inlets/outlets with 1.5 mm biopsy punch
  Channel height : ~20 um
  Constriction width : ~8 um (narrower than MCF-7 diameter ~22 um; forces deformation)

Electrode fabrication:
  Substrate   : 4 inch glass wafer
  Material    : Gold, patterned by lift-off process
  Width       : 20 um; spacing within pair: 30 um
  Configuration: Coplanar, patterned on bottom glass substrate (4 pairs total)
  Outer pairs : 2 pairs flanking constriction (sense undeformed cells)
  Inner pairs : 2 pairs inside constriction (sense fully deformed cells)

Bonding:
  Oxygen plasma treatment of PDMS and glass surfaces; align using XY positioner;
  bond permanently; bake 120 C 1 h to strengthen bond.

Impedance measurement:
  Analyser    : HF2IS Impedance Spectroscope (Zurich Instruments)
  Input V     : 500 mV amplitude
  Frequencies : 1 MHz and 2 MHz (simultaneous multi-frequency acquisition)
  Method      : Differential: ΔZ = (Z_medium_only − Z_cell+medium) / (Z_cell+medium × Z_medium_only)
  Advantage   : Eliminates baseline drift; rejects multi-cell events; does not require short/straight
                constriction geometry for detectable signal; measures both deformed and undeformed states

Electrical circuit model:
  Type        : Single-shell Foster-Schwan model
  Components  : Ri (cell interior resistance), Cmem (cell membrane capacitance),
                Rmed (medium resistance), Cmed (medium capacitance), CDL (double-layer capacitance)
  Assumptions : Cell interior capacitance and membrane resistance neglected (simplified analysis)
  Validated against impedance measurements from single cells (Sun & Morgan 2010; Morgan et al. 2006)

Pressure control:
  System      : Fluigent MFCS-EZ
  Application : Positive pressure at channel inlet drives cell flow
  Pressures   : 200 mbar (Figure S4) and 500 mbar (Figure 3 / Figure S3) tested


CELL LINES
----------
- MCF-7 (human breast adenocarcinoma): standard cancer cell deformability model.
  Cultured in standard conditions. Trypsinized and resuspended in PBS for live experiments.
  Average cell size: 22.01 um.

- modMCF-7 (PMA-modified MCF-7): MCF-7 treated with 500 nM PMA (Sigma-Aldrich) for 18 h at
  37 C. PMA activates protein kinase C (PKC), inducing cortical actin remodelling and
  increasing cell deformability. After treatment, cells resuspended in PBS for measurement.
  Average cell size: 22.42 um. Dose-response tested at 100, 300, 500 nM (Figure S6).

- fixedMCF-7 (formaldehyde-fixed MCF-7): MCF-7 fixed in 4% methanol-free formaldehyde
  (ThermoScientific) for 8 min; quenched with 0.127 M glycine for 5 min at room temperature;
  resuspended in PBS. Crosslinking maximally stiffens cytoskeleton. Average cell size: 23.37 um.

- RBC (human red blood cells): highly deformable positive reference. Biconcave disc ~8 um
  diameter. Readily transits 8 um constriction with minimal entry resistance. Resuspended in PBS.

Size note: All three MCF-7 populations show similar size distributions (avg 22–23 um),
confirming that observed differences in passage time and impedance reflect mechanical and
electrical properties, not size effects.

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a heterogeneous sandwich immunoassay for Human IgG implemented
on a digital microfluidic (DMF) device. The digital approach manipulates samples and
reagents as discrete droplets on a 2-D array of electrodes, as opposed to the streams of
fluid used in microchannels. Capture antibody (Fc-specific anti-human IgG) is physisorbed
directly onto the hydrophobic Cytop/ITO top plate of the DMF device, and all incubation
and wash steps are performed via DMF actuation at 75 V_rms, 18 kHz -- eliminating the need
for beads, magnets, BSA blocking, or a carrier oil interface.

The protocol is divided into two phases:
  1. Off-device: capture antibody spot immobilization on the Cytop/ITO top plate
  2. On-device: DMF-actuated antigen incubation, rinse, detection antibody incubation,
     final rinse, and fluorescence plate reader readout

Key advantages over conventional 96-well plate immunoassays:
  - Analysis time reduced from up to 2 days to 2.5 h total
  - Sample and reagent volumes reduced ~100-fold (1 uL vs 100 uL per assay)
  - Waste volumes reduced ~3 orders of magnitude (4 uL vs 3.5 mL per assay)
  - Diffusion-limited kinetics eliminated by active droplet transport
  - BSA blocking step eliminated by Pluronic F-127 additives
  - Dynamic range ~1 order of magnitude (R^2 = 0.9964); reproducibility %RSD < 25%
  - Multiplexed devices (6-10 platforms wired in series) enable parallel replicate assays


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : Patterned chromium electrodes on glass substrate (80 St George St. fabrication
               facility, University of Toronto). Two designs used:
               - Design A: 10 x 1x1 mm actuation electrodes + 2 x 2.5x2.5 mm reservoir electrodes
               - Design B: 20 x 1x1 mm actuation electrodes + 4 x 2.5x2.5 mm reservoir electrodes
               Inter-electrode gap: 40-75 um.
               Coated with 2 um parylene C (vapor deposition, Specialty Coating Systems) +
               130 nm Cytop (2.25% w/w in CT-SOLV180, spin-coated 1000 RPM 60 s,
               post-baked 180 C 15 min).

Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd, Stillwater MN).
               Coated with 130 nm Cytop (as above).
               Pre-spotted with capture antibody before device assembly.
               Discarded after each assay; bottom plate reused.

Spacer       : Two pieces of double-sided tape, ~150 um thick.
               Defines the gap between top and bottom plates and sets droplet volume.

Droplet volume : 1 uL (sandwiched between plates ~150 um apart).

Hydrophobic coating note:
  Teflon-AF (50 nm, standard DMF coating) was found too fragile for surface-based assays.
  Antibody spot printing caused flaws and tears in Teflon-AF, preventing DMF actuation.
  Cytop (130 nm) was selected for its greater mechanical ruggedness -- spots can be
  dried and rinsed without causing the hydrophobic layer to delaminate.

Multiplexing : 6 or 10 DMF platforms wired in series on a single device. Homologous
               electrodes bussed together for simultaneous control of replicate assays.
               Devices placed on a multiwell plate for fluorescence measurement.

Actuation    : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz (function generator output amplified); applied manually
               to exposed contact pads on bottom plate surface.
               Monitored by CCD camera on stereomicroscope with fluorescence imaging
               (Olympus Canada, Markham ON).

Detection    : PheraStar multiwell plate reader (BMG Labtech, Durham NC).
               lambda_ex = 485 nm, lambda_em = 520 nm, focal height = 12.1 mm.
               Device remains on multiwell plate throughout assay; inserted into
               plate reader after all DMF steps are complete.

  Notes       : Waste contains unbound Human IgG and matrix proteins.

Step 5 | First Rinse -- Removal of Non-Specifically Bound IgG
  Reagents    : PluronicF127_RinseBuffer (1 uL), AntiHumanIgG_Capture (surface-bound)
  Operation   : DMF actuation -- 2-pass rinse across capture spot
  Duration    : 2 min
  Passes      : 2
  Actuation   : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz
  Notes       : 10 mM phosphate pH 7.4 + 0.00625% Pluronic F-127. Fig. 3 (inset) shows

  Passes      : 10

  Duration    : 2 min
  Passes      : 2
  Actuation   : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz

Title        : Automated Digital Microfluidic Platform for Magnetic-Particle-Based Immunoassays with Optimization by Design of Experiments
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ac401847x.pdf

Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2013, Vol. 85, pp. 9638-9646

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a fully automated digital microfluidic (DMF) platform for performing
magnetic-particle-based sandwich immunoassays from sample to analysis with minimal manual
intervention. The target analyte is thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), clinically relevant for
thyroid disease screening (normal range 0.3-4 uIU/mL; hyperthyroidism: <0.3 uIU/mL).

The platform integrates three core hardware components:
  1. A 90 Pogo pin interface (two 15x3 arrays, 100 mil spacing) for digital microfluidic control,
     enabling 15 high-voltage inputs per square inch on a 3x2 in. DMF device.
  2. A motorized Hamamatsu H10682-110 PMT for chemiluminescent detection, with motor-driven
     engage/disengage and a light-blocking shutter (dark count < 50 counts/s in enclosure).
  3. A "magnetic lens" assembly: a neodymium bar magnet (3 x 0.5 x 0.25 in., Br=1.32 T)
     flanked by two AISI 1080 steel machined armatures acting as triangular field directors.
     Motor-driven vertical engagement (~150 um gap, ~600 uN vertical force) focuses the
     magnetic field to a narrow zone, enabling up to 8 simultaneous parallel magnetic
     separations -- vs. a maximum of 2 with the prior neodymium disc geometry.

The protocol implements a 3^3 full factorial Design of Experiments (DOE) optimization --
the first reported DOE optimization for immunoassays in any microfluidic system -- varying
three factors: sample volume (1, 3, 5 unit droplets), sample incubation time (3, 6, 9 min),
and TSH concentration (0, 0.4, 4 uIU/mL), totalling 108 discrete experiments. The resulting
optimized protocol achieves a 5-fold lower limit of detection (0.15 uIU/mL) and a 2-fold
reduction in sample incubation time relative to the prior prototype setup (Ng et al., 2012).

-------------------
Bottom plate : 80 actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm each), interdigitated borders
               (140 um peak-to-peak sinusoids), interelectrode gaps 30-80 um.

               Substrate thickness ~1.15 mm. Contact pads on periphery for Pogo pin interface.
Top plate    : Grounded brass leaflets connected at device hinge on loading.

Unit droplet volume  : ~800 nL
Reservoir volume     : ~3.5 uL
Actuation            : Sine wave AC, 100-120 Vrms, 10 kHz; Microdrop software + Arduino-based
                       high-voltage switching instrument.
Mixing mode          : Unit droplet shuttled in circular motion across 4+ electrodes.

Magnetic lens positions:
  Disengaged : ~3.8 cm below device (no field influence on droplets)
  Engaged    : ~150 um below device; vertical force ~600 uN (>470 uN minimum for immobilization)
  Field decay: <35 uN at >4 mm from magnet center (minimizes stray particle attraction outside
               separation zone; contrast with disc magnet where stray force at 10 mm = ~50/100 uN)

PMT positions:
  Disengaged : ~5 cm above device; shutter closed

This protocol implements the first fully automated CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing
assay on a digital microfluidic platform. The ACE platform automates all steps
— cell seeding, culture, lipid-mediated transfection, CRISPR-Cas9 knockout, drug
inhibition, and fluorescence-based viability readout — for lung cancer cells on a
single device.

The specific assay interrogates the MAPK/ERK (RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK) signaling
pathway by knocking out the RAF1 gene in NCI-H1299 lung squamous cell carcinoma
cells using CRISPR-Cas9, combined with dose-response treatment using the RAF
kinase inhibitor Sorafenib Tosylate. The combination of genomic disruption and
enzymatic inhibition results in lower IC50 values compared to inhibitor treatment
alone, confirming successful on-device gene editing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CELL LINE AND REAGENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cell Line       : NCI-H1299 human lung squamous cell carcinoma, dual-labeled
                  stable line (Genecopoeia SL001). Stably expresses eGFP at AAVS1
                  locus and mCherry. Grown in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, no antibiotics,
                  37 degrees C, 5% CO2.

Plasmids        :
  - pCRISPR_ctrl  : All-in-one pCRISPR/Cas9 plasmid (~10.5 kb) with sgRNA
                    targeting eGFP (non-genomic control, AAVS1 locus).
  - pCRISPR_RAF1  : All-in-one pCRISPR/Cas9 plasmid (~10.5 kb) with sgRNA
                    RAF1_sg94 targeting the human RAF1 genomic locus.
                    Designed via Benchling; assembled by restriction
                    digestion/ligation into All-in-one_CRISPR/Cas9_LacZ backbone.

Transfection    : Invitrogen Lipofectamine 3000 + P3000 reagent (Thermo Fisher).
                  On-device optimum lipid:media ratio is 1:1 (not the off-chip
                  manufacturer default of 1:10). The 1:1 ratio compensates for
                  the increased surface-area-to-volume ratio at microscale and
                  yields ~65% transfection efficiency vs ~15% at 1:10 (Fig. 2d).

Drug            : Sorafenib Tosylate (Selleckchem). RAF kinase inhibitor targeting
                  the MAPK/ERK pathway upstream at BRAF/RAF1.
                  Six concentrations: 0, 7.5, 15, 30, 60, 120 uM in complete media.

Stains          :
  - Hoechst 33342 (1 uM): nuclear stain; used ONLY at Day-1 transfection-
                           efficiency checkpoint. lambda_ex=350nm, lambda_em=461nm.
  - Calcein-AM violet (5 uM): live-cell esterase viability probe; used ONLY at
                               Day-5 readout. lambda_ex=408nm, lambda_em=450nm.
                               NOTE: Hoechst and Calcein-AM must NOT be used at
                               the same timepoint due to spectral overlap at ~450-
                               461nm.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVICE DESCRIPTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The DMF device consists of two parallel plates separated by a 140 um spacer.
The bottom plate contains chromium-patterned electrodes with dielectric and
hydrophobic layers (DuPont AF) for droplet actuation via electrowetting-on-
dielectric (EWOD) at ~200 VRMS, 10 kHz. Electrode boundaries are interlaced to
improve droplet movement for protein-rich solutions over multi-day culture.

The top plate (ITO-coated) contains six 1.2 mm diameter hydrophilic spots
microfabricated for adherent cell culture. Cells are passively dispensed onto
these spots; a fraction of the moving 690 nL droplet pins to the hydrophilic
site, forming a ~160 nL culture microvessel. Devices are incubated inverted in
a 3D-printed humidified chamber at 37 degrees C.

Reservoirs hold: cell suspension, Lipofectamine, Opti-MEM, plasmid DNA, P3000
reagent, complete media, Hoechst stain, Calcein-AM stain, and Sorafenib Tosylate.
A waste reservoir collects excess liquid from passive dispensing steps.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Arms            : 2 (Ctrl sgRNA arm / RAF1_sg94 arm)
Sites per arm   : 6 (one per drug concentration)
Total sites     : 12
Drug doses (uM) : 120, 60, 30, 15, 7.5, 0
Duration        : 5 days (Day 0 seeding through Day 5 viability readout)
Readout         : Calcein-AM violet fluorescence cell count, normalised to
                  vehicle control (0 uM site) for each arm.
Analysis        : Sigmoid dose-response curve fit; IC50 extracted per arm;
                  F-test for significance in linear region (2.5-50 uM, P<0.05).

QC gates        : Two independent QC branches in the CFG:
                  - Ctrl arm: gated on signalCtrl6 (0 uM Ctrl sgRNA vehicle).
                  - RAF1 arm: gated on signalRaf6 (0 uM RAF1_sg94 vehicle).
                  Pass = positive fluorescence signal (dispose viability droplets,
                  data accepted). Fail = zero/negative signal (drain droplets,
                  arm flagged). The two gates are independent; failure of one arm
                  does not invalidate the other.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DAY 0 — CELL SEEDING
  1. Grow NCI-H1299 cells in T-75 flasks, rinse with PBS, trypsinize, centrifuge
     at 1000 x g for 5 min, resuspend in complete media + 0.05% w/v Pluronics
     F-68 to ~1.75e6 cells/mL.
  2. Pipette 2 uL of cell suspension onto the ITO reservoir edge. Apply ~200 VRMS
     at 10 kHz to actively dispense 690 nL unit droplets. Passively dispense onto
     each of the 12 hydrophilic spots to form 160 nL culture microvessels.
  3. Invert device into 3D-printed humidified chamber. Incubate at 37 degrees C,
     5% CO2, 16h overnight to allow H1299 cell adhesion to hydrophilic spots.

DAY 1 — TRANSFECTION (7-STEP ACTUATION SEQUENCE)
  Step 1: Dilute Lipofectamine 3000 in Opti-MEM. Add 2 uL of the dilution to
          a reservoir. Actively dispense 360 nL Lipofectamine-Opti-MEM droplets
          per site (12 total, 6 per arm).
  Step 2: Mix 500 ng/uL of pCRISPR plasmid (ctrl or RAF1) with 1 uL P3000
          reagent in 25 uL Opti-MEM. Add to a separate reservoir. Actively
          dispense 360 nL DNA-P3000-Opti-MEM droplets per site.
          Ctrl arm: pCRISPR_ctrl (eGFP sgRNA).
          RAF1 arm: pCRISPR_RAF1 (RAF1_sg94 sgRNA).
  Step 3: Merge lipid droplet with DNA droplet on 2x2 electrode array. Mix in
          square configuration for 10 min to form lipid-DNA complexes.
  Step 4: Dilute complexes 1:1 by merging with a 690 nL Opti-MEM unit droplet.
          (On-device optimum: 1:1 ratio yields ~65% transfection efficiency.)
  Step 5: Passively dispense 6x160 nL of diluted complexes onto each hydrophilic
          cell culture spot.
  Step 6: Incubate 24h overnight at 37 degrees C, 5% CO2.
  Step 7: Transfection-efficiency checkpoint — dispense 1 uM Hoechst 33342 in
          liquid media (6x160 nL per site). Incubate 30 min. Image with
          fluorescence microscope (UV filter: 250 ms, GFP filter: 500 ms, mCherry
          filter: 1000 ms) using custom 3D-printed microscope holder.
          Analyse with CellProfiler transfection pipeline (Fig. 2a):
            Module 1: Gaussian smooth (sigma=1), Otsu global threshold, detect
                      nuclei 20-100 px, declump by intensity.
            Module 2: Threshold mCherry image (TCF=1.0), binarize.
            Module 3: Overlap — mask nuclei with mCherry-positive regions.
            Module 4: Efficiency (%) = overlapping nuclei / total nuclei x 100.
          Dispose all Hoechst/detection droplets before Day 2.

DAY 2 — MEDIA MAINTENANCE
  1. Remove lipid-DNA complexes and Hoechst stain by passively dispensing fresh
     complete media (6x160 nL per site) to wash. Drain spent droplets to waste.
  2. Replenish each site with fresh complete media (6x160 nL). Maintain cells
     at 37 degrees C, 5% CO2 for 24h.

DAY 3 — SORAFENIB DRUG DOSING
  1. Prepare Sorafenib Tosylate serial dilutions on-device:
     Stock -> 120 uM -> 60 uM -> 30 uM -> 15 uM -> 7.5 uM -> 0 uM (vehicle).
     Each step: actively dispense drug droplet, merge with complete media droplet,
     mix for 30s. Split each concentration into one Ctrl-arm aliquot, one RAF1-arm
     aliquot, and one carry for the next dilution step. The 0 uM step requires no
     carry (terminal step).
  2. Passively dispense one drug aliquot (0.7 uL) onto each cell culture spot:
     Sites 1 and 1: 120 uM (highest dose)
     Sites 2 and 2: 60 uM
     Sites 3 and 3: 30 uM
     Sites 4 and 4: 15 uM
     Sites 5 and 5: 7.5 uM
     Sites 6 and 6: 0 uM (vehicle control, QC baseline)
  3. Incubate 48h at 37 degrees C, 5% CO2 (bridges Day 3 to Day 5 readout).

DAY 5 — CALCEIN-AM VIABILITY ASSAY AND DETECTION
  1. Prepare 5 uM Calcein-AM violet in complete media. Passively dispense 6x unit
     droplets to each of the 12 cell culture spots.
  2. Incubate 30 min at 37 degrees C.
  3. Image using single-module CellProfiler pipeline (Fig. 4 imaging pipeline):
     Gaussian smooth (sigma=1), Otsu global threshold, detect objects 20-100 px
     (TCF=1.25), declump by intensity. Count viable cells per site.
  4. Normalise cell counts at each drug concentration to the vehicle control
     (0 uM site) for the respective arm to obtain % cell survival.
  5. QC gate — Ctrl arm: if signalCtrl6 > 0 (vehicle baseline positive), data
     accepted (dispose viability droplets). If signalCtrl6 <= 0, arm flagged
     bad (drain droplets).
  6. QC gate — RAF1 arm: independent gate on signalRaf6 using same logic.
  7. Dispose all signal droplets. Experiment ends.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IMAGING AND ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Microscope      : Olympus IX73 inverted fluorescence microscope with Hamamatsu
                  C1140-42U digital camera, HC ImageLive software.
Filter sets     : UV (250 ms), GFP (500 ms), mCherry (1000 ms).
                  Hoechst: lambda_ex=350nm, lambda_em=461nm.
                  GFP:     lambda_ex=488nm, lambda_em=509nm.
                  mCherry: lambda_ex=585nm, lambda_em=608nm.
                  Calcein-AM violet: lambda_ex=408nm, lambda_em=450nm.

Transfection    : CellProfiler 2.2.0 r9969F42 transfection pipeline.
efficiency      : Efficiency (%) = mCherry-positive nuclei / total nuclei x 100.
                  Corrected against non-transfected negative control.

Knockout        : CellProfiler knockout pipeline.
efficiency      : Knockout (%) = GFP-negative nuclei / total nuclei x 100.
                  GFP threshold: Otsu method (2-class, TCF=0.65).
                  Cells with >90% GFP-positive pixel overlap are not counted as
                  knocked out.

Viability       : Calcein-AM violet fluorescence cell count normalised to 0 uM
                  vehicle control. Sigmoid dose-response curve fit. IC50 extracted.
                  Statistical significance: F-test in linear region (2.5-50 uM).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KEY RESULTS (from paper)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Transfection    : ~74.7% +/- 6.8% efficiency at 48h post-transfection on-device.
efficiency        Comparable to well-plate (no significant difference, P>0.05).

GFP knockout    : ~35% average on-chip, comparable to well-plate ~39% (P>0.05).
efficiency        Consistent across three sgRNA loci (sg_12, sg_497, sg_683).

MAPK/ERK assay  : IC50 for Sorafenib Tosylate:
                    Ctrl sgRNA arm  : 7.54 uM (on-chip), ~9 uM (off-chip)
                    RAF1_sg94 arm   : 13.2 uM (on-chip), ~17 uM (off-chip)
                  ~1.8-fold reduction in IC50 with RAF1 CRISPR targeting vs control
                  (P<0.05, F-test). Confirms successful on-device RAF1 knockout and
                  sensitisation to Sorafenib inhibition.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KNOWN BUGS IN ORIGINAL .BS FILE (CORRECTED)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Fix 1 — Wrong manifest at Day-1 Hoechst checkpoint:
  Original : hoechstTfx* variables dispensed from manifest calceinAM
  Corrected: hoechstTfx* variables dispensed from manifest hoechst
  Reason   : Calcein-AM is a cytoplasmic esterase probe (lambda_em~450nm), not a
             nuclear stain. The CellProfiler transfection pipeline requires Hoechst
             33342 (lambda_em~461nm) to identify nuclei in Module 1. Using
             Calcein-AM would produce invalid nuclear object detection and incorrect
             transfection efficiency measurements.

Fix 2 — Double-use of spent drug dilution variables:
  Original : drugConc120 (and other intermediates) split twice in two separate
             code sections, causing a fluid-ownership violation in the BioScript
             compiler.
  Corrected: Each dilution step immediately produces three named outputs:
             _ctrlAliquot, _raf1Aliquot, _carry. Each variable is split exactly
             once. The carry feeds the next dilution step; the two aliquots are
             delivered to their respective arms.

Perform cDNA synthesis followed by quantitative PCR (qPCR). First, mix the RNA template, random primers, dNTPs, and RNase-free water to a final volume of 20 uL. Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Isolation of Single Cells for -Omics (DISCO) — Single-Cell Genomics Pipeline

REAGENTS USED:
  - Adherent Cell Suspension (U87 human glioblastoma or B16 murine melanoma cells cultured on a DISCO top-plate, ~0.5x10^6 cells/mL loading density)
  - Wash Buffer (DPBS with 0.05% v/v Pluronic F68)
  - Fixative Solution (HOPE Fixative solution I)
  - Permeabilization Buffer (ice-cold acetone)
  - Immunostaining Reagents (CD47-APC antibody, clone CC2C6; Hoechst 33342 nuclear stain)
  - Collection Buffer (DPBS with 0.05% v/v F68, used as the virtual-microwell collection droplet)
  - Whole Genome Amplification Reagent (Repli-g single cell kit, Qiagen)
  - QC-1 PCR Mix (Taq DNA Polymerase, primers for conserved loci on chromosomes 4, 12, 13, 22)
  - DNA Cleanup Reagent (DNA Clean and Concentrator columns, Zymo Research)
  - QC-2 PCR Mix (AmpFlSTR Identifiler PCR Amplification Kit, STR + Amelogenin loci)
  - Library Prep Reagent (Nextera DNA Flex Library Prep Kit, Illumina)

STEPS:
1. Cell seeding and culture: Adherent cells are loaded onto the DISCO top plate at a density of ~0.5x10^6 cells/mL and incubated for 24 h at 37 C in a humidified atmosphere.
2. Fixation: A fixative droplet is delivered to the virtual microwell and incubated 20 min at 4 C, followed by a wash step with DPBS/F68.
3. Permeabilization: An ice-cold acetone droplet is delivered to the fixed cells and incubated at -20 C for 10 min, followed by a wash step.
4. Immunofluorescent staining: The permeabilized cells are labeled with an anti-CD47-APC antibody and Hoechst 33342 nuclear stain to enable phenotype-based, AI-driven cell selection (CNN-based image segmentation, AUC = 0.991).
5. Cell selection and laser lysis: The user (manually or via the trained CNN) selects a single cell of interest; a focused Q-switched Nd:YAG laser pulse (532 nm, ~0.8 um spot size) lyses the targeted cell, releasing its contents into a collection droplet (virtual microwell). Cells with insufficient/ambiguous phenotype signal are excluded from downstream processing.
6. Whole genome amplification (WGA): The single-cell lysate is combined with the Repli-g multiple displacement amplification (MDA) reagent and incubated isothermally (~30 C) to amplify the genome.
7. Quality control 1 (QC-1): The amplified product is PCR-amplified at four conserved loci (chromosomes 4, 12, 13, 22) via standard thermal cycling (94 C denature / 55 C anneal / 72 C extend) and evaluated by gel electrophoresis; samples with fewer than 3 of 4 expected loci are discarded.
8. DNA cleanup: The QC-1-passing product is purified/concentrated using DNA Clean and Concentrator columns.
9. Quality control 2 (QC-2): The cleaned DNA is PCR-amplified at 15 short tandem repeat (STR) loci plus Amelogenin (94 C denature / 59 C anneal / 72 C extend) and evaluated by microfluidic gel electrophoresis; samples with fewer than 12 of 16 expected loci are discarded.
10. Sequencing library preparation: The QC-2-passing DNA is tagmented and library-prepped using the Nextera DNA Flex kit, then the finished single-cell whole-genome sequencing library is collected off-chip for storage (-20 C/-80 C) and downstream next-generation sequencing (Illumina MiSeq).

INTERPRETATION: Successful single-cell genomic analysis by DISCO is confirmed by high sequencing uniformity (Lorenz curve near-theoretical distribution), minimal amplification bias from MDA, negligible background DNA contamination from non-selected cells (<5% vs. bulk), copy-number-variant (CNV) profiles concordant between single cells and bulk samples (R^2 = 0.843), and strong agreement between AI-selected and manually-selected single-cell genomes (R^2 = 0.894), supporting use of DISCO for deep single-cell -omics analysis of heterogeneous or rare adherent cell populations, including detection of single-nucleotide-level CRISPR-induced variants.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-Scale Estrogen Assays in Breast Tissue, Blood, and Serum
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/scitranslmed.3000105
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.3000105
Journal      : Science Translational Medicine, 2009, Vol. 1, Issue 1, Article 1ra2
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF / EWOD) on single-plate open-top ITO electrode array
Analyte      : Estradiol (17-beta-estradiol)
Sample types : Whole blood, serum, breast tissue homogenate, estradiol standard solutions
Sample volume: 1 uL per assay (1000-4000x smaller than conventional biopsy methods)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a miniaturised, automated digital microfluidic method for extraction
and quantification of estradiol (the most biologically active form of estrogen) from 1-uL
clinical samples, including whole blood, serum, and breast tissue homogenate from
postmenopausal breast cancer patients.

Estrogen is a key hormone in human reproductive physiology and plays an important role in the
pathogenesis of breast cancer. Local breast tissue estrogen concentrations are not routinely
measured because conventional methods require invasive biopsies of hundreds to thousands of mg
of tissue, followed by 5-6 h of laboratory processing (lysis, homogenisation, extraction,
purification, resolubilisation). The DMF method described here reduces this to 10-20 min on a
1-uL sample, while achieving recoveries of 86-119% (ELISA, CV 7-10%).

The method uses digital microfluidics (EWOD) to automate a complete liquid-liquid extraction
workflow: (1) cell lysis with DCM/acetone, (2) steroid dissolution in methanol, and (3)
liquid-liquid partitioning in isooctane to remove interfering compounds (porphyrin m/z 715,
DNA helicase m/z 677, tyrosine m/z 178), which suppress estradiol ionisation in mass
spectrometry. Detection is performed by ELISA (absorbance 450 nm) and LC-MS/MS with selected
reaction monitoring (SRM, m/z 271/145; retention time ~3.2 min).

Breast tissue application: replicate analyses of 1-uL samples from postmenopausal breast cancer
patients yielded 522 pg estradiol/mg tissue (CV 1%), confirming suitability for quantitative
analysis from fine-needle aspiration-scale biopsies.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type         : Single-plate open-top DMF (EWOD)
Electrodes   : ITO (indium tin oxide), 1.5-mm pitch
Substrate    : Glass coated with Teflon-AF dielectric
Configuration: Open-top during sample drying; top plate affixed before solvent loading

Reservoirs:
  - Sample reservoir (blood, serum, tissue homogenate, or standard solution)
  - Lysing solvent reservoir (DCM/acetone 80:20 v/v)
  - Polar extraction solvent reservoir (methanol, HPLC grade)
  - Non-polar extraction solvent reservoir (isooctane, 99.8%)
  - Collection reservoir (pooled extract output)

Extraction zone:
  A photoresist "wall" defines the liquid-liquid extraction zone, separating the isooctane
  pool from the collection reservoir. The DMF device drives the methanol droplet in circular
  paths within the isooctane pool (~20 s per cycle, movie S1 in paper) before separating and
  directing the aqueous extract toward the collection reservoir. Phase separation at the wall
  is straightforward compared to microchannel-based liquid-liquid extraction, where separating
  one liquid phase from another after contact is inherently difficult.

Droplet volumes:
  Unit droplet (methanol extract): 200-400 nL
  Lysis wave option 1: 9 x 1.1 uL DCM/acetone (9.9 uL total)
  Lysis wave option 2: 5 x 2.2 uL DCM/acetone (11.0 uL total)
  Methanol extraction option 1: 9 x 1.1 uL methanol (9.9 uL total)
  Methanol extraction option 2: 5 x 2.2 uL methanol (11.0 uL total)


REAGENTS
--------

Lysing solvent       : DCM/acetone 80:20 (v/v)
                       Dichloromethane (Sigma); acetone HPLC grade
                       Function: lyse cells; dissolve lipid/protein matrix to free steroids

Polar extraction     : Methanol, HPLC grade (Fisher Scientific)
solvent                Function: dissolve free steroids from dried lysate into polar phase

Non-polar extraction : Isooctane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane), 99.8% (Sigma)
solvent                Function: partition interferents from polar estradiol-containing phase;
