PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : OrganoID: A Versatile Deep Learning Platform for Tracking and Analysis of Single-Organoid Dynamics
Source Link  : https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010584
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010584
Journal      : PLoS Computational Biology, 2022, Vol. 18, Issue 11, Article e1010584
Platform     : Organoid culture (Matrigel dome, 24-well plate) + brightfield / PI fluorescence
               timelapse microscopy + OrganoID deep learning image analysis pipeline


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a gemcitabine dose-response experiment on human PDAC (pancreatic ductal
adenocarcinoma) patient-derived organoids, designed to demonstrate OrganoID -- a robust, open-source
deep learning platform for automated pixel-by-pixel organoid detection, identification, and
longitudinal single-organoid tracking in brightfield and phase-contrast microscopy images.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Organoid embedding in Matrigel and pre-treatment equilibration (24 h)
  2. Gemcitabine dose-response treatment (7 conditions: 0, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000 nM)
     with concurrent PI fluorescence labelling and 72 h brightfield timelapse imaging
  3. OrganoID automated analysis: U-Net inference, Canny edge + watershed identification,
     Munkres Hungarian tracking, per-organoid PI normalisation, and morphological feature
     extraction (circularity, solidity, eccentricity)
  4. MTS endpoint viability assay (gold standard EC50 benchmark) and morphology QC

OrganoID achieves >95% organoid count agreement and >97% area agreement with manual
segmentation, maintains >89% single-organoid tracking accuracy over 92 h, and resolves
dose-response EC50 values (via area-normalised PI fluorescence: 24.45 nM) that closely
approach the MTS gold standard (26.13 nM), without fluorescent cell labelling.


DEVICE / PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE
--------------------------------
Culture format    : 24-well plate; 40 uL Matrigel domes per well; 500 uL media overlay.
Matrix            : Matrigel (Corning, growth factor reduced); ice-cold resuspension;
                    polymerisation at 37 C for 20 min before media overlay.
Complete media    : Advanced DMEM/F12 + 10% FBS + EGF + Noggin + R-spondin1 + Wnt3a.
Microscope        : Inverted brightfield / fluorescence microscope.
Imaging channels  : Brightfield (organoid morphology); PI fluorescence (ex 488 nm / em 617 nm).
Imaging interval  : Every 4 h over 72 h (18 frames per well per condition).
Image resolution  : 512x512 pixels (auto-resized by OrganoID pre-processing).


ORGANOID SOURCE
---------------
Cell type    : Human PDAC patient-derived organoids (two patients).
Passage      : 3-8.
Density      : ~500 organoids/mL in ice-cold Matrigel.
Pre-culture  : 24 h equilibration at 37 C / 5% CO2 in complete media before drug addition.


REAGENTS
--------
Drug           : Gemcitabine (dFdC); FDA-approved nucleoside analogue; inhibits
                 ribonucleotide reductase and DNA/RNA synthesis; 10 mM DMSO stock.
Concentrations : 0 (DMSO vehicle), 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000 nM; n=6 replicates/condition.
Vehicle        : DMSO at 0.1% v/v final (matched across all conditions).
Viability stain: Propidium iodide (PI); 1 ug/mL; added at time of drug treatment;
                 labels dead/necrotic cells; continuous labelling throughout imaging.
                 Excitation 488 nm / emission 617 nm.
MTS reagent    : (3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-5-(3-carboxymethoxyphenyl)-2-(4-sulfophenyl)-
                 2H-tetrazolium); readout at 490 nm; run on fresh organoid aliquot at endpoint;
                 4 h incubation at 37 C.


ORGANOID ID PIPELINE
--------------------
Language           : Python.
Neural network     : Keras (TensorFlow backend); modified U-Net architecture.
Filters (layer 1)  : 8 (vs 64 in original U-Net; 98% parameter reduction).
Trainable params   : <500,000.
Activation (hidden): ELU (exponential linear unit; avoids vanishing gradient problems).
Activation (output): Sigmoid (normalised organoid probability per pixel).
Preprocessing      : Auto-contrast and resize to 512x512 pixels.

Training:
  Dataset        : 66 manually labelled brightfield / phase-contrast images (PDAC, 2 patients).
  Split          : 52 training pairs / 14 validation pairs.
  Augmentation   : Augmentor package (rotation, zoom, elastic distortion, shear); 2000 images.
  Optimizer      : Adam (learning rate 0.001).
  Loss           : Unweighted binary cross-entropy.
  Weight init    : He method.
  Dropout        : 12.5% neuron weights zeroed after each batch.
  Batch size     : 8 augmented images per backpropagation round.
  Early stopping : Halt once 10 epochs pass with no improvement in validation loss.
  Convergence    : 37 epochs; validation cross-entropy loss minimum 0.088 at 8 filters.

Identification pipeline (single-organoid resolution):
  Step 1: Threshold detection image at 0.5; morphological opening to remove noise.
  Step 2: Canny edge detection on raw network prediction image
          (Sobel filter; Gaussian sigma=2; Thi=0.05, Tlo=0.005).
  Step 3: Remove Canny edges from thresholded image to mark organoid centres.
  Step 4: Watershed transform (centres as basin initialisers; prediction image as
          inverted heightmap). Libraries: scipy, scikit-image.
  Step 5: Discard detections with total area < 200 pixels.

Tracking module:
  Algorithm     : Munkres variant of the Hungarian algorithm.
  Cost function : Inverse of shared pixel count between consecutive detections.
  Pseudo-assign : Extra matrix rows/columns for missing or newly appearing organoids.
  Accuracy      : >89% (fraction of organoids correctly matched at each frame) over 92 h.
  Robustness    : Accuracy unaffected when frames discarded to simulate 12 h interval.

Performance (test dataset):
  PDAC IOU (mean +/- SD)         : 0.74 +/- 0.081 (benchmark >= 0.5)
  ACC  IOU                       : 0.78 +/- 0.09
  Colon IOU                      : 0.72 +/- 0.08
  Lung  IOU                      : 0.87 +/- 0.04
  Mouse small intestine IOU      : 0.70 +/- 0.15
  Organoid count CCC             : 0.95 (95% CI 0.89-0.98)
  Organoid area CCC              : 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.97)
  False positive rate (bubbles)  : 4.2%
  Segmentation speed             : ~300 ms per image (Intel i7-9750H 2.6GHz, <200 MB RAM)

Step 1 | Organoid Embedding in Matrigel
  Reagents    : PDAC organoids (~500/mL), Matrigel (ice-cold, growth factor reduced)
  Operation   : Resuspend organoids in ice-cold Matrigel; seed 40 uL domes per well
  Gelation    : 37 C for 20 min (heat at 37 C for 20 min in BioScript)
  Purpose     : Creates 3D extracellular environment recapitulating in situ tumour matrix.
                mix abstracts the resuspension and dome-seeding step (no DMF mixing).

Step 2 | Media Overlay and Pre-Treatment Equilibration
  Reagents    : Complete media (500 uL per well)
  Operation   : Overlay after Matrigel gelation; equilibrate at 37 C / 5% CO2 for 24 h
  Duration    : 24 h = 1440 min (heat at 37 C for 1440 min in BioScript)
  Purpose     : Allows organoids to adapt to culture conditions before drug challenge.

Step 3 | Vehicle Control Treatment (0 nM Gemcitabine)
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, DMSO vehicle (0.1% v/v final), PropidiumIodide (1 ug/mL)
  Operation   : Mix drug/vehicle into media; add PI; image at 37 C every 4 h for 72 h
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min (heat at 37 C for 4320 min in BioScript)
  Detection   : organoidDetection module; 30 s
  QC branch   : controlSignal > 0 → dispose (organoids detected, growing normally; experiment valid)
                controlSignal <= 0 → drain (no organoids in control; experiment setup failure)
  Notes       : heat + organoidDetection together abstract the full 18-frame timelapse run
                with concurrent OrganoID U-Net inference and tracking.

Step 4 | 3 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_3nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal3nM > 0 → dispose; signal3nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Lowest dose; minimal effect on area or count (Fig 3B).

Step 5 | 10 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_10nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal10nM > 0 → dispose; signal10nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Organoid count begins to fall sharply above 10 nM (Fig 3B bottom).

Step 6 | 30 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_30nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal30nM > 0 → dispose; signal30nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Clearest representative dose in paper (Fig 3A): organoid area initially
                rises (early growth) then falls; count drops; PI fluorescence rises
                proportionally to concentration.

Step 7 | 100 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_100nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal100nM > 0 → dispose; signal100nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Without area normalisation, total PI at 100 nM paradoxically exceeds
                1000 nM signal (Fig 3C top). OrganoID per-organoid area normalisation
                corrects this discrepancy (Fig 3C bottom), aligning responses correctly.

Step 8 | 300 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_300nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal300nM > 0 → dispose; signal300nM <= 0 → drain

Step 9 | 1000 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_1000nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal1000nM > 0 → dispose; signal1000nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Highest dose. Essentially all organoids killed by 48 h. Circularity and

                organoid architecture (moderate-to-large Cohen d effect sizes; Fig 3E).

                cell turnover and structural protein production.

Step 10 | MTS Endpoint Viability Assay (Gold Standard)
  Reagents    : Fresh PDAC organoids, MatrigelMatrix, CompleteMedia, MTS reagent
  Operation   : Re-embed fresh organoid aliquot; overlay media; incubate MTS 4 h at 37 C
  Duration    : Gelation 20 min + MTS incubation 4 h = 240 min (heat at 37 C for 240 min)

  Result      : MTS EC50 = 26.13 nM (Fig 3D; gold-standard reference)
  Notes       : Run on fresh organoid aliquot, not timelapse wells. Off-device 4-parameter

Step 11 | Single-Organoid Morphology Analysis
  Reagents    : Fresh PDAC organoids, MatrigelMatrix, CompleteMedia
  Operation   : Re-embed; overlay media; detect morphological features on reference well
  Detection   : morphologyAnalysis module; 60 s
  QC branch   : morphologySignal > 0 → dispose (metrics computed; pipeline operational)

  Metrics computed (scikit-image regionprops on OrganoID labeled masks):
    Circularity  : Inverse ratio of organoid perimeter to perimeter of perfect circle

    Solidity     : Ratio of organoid area to convex hull area.
                   Decreases with gemcitabine dose. EC50 = 27.05 nM.
    Eccentricity : Elliptical deviation from a perfect circle.
                   Increases with gemcitabine dose. EC50 = 18.08 nM.
    Effect size  : Cohen's d statistic (difference in means / pooled SD) computed across
                   all pairwise concentration combinations (Fig 3E heatmap).
  Normalisation: Tracking-based per-organoid normalisation (each organoid normalised to
                 its own first-detection value) significantly reduces CV vs batch
                 normalisation: fluorescence (p=2e-30), area (p=2e-29),
                 perimeter (p=2e-63) -- Welch t-test (Fig S6).

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Multistep Proteomic Sample Processing (Reduction, Alkylation, Tryptic Digestion) with MALDI-MS Readout

REAGENTS USED:
  - Protein Sample (e.g., insulin, lysozyme, or BSA in working buffer)
  - TCEP (Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine reductant, 10 mM in working buffer)
  - Iodoacetamide (alkylating agent, 12 mM in working buffer)
  - Trypsin (protease, in working buffer)

STEPS:
1. Reduction: Dispense the protein sample droplet and a droplet of TCEP reductant onto the array. Merge and actively mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at room temperature (23°C) for 30 minutes to reduce disulfide bonds to free thiols.
2. Alkylation: Dispense a droplet of iodoacetamide and merge with the reduced sample droplet. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at room temperature (23°C) for 10 minutes to covalently cap the free thiols and prevent disulfide reformation.
3. Digestion: Dispense a droplet of trypsin and merge with the alkylated sample droplet. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at room temperature (23°C) for 60 minutes to enzymatically digest the protein into constituent peptides.
4. Detection: Analyze the final peptide digest by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS) for 1 minute to confirm reduction, alkylation, and digestion, and to identify peptides. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: Successful processing is confirmed by mass shifts in the MALDI-MS spectrum: loss of the intact disulfide-linked mass after reduction, a +57 Da shift per thiol after alkylation, and the appearance of characteristic tryptic peptide masses (searchable against a protein database, e.g., via Mascot) after digestion.

A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the linear, non-branching portion of the Luk & Wheeler (2009) DMF workflow: sequential on-chip reduction, alkylation, and tryptic digestion, read out by MALDI-MS. Reagent identities (TCEP, iodoacetamide, trypsin), incubation temperature (room temperature / 23°C), and hold times (30 min reduction, 60 min digestion) are taken directly from the paper's Qualitative Analysis section describing stages ii-iv of the workup. The 10-minute alkylation hold reflects the paper's reported time-to-completion for full alkylation, rather than the shorter 2-minute intermediate timepoint the paper uses only to visualize partially-alkylated species in Figure 3c. Dispense volumes are abstracted to a generic 100-unit droplet, since BioScript's volumetric unit model does not natively express the paper's ~100 nL droplets at analyte-specific molar concentrations (e.g., 40 µM insulin, 10 mM TCEP, 12 mM iodoacetamide). Unlike the ELISA-style scripts in this test suite, this protocol has no repeat/wash cycles, which is intentional and matches the paper's central claim: DMF droplets act as isolated microreactors, so no intermediate wash or purification step is needed between reduction, alkylation, and digestion.

ASSAY TYPE: Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis Protocol on Digital Microfluidic Chips (Flow-Based Microfluidic System for Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Plasmid DNA Stream (pJL1-sfGFP-DQNAT-6xHis acceptor protein plasmid, energy mix, salts, and metabolites)
  - S30 Cell-Free Extract Stream (E. coli BL21 Star (DE3) S30 crude extract plus T7 RNA polymerase)

  - Elution Buffer (PBS with 300 mM imidazole, for IMAC product recovery)

STEPS:
1. Protein Synthesis Module: A plasmid/energy/salts/metabolites stream and an S30 extract/T7 RNA polymerase stream are combined at the inlet of a serpentine microfluidic chip and mixed by diffusion as they travel through the channel; each chip provides a 30 min reaction residence time, and multiple chips are linked in series (up to four chips for a 2 h total residence time) to continuously synthesize sfGFP-DQNAT-6xHis.
2. Protein Glycosylation Module: The synthesized protein stream is continuously flowed over CjPglB oligosaccharyltransferase that is site-specifically biotinylated and tethered to the channel surface (via silane-PEG5000-biotin/NeutrAvidin/biotin chemistry), together with CjLLO glycan donor; the device is held at 30 C and the reaction proceeds across a series of chips at 30 min residence time per chip, achieving up to 100% glycosylation efficiency within 2 h.
3. Protein Purification Module (Loading/Flowthrough): The glycosylated protein stream is passed through a channel packed with Ni2+-charged affinity resin held in place by an array of posts at the outlet; hexahistidine-tagged glycoprotein binds the resin while unbound material exits as the flowthrough fraction.
4. Protein Purification Module (Wash): The inlet stream is switched to wash buffer (PBS + 10 mM imidazole) at 2 uL/min to remove non-specifically bound proteins and cellular debris from the resin bed; the wash fraction is collected.
5. Protein Purification Module (Elution): The inlet stream is switched to elution buffer (PBS + 300 mM imidazole) at 2 uL/min to recover the purified hexahistidine-tagged glycoprotein product as the elution fraction; the resin-bound flowthrough droplet is then discarded.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Miniaturized Scalable Arrayed CRISPR Screening in Primary Cells Enables
               Discovery at the Single Donor Resolution
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-13532-z
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-13532-z
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2025, Vol. 15, Article 29350
Platform     : DropGenie Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Electroporation System
               (48-site SBS-format cartridge, Tri-Drop Electroporation architecture,
               Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler, Assist Plus 8-channel liquid handler)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a next-generation digital microfluidics (DMF) electroporation
platform for high-throughput, low-input genome engineering in primary human cells.
The DropGenie system manipulates nanoliter- to microliter-scale droplets on a planar
electrode array using electrostatic actuation, enabling 48 independently programmable
reaction sites on a single SBS-format cartridge. The platform integrates with laboratory
automation (Assist Plus, Echo 655) and requires as few as 3,000 primary cells per edit
-- up to 100-fold fewer than conventional cuvette-based electroporation systems.

The protocol is divided into three functional arms validated in the paper:
  1. ARM 1 -- CRISPR-Cas9 RNP knockout (TRAC gene) in primary human T cells
              (Pan CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, and Regulatory T cells)
  2. ARM 2 -- Precise knock-in (GFP and anti-HER2 CAR) at the TRAC locus via
              homology-directed repair (HDR) using cssDNA and dsDNA templates
  3. ARM 3 -- Arrayed CRISPR-Cas9 exhaustion screen in chronically stimulated
              primary human CD4+ T cells; 45 targets, 192 edits total

The platform uses Tri-Drop Electroporation: two conductive DMFection Buffer droplets
flank a central cell-and-cargo droplet on the electrode array. Electrode actuation
forms a transient, low-current electroporation zone that delivers RNPs and mRNA while
minimising Joule heating, hydrolysis by-products, and viability-compromising effects
characteristic of cuvette-based systems.

A complete arm-to-readout workflow (activation, transfection, recovery, assay) is
described below. The BioScript file encodes ARM 1 and ARM 2 as sequential validation
arms followed by ARM 3 (the arrayed screen).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Cartridge format : SBS (Society for Biological Screening) standard format;
                   compatible with robotic liquid handlers.
Reaction sites   : 48 independently programmable electroporation sites per cartridge.
Droplet paradigm : Tri-Drop Electroporation -- two flanking DMFection Buffer droplets
                   bridge anode and cathode electrodes around a central cell droplet,
                   forming the electroporation zone without moving parts.
Guide deposition : sgRNAs pre-deposited dry onto the cartridge substrate in 40 nL spots
                   by Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler (Beckman Coulter), mixed with
                   Poly-L-glutamic acid (PGA) carrier and desiccated before assembly.
Cell loading     : Assist Plus 8-channel 125 uL Integra Voyager pipette; 100 uL per well.
Cell offloading  : Assist Plus into 96-well round-bottom plate post-transfection.
Downstream       : Flow cytometry (Attune NxT), Sanger sequencing (ICE analysis),
                   high-content imaging (Incucyte Live-Cell Analysis System),
                   sandwich ELISA (RayBiotech).

Electroporation parameters:
  T cell KO (Pan CD3+):  500 V, 3 ms, 2 pulses, 5 min pre-pulse incubation
  T cell KO (CD4+/Treg): 550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses, 5 min pre-pulse incubation
  T cell knock-in:        500 V, 2 ms or 4 ms, 2 pulses
  Exhaustion screen:      550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses


CELL TYPES
----------
- Primary human skeletal muscle myoblasts (Zen-Bio; adherent):
  Cultured in Skeletal Muscle Cell Growth Media (Zen-Bio); 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Used for EGFP mRNA transfection and MBNL1 knockout validation.
  Input: 3,000 cells per edit.

- Primary human Pan CD3+ T cells (suspension):
  Derived from PBMCs from fresh leukopak (Charles River Laboratories) by density
  gradient (Histopaque-1077) and negative selection (EasySep Human T Cell Enrichment Kit,
  STEMCELL Technologies). Cryopreserved until use.
  Used for TRAC KO and GFP/CAR knock-in experiments.
  Input: 10,000 cells per edit.

- Primary human CD4+ Helper T cells (AllCells; suspension):
  Negatively selected peripheral blood CD4+ T cells.
  Used for the arrayed CRISPR exhaustion screen.
  Input: 10,000 cells per edit.

- Primary human CD4+CD25+ Regulatory T cells (iQ Biosciences; suspension):
  Peripheral blood-derived; represent 5-10% of circulating CD4+ T cells.
  Used to demonstrate editing in rare T cell subsets.
  Input: 10,000 cells per edit.


PROTOCOL STEPS -- ARM 1: TRAC KNOCKOUT IN PRIMARY HUMAN T CELLS
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Step 1 | T Cell Activation (off-chip, 3 days)
  Cell type    : CD4+ Helper T cells (AllCells) or Pan CD3+ T cells
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media (RPMI 1640 + GlutaMax + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep)
  Cytokines    : 400 IU/mL IL-2 + 25 ng/mL IL-7 (Miltenyi) + 50 ng/mL IL-15 (Miltenyi)
  Activator    : ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28 T Cell Activator (STEMCELL) at 25 uL/mL
  Concentration: 1.25e6 cells/mL
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  Purpose      : Expand and activate T cells to permissive state for electroporation.

Step 2 | Cell Wash and Resuspension in Transfection Buffer
  Buffer       : DMFection Buffer (DropGenie proprietary)
  Transfection : 0.01% Surfactant F (ITW Reagents) in DMFection Buffer
  Concentration: 1.0e7 cells/mL in Transfection Buffer
  Purpose      : Remove culture media components that interfere with electroporation.
  Assessment   : Viability > 80% required (NucleoCounter NC-202, ChemoMetec).

Step 3 | sgRNA Pre-Deposition onto Cartridge Substrate
  Method       : Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler (Beckman Coulter)
  Volume       : 40 nL spots per site
  Carrier      : Poly-L-glutamic acid (PGA, Sigma Aldrich) at 100 mg/mL
  sgRNA stock  : 100 pmol/uL (T cells), 200 pmol/uL (myoblasts)
  Mix ratio    : Combined to final sgRNA concentration of 55.6 pmol/uL (T cells)
  Process      : Dry-deposit and desiccate before cartridge assembly.
  Guides       : TRAC sgRNA (ARM 1); ExhaustionTarget sgRNAs (ARM 3; 45 targets)

Step 4 | Cartridge Loading (cells + Cas9 RNP)
  Cells loaded : 10,000 per edit (concentration 1.0e7 cells/mL, 100 uL per well)
  SpCas9       : 0.42 pmol per edit (final concentration 42 pmol in 100 uL, Aldevron)
  sgRNA        : 2.1 pmol per edit (pre-deposited dry on substrate)
  Loading tool : Assist Plus 8-channel 125 uL Integra Voyager pipette
  Incubation   : 5 min at room temperature (pre-pulse; abstraced as heat 25 C, 5 min)
  Note         : RNP complexes form in situ on the cartridge substrate during incubation.

Step 5 | Electroporation (Tri-Drop; 550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses)
  Method       : Tri-Drop Electroporation on DropGenie electrode array.
                 Two conductive DMFection Buffer droplets flank the central cell droplet.
                 Electrode actuation (550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses) delivers RNP cargo.
  Parameters   : 550 V, 2 ms pulse duration, 2 pulses (CD4+ / Treg arm)
                 500 V, 3 ms pulse duration, 2 pulses (Pan CD3+ arm)
  Dead volume  : Cartridge dead volume accounted for in total cell input calculation.

Step 6 | Offload and Post-KO Culture (3 days)
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 200 IU/mL IL-2
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  Offload tool : Assist Plus into 96-well plate

Step 7 | Knockout Detection (flow cytometry)
  Staining     : Anti-TCR alpha/beta antibody (surface); Ghost Dye Violet 510 (viability)
  Instrument   : Attune NxT Flow Cytometer (Thermo Fisher)
  Gating       : Live > Singlets > CD4+ or CD8+ > TCR alpha/beta-negative
  Detection    : knockoutDetection module (BioScript abstraction)
  Results      : CD4+ TRAC KO: 90.41% +/- 3.27; CD8+ TRAC KO: 91.87% +/- 3.13
                 Viability: 97.23% +/- 0.28 (TRAC RNP), 97.83% +/- 0.09 (NTC RNP)
  Branch       : knockoutSignal > 0  -> ARM 2 proceeds (dispose)
                 knockoutSignal <= 0 -> drain (insufficient KO)
  Regulatory T cells: 76.78% +/- 8.62 TCR KO; viability 97.22% +/- 0.89


PROTOCOL STEPS -- ARM 2: GFP KNOCK-IN AT TRAC LOCUS (HDR)
-----------------------------------------------------------

Step 8 | T Cell Activation (Dynabead protocol, separate donor)
  Cells        : Pan CD3+ T cells (separate leukopak donor)
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 200 IU/mL IL-2 + 10 ng/mL IL-7 + 5 ng/mL IL-15
  Activator    : Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28 (Gibco), bead:cell ratio 2:5
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate, 2.5e5 cells/mL
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  Pre-loading  : Dynabeads removed magnetically before cartridge loading.

Step 9 | RNP Assembly (on ice, 20 min)
  sgRNA        : 110 pmol TRAC sgRNA
  SpCas9       : 33 pmol SpCas9 (Aldevron)
  Complexing   : Mix on ice for 20 min (IR: 4 C, 1200.0 SECOND)
  Per edit     : 1.1 pmol sgRNA, 0.33 pmol Cas9

Step 10 | Cartridge Loading (cells + RNP + cssDNA template)
  Cells        : 10,000 per edit (1.0e7 cells/mL, 100 uL per well)
  Template     : GFP cssDNA (Full Circles Therapeutics); 4 kb circular single-stranded DNA
  Concentrations tested: 0.03 ug and 0.06 ug per edit
  Purpose      : cssDNA provides improved genomic integration efficiency vs dsDNA and
                 avoids immunogenic response associated with linear dsDNA.

Step 11 | Electroporation (500 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses)
  Parameters   : 500 V, 2 ms pulse duration, 2 pulses
                 Also tested: 500 V, 4 ms, 2 pulses

Step 12 | Offload and 10-day Expansion
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 300 IU/mL IL-2
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate
  Duration     : 10 days at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 14400 min; IR: 864000.0 SECOND)

Step 13 | GFP Knock-In Detection (flow cytometry + fluorescence microscopy)
  Flow         : GFP positivity gating + TRAC KO co-stain (Attune NxT)
  Microscopy   : EVOS Cell Imaging System (Thermo Fisher), Day 10
  Detection    : knockInDetection module (BioScript abstraction)
  Results      : 52.37% +/- 9.70 GFP+ cells at 0.03 ug / 500V / 2ms / 2 pulses
                 41.14% +/- 9.45 at 0.06 ug / 500V / 2ms / 2 pulses
                 Significantly higher than no-template (11.21% +/- 2.83) and
                 off-chip controls (10.62% +/- 4.49) (p < 0.0001)
  Branch       : knockInSignal > 0  -> ARM 3 proceeds (dispose)
                 knockInSignal <= 0 -> drain

Anti-HER2 CAR-T generation (additional validation, same ARM 2 workflow):
  Template     : 3 kb dsDNA encoding anti-HER2 CAR (Integrated DNA Technologies);
                 flanked by TRAC-targeting homology arms.
  Detection    : Protein L staining (GenScript, 1:300 in 4% BSA) + CD3 co-stain
  Results      : HER2 CAR expression up to 40% (average 27.03%); viability > 55%
                 No dose-dependent differences across template concentrations.


PROTOCOL STEPS -- ARM 3: ARRAYED CRISPR EXHAUSTION SCREEN
----------------------------------------------------------

Step 14 | CD4+ T Cell Activation (screen donor)
  Cells        : CD4+ Helper T cells (AllCells), 1.25e6 cells/mL
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 400 IU/mL IL-2 + 25 ng/mL IL-7 + 50 ng/mL IL-15
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)

Step 15 | Guide Pre-Deposition for 45-Target Screen
  Tool         : Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler
  Volume       : 40 nL per site
  Targets      : 45 candidate exhaustion regulators; 4 replicates each = 180 edits
                 + NTC and off-chip controls = 192 total edits (4 cartridge runs)
  Targets include (top hits): SIN3A, PAF1, PRDM1, SETBP1, STAT1, LAG3, ID2, TOX,
                              NR4A1, NR4A2, DNMT3A, EZH2, FOXO1, BATF, TCF7,
                              and 30 additional exhaustion-associated genes.

Step 16 | Cartridge Loading (screen arm)
  Cells        : 10,000 per edit (1.0e7 cells/mL, 100 uL per well)
  SpCas9       : 1 pmol per edit
  sgRNA        : 2 pmol per edit (pre-deposited dry)
  Incubation   : 5 min at room temperature (IR: 25 C, 300 SECOND)
  Vs. conventional: 500,000 cells, 100 pmol Cas9, 50 pmol sgRNA per edit
  Reduction    : 50x fewer cells, ~100x less Cas9, ~25x less sgRNA (Fig. 3G)

Step 17 | Electroporation (550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses)
  Parameters   : 550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses (CD4+ T cell optimised parameters)

Step 18 | Post-KO Recovery (3 days)
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 200 IU/mL IL-2
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)

Step 19 | Chronic Exhaustion Induction (9 cycles x 3 days = Days 3-28)
  Protocol     : ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28 T Cell Activator (25 uL/mL) +
                 10 IU/mL IL-2 in 50 uL Basal T Cell Media.
                 Media changed every 3 days with fresh stimulation mix.
  Cycles       : 8 x 3-day cycles (IR: 259200.0 SECOND each = 3 days at 37 C)
                 + 1 final 48 h cycle (IR: 172800.0 SECOND = 2 days at 37 C)
  Total        : 9 cycles covering Days 3-28 of chronic stimulation
  BioScript    : Loop unrolled (no loop primitive in lilott8/BioScript); 9 sequential
                 mix + heat pairs (stimCells_c1 through stimCells_c9).
  Purpose      : Recapitulate progressive T cell dysfunction (gradual exhaustion in vivo
                 model); avoids acute activation-induced cell death.

Step 20 | LAG-3 Staining (exhaustion phenotype readout)
  Stain        : PE-LAG3 (BioLegend) + Ghost Dye Violet 510 + CD4 co-stain
  Incubation   : 20 min in Flow Cytometry Buffer at 4 C in dark
  Readout      : % LAG3-negative CD4+ T cells (exhaustion escape frequency)
  Detection    : exhaustionPhenotypeDetection module (BioScript abstraction)
  Gating       : Live > Singlets > CD4+ > LAG3-
  Branch       : screenSignal > 0  -> escape hit confirmed (dispose stainedForFACS)
                 screenSignal <= 0 -> no rescue (drain)

Step 21 | Cytokine Secretion Readout (ELISA)
  Collection   : Supernatants collected Day 28 (48 h after final re-stimulation)
  Stored       : -80 C until processing
  Kits         : TNFalpha and IFNgamma sandwich ELISA (RayBiotech)
  Dilution     : 3.84x or 2.5x in Assay Diluent B (RayBiotech)
  Curve fit    : 4-Parameter Logistic (4PL) regression for concentration interpolation
  Normalisation: Background-subtracted using media-only (MO) control; normalised to
                 cell count by flow cytometry and adjusted for dilution factor.
  Detection    : cytokineDetection module (BioScript abstraction; detect on screenSignal)

Step 22 | Composite Exhaustion Escape Scoring (off-chip, terminal)
  Metric       : z-score normalized sum of: IFNgamma + TNFalpha + % LAG3-negative CD4+ cells
  Exclusions   : Viability < 70% or CD4+ frequency < 90% deprioritised (confounders)
  Top hits     : SIN3A, PAF1, PRDM1, SETBP1, STAT1 (radar plot; Fig. 3F)
  Output       : Ranked target list; radar plots per top hit across all three axes.

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first reported use of digital microfluidics (DMF) for
combinatorial chemical synthesis. The method performs thioacid-aziridine ligation of
peptidomimetics and their subsequent desulfurization entirely on-chip, with an integrated
magnetic separation step to remove Raney Nickel (RaNi) catalyst from reaction products.
The approach represents a greater than 1000-fold reduction in reagent consumption compared
to macroscale bench synthesis (microlitres vs millilitres) and requires no stir bars,
rotary evaporators, or traditional gloveboxes.

The protocol is divided into two functional parts:
  PART 1 (Steps 1-4, 16 total steps): Combinatorial thioacid-aziridine ligation
    producing 4 peptidomimetic products (A1-B1, A1-B2, A2-B1, A2-B2) under N2
    atmosphere at room temperature for 1 hour in methanol.
  PART 2 (Steps 5-8, 16 total steps): On-chip desulfurization using Raney Nickel
    catalyst at room temperature for 15 minutes, followed by magnetic immobilisation
    of RaNi and solvent evaporation to isolate 4 desulfurized analogues.

Characterisation: ESI-MS (all 8 products, triplicate) and 1H NMR (desulfurized A1-B1,
compared to macroscale synthesis; spectra nearly identical).

Title        : Microfluidic Cell Retention Device for Perfusion of Mammalian Suspension Culture
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-06949-8
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-06949-8
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2017, Vol. 7, Article 6703
Platform     : Inertial microfluidic spiral channel (PDMS) coupled to stirred perfusion bioreactor


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a novel membrane-less cell retention device based on inertial sorting
for continuous perfusion culture of suspended mammalian CHO cells. The spiral microchannel
with trapezoidal cross-section focuses CHO cells (17.7 +/- 2.5 um diameter) near the inner
wall of the channel using a combination of shear gradient-induced and wall-induced lift forces
(F_L proportional to a^4) and Dean drag forces (F_D proportional to a) generated by
counter-rotating Dean vortices in the curved channel geometry. Cells are retained through the
inner outlet (retentate, recycled to bioreactor), while the cell-limited harvest stream exits
through the outer outlet (permeate, collected as IgG1-containing product).

The device eliminates membrane fouling, product retention, and filter replacement contamination
risks associated with conventional tangential flow filtration (TFF) and alternating tangential
flow filtration (ATF) hollow-fiber membrane systems. As a passive operation requiring no active
field (no electric field, no acoustic wave), it is simple, low-maintenance, and biocompatible.
IgG1 recovery exceeds 99% because the smallest channel dimension (~100 um) is far larger than
any antibody molecule, allowing free passage of product into the harvest stream.

Three sequential perfusion cultures of CHO-DG44 cells (IgG1 against CD40 ligand) were run
for 18-25 days each in a 350 mL lab-scale bioreactor at >20 million cells/mL, demonstrating
cell viability >97% throughout and a total IgG1 yield of 263 mg per run.

               Channel dimensions (~100 um) within limit of injection-moulding (polystyrene).
Fabrication  : Standard soft lithography. Molds designed in Rhinoceros (McNeel North America);
               aluminum molds fabricated by micromachining (Whits Technologies, Singapore).
               PDMS poured into molds; cured at 150 C for 15 min on hotplate. Bonded to flat
               glass slide (260230, Ted Pella) or thin PDMS layer (<500 um) by oxygen plasma
               treatment (Harrick Plasma). Cured at 95 C overnight. Silicone tubings inserted
               (Masterflex, Cole-Parmer). Clamped with binder clips for robust operation.

Single spiral channel:
  Width          : 600 um
  Inner depth    : 80 um
  Outer depth    : 130 um
  Loops          : 8
  Volume         : 28 uL
  Footprint      : 26 x 26 mm
  Outlet width   : 300 um (single channel)

Parallel configuration (used for perfusion cultures):
  Channels per layer : 4 spiral channels combined in single layer
  Inner outlet width : 520 um (enlarged for parallel configuration)
  Perfusion rate     : ~700 mL/day (4-spiral single layer at 1 mL/min input)

Modified high-density channel (Fig. 2d, for 30-40e6 cells/mL):
  Width          : 1000 um
  Inner depth    : 260 um
  Outer depth    : 80 um
  Flow rate      : 4 mL/min input; R_OO/R_IO = 1:0.1

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic RT-qPCR Platform for Multiplex Respiratory Pathogen Detection

Overview: A multi-target RT-qPCR assay protocol executed on a digital microfluidic platform capable of simultaneously dispensing, merging, and amplifying samples to identify up to 11 pathogens from single specimens.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Extracted RNA/DNA Sample (nasal or throat swab nucleic acid extract, 5 uL)
  - RNase-Free Water (6.25 uL)
  - 2x One Step Q Probe Mix (RT-qPCR master mix component, 12.5 uL)
  - One Step Q Probe Enzyme Mix (reverse transcriptase/polymerase enzyme mix, 1.25 uL)
  - 12 Dried Primer-Probe Sets, pre-stored and dehydrated at individual reaction spots on-chip, one per target: MP, CP, SP, RSVA, ADV, HKU1, 229E, HMPV, N (SARS-CoV-2), ORF1ab (SARS-CoV-2), FLUA, FLUB

STEPS:
1. Master Mix Preparation: Dispense 5 uL RNA/DNA sample, 6.25 uL RNase-free water, 12.5 uL 2x One Step Q Probe Mix, and 1.25 uL One Step Q Probe Enzyme Mix; combine sequentially into a single 25 uL RT-qPCR amplification master mix.
2. Droplet Splitting to Reaction Spots: Transport and split the master mix (2 uL per spot) onto each of the 12 on-chip reaction spots, rehydrating the pre-stored dried primer-probe set at each spot to form 12 independent reaction mixtures (one per pathogen target).
3. Reverse Transcription: Heat each of the 12 reaction mixtures at 50 C for 15 min to reverse-transcribe viral/bacterial RNA into cDNA.
4. Initial Denaturation: Heat each of the 12 reaction mixtures at 95 C for 30 s.
5. Thermal Cycling (Amplification): For each of the 12 reaction mixtures independently, cycle 45 times through 95 C for 10 s (denaturation) then 60 C for 30 s (annealing/extension), with real-time fluorescence acquisition during the anneal/extend step of each cycle.
6. Detection: Acquire the real-time fluorescence signal (delta Rn) from each of the 12 reaction spots over the amplification run; a Ct value is computed per spot from the cycle at which fluorescence crosses ten times the standard deviation above the mean baseline (cycles 3-15), and each spot's reading is compared against its corresponding detection-limit threshold to call the sample positive or negative for that target.
7. Disposal: Dispose of each of the 12 analyzed reaction droplets after the amplification/detection run completes.

INTERPRETATION: Successful multiplex detection is confirmed by pathogen-specific amplification curves crossing threshold within 45 cycles for true positives, no amplification (or amplification only after 45 cycles) for true negatives, and reported diagnostic performance (versus off-chip benchtop RT-qPCR) of TPR 93.33%, TNR 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 99.56%, ACC 99.85% (on the plasmid/clinical validation panel), and a Kappa value of 0.963, supporting use of the DMF RT-qPCR platform for field and point-of-care respiratory pathogen screening in medical resource-limited settings.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics for Aerosol Impaction, Extraction, and Colorimetric Detection of Inorganic Ions (Sulfate, Nitrate, Ammonium)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Ambient/Laboratory-Generated Aerosol Sample (impacted directly onto the digital microfluidic chip surface via an integrated 5-nozzle inertial impactor, 1 L/min air flow)
  - Distilled Water (sub-microliter scanning/extraction droplet, ~0.5 uL)
  - Methylthymol Blue (MTB) - Barium Reagent (sulfate colorimetric assay, competitive complexation, detected at 608 nm)
  - Ammonium Colorimetric Reagent (detected at 365 nm)
  - Nitrate Colorimetric Reagent (acidic reagent, detected at 540 nm)
  - Sulfate/Ammonium/Nitrate Liquid Standards (six concentrations each, dispensed from on-chip reservoirs to build calibration curves)

STEPS:
1. Aerosol Collection: Air is drawn through five inertial-impactor nozzles (0.24 mm diameter, 1 L/min total flow) built into the chip's top plate, depositing particles >100 nm in diameter directly onto the CYTOP-coated actuation electrodes of the bottom plate (collection efficiency >95% for particles >100 nm).
2. Extraction: After the air flow is stopped, a sub-microliter distilled-water droplet is dispensed from an on-chip reservoir in oil, actuated through the oil/air interface, and scanned twice across the five-electrode impaction area to fully dissolve the deposited aerosol into a single concentrated extract droplet.
3. Sulfate Calibration: Six standard sulfate concentrations are sequentially dispensed and each mixed with the MTB-Ba reagent; the resulting droplet is actuated between two horizontal optical fibers and absorbance is measured at 608 nm to build a calibration curve (LOD ~11 ppm).
4. Sulfate Sample Measurement: The aerosol extract droplet is mixed with the MTB-Ba reagent and absorbance is measured at 608 nm; the mixed droplet is then discarded.
5. Ammonium Calibration: Six standard ammonium concentrations are sequentially dispensed and each mixed with the ammonium reagent; absorbance is measured at 365 nm to build a calibration curve (LOD ~0.256 ppm).
6. Ammonium Sample Measurement: The aerosol extract droplet is mixed with the ammonium reagent and absorbance is measured at 365 nm; the mixed droplet is then discarded.
7. Nitrate Calibration (unstable): Six standard nitrate concentrations are sequentially dispensed and each mixed with the acidic nitrate reagent; because a precipitate forms over the first 3-4 minutes, droplets are held ~150 s post-mixing before absorbance is measured at 540 nm (nonzero y-intercept observed, indicating reduced sensitivity).
8. Nitrate Sample Measurement: The aerosol extract droplet is mixed with the nitrate reagent, held 150 s, and absorbance is measured at 540 nm; the mixed droplet is then discarded, and the extract droplet itself is discarded once all three assays are complete.

INTERPRETATION: Successful ion quantification is confirmed by linear calibration curves (R^2 ~0.95-0.98) for sulfate and ammonium comparable to off-chip Tecan plate-reader results, on-chip limits of detection of 11 ppm (sulfate) and 0.256 ppm (ammonium) sufficient for converted air-concentration LODs of 0.275 ug/m3 and 6.5 ng/m3 respectively at 1 L/min for 1 h sampling, negligible cross-ion interference, and an unresolved precipitate-driven artifact that prevents stable nitrate quantification on-chip despite a linear off-chip response.

====================

Title        : Single-Cell Chemoproteomics Identifies Metastatic Activity Signatures in Breast Cancer
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/epdf/10.1126/sciadv.adp2622
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adp2622
Journal      : Science Advances, 2024, Vol. 10, Article eadp2622
Authors      : Kavya Smitha Pillai, Olivia Laxton, Gang Li, Jing Lin, Olga Karginova,
               Rita Nanda, Olufunmilayo I. Olopade, Savaş Tay, Raymond E. Moellering
Platform     : Single-Cell Activity-Dependent Proximity Ligation (scADPL) coupled to
               valve-based push-up PDMS microfluidic chip with five-chamber assay units


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated chemoproteomic microfluidic platform, scADPL, for
multiplexed endogenous protein activity measurements at single-cell resolution. Unlike
mRNA or bulk protein abundance methods, scADPL directly reports on the active subpopulation
of the proteome, capturing posttranslational regulation invisible to genomic or transcriptomic
approaches.

The platform integrates two components:
  1. Activity-based chemical probes (Cat-Bio for cathepsins; FP-Bio for serine hydrolases)
     that covalently label the active sites of target enzyme families in live cells.
  2. Activity-Dependent Proximity Ligation (ADPL) chemistry that converts probe-protein
     labelling events into amplifiable, barcoded oligonucleotide amplicons, quantified
     by qPCR or ddPCR.

These are coupled to a valve-based PDMS microfluidic chip that automates:
  (i)  Single-cell isolation and brightfield/fluorescence imaging
  (ii) Nanoliter-volume manipulation to achieve optimal proteome concentrations for ADPL
  (iii) Dead volume minimisation for maximum sensitivity and reproducibility

The protocol is organised into four experimental phases:
  PHASE 1 : Single-plex validation of CTSL activity (ddPCR) and NCEH1 target specificity
            (qPCR + JW480 inhibitor) in SKOV3 single cells
  PHASE 2 : Multiplexed Ag-6 panel (NCEH1, MGLL, CTSL, FAAH, CTSB, uPA) profiling in
            SKOV3 single cells with reproducibility and bulk sADPL concordance validation
  PHASE 3 : Heterogeneity profiling across cell lines (HEK293T vs SKOV3;
            aggressive SKOV3 vs non-aggressive OVCAR3 ovarian cancer)
  PHASE 4 : Patient-derived organoid (PDO) profiling from TNBC primary and metastatic
            tumours (between-patient) and ER+ pleural effusion / lymph node (within-patient)

Key quantitative outcomes:
  - sADPL detection threshold: 10 pg whole proteome; single HeLa cell ~2 ng total protein
  - Average scADPL CTSL signal: 54-fold above vehicle-only control (ddPCR)
  - Average scADPL NCEH1 signal: ~64-fold above vehicle-only control (qPCR)
  - JW480 (selective NCEH1 inhibitor, 2 uM): >90% NCEH1 signal inhibition;
    no significant effect on remaining five Ag-6 targets
  - Multiplexed Ag-6 reproducibility (day 1 vs day 2): Pearson r = 0.9981
  - scADPL vs bulk sADPL correlation: Pearson r = 0.9288
  - PCA of SKOV3 vs OVCAR3 scADPL profiles: PC1 = 84.67%, PC2 = 8.37%


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type       : Valve-based push-up PDMS microfluidic chip

CHEMICAL PROBES AND DETECTION CHEMISTRY
-----------------------------------------

Activity Probes (applied off-chip to live cells before loading):

    Concentration  : 5 uM

    Targets        : CTSL (cathepsin L), CTSB (cathepsin B)
    Chemistry      : Biotin-tagged covalent cysteine protease probe

  FP-Bio (serine hydrolase family-wide):
    Concentration  : 2 uM
    Incubation     : 30 min at 37 C in complete media
    Targets        : NCEH1, MGLL, FAAH, uPA
    Chemistry      : Fluorophosphonate biotin; labels active-site serine covalently

ADPL Detection Reagents (added on-chip at Chamber IV):
  Streptavidin-oligo conjugate (SA-oligo) : 4000 pM; binds biotin tag on probe-protein complex
  Antibody-oligo conjugate (ab-oligo)     : 200 pM per target; six antibodies for Ag-6 panel

  Antibodies used:
    NCEH1 : NCEH1 polyclonal antibody (in-house; refs 33, 36)
    CTSB  : Abcam ab58802
    FAAH  : Abcam ab54615
    MGLL  : Abcam no. 24701
    uPA   : Abcam no. 24121
    CTSL  : R&D Systems AF952-SP
    RPE   : Abcam no. 34721 (spike-in control antibody)

Proximity Ligation (Chamber V):
  Splint oligonucleotide : 100 nM; bridges SA-oligo and ab-oligo when both bound to

  Ampligase              : 0.05 U (Lucigen E0001-5D3); seals nick in ligation buffer
  Ligation buffer        : 0.3 mM NAD+, 10 mM DTT, 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.3,

Lysis Buffer (MCP):

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

PHASE 1 | Single-Plex Validation

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents    : PBS, Pluronics F-127
  Operation   : mix 5 min (300 s)
  Purpose     : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS; passivates PDMS channel surfaces,
                reduces non-specific cell adhesion before loading

Step 2 | Off-Chip Probe Labelling (SKOV3, single-plex)
  Cat-Bio arm : SKOV3 + Cat-Bio 5 uM; mix 5 s; heat 37 C, 120 min (7200 s)
  FP-Bio arm  : SKOV3 + FP-Bio 2 uM; mix 5 s; heat 37 C, 30 min (1800 s)
  Wash        : PBS wash after labelling; resuspend 50,000-100,000 cells/mL in PBS

Step 3 | On-Chip Single-Cell Trapping (Chamber II)
  Operation   : mix 2 s (abstracts pressure-driven hydrodynamic single-cell capture)
  Notes       : One cell captured per assay chamber; RPE spike-in dispensed at this stage

Step 4 | On-Chip Cell Lysis (Chamber III)
  Operation   : MCP lysis buffer added; mix 60 s; RPE spike added; mix 5 s
  Notes       : Nanoliter dead volume minimised vs bulk sADPL for maximum sensitivity

Step 5 | On-Chip Proximity Barcoding (Chamber IV)
  Operation   : SA-oligo (4000 pM) + ab-oligo (200 pM) premixed 5 s; added to lysate;
                mix 120 s; heat 25 C, 120 min (7200 s)
  Notes       : Both recognition elements bind same probe-protein complex in proximity

Step 6 | On-Chip Proximity Ligation (Chamber V)
  Operation   : Splint oligo added; mix 2 s; ligation buffer added; mix 2 s;
                heat 40 C, 45 min (2700 s)
  Product     : Ligated barcoded amplicons

Step 7 | Off-Chip Amplicon Retrieval and Preamplification
  Flush       : 9 uL water flush off-chip
  Preamplify  : 11 uL reaction (2.5x buffer, 100 nM primers, 200 uM dNTPs,
                9 U Phusion high-fidelity DNA polymerase; NEB M0503L); 18 cycles
  IR abstraction: mix 18m (1080.0 SECOND in IR; cycle count not supported by compiler)

Step 8 | CTSL Detection by ddPCR
  Module      : ddPCRQuantification
  Duration    : 30 s detection window
  Expected    : 54-fold above vehicle-only control (Cat-Bio vs DMSO; Fig. 1B; n=2)
  QC gate     : ctslSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2); ctslSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB3)

Step 9 | NCEH1 Specificity Validation: JW480 Pre-Treatment
  Cells       : SKOV3; JW480 2 uM pre-treatment 30 min at 37 C (1800 s)
  Probe       : FP-Bio 2 uM, 30 min at 37 C (1800 s)
  On-chip     : Full scADPL workflow (trap -> lyse -> barcode -> ligate -> preamplify)
  Module      : qPCRQuantification (selected over ddPCR from this step forward;
                higher SNR; amenable to multiplexing)
  Expected    : >90% NCEH1-specific signal suppression vs uninhibited control;
                no significant effect on other five Ag-6 targets (Fig. 1C, Fig. 2B)
  QC gate     : nceh1Signal > 0 -> dispose (BB5); nceh1Signal <= 0 -> drain (BB6)


PHASE 2 | Multiplexed Ag-6 Panel (SKOV3, n=8 single cells per condition)

Step 10 | Dual-Probe Pulse Labelling
  Cells       : SKOV3; FP-Bio 2 uM 30 min at 37 C; then Cat-Bio 5 uM added,
                additional 90 min at 37 C (both probes present for final 30 min overlap)
  IR          : labelledFP_Ag6 heat 1800 s; labelledDual heat 5400 s at 37 C

Step 11 | On-Chip Multiplexed scADPL
  Same chamber-by-chamber workflow as Steps 3-7 above.
  Six orthogonal Taqman barcode channels in forward primer sequences enable
  simultaneous target-specific qPCR quantification from the same single-cell lysate.
  All six measurements per isolated cell (n=8 cells; Fig. 2A).

Step 12 | Six-Channel qPCR Quantification
  Instrument  : CFX384 Real-Time System (Bio-Rad); 384-well plates
  Mix         : Luna Universal Probe qPCR Master Mix; 0.9 uM primers, 0.45 uM Taqman probe
  Module      : qPCRQuantification; 30 s detection window
  Expected fold-changes vs no-probe DMSO:
    NCEH1 : >20-fold   MGLL : >20-fold   CTSL : >20-fold
    FAAH  : detectable  CTSB : detectable  uPA  : detectable
  QC gate : ag6Signal > 0 -> dispose (BB8); ag6Signal <= 0 -> drain (BB9)


PHASE 3 | Cell-Line Heterogeneity Profiling

Step 13 | Dual-Probe Labelling of HEK293T and OVCAR3
  HEK293T and OVCAR3 each labelled identically to Step 10.
  Processed on separate chip runs; n > 10 single cells per target per cell line.

Step 14 | On-Chip scADPL for HEK293T and OVCAR3
  Full scADPL workflow (Steps 3-7) for each cell line independently.

Step 15 | qPCR + Fluorescence Imaging Readout; PCA Analysis
  Module      : fluorescenceImaging (abstracts PCA + heatmap analysis; 30 s)
  Normalisation:
    Fig. 3A   : Activity normalised to HEK293T reference population
    Fig. 3B   : Activity normalised to OVCAR3 reference population
    Both      : RPE internal control per cell
  Results:
    SKOV3 vs HEK293T : All six Ag-6 targets significantly higher in SKOV3
                       (p <= 0.0001 to 0.03; Fig. 3A)
    SKOV3 vs OVCAR3  : Five of six targets significant; NCEH1 highest fold-change (Fig. 3B)
    mRNA vs activity : FAAH and CTSB show discordant mRNA vs protein activity profiles
                       (Fig. 3C; Human Protein Atlas mRNA data)
    PCA              : SKOV3 vs OVCAR3 resolved; PC1 = 84.67%, PC2 = 8.37% (Fig. 3F)
    Heatmaps         : Per-cell Z-score activity profiles reveal intra-population
                       heterogeneity across all six Ag-6 targets (Fig. 3D/E)
  QC gate : heteroSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB11); heteroSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB12)


PHASE 4 | Patient-Derived Organoid Profiling

Step 16 | PDO Preparation and Anti-CD45-FITC Immune Cell Staining
  Protocol    : IRB 16352A; fresh core biopsy or pleural effusion specimens
                enzymatically digested (1 h for biopsy) or centrifuged (450g, 10 min
                for pleural effusion); Matrigel 24-well culture to 50-100 mm;
                Dispase 37 C 20 min -> TrypLE 37 C 5-10 min -> 2% FBS stop ->
                40 mm strainer -> 450g 5 min -> 500 uL BC PDO media on ice
  Staining    : FITC-conjugated anti-CD45 antibody; 30 min on ice (4 C, 1800 s)
  Purpose     : CD45+ immune cells identified by on-chip FITC imaging and excluded
                from scADPL analysis; only CD45-FITC-negative tumour cells processed
                (fig. S6 in paper)

Step 17 | Dual-Probe Labelling of PDO Single-Cell Suspension
  Same as Step 10: FP-Bio 30 min at 37 C (1800 s);
  Cat-Bio added, 90 min at 37 C (5400 s)

Step 18 | On-Chip Trapping with Tumour-Cell Imaging Gate
  Trap        : mix 2 s (hydrodynamic capture)
  Imaging QC  : detect fluorescenceImaging 10 s; confirms FITC-negative (tumour) cell
                in chamber before proceeding to lysis

Step 19 | On-Chip scADPL for PDO Tumour Single Cells
  Full scADPL workflow: lyse 60 s -> RPE spike 5 s -> barcode 7200 s at 25 C ->
  ligate 2700 s at 40 C -> preamplify 1080 s

Step 20 | Ag-6 qPCR on PDO Single Cells
  Module      : qPCRQuantification; 30 s
  Normalisation: Z-scores calculated within each target, normalised to:
    TNBC      : PDO1 (primary tumour reference)
    ER+       : Lymph node metastasis reference
    Both      : RPE spike-in per cell
  Results:
    TNBC PDOs : Higher Ag-6 in all metastatic vs primary tumours;
                highest activity in liver metastases (PDO3, PDO4; Fig. 4C)
    ER+ PDOs  : Highest Ag-6 in pleural effusion cells, concordant with MDA-MB-231
                (pleural-derived cell line); left pleural (early stage) shows greater
                intertarget heterogeneity and elevated CTSL; right pleural (later stage)
                shows general Ag-6 increase, decreased variability; lymph node shows
                general decrease in Ag-6 activity (Fig. 4D/E)
    scADPL vs bulk sADPL: concordant in ER+ PDO samples (Fig. 4D)
    General model: Ag-6 activity peaks in cells undergoing EMT or early metastasis;
                   slightly decreases in established metastatic lesions (Fig. 4F)
  QC gate : pdoSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB14, pdoWithQPCR + pdoTumourSignal);
            pdoSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB15)
  Terminal  : dispose(pdoSignal) -> BB16 (NOP; experiment ends)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Ultrasensitive Digital Quantification of Cytokines and Bacteria Predicts Septic Shock Outcomes
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-16124-9
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-16124-9
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2020, Vol. 11, Article 2607
Platform     : Digital proximity ligation assay (dPLA) + droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) on Bio-Rad QX200


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a combined dPLA and ddPCR pipeline for simultaneous femtomolar-sensitivity
quantification of host cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-alpha) and bacterial DNA biomarkers (gram-negative
(GN) 16S rRNA gene, gram-positive (GP) 16S rRNA gene, and the antibiotic-resistance gene blaTEM)
from human biological samples (BALF and plasma). The method overcomes the limitations of conventional
ELISA (poor sensitivity, incompatibility with simultaneous nucleic acid measurement) by combining
proximity ligation assay (PLA) with droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), achieving sub-femtomolar protein
detection and single-copy DNA resolution.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. DNA extraction (QIAamp cador Pathogen Mini Kit) from human BALF or plasma
  2. dPLA for IL-6 and TNF-alpha quantification with ddPCR readout
  3. Triplex ddPCR for simultaneous GN + GP + blaTEM quantification

Results are applied to two clinical cohorts:
  - Cohort 1 (BALF): 23 asthma patients vs 11 healthy subjects
    Finding: elevated GN bacteria and IL-6 in asthma vs healthy (p<0.01 and p<0.01)
  - Cohort 2 (Plasma/ICU): 32 septic shock patients at time points t1 and t2 (t3 for Group B)
    Finding: temporal changes in IL-6 and GN bacteria predict mortality; decision-tree
    classifier achieves >90% accuracy using only t1 measurements of GN and TNF-alpha

Assay performance outperforms many commercial ELISA kits:
  IL-6 LOD  : 0.02 pg/mL (0.73 fM) in BALF; 0.84 pg/mL (40 fM) in plasma (SDB-II)
  TNF-alpha LOD : 0.08 pg/mL in both BALF and plasma (HMB)
  GN LOD    : 0.06 CPN/uL (0.09 aM); GP LOD: 0.06 CPN/uL (0.09 aM)
  blaTEM LOD: 0.9 CPN/uL (1.57 aM); CV as low as 1.3%; stable >100 days

SAMPLE COHORTS
--------------

Cohort 1 — BALF (Asthma vs Healthy):
  Asthma (n=23): Average age 46 [38-53]; 53% female; 65% white, 30% black, 4% other.
                 Criteria: EPR 3 Guidelines on Asthma. Bronchoscopy within 4 weeks of visit.
  Healthy (n=11): No respiratory medication; good health.
  IRB: University of Chicago; written informed consent.

Cohort 2 — Plasma/ICU (Septic Shock):
  Protocol IRB: 18-1163 (University of Chicago); Declaration of Helsinki.
  Total (n=32): Adults >18 y; Medical ICU; vasoactive medication; suspected infection;
                enrolled within first 24h of Sepsis-3 shock diagnosis.
  Blood collection: 30 mL sodium citrate tubes; plasma isolated within 2h (500 g, 15 min);
                    stored at -80 C. All patients received antibiotics prior to collection.
  Time points:
    t1 = within first 24h of diagnosis (enrollment)
    t2 = 24-48h after t1 (all patients)
    t3 = upon resolution of septic shock (Group B only)
  Clinical scores: APACHE-II and SOFA on day of enrollment.
  Patient groups:
    Group A (n=7):  Early recovery. Shock resolved within 48h (no vasopressors; MAP >65 mmHg).
                    Samples at t1 and t2.
    Group B (n=13): Late recovery. Shock resolved after 48h.
                    Samples at t1, t2, and t3.
    Group C (n=12): Death. Never resolved shock. Died in ICU on vasopressors.
                    Samples at t1 and t2.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | DNA Extraction from Human Sample
  Input          : 100 uL human plasma or BALF
  Kit            : QIAamp cador Pathogen Mini Kit (Qiagen #54104)
  Protocol       :
    1. Combine 100 uL sample + 100 uL PBS + 20 uL proteinase K
    2. Add 100 uL buffer VXL; incubate RT for 15 min
    3. Add 350 uL buffer ACB; mix thoroughly
    4. Load lysate to QIAamp Mini column; centrifuge 6000 g, 1 min
    5. Wash with AW1 buffer; centrifuge 6000 g, 1 min
    6. Wash with AW2 buffer; centrifuge 6000 g, 1 min
    7. Add 100 uL AVE elution buffer; incubate 1 min; centrifuge 20000 g, 1 min
    8. Collect eluate; store at -20 C until ddPCR
  Background correction: PBS blank extraction performed in parallel; average background
                         signal subtracted from all human sample measurements.
  Note           : Preconcentration of sample during DNA extraction further improves LOD.

Step 2 | IL-6 dPLA — Proximity Probe Preparation and Incubation
  Inputs         : Human plasma or BALF (diluted 5-fold in SDB-II or 0.1x TM buffer)
                   IL-6 proximity probes A and B (200 pM each; from TaqMan Protein Assays Open Kit)
  Probe prep     : 2 uL 1 mg/mL biotinylated antibody diluted to 200 nM in ADB; combine 5 uL
                   200 nM 5'/3' prox-oligos with 5 uL 200 nM antibody (1 h, RT); dilute to 10 nM.
  Reaction setup : 2 uL protein solution + 2 uL APS (200 pM/probe)
  Incubation     : 37 C, 60 min (antibody binds IL-6; oligonucleotides brought into proximity)
  Specificity    : IL-6-specific signal 1-2 orders of magnitude above cross-reactive IL-10 / TNF-alpha signal

Step 3 | IL-6 dPLA — Ligation and Stop
  Ligation mix   : 50 uL 20x ligation reaction buffer + 909 uL nuclease-free water + 1 uL DNA ligase (1x)
  Reaction       : Add 96 uL ligation solution to 4 uL protein/probe solution; 37 C, 10 min
  Stop           : Heat 95 C, 5 min (heat denaturation; IL-6 protocol)
  Output         : Ligated PLA product ready for ddPCR amplification

Step 4 | IL-6 dPLA — ddPCR Reaction Setup and Thermal Cycling
  Reaction setup : 9 uL PLA eluate + 10 uL 2x ddPCR Supermix for Probes + 1 uL 20x Universal PCR Assay
                   Total volume: 20 uL; emulsified per Bio-Rad QX200 protocol
  Thermal cycling:
    Preheat   : 95 C, 10 min
    Cycles    : 40x [94 C 30s / 60 C 1min]
    Final ext : 98 C, 10 min; ramp rate 2.5 C/s
  Readout        : Bio-Rad QX200 droplet reader; QuantaSoft Pro v1.0.596
  Quantification : CPN/uL converted to pg/mL via IL-6 calibration curve (R2 = 0.99)
  LOD            : 0.84 pg/mL (40 fM) in plasma SDB-II; 0.02 pg/mL (0.73 fM) in BALF
  Resolution     : ~0.04 pg/mL (patient-dependent)
  Total time     : ~2 h

Step 5 | TNF-alpha dPLA — Proximity Probe Incubation
  Buffer         : HMB (homemade Nong's buffer) — SDB-II incompatible with TNF-alpha
  Reaction setup : 2 uL plasma (5-fold diluted in HMB) + 2 uL APS (200 pM/probe)
  Incubation     : 4 C, overnight (~12 h; modelled as 720 min in BioScript)
  Critical note  : TNF-alpha degrades rapidly and is sensitive to storage and buffer conditions.
                   Overnight incubation required to maximise signal with HMB.
                   For BALF samples: 0.1x TM buffer + 0.5% gelatin used instead.

Step 6 | TNF-alpha dPLA — Ligation and Protease Stop
  Ligation       : 96 uL ligation solution added to 4 uL probe/sample; 37 C, 10 min
  Stop method    : Protease digestion (NOT heat, unlike IL-6)
                   2 uL 1x protease (in PBS) -> 37 C 10 min -> 95 C 15 min for inactivation
  Note           : Protease stop avoids non-specific signal from TNF-alpha antibody denaturation.

Step 7 | TNF-alpha dPLA — ddPCR Reaction Setup and Thermal Cycling
  Setup and cycling: Identical to IL-6 ddPCR (Step 4)
  LOD            : 0.08 pg/mL in plasma (HMB); 0.08 pg/mL in BALF (TM buffer); 4.58 fM undiluted
  Calibration    : R2 = 0.92

Step 8 | Triplex ddPCR — GN Bacteria + GP Bacteria + blaTEM
  Inputs         : Extracted DNA (from Step 1)

                   GP primers/probe (Bac_fwd + Bac_rev + FAM-GP_probe)
                   blaTEM primers/probe (TEM_fwd + TEM_rev + FAM-blaTEM_probe)
  Reaction setup : 1x ddPCR Supermix for Probes; 900 nM each primer;

                   380 nM blaTEM probe (FAM-high); total volume 20 uL

    Preheat   : 95 C, 10 min
    Cycles    : 40x [94 C 30s / 62 C 1min]
    Final ext : 98 C, 10 min; ramp rate 2.5 C/s
  Alternative cycling (blaTEM simplex):
    95 C 10 min; 40x [94 C 30s / 50 C 15s / 70 C 20s]; 98 C 10 min

    HEX-positive  = GN signal
    FAM-medium    = GP signal
    FAM-high      = blaTEM signal

  Note           : Detects both pathogenic bacteria and endogenous microbiota.

Step 9 | Decision-Tree Classification of Patient Outcome
  Inputs         : GN bacteria (CPN/uL) and TNF-alpha (pg/mL) at t1
  Classifier     : DecisionTreeClassifier (scikit-learn, Python); max_depth=2
  Validation     : StratifiedKFold cross-validation (n_splits=5); standardised features
  Thresholds     : GN <85 CPN/uL at t1 -> Group C (death); 100% accuracy
                   GN >=85 CPN/uL + TNF-alpha threshold -> Group A or B
  Accuracy       : Group A 85.71%; Group B 92.31%; Group C 100%; k-fold average >90%
  Comparison     : Decision tree outperforms LDA and logistic regression (less overfitting
                   at n=32; controlled by max_depth)
  Key finding    : Counterintuitive relationship: lower GN at t1 predicts death.
                   Supports the hypothesis that mortality is driven by excessive host
                   cytokine response (increasing IL-6), not by direct bacterial burden.
                   IL-6 temporal change (not absolute level) is the strongest predictor:
                   89% of patients with IL-6 increase at t2 were in Group C (death);
                   85% of patients with IL-6 decrease at t2 were in Group A or B.
  Note           : Patient group classification was performed by independent clinicians
                   without access to molecular measurements (no classification-related confounders).


KEY BIOLOGICAL FINDINGS
-----------------------

BALF (Asthma):
  - Almost all asthma patients had elevated GN bacteria; only 55% of healthy individuals did.
  - IL-6 significantly elevated in asthma vs healthy (p<0.01); supports IL-6 as airway
    inflammation biomarker and potential asthma phenotype marker (IL-6-high phenotype).
  - TNF-alpha uniformly low in all BALF samples (<0.5 pg/mL, near assay LOD).
  - Two GN subpopulations observed in both groups (~20 CPN/uL and ~2 CPN/uL).

Plasma (Septic Shock):
  - GN: Group A decreased rapidly (avg -157 CPN/uL, t1->t2); Group B increased (avg +108 CPN/uL);
    Group C decreased slightly — counterintuitively predicts death.
  - GP: Groups A and C decreased to nondetectable at t2; Group B remained at moderate levels
    (13-36 CPN/uL) across all 3 time points — surprising since Group B ultimately recovered.
  - blaTEM: Most patients below LOD. One Group B patient showed blaTEM rise from 0 to >300
    CPN/uL at t3; confirmed by blood culture (beta-lactam-producing bacteria). Digital assay
    result available same day vs days for culture.
  - TNF-alpha: Group B had highest levels at t1 and t2; dropped to <10 pg/mL by t3 (resolution).
    Group C had very low TNF-alpha (progressed beyond initial cytokine secretion peak by t1).
  - IL-6 absolute levels not correlated with outcome; temporal changes strongly correlated.
    Increasing IL-6 -> death; decreasing IL-6 -> recovery (Fig. 5c-e).
  - dPLA resolution (~0.04 pg/mL) allows detection of IL-6 changes too small for conventional ELISA.

PROTOCOL: [18F]FDG Radiosynthesis on Digital Microfluidics (OFAT-Optimized)
================================================================================

Source Link : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_ab1a29cf1f1a4c74999bfd94b207f38b.pdf
Paper DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1039/d2lc00764a
BioScript   : fdg_radiosynthesis_ofat.bs
Platform    : Digital Microfluidics (EWOD / DMFB electrode-array device)
Optimization: One-Factor-At-A-Time (OFAT) + Machine Learning (Ridge Regression)
Product     : [18F]FDG (2-[18F]fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OFAT-OPTIMAL PARAMETERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Parameter                          Optimal Value
  ---------------------------------  ----------------
  Mannose triflate / [18F] volume    1.0 (equal ratio)
  Mannose triflate concentration     30 mM
  Radiolabeling temperature          100 C
  Radiolabeling time                 5 min
  NaOH concentration                 1.0 M
  Deprotection temperature           50 C
  Deprotection time                  5 min

  Fluorination efficiency (OFAT)   : 70.82 +/- 1.54%
  Overall synthesis yield (OFAT)   : 66.64%
  Overall synthesis yield (ML)     : 79.13%
  Total synthesis time             : ~19 +/- 2 min
  Post-purification purity         : ~93.05 +/- 2.46%

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. [18F]Fluoride         - No-carrier-added [18F]fluoride ion in [18O]-enriched H2O
  2. Mannose Triflate      - 30 mM in anhydrous acetonitrile (MeCN); substrate for
                             [18F] fluorination
  3. Kryptofix K222        - K222 / K2CO3 complex; activates [18F]fluoride for
                             nucleophilic substitution
  4. NaOH                  - 1.0 M sodium hydroxide; deprotection agent

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVICE SETUP
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - DMF bottom plate: chromium-coated glass, standard photolithographic fabrication
  - Dielectric layer : parylene-C (7 um)
  - Hydrophobic layer: Teflon AF 1600 (150 nm), spin-coated at 1500 rpm
  - Top plate        : ITO-coated glass, Teflon AF 1600 coated
  - Inter-plate gap  : ~140 um (2x double-sided tape spacer)
  - Actuation        : 160 V_RMS sine wave at 15 kHz; 104 pogo-pin holder
  - Heating/cooling  : 14.8 x 14.8 mm TEC/Peltier module (10 central electrodes
                       defined as reaction site)
  - Reagent delivery : stepper-motor-driven syringe system
  - Purification site: alumina disc (6 mm dia., neutral alumina 50-300 um in PDMS)
                       sandwiched between top and bottom plates

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 - Deliver [18F]Fluoride
  - Dispense no-carrier-added [18F]fluoride to the reaction site via syringe.

STEP 2 - Activate [18F] (Carrier Evaporation)
  - Heat [18F]fluoride droplet at 120 C for 10 min.
  - Evaporates [18O]-H2O carrier; TEC/Peltier heater used.

STEP 3 - Resuspend with Kryptofix K222 / K2CO3
  - Dispense Kryptofix K222 droplet and mix with activated [18F] for 5 s.
  - Perform MeCN azeotropic dry: heat at 120 C for 5 min to remove residual water.

STEP 4 - Merge Mannose Triflate with Activated [18F]
  - Dispense 30 mM mannose triflate droplet (volume ratio 1:1 with [18F]).
  - Mix with activated [18F] droplet for 10 s to form reaction droplet.

STEP 5 - Fluorination (Radiolabeling)
  - Heat reaction droplet at 100 C for 5 min.
  - Nucleophilic substitution incorporates [18F] into mannose triflate scaffold.

STEP 6 - Deprotection (NaOH Hydrolysis)
  - Dispense 1.0 M NaOH droplet; mix with reaction droplet for 5 s.
  - Heat at 50 C for 5 min.
  - Hydrolyses the intermediate to yield crude [18F]FDG at room temperature.

STEP 7 - On-Chip Alumina Disc Purification
  - Actuate crude [18F]FDG droplet to the purification site (6 mm alumina disc).
  - Incubate at 25 C for 40 min; move droplet around adjacent electrodes to
    enhance contact with disc.
  - Removes Kryptofix K222, unreacted [18F]fluoride, and free F-.
  - Expected purity: ~93.05 +/- 2.46%.
  - After incubation, actuate purified droplet away from disc; collect manually
    by pipette for downstream processing.

STEP 8 - Detect Fluorination Efficiency (Quality Gate)
  - Analyse purified product by radioactive TLC (silica gel HLF plates).
  - Detection time: 30 s.
  - Quality threshold: fluorination efficiency >= 70%.
    PASS (>= 70%) -> drain / collect product for use.
    FAIL (< 70%)  -> do not collect; dispose.

STEP 9 - Waste Disposal
  - Dispose all final merged droplet variables:
    protected18F (crude [18F]FDG), activatedF18 (activated [18F] intermediate),
    reactionDroplet (fluorination intermediate).
  - Note: precursor variables (f18Drop, k222Drop, mannoseTriflate, naohDrop)
    were consumed into these during mix operations and no longer exist.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETECTION & ANALYSIS INSTRUMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Dose calibrator         : CRC 55 TR (Capintec) - radioactivity measurement
  - TLC scanner             : MiniGITA star (Raytest) - fluorination efficiency
  - TLC plates              : Silica Gel HLF 250 um, 10x20 cm scored (Analtech)
  - Gamma spectrometer      : in-house; identity and purity of [18F]fluoride

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - The OFAT method requires only 8 experiments (1 base + 7 variable) compared
    to 2187 experiments needed for a full 3^7 factorial design.
  - Significant parameters identified by OFAT (p < 0.05, t-test):
      mannose triflate concentration, NaOH concentration, radiolabeling
      temperature, deprotection time, mannose triflate / [18F] volume ratio.
  - Non-significant parameters: radiolabeling time, deprotection temperature.
  - ML model (Ridge regression, 55-experiment database, 80/20 train/test split,
    10-fold cross-validation) further improved overall yield to 79.13%.
  - Conditions predicted for 100% incorporation (110 C, 1.4 M NaOH, 90 mM
    mannose triflate) were not practically achievable on-chip due to poor droplet
    movement fidelity at extreme concentrations and temperatures.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Heterogeneous Magnetic-Bead Sandwich Immunoassay on a Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform, applied to Human Insulin and Interleukin-6 (IL-6) Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample Droplet (analyte solution containing human insulin or IL-6 antigen)
  - Capture-Antibody-Conjugated Magnetic Bead Droplet (magnetic beads coated with antigen-specific capture antibody)

3. Immobilize the magnetic beads at the reaction site using a permanent magnet positioned beneath the chip.
4. With the beads held in place by the magnet, split off and remove the excess supernatant (unbound sample and unbound reporter antibody) to a waste reservoir.
5. Dispense a fresh wash-buffer droplet and merge it with the immobilized bead droplet, then split off and remove the diluted supernatant again; repeat this dilution-based wash cycle (~1:6 dilution per cycle) for 5 cycles to achieve a cumulative ~7776-fold dilution of unbound material and near-complete bead retention.
6. Release the washed magnetic-bead droplet from the magnet and transport it across five electrodes to resuspend the beads via the internal recirculating flow generated by droplet motion.
7. Dispense a chemiluminescent (HRP) substrate droplet and merge it with the resuspended, washed bead droplet to initiate the enzyme-substrate chemiluminescent reaction.
8.
