================================================================================
  DMF RIBOZYME CLEAVAGE ASSAY PROTOCOL
  Digital Microfluidics Chips for the Execution and Real-Time Monitoring
  of Multiple Ribozymatic Cleavage Reactions
================================================================================

  Source Link : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_d4758ae71a674751b0117f1e8194db35.pdf
  Paper DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.1c00239
  Journal     : ACS Omega, 2021, Vol. 6, pp. 22514-22524

================================================================================
  OVERVIEW
================================================================================

This protocol describes the execution of inducible cis-acting hammerhead
ribozyme (HHR) cleavage reactions on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) chip,
with real-time fluorescence monitoring. The ribozyme undergoes self-cleavage
upon binding to a short single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) input strand. The
cleaved-off RNA output strand is detected via a toehold-mediated strand
displacement reaction (TMSDR), which displaces a quencher (BHQ-3) from a
Cy5-labeled fluorescent probe, generating a measurable fluorescence signal.
The platform supports up to 8 simultaneous reactions (6 assays + 1 positive
control + 1 negative control) per chip.

================================================================================
  CHIP SPECIFICATIONS
================================================================================

  Platform           : Digital Microfluidics (DMF), electrowetting-on-dielectric
  Chip 1 (kinetics)  : 6 reservoirs, 8 detection points, 3 mixing zones (4 electrodes each)
  Chip 2 (multi-rxn) : 5 reservoirs, 3 x 17 electrode matrix, 8 detection points
  Electrode spacing  : 60 um interelectrode gap (2x wiring thickness of 30 um)
  Electrode shape    : Skewed-wave edges (prevents dielectric breakdown and droplet stranding)
  Droplet volume     : 0.5 +/- 0.08 uL (dispensed), 2 uL (cleavage buffer, pipetted)
  Actuation          : 178 V RMS, 15 kHz sine wave, 0.7 s per electrode step

================================================================================
  REAGENTS AND MATERIALS
================================================================================

  All general-use chemicals purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (St. Louis, MO)
  unless otherwise stated.

  1. RIBOZYME SOLUTION
     - Type       : Inducible cis-acting hammerhead ribozyme (HHR)
     - Stock conc : 2.5 uM in nuclease-free water
     - Load vol   : 2.5 uL per reservoir
     - Working    : ~0.5 uM after merging with cleavage buffer (1:5 dilution)

  2. CLEAVAGE BUFFER (1.25x concentrated)
     - 125 mM NaCl
     - 62.5 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5
     - 31.25 mM KCl
     - 12.5 mM MgCl2
     - 0.0625% Tetronic 304 (surfactant to prevent biofouling)
     - 2.5 uM Quenched Probe (QP)
     - 6.25 uM Input ssDNA (IP) -- or as specified per experiment
     - Load vol   : 2 uL pipetted directly onto detection points

  3. QUENCHED PROBE (QP)
     - Composition : Two ssDNA strands (purchased from Alpha DNA, Montreal, Canada)
         F-strand  : 5' end labeled with Cy5 fluorophore; 0.625 uM
         Q-strand  : 3' end labeled with Black Hole Quencher-3 (BHQ-3); 0.7 uM
     - Prepared in 1.25x cleavage buffer (125 mM NaCl, 62.5 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5,
       31.25 mM KCl)
     - Annealing protocol (Biorad T100 thermocycler):
         Step 1 : 95 degC for 3 min  (denaturation)
         Step 2 : 50 degC for 15 min (annealing)
         Step 3 : 37 degC for 15 min (annealing)
     - Stored in bulk at -20 degC
     - Add 0.05% Tetronic 304 (per 10 uL) before use

  4. INPUT STRAND (IP)
     - Type     : Single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) activator
     - Function : Binds to ribozyme, inducing fold into active HHR, triggering self-cleavage
     - Conc     : 6.25 uM in cleavage buffer (standard); 0.01-10 uM for biosensor assays

  5. DI WATER
     - Used to fill 5 surrounding wells (30 uL each) on the 384-well plate
       to maintain humidity and prevent droplet evaporation during scanning

================================================================================
  RIBOZYME TRANSCRIPTION (Upstream Preparation)
================================================================================

  1. Design primers F1, F2, R1, R2 using the tool Primerize
     (https://primerize.stanford.edu)

  2. Assembly PCR (total volume: 100 uL):
     - Primers : F1 (2 uM), R1 (0.2 uM), F2 (0.2 uM), R2 (2 uM)
     - Enzyme  : HotStar Taq Plus (QIAGEN) with 1x reaction buffer
     - Additives: 1x Q-solution (QIAGEN), 0.2 mM dNTPs, milli-Q water
     - PCR program:
         95 degC x 15 min  (initial denaturation)
         15 cycles of:
           95 degC x 30 s  (denaturation)
           50 degC x 30 s  (annealing)
           72 degC x 30 s  (extension)
     - Ethanol precipitate the PCR product

  3. In vitro RNA synthesis (1 mL reaction):
     - Pool 10 x 100 uL PCRs, precipitate, resuspend in 150 uL milli-Q water
     - Reaction mix:
         80 mM HEPES, pH 7.5
         24 mM MgCl2
         40 mM dithiothreitol (DTT)
         2 mM spermidine
         6 ug/mL T7 RNA polymerase
         150 uL resuspended PCR product
         2 mM rNTPs
         1x pyrophosphatase (Roche Diagnostics)
         200 U (40 uL) RiboLock (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
     - Incubate 30 min at 37 degC
     - Add 10 U DNase (New England Biolabs); incubate 30 min at 37 degC
     - Extract RNA with phenol-chloroform; ethanol precipitate aqueous phase

  4. RNA purification:
     - Run on 10% denaturing polyacrylamide gel (8 M urea)
     - Visualize with UV-shadowing; excise highest band
     - Elute in 0.3 M NaCl overnight at 4 degC
     - Ethanol precipitate; resuspend in nuclease-free water

================================================================================
  DMF CHIP FABRICATION
================================================================================

  1. Design photomask in AutoCAD 2018; print on transparency film
     (CAD/Art services, Bandon, OR)

  2. Coat glass substrate with S1811 photoresist (Telic)

  3. UV expose for 8 s on Quintel Q-4000 mask aligner (Neutronix Quintel)

  4. Develop with MF321 developer (Rohm and Haas); bake 115 degC for 1 min

  5. Etch chromium layer with CR-4 chromium etchant (OM Group)

  6. Strip remaining photoresist with AZ-300T stripper (2 min)

  7. Rinse with DI water, air dry; silanize (DI water : 2-propanol :
     (trimethoxysilyl)-propyl methacrylate = 50:50:1) for 15 min

  8. Cover electrode pads with Kapton tape

  9. Deposit dielectric: 7 um Parylene-C via SCS Labcoter 2 PDS 2010

  10. Cut top plate from ITO-precoated glass slide
      (cat. no. CG-61IN-S207, Delta Technologies)

  11. Deposit hydrophobic layer: 1% Teflon-AF (FC40) on both plates
      - Spin coat: 500 rpm / 100 rpm/s / 30 s, then 3000 rpm / 500 rpm/s / 60 s
      - Bake: 160 degC for 10 min

  12. Assemble device: sandwich two layers of double-sided tape (3M Canada,
      70 um each) between bottom substrate and top plate

================================================================================
  AUTOMATION SYSTEM SETUP
================================================================================

  - Software         : In-house Python 2.7 scripts
  - Microcontroller  : Arduino Uno (Adafruit)
  - Signal generator : Agilent Technologies (15 kHz sine wave)
  - Amplifier        : PZD-700A (Trek Inc.) -- amplifies to 178 V RMS
  - I/O expander     : Maxim 7300 (Digikey), I2C communication
  - Interface        : Pogo pins connecting control board to chip contact pads
  - Top plate grounded via ground wire

  Protocol files specify sequential electrode actuation parameters
  (pulse time, period) and are run via command line.

================================================================================
  PROTOCOL STEPS
================================================================================

  STEP 1 -- CHIP CLEANING
  ------------------------
  1. Clean DMF substrate with RNAse Away, then IPA, then DI water
  2. Air-dry thoroughly before use

  STEP 2 -- REAGENT LOADING
  --------------------------
  1. Mount cleaned chip onto the automation system
  2. Pipette 2.5 uL of ribozyme solution (2.5 uM) into each ribozyme reservoir
  3. Pipette 2 uL of cleavage buffer (1.25x, containing IP and QP) directly
     onto each detection point
  4. Place the ITO top plate onto the chip and connect to ground wire

  STEP 3 -- DISPENSE RIBOZYME DROPLETS
  --------------------------------------
  1. Actuate dispense electrode pattern to stretch reservoir droplet
  2. Switch off the third electrode to pinch off a ~0.5 uL ribozyme droplet
     (actuation: 178 V RMS, 15 kHz, 0.7 s per step)
  3. Repeat for all assay lanes (rxn1, rxn2, rxn3) and for positive control (PC)
  4. For negative control (NC): dispense 2 uL quenched probe only (no ribozyme,
     no input strand) onto the NC detection point

  STEP 4 -- MOVE AND MERGE DROPLETS
  -----------------------------------
  1. Actuate electrodes sequentially to move each ribozyme droplet toward
     its corresponding detection point
  2. Merge the ribozyme droplet (~0.5 uL) with the pre-pipetted cleavage
     buffer droplet (2 uL) at the detection point
  3. Mix the merged droplet by actuating 4 electrodes back-and-forth for 10 s

     Reaction assignments:
       rxn1    : ribozyme droplet 1 + cleavage buffer 1  (assay replicate 1)
       rxn2    : ribozyme droplet 2 + cleavage buffer 2  (assay replicate 2)
       rxn3    : ribozyme droplet 3 + cleavage buffer 3  (assay replicate 3)
       pcMix   : ribozyme droplet PC + PC buffer          (positive control)
       ncProbe : quenched probe only -- NO mix operation  (negative control)

     Note: ncProbe is dispensed fresh and incubated directly at its detection
     point. It is NEVER mixed with any ribozyme droplet. Using a consumed
     ribozyme variable here would violate BioScript's use-once type system.

     Positive control buffer contains ssDNA equivalent to the expected
     cleaved-off output RNA strand, directly displacing the quencher
     without requiring ribozyme activity.

  STEP 5 -- INCUBATION
  ---------------------
  Upon merging, in the assay droplets:
    - The input strand (IP) binds to the ribozyme
    - HHR folds into its active form and self-cleaves
    - The cleaved-off RNA output strand hybridizes to the F-strand of the
      quenched probe, displacing the BHQ-3 Q-strand (TMSDR)
    - Cy5 fluorophore is unquenched and emits fluorescence

  All five droplets are incubated simultaneously:
    rxn1, rxn2, rxn3, pcMix  -- heated at detection points
    ncProbe                   -- heated at its detection point (no prior mix)

  Temperature : 37 degC (maintained by plate reader during scanning)

  To extract cleavage rate constants:
    1. Calculate inverse of fluorescence intensities at each time point

         Y         = amount of uncleaved ribozyme (1/fluorescence)
         X         = time (min)
         K         = observed cleavage rate constant (kobs, min-1)
         Y0        = initial value of Y

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Platform for the Detection of Rubella Infection and Immunity: A Proof of Concept
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ClinChemV61I2.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2014.232181
Journal      : Clinical Chemistry, 2015, Vol. 61, No. 2, pp. 420-429
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF), two-plate, air-filled, with motorised PMT and magnetic lens assembly


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a shoebox-sized DMF immunoassay platform for the detection of rubella
virus (RV)-specific IgG and IgM antibodies from patient serum, plasma, or whole blood. The
system is motivated by the need for decentralised diagnostics in resource-limited settings to
prevent congenital rubella syndrome (CRS): 100,000 infants are born with CRS each year, and
rural-to-laboratory transport for standard centralised testing is often cost-prohibitive.

Two protocols are encoded in sequence on the same DMF device and .bs file:
  1. RV IgG immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA): detects immunity or past/current infection.
     Clinical cutoff: 10 IU/mL. LOD: 0.03 IU/mL; LOQ: 0.1 IU/mL.
     Run time: ~25 min per quadruplicate set. Intraassay CVs: 0.3-6.5%.
  2. RV IgM immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA + on-chip IgG blocking pretreatment):
     the critical test for diagnosing active rubella infection and identifying pregnancies
     at risk for CRS. Run time: ~35 min per quadruplicate set. Intraassay CVs: 1.5-13.4%.

Both assays use rubella-virus-coated paramagnetic microparticles for analyte capture,
HRP-conjugated detection antibodies for signal transduction, and SuperSignal ELISA Femto
chemiluminescent substrate (H2O2 + luminol-enhancer) for readout. Signal is detected by an
integrated motorised PMT (photomultiplier tube); readout is in RLU (relative light units)
over a 10 s integration window.

Diagnostic performance was evaluated against 25 plasma/serum samples from the SeraCare
PTR201 commercial mixed-titer performance panel, using Abbott EIA as the reference standard.
Both assays achieved 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (AUC = 1.00 for each).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration  : Two-plate DMF (top plate ground + bottom plate electrode array); air-filled gap.
Gap            : ~140 um between top and bottom plates.
Instrument     : ~7 x 9 x 12 inches (shoebox-sized); computer-controlled via DropBot.
Bottom plate   : 80 actuation electrodes (2.54 x 2.54 mm each); reservoir electrodes for
                 sample/reagent storage and waste removal; chromium electrode layer + insulator
                 + Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating on glass substrate.
Top plate      : ITO ground electrode + Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating on glass.
Unit droplet   : ~900 nL (electrode area x 140 um gap).
Actuation      : 80-100 V_rms, 10 kHz sine wave; Pogo pin interface (90 pins);
                 controlled by DropBot (open-source DMF automation system).

Magnetic lens  : Motorised neodymium magnet assembly.
                 Active position: ~150 um below device; immobilisation force: ~600 uN.
                 Inactive position: 3.8 cm below device (allows droplet resuspension).
                 Minimum release threshold: ~500 uN (exceeds droplet surface tension).
                 Function: concentrates particles into pellet in the separation zone;
                 deactivation allows a fresh droplet to be mixed over the pellet to
                 resuspend particles for subsequent reagent incubation steps.

PMT detector   : Motorised; positioned a few hundred um above device droplet centre when active;
                 5 cm above when inactive (LED + webcam used for droplet monitoring).
                 PMT protection: 2 position sensors, shutter, light-tight enclosure grooves.
                 Integration: 10 s mean signal; output in RLU.
                 Advantage: no excitation source, filters, or lenses required.

Fabrication    : University of Toronto Nanofabrication Centre cleanroom.


REAGENTS
--------
Particles        : RV-coated paramagnetic microparticles (Abbott Architect rubella kit);
                   pre-washed 2x in Superblock, resuspended at ~10x stock (1.5e8 particles/mL).
Wash buffer      : Custom DMF-compatible formulation + 0.05% Pluronic L64.
Conjugate diluent: Custom DMF-compatible formulation + 0.05% Pluronic L64.
HRP conjugate    : (Protocol 1) HRP-conjugated goat polyclonal antihuman IgG, 21 ng/mL.
                   (Protocol 2) HRP-conjugated goat antihuman IgM, 23 ng/mL.
Substrate        : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fischer Scientific):
                   stable peroxide (H2O2) + luminol-enhancer; 900 nL each.
Pretreatment     : Goat antihuman IgG (Abbott Architect IgM pretreatment reagent, 3x dilution
                   in conjugate diluent); 900 nL per IgM assay.
Sample diluent   : Dulbecco PBS + 4% BSA; all samples pre-diluted 10x off-chip before loading.
Pluronic additive: 0.05% Pluronic L64 added to all on-chip reagents; prevents protein
                   adsorption and cross-contamination in the air-filled DMF device.
Calibrators      : RV IgG: 0, 5, 10, 15, 75, 250 IU/mL (Abbott Architect).
                   RV IgM cutoff: Cal 1 (Abbott Architect); RF IgM content 27.0 IU/mL.
Performance panel: SeraCare PTR201-01-25 (25 plasma/serum samples; collected 1994-1995).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

PROTOCOL 1 | RV IgG IMMUNOASSAY (7 steps, ~25 min per quadruplicate)

Step 1 | Particle dispense and magnetic separation
  Reagents : VirusCoatedParticles
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units); 1.5e8 particles/mL in Superblock
  Operation: Dispense from reservoir; magnetic lens activated (~150 um below device, ~600 uN);
             particles pellet in separation zone; Superblock diluent moved to waste.
  Duration : ~5 s
  Notes    : Particle pellet retained on-chip; resuspended in next step.

Step 2 | Sample incubation
  Reagents : SampleIgG (pre-diluted 10x in DPBS/4% BSA off-chip)
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units)
  Operation: Dispense; deliver to particle pellet; mix in circular motion 3 min.
             RV IgG from sample binds RV-coated particle surface.
             Magnetic lens re-activated; supernatant disposed.
  Duration : 3 min (180 s; IR: 180.0 SECOND)

Step 3 | First wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: 4 sequential wash steps. Each: dispense fresh buffer droplet; deliver to pellet;
             mix; magnetic lens activated; supernatant disposed.
             Removes unbound sample antibody and non-specific proteins.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s; IR: 30.0 SECOND each)

Step 4 | HRP conjugate incubation
  Reagents : HRPConjugateIgG (21 ng/mL HRP-conjugated goat polyclonal antihuman IgG)
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units)
  Operation: Dispense; deliver to particle pellet; mix 2 min.
             HRP-anti-IgG binds RV IgG captured on particles (sandwich immunocomplex).
             Magnetic lens re-activated; unbound conjugate disposed.
  Duration : 2 min (120 s; IR: 120.0 SECOND)

Step 5 | Second wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: Identical to Step 3. Removes excess unbound HRP conjugate before substrate.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s)

Step 6 | Substrate addition, reaction, and chemiluminescent detection
  Reagents : H2O2 (stable peroxide), LuminolEnhancer (SuperSignal ELISA Femto)
  Volume   : 900 nL each (1 unit each)
  Operation: Dispense H2O2 and luminol-enhancer as separate 1-unit droplets; merge (5 s mix);
             deliver substrate mix to particle pellet; mix 2 min. HRP catalyses luminol
             oxidation in H2O2; photons collected by motorised PMT over 10 s.
             Signal reported as RLU; normalised to cutoff calibrator (s/co).
  Substrate mix duration : 5 s
  Reaction duration      : 2 min (120 s)
  Detection duration     : 10 s
  Detection module       : rvIgGDetection
  Interpretation:
    s/co >= 1.0    -> positive  (immune to rubella)
    s/co 0.69-0.99 -> equivocal (gray zone)
    s/co < 0.69    -> negative  (susceptible to rubella)

Step 7 | Diagnostic gate (BB2 / BB3)
  Branch pass (BB2): igGSignal > 0 -> dispose(igGReaction); patient IgG-positive.
  Branch fail (BB3): igGSignal <= 0 -> drain(igGReaction); patient IgG-negative/equivocal.
  Join (BB4): dispose(igGSignal); Protocol 2 begins.


PROTOCOL 2 | RV IgM IMMUNOASSAY + ON-CHIP IgG BLOCKING (7 steps + pretreatment, ~35 min)

Step 8 | On-chip sample pretreatment (IgG blocking)
  Reagents : SampleIgM (pre-diluted 10x in DPBS/4% BSA off-chip),
             PretreatmentReagent (goat antihuman IgG, 3x dilution in conjugate diluent)
  Volumes  : 1.8 uL sample (2 units) + 900 nL pretreatment (1 unit)
  Operation: Dispense both; merge on-chip; mix 7 min.
  Duration : 7 min (420 s; IR: 420.0 SECOND)
  Purpose  : Exogenous antihuman IgG blocks two interference sources in the IgM assay:
               (i)  Endogenous RV IgG competing for particle binding sites
                    -> prevents false negatives (Fig. 3A panel 2).
               (ii) RV IgG / RF IgM immunocomplexes binding non-specifically to particles
                    -> prevents false positives from rheumatoid factor (Fig. 3A panel 3).
  Evidence : Pretreatment significantly suppresses nonspecific signal in IgG+IgM samples
             (P=0.0003); pure IgG (P=0.5) and pure IgM (P=0.6) samples unaffected (Fig. 3B).
             RF IgM in RV IgG calibrators: 1.4-1.85 IU/mL (low).
             RF IgM in RV IgM Cal 1: 27.0 IU/mL (high; pretreatment critical for cutoff use).

Step 9 | Particle dispense and magnetic separation
  Reagents : VirusCoatedParticles
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units); identical stock as Protocol 1.
  Operation: Identical to Protocol 1 Step 1.
  Duration : ~5 s

Step 10 | Pretreated sample incubation
  Reagents : igMPretreatedSample (from Step 8), igMParticles (from Step 9)
  Volume   : (combined pretreated sample droplet delivered to particle pellet)
  Operation: Mix 3 min. RV IgM from pretreated sample binds RV-coated particles;
             IgG/RF IgM competition blocked. Magnetic lens re-activated; supernatant disposed.
  Duration : 3 min (180 s)

Step 11 | First wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: Identical to Protocol 1 Step 3. Removes unbound antibody and pretreatment components.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s)

Step 12 | HRP conjugate incubation
  Reagents : HRPConjugateIgM (23 ng/mL HRP-conjugated goat antihuman IgM)
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units)
  Operation: Dispense; deliver to particle pellet; mix 2 min.
             IgM-specific conjugate; distinguishes this step from Protocol 1 Step 4.
             HRP-anti-IgM binds selectively to RV IgM on particles.
             Magnetic lens re-activated; unbound conjugate disposed.
  Duration : 2 min (120 s)

Step 13 | Second wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: Identical to Step 11. Removes excess HRP-anti-IgM before substrate.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s)

Step 14 | Substrate addition, reaction, and chemiluminescent detection
  Reagents : H2O2 (stable peroxide), LuminolEnhancer (SuperSignal ELISA Femto)
  Volume   : 900 nL each (1 unit each)
  Operation: Identical to Protocol 1 Step 6.
             Cutoff defined by Cal 1 (s/co = 1); s/co = mean signal / mean Cal 1 signal.
  Substrate mix duration : 5 s
  Reaction duration      : 2 min (120 s)
  Detection duration     : 10 s
  Detection module       : rvIgMDetection
  Interpretation:
    s/co >= 1.0    -> positive  (active rubella infection; CRS risk if pregnant)
    s/co 0.75-0.99 -> equivocal (gray zone; retest required per WHO guidance)
    s/co < 0.75    -> negative  (no evidence of acute rubella infection)

Step 15 | Diagnostic gate (BB5 / BB6)
  Branch pass (BB5): igMSignal > 0 -> dispose(igMReaction); active rubella infection confirmed.
  Branch fail (BB6): igMSignal <= 0 -> drain(igMReaction); IgM-negative/equivocal.
  Terminal (BB7): dispose(igMSignal); NOP. Experiment ends.

EQUIVOCAL NOTE: Equivocal results (s/co in gray zone) are interpreted as positive for
sensitivity/specificity calculations per WHO guidance. In clinical practice, all positive or
equivocal patients are retested to confirm final diagnosis. 2 of 25 panel samples produced
positive-equivocal discrepancies between DMF and Abbott EIA at s/co values near the cutoff;
attributed to assay variability (CV ~15%) and 20-year sample age. Final diagnostic accuracy
remained 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity for both assays.


ON-CHIP DILUTION (SUPPLEMENTARY SUB-PROTOCOL)
----------------------------------------------
For patient samples exceeding the linear range (>250 IU/mL) or for whole blood compatibility:

Method   : Serial 2x on-chip dilution.
  Step 1 : Dispense 1 sample droplet (1.8 uL) + 1 diluent droplet (1.8 uL); merge and mix.
  Step 2 : Split pooled droplet into 2 equal sub-droplets.
  Step 3 : Store one sub-droplet; repeat Steps 1-3 with the other.
  4 iterations yield: 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x diluted droplets (125, 62.5, 31.3, 15.6 IU/mL
  from a 250 IU/mL sample).

Blood matrix: Interassay CVs marginally higher for blood samples (10-15%) vs standard (6-9%).
  At 1/4 and 1/8 blood dilutions: signal significantly different from calibrator (P < 0.05).
  At 1/16 and 1/32: indistinguishable from calibrator (P > 0.05).
  Conclusion: 1/16 or 1/32 blood dilution removes matrix interference without reducing
              analyte below LOQ.

BioScript note: Not encoded in this .bs file. BioScript has no loop/repeat construct;
  serial dilution steps would need to be hardcoded per iteration in a separate .bs file.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : High-throughput co-culture system for analysis of spatiotemporal cell-cell signaling
Source Link  : https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0956566323000313
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bios.2023.115089
Journal      : Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2023, Article 115089
Authors      : Minjun Son, Andrew G. Wang, Emma Kenna, Savas Tay
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidics with pneumatic valve control; 192-chamber high-throughput array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated high-throughput microfluidic co-culture system for
spatiotemporal study of cell-cell signaling. The device enables: (i) chemical stimulation
of sentinel macrophages to initiate cytokine secretion, (ii) formation of diffusion-mediated
cytokine gradients over a receiving fibroblast population, (iii) live single-cell NF-kB
translocation imaging across 192 chambers, (iv) spatially resolved cell retrieval from
near/mid/far regions of the receiving chamber, and (v) downstream gene expression
quantification by RT-qPCR or RNA sequencing.

Two experimental arms are encoded in a single .bs file:
  ARM 1 (main, BB1-BB10): LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages as cytokine source in
                           pre-chamber; paracrine signaling to RelA-DsRed NIH3T3 fibroblasts
                           in receiving chamber.
  ARM 2 (supplemental, BB10-BB16): Fixed-dose 30 ng/mL TNF-a loaded directly into
                                    pre-chamber; no macrophages; controlled distance-dependent
                                    gene expression model. Continues as sequential continuation
                                    from BB10; compiler assigns BB10-BB16.

The protocol reproduces the key experimental conditions of Sections 3.2-3.5 of the paper,
covering macrophage-to-fibroblast paracrine signaling, distance-dependent NF-kB dynamics,
spatially resolved gene expression (Tnfaip3/A20, Casp4, Ccl5/RANTES, GAPDH), and
spatial distribution of sentinel cell density effects on population-level response.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication : Two-layer PDMS soft lithography; AutoCAD design; bonded to
              127.8 x 85.5 x 1 mm glass substrate (Marienfeld); oxygen plasma (Harrick PDC-001).

Layer 1 (fluid) : Thin PDMS ~50 um height; spun at 2300 RPM from ~10 g mixture on
                  chlorotrimethylsilane-treated fluid mold; contains cell chambers and channels.

Layer 2 (control): Thick PDMS slab; pneumatic valve features; aligned to fluid layer
                   using custom stereomicroscope with XYZ translation stage.

Array format  : 192 chambers in 8x24 arrangement; 96 independently controllable row-column pairs.
                Each unit: small pre-chamber (source) + large receiving chamber.

Receiving chamber: Partitioned into 3 regions (near / mid / far) by pneumatic partitioning valves.
                   Forest of pillars between chamber bottom and sink channel.
                   Cell retrieval side channels (1 per region) lead to dedicated outlets.

Sink channel  : Flushed by gentle peristaltic pumping; provides shear-free cytokine removal;
                mimics capillary clearance of secreted cytokines (Kumar et al., 2019).

Valves        : 88 solenoid-controlled inputs (Festo 197334, Tygon tubes Cole-Parmer ND-100-80).
Control GUI   : Custom Matlab GUI (Gomez-Sjoberg et al., 2010); pre-written scripts for automation.
Imaging       : Nikon Ti2 epifluorescence microscope; temperature/CO2/humidity-controlled enclosure.


CELL LINES
----------
- RelA-/- RelA-DsRed NIH3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (3T3s):
  Receiving chamber cells. NF-kB translocation tracked via nuclear DsRed signal.
  Media: DMEM high glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 2 mM GlutaMAX (Gibco)
         + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Lonza).
  Loading concentration: 5e5 cells/mL; target ~70% confluency (200-400 cells/chamber).

- RelA-GFP RAW264.7 macrophage-like cells:
  Pre-chamber sentinel cells. NF-kB tracked via GFP.
  Stimulated with 50 ng/mL LPS (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps) for 10 min in pre-chamber.

- Primary murine adult fibroblasts (RelA-YFP knock-in mouse):
  Used in cell-patterning experiments (Section 3.5, Fig. 5).

- Bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMMΦ, RelA-YFP knock-in mouse):
  Used in cell-patterning experiments (Section 3.5, Fig. 5).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming and Chamber Coating (Fibronectin)
  Reagents    : Fibronectin (Sigma-Aldrich FC010), PBS, DMEM high glucose
  Operation   : Fibronectin loaded through inlet channels into receiving chambers
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s in IR)
  Wash        : Fresh DMEM flowed through chambers to remove unbound fibronectin
  Purpose     : Promotes fibroblast attachment to glass substrate

Step 2 | RelA-DsRed 3T3 Fibroblast Loading into Receiving Chambers
  Cell line       : RelA-/- RelA-DsRed NIH3T3
  Concentration   : 5e5 cells/mL in complete DMEM
  Target loading  : ~70% confluency, 200-400 cells per chamber
  Operation       : Valve-directed flow through cell loading channel (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Adhesion        : 37 C / 5% CO2 for 4-6 h (300 min nominal; 18000 s in IR)
  Notes           : Cells spread evenly before macrophage loading; adhesion verified visually

Step 3 | Hoechst 33342 Nuclear Staining (Optional)
  Reagent         : 1 uM Hoechst 33342
  Incubation      : 10 min at 37 C (600 s in IR)
  Purpose         : Enables nucleus tracking during live-cell epifluorescence imaging
  Notes           : Applied selectively; performed before macrophage loading

Step 4 | RelA-GFP RAW264.7 Macrophage Loading into Pre-Chamber
  Cell line       : RelA-GFP RAW264.7
  Cell number     : 10-100 per pre-chamber; controlled-density experiments use 60 +/- 15
  Suspension      : DMEM high glucose
  Operation       : Flow through source channel; separator valve CLOSED during loading
  Settling        : 30 min at 37 C (1800 s in IR)
  Notes           : Pre-chamber and receiving chamber remain separated by closed separator valve

Step 5 | LPS Stimulation of Macrophages and Wash
  LPS             : 50 ng/mL (InvivoGen tlrl-3pelps)
  Stimulus duration: 10 min (600 s in IR); separator valve CLOSED
  Wash            : Fresh DMEM flowed through pre-chamber to remove LPS before separator opens
  Purpose         : Activates canonical NF-kB via TLR4; triggers TNF-a and cytokine secretion
  Notes           : LPS washed out to prevent direct fibroblast activation by LPS

Step 6 | Separator Valve Opening and Cytokine Gradient Formation
  Operation       : Separator valve opened; peristaltic sink pumping initiated simultaneously
  Tracer (QC)     : Cyanine 5 (Cy5) used to characterise gradient formation kinetics
  Gradient duration: 400 min (24000 s in IR); near region rises by 30 min; full equilibration ~400 min
  Sink pumping    : Gentle peristaltic; removes cytokines at far end; maintains gradient
  Detection       : gradientDetection module; 10 s
  QC gate (BB1->BB2/BB3): gradientSignal > 0 -> dispose(gradientChamber) [BB2];
                           gradientSignal <= 0 -> mix waste + drain [BB3]

Step 7 | Live-Cell NF-kB Translocation Imaging
  Duration        : 200 min (12000 s in IR) post separator opening
  Temperature     : 37 C / 5% CO2 / humidity controlled
  Quantification  : Nucleus/cytosol RelA-DsRed ratio per 3T3 (Kudo et al., 2018)
  Detection       : nfkbTranslocationDetection module; 30 s
  Notes (BB4)     : sinkFlow and gradientJoin are two distinct FreshMedium dispenses;

  Findings        : Signaling range correlates with macrophage number; buffered at ~60 macrophages;
                    near cells: rapid strong NF-kB then rapid decay;
                    far cells: slower, lower amplitude, more heterogeneous oscillatory response
  QC gate (BB4->BB5/BB6): nfkbSignal > 0 -> dispose(imagingChamber) [BB5];
                           nfkbSignal <= 0 -> mix waste + drain [BB6]

Step 8 | Spatially Resolved Cell Retrieval (Near / Mid / Far)
  TrypLE flow     : ~10 s (Gibco TrypLE)
  TrypLE incubation: ~60 s (partitioning valves closed before full detachment)
  Total detachment: 70 s (70 s mix duration in BioScript)
  Partitioning    : Pneumatic partitioning valves closed to isolate near / mid / far regions
  PBS retrieval   : Rapidly flowed through cell retrieval side channels to outlet
  Collection      : ~100 cells per region collected as ~2 uL droplet at outlet
  Lysis           : Deposited into 10 uL ice-cold lysis buffer (0.1% Triton-X-100 + RNase inhibitor, Takara)
  Storage         : Biological intent: -80 C long-term cryostorage

  Timepoints      : 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 h post separator opening; triplicate at each
  Detection       : geneExpressionDetection module on nearLysate; 30 s
  QC gate (BB7->BB8/BB9): geneExprSignal > 0 -> dispose lysates [BB8];
                           geneExprSignal <= 0 -> mix waste per region + drain [BB9]

Step 9 | Downstream qPCR Gene Expression Quantification
  Pipeline        : SmartSeq2 reverse transcription + pre-amplification (Picelli et al., 2014)
  Genes           : Tnfaip3 (A20), Casp4, Ccl5 (RANTES), GAPDH (control)
  Replicates      : Triplicate per timepoint per region
  Normalisation   : Each gene level normalised to maximum across all samples
  Simulation      : NF-kB dynamics input to ODE; degradation rate varied 20-fold (Fig. 4C);
                    degradation rate explains distance-dependent patterns


SUPPLEMENTAL ARM: Fixed-Dose TNF-a Stimulation (Section 3.4, Fig. 4)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Rationale       : Macrophage variability (Fig. 3C) prevents reproducible NF-kB profiles across

                  degradation rate determines distance sensitivity of NF-kB target gene expression


CELL PATTERNING ARM: Spatial Distribution of Sentinel Cells (Section 3.5, Fig. 5)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cell lines      : Primary murine adult fibroblasts (RelA-YFP) + BMMΦ (RelA-YFP knock-in mouse)
LPS dose        : 3 ng/mL; sub-threshold for direct fibroblast activation
Patterning      : Macrophages loaded at near (0-0.5 mm) or mid (1-1.5 mm) position via side channels

ASSAY TYPE: Picoliter-Scale Electrowetting Digital Microfluidic Pyrosequencing (Bead-Bound DNA Extension Coupled to ATP-Sulfurylase/Luciferase Chemiluminescent Detection)

REAGENTS USED:

  - Polymerase (DNA polymerase used to catalyze template-directed nucleotide incorporation)
  - dNTP (single deoxynucleotide triphosphate, e.g. dATP, cyclically dispensed one base at a time during sequencing-by-synthesis)
  - APS (adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate, substrate for ATP sulfurylase)
  - ATP Sulfurylase (enzyme converting released pyrophosphate + APS into ATP)
  - Luciferin (D-luciferin substrate for firefly luciferase, 400 ug/mL working concentration)
  - Luciferase (QuantiLum recombinant firefly luciferase, 1.0-2.0 ug/uL working concentration for optimal picoliter-scale signal)
  - Wash Buffer (50 mM TRIS pH 7.6, 5.0 mM magnesium acetate, 0.5 mM EDTA, 1.0 mM DTT, 0.01-0.02% wt Tween 20, used to rinse beads between cycles and prevent cross-contamination)

STEPS:
1. Bead loading: Dispense the DNA-bound paramagnetic bead droplet and a polymerase droplet, magnetically hold the beads at the reservoir exit, and mix to form the primed template droplet.
2-5. Nucleotide addition (repeated once per base in the sequencing cycle): Dispense a single dNTP droplet and mix it with the bead-bound template so that, per Equation 1 (DNA + dNTP --Polymerase--> DNA-dNP + PPi), a correct incorporation releases pyrophosphate (PPi) into the droplet.
6. ATP generation: Dispense APS and ATP sulfurylase droplets and sequentially mix them with the extension droplet so that, per Equation 2 (PPi + APS --ATP Sulfurylase--> ATP + SO4^2-), the released PPi is converted to ATP.
7. Chemiluminescent detection: Dispense luciferin and luciferase droplets and sequentially mix them with the ATP-containing droplet so that, per Equation 3 (ATP + Luciferin + O2 --Luciferase--> AMP + PPi + Oxyluciferin + CO2 + Light), light is produced in proportion to the amount of ATP (and therefore the number of bases incorporated); observe/quantify the resulting chemiluminescence intensity with a cooled CCD camera over a fixed exposure window.
8. Signal evaluation and bead rinse: If the detected intensity falls below the empirically determined limit-of-detection threshold (~7 nM ATP equivalent, S/N = 5), dispose of the reacted droplet and re-form the bead-bound template by mixing the magnetically-held beads with a fresh wash-buffer droplet before the next cycle, to eliminate dilution/cross-contamination effects; otherwise carry the reacted droplet forward as the template for the next nucleotide-addition cycle.
9. Cycle repeat: Repeat steps 2-8 for each subsequent base in the sequencing run.
10. Final rinse and disposal: After the sequencing cycles are complete, rinse the bead-bound template with successive wash-buffer droplets to remove residual reagent, then discard.

INTERPRETATION: Successful pyrosequencing chemistry on the picoliter-scale device is confirmed by a linear chemiluminescence response to ATP concentration (limit of detection ~7 nM ATP, corresponding to single-nucleotide incorporation on ~2 amol of DNA in a 300 pL droplet) and by luciferase-concentration optimization (1.0-2.0 ug/uL) yielding sufficient initial peak intensity for reliable detection despite the inherently lower light output at picoliter droplet volumes, supporting the feasibility of miniaturized digital-microfluidic pyrosequencing for low-reagent-volume, field-portable DNA sequencing.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Expansion of Patient-Derived Circulating Tumor Cells from Liquid Biopsies Using a CTC Microfluidic Culture Device
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2017.125
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2017.125
Journal      : Nature Protocols, 2018, Vol. 13, No. 1, pp. 34-58
Platform     : Three-layer PDMS microfluidic device (gradient generator / barrier layer / microwell array) fabricated by soft lithography


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidics-based method for the ex vivo expansion of patient-derived
circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from liquid biopsies (peripheral blood) into CTC clusters, without
prior enrichment or exogenous growth factor supplements. The approach co-cultures CTCs with
patient-derived white blood cells (WBCs) in inverted dome-shaped elliptical microwells under
hypoxia (1% O2, 37 C), mimicking the tumor microenvironment niche. Monocyte-derived macrophages
within the co-culture differentiate into tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and are proposed as
key drivers of cluster formation.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. Device priming and gradient generator calibration with FITC fluorescent dye (Steps 53-71)
  2. Blood preparation: RBC lysis and nucleated cell resuspension (Steps 72-77)
  3. CTC cluster culture in microwells under hypoxia for 14 days (Steps 78-79)
  4. Drug screening using the integrated gradient generator (Step 82)
  5. Immunofluorescence staining and imaging of CTC clusters (Steps 83-86)

Optional downstream procedures include post-enrichment with anti-CD45 microbeads (Step 81)
and DNA/RNA FISH for cancer cell identification (Steps 87-99).

Overall cluster formation success rate: >50% of clinical blood samples.
Assay duration from blood draw to cluster read-out: 2 weeks.
Drug screening after cluster formation: 48 h drug exposure + fluorescence read-out.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Concentration gradient generator (uppermost).
            Fabricated by standard PDMS replica molding on silicon wafer / SU-8 master
            (photolithography). Tree-like branched channel network splits two inlet streams
            into 8 output channels with a stable concentration gradient.
            Inlets: 2 (drug / vehicle control). Outlets: 8 channels.

Layer ii  : Barrier layer (middle).
            Fabricated from aluminum mold by machining; PDMS soft replica.
            Millimeter-scale barrier channels compartmentalise the 8 gradient outputs into
            individual cell-culture lanes, preventing cross-mixing at the microwell region.

Layer iii : Microwell layer (bottom).
            Fabricated by diffuser back-side lithography on a 4-inch soda lime mask plate
            coated with SU-8 3050 (double coat, >300 um total thickness).
            Opal diffuser (45 deg) generates dome-shaped exposure profile.
            Results in inverted dome-shaped elliptical microwells:
            150 um (width) x 250 um (length) x 150 um (depth); average diameter 187.5 um.
            1350 microwells per 60-mm Petri dish (laser ablation variant).
            8 columns of microwells aligned to 8 barrier channels.

Assembly   : Layers bonded by oxygen plasma treatment (150 W, 0.05 torr, 90 s) forming
             covalent -O-Si-O- bonds; baked at 80 C for >=1 h.
Material   : PDMS (Sylgard 184, 10:1 base:curing agent); biocompatible, optically
             transparent (240-1100 nm), elastomeric for accurate replica molding.

Alternate microwell fabrication: Laser ablation (CO2 laser, VLS 2.30; 10% speed, 50% power;
             laser-to-substrate distance 3 cm) on 35- or 60-mm Petri dishes (Box 1).

--------------------------------
- MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 (ATCC): commercially available breast cancer cell lines used for
  device characterisation and spheroid formation validation.
  Culture: DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen-strep, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- Patient blood samples: 10 mL per patient, EDTA Vacutainer tubes, kept on ice.
  Cancer types validated: breast, lung, spinal cancer; locally advanced, early-stage,
  and refractory metastatic disease.
  Ethical approval: DSRB references 2012/00105, 2012/00979, 2010/00270, 2010/00691.

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 53-56 | Device Priming
  Reagents  : 70% (vol/vol) ethanol, PBS (1x)
  Operation : Two syringes of 70% ethanol injected at 50 uL/min (~5 min) via two syringe pumps
              to prime the gradient generator and remove air bubbles. Followed by two syringes
              of PBS at 100 uL/min (~5 min) to remove ethanol residue.
  Purpose   : Hydrophilise PDMS channels; remove air; sterilise device before cell culture.
  Critical  : Replace syringe by disconnecting from tip (not tubing) to avoid new air bubbles.

Step 57-68 | Gradient Generator Calibration (FITC Dye)
  Reagents  : 100 uM FITC fluorescent dye (fluorescein isothiocyanate isomer I) in PBS,
              deionised (DI) water
  Operation : Syringe 1 (FITC dye) and Syringe 2 (DI water) pumped simultaneously at equal
              flow rates. After 30 min equilibration, 60 uL collected from each of the 8
              channels into a 384-well plate (Tecan Infinite M200 fluorescence plate reader).
  Flow rates : 25, 50, 100, 150, 200 uL/min (5 independent runs per device).
  Additional : 20 uM FITC at 100 uL/min to confirm concentration-independence of gradient.
  Repeats   : Three independent devices (Step 68).
  Results   : Concentration gradients similar across flow rates; close to theoretical values;
              no leakage observed; gradient independent of dye concentration.
  Purpose   : Verify uniform outlet flow rates, stable gradient generation, and device integrity.

Step 72-73 | Blood Preparation - RBC Lysis
  Reagents  : Patient blood (10 mL, EDTA Vacutainer), RBC lysis buffer (G-Bioscience 786650)
  Ratio     : 10 mL blood + 20 mL RBC lysis buffer (1:2 vol/vol)
  Duration  : 3 min at room temperature with gentle mixing (hypotonic hemolysis by osmotic stress)
  Critical  : Both blood and buffer at room temperature before mixing. Do not exceed 5 min.

Step 74-75 | Nucleated Cell Isolation
  Operation : Centrifuge lysed sample 1000g, 5 min, room temperature. Remove supernatant
              (plasma + lysed RBC fragments). Resuspend pellet in 5 mL PBS; centrifuge 335g,
              3 min to wash. Repeat wash if debris remains.
  Result    : Nucleated cell fraction (WBCs + CTCs); RBC lysis does not significantly affect
              nucleated cell viability.
  Storage   : Optional: add 10% (vol/vol) DMSO; cryopreserve at -80 C up to 4 weeks;
              long-term in liquid nitrogen up to 1 year.

Step 76-77 | Cell Resuspension and Seeding
  Reagents  : Supplemented DMEM (10% FBS, 1% pen-strep)
  Volume    : Resuspend in 1 mL per 1000 microwells; add 200-300 uL per channel.
  Seeding   : Volume-based (not count-based); multichannel pipette for simultaneous seeding.
  Culture   : 37 C, 5% CO2, 1% O2 (hypoxia incubator, humidified). Day 0.
  Note      : No surfactant coating required for clinical samples; non-adherent blood cells
              provide cushioning for CTCs in microwells.

Step 78 | Day-3 Media Change
  Operation : Remove 0.2 mL old medium (hand pipette or syringe pump at 200 uL/min).
              Replace with 0.2 mL fresh supplemented DMEM.
  Critical  : Minimal disturbance to microwell clusters to prevent cell loss.
              Increase frequency of media change if media turns yellow before 72 h.

Step 79 | Day-14 Cluster Assessment
  Operation : Phase-contrast microscopy of full microwell array.
  Criteria  :
    Morphological : Multilayered cell aggregate with defined boundaries.
    Cell count    : >=8 cells per 250 um^2 (Hoechst staining, Step 83A/83B).
    Cell density  : Low grayscale values in ImageJ histogram of microwell region.
  Threshold : >=50% microwells contain clusters = positive sample.
  Results   : >50% cluster formation rate across >300 clinical samples screened;

  Note      : Cultures can be retained up to 2 months; can be passaged as spheroids to

ASSAY TYPE: Tissue-Digital Microfluidic Isolation of Single Cells for -Omics (tDISCO) for Spatially-Resolved Single-Cell Transcriptomic and Proteomic Profiling of Proximal vs. Distal Astrocytes after Ischemic Stroke

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cryosectioned Brain Tissue Biopsy (2 mm diameter punch from a cortical stroke tissue section, mounted on the tDISCO top-plate)
  - Fixation Reagent (paraformaldehyde-based fixative, applied on-chip)
  - DAPI Nuclear Stain (marks all nuclei)
  - Anti-GFAP Antibody (fluorescent astrocyte marker)
  - Anti-NEUN Antibody (fluorescent neuronal marker)
  - Cell Lysis/Receiving Buffer (droplet positioned above the tissue for laser-induced single-cell lysis and lysate collection)

STEPS:
1. Mount a 2 mm cryosectioned cortical tissue biopsy onto the tDISCO top-plate.
2. Fix the mounted tissue biopsy in place on-chip using the fixation reagent.
3. Stain the fixed tissue on-chip with DAPI, anti-GFAP, and anti-NEUN to mark nuclei, astrocytes, and neurons, respectively.
4. Image the stained tissue at low magnification (20X) to map DAPI+/GFAP+ and DAPI+/NEUN+ cells and record their distance from the stroke lesion.
5. Select a single target cell (e.g., a GFAP+ astrocyte at a defined distance from the injury site) and re-image at high magnification (100X) to confirm its identity and position before lysis.
6. Dispense a receiving-buffer droplet and use digital microfluidic actuation to position it directly over the selected single cell.
7. Fire the focused laser at the targeted cell to induce a cavitation bubble that mechanically lyses the cell, releasing its contents into the overlying receiving-buffer droplet.
8. Actuate the single-cell lysate droplet away from the tissue for downstream -omics processing (library preparation for transcriptomics, or digestion for proteomics).
9. Replenish a fresh receiving-buffer droplet over the same tissue section and repeat steps 5-8 to iteratively isolate additional single cells (e.g., a second GFAP+ astrocyte at a different lesion distance, or a DAPI+/NEUN+ neuron) from the same biopsy.
10. Pool/queue the collected single-cell lysate droplets for transcriptomic (RNA-seq) and proteomic (LC-MS/MS) analysis, comparing molecular profiles across cells at varying distances from the stroke lesion to resolve the spatial boundaries of the astrocyte response.

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Actuator Bead-Based Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Cardiac Marker Detection (cTnI / CK-MB / Myoglobin)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cardiac Sample (biological sample, e.g. whole blood, serum, or plasma, containing a cardiac marker such as cardiac troponin I, CK-MB, or myoglobin)
  - Capture Beads (magnetically responsive beads coated with primary capture antibody)
  - Blocking Antibody (blocking protein/antibody reagent)
  - Reporter Antibody (secondary reporter antibody)
  - Wash Buffer (droplet-based merge-and-split dilution wash buffer, 0.05M TRIS, 0.1 M NaCl, 0.1 mg/mL BSA, 0.02% Tween20, pH 9.5)
  - Chemiluminescent Substrate (detection substrate, e.g. APS-5)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a cardiac sample droplet, a capture-bead droplet, and a blocking-antibody droplet.
2. Mix the capture beads with the blocking antibody to form reagent 1.
3. Combine the sample droplet with reagent 1 to form the assay droplet; incubate at room temperature (~23C) for 3 minutes to allow capture antibody-antigen binding.
4. Execute a droplet-based wash step: merge the assay droplet with wash buffer and discard the resulting supernatant, removing unbound sample material.
5. Dispense a reporter-antibody droplet and merge it with the assay droplet; incubate 2 minutes at room temperature to form the capture-antibody-antigen-reporter-antibody complex.
6. Execute a droplet-based wash protocol (11 repeated merge-and-split dilution washes with wash buffer) to deplete unbound reporter antibody and antigen from the bead droplet.
7. Combine the washed bead droplet with chemiluminescent substrate; incubate ~2 minutes at 25C.
8. Detect the chemiluminescent signal for 5 seconds, indicative of the quantity of the cardiac marker in the biological sample.
9. If the measured signal exceeds the top-end of the standard curve, execute an auto-dilution sequence (merge with a diluent droplet, re-detect) to bring the concentration back within the linear range of detection.
10. Discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful cardiac marker quantification is confirmed by a calibration curve relating chemiluminescent response (counts/s) to marker concentration (ng/mL) for cTn-I, CK-MB, and myoglobin, with good linearity and recovery percentages clustered near 100% across the calibrator concentration range, and with total assay time (sample loading to detectable signal) of well under 5-10 minutes for multiplexed cardiac marker panels, supporting use of the platform for rapid triage of chest-pain patients and assessment of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) risk.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Cellular Decision Making by Non-Integrative Processing of TLR Inputs
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(17)30359-5
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2017.03.027
Journal      : Cell Reports, 2017, Vol. 19, pp. 125-135
Platform     : Automated microfluidic cell culture chip + widefield live-cell fluorescence microscopy


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a single-cell live-imaging microfluidic approach to study how cells process
simultaneous inflammatory signalling inputs through a shared downstream pathway. Mouse 3T3 fibroblasts
expressing p65-DsRed at near-endogenous levels are cultured in automated microfluidic chambers and
stimulated with combinatorial TLR4 (LPS) and TLR2 (PAM) agonists across a 3x3 dose matrix. NF-kB
nuclear translocation dynamics are quantified continuously over 8 hours at single-cell resolution.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Automated microfluidic cell culture: fibronectin coating, cell seeding, pre-culture,
     and 9-condition LPS x PAM co-stimulation matrix (step increase via chamber media exchange)
  2. NF-kB live imaging and bagging classifier-based response classification:
     single cells classified as LPS-like, PAM-like, or uncertain/mixed using a
     trained ensemble of N=50 decision-tree classifiers (n=0.6 majority vote threshold)
  3. Sequential cross-tolerance stimulation: two schemes test TLR cross-tolerance mediated
     by shared negative feedback (IkB, A20, miR-146a) at the TRAF6 node
  4. miR-146a TaqMan qPCR validation: bulk stimulation + RNA isolation + two-step
     qPCR confirms miR-146a as the slow, sustained, ultrasensitive negative feedback
     that mediates PAM response shutoff and enables cross-TLR tolerance

The central finding is "non-integrative processing": under TLR2-TLR4 co-stimulation, single cells
respond with an NF-kB dynamic profile characteristic of either TLR4 (LPS-like) or TLR2 (PAM-like)
activation, rather than a mixed or combined response. This is mediated by switch-like NF-kB activation,
receptor-specific processing timescales (endosomal delay for TLR2), cell-to-cell variability in TLR
receptor numbers, and multilayer negative feedback enabling cross-tolerance.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Platform     : Automated microfluidic cell culture system (Gomez-Sjoberg et al. Anal. Chem. 2007;
               Kellogg et al. Nat. Protoc. 2014; Kellogg & Tay, Cell 2015)
Chamber size : 1.12 mm x 0.9 mm x 0.040 mm per chamber
Cells/chamber: ~100 cells at imaging; seeded at 200 cells/chamber
Parallelism  : All 9 LPS-PAM dose combinations run in parallel on a single chip
               Duplicate chambers per condition (2 chambers per LPS-PAM combination)
Atmosphere   : 37 C, 5% CO2; maintained via on-stage incubation chamber
Stimulus     : Delivered as step increase (chamber media exchange); stimulus vials
               pressured with 5% CO2, kept on ice before delivery
Post-stim    : Chambers sealed immediately after stimulus delivery
Imaging      : 5-6 min interval acquisitions for 480 min (8 hours)


CELL LINE
---------
Mouse 3T3 fibroblasts (p65^(-/-) background):
  - Re-express p65-DsRed under control of 1.5 kb endogenous p65 promoter
  - Clonally derived to express p65-DsRed at near-endogenous (lowest detectable) level
  - H2B-GFP nuclear marker driven by ubiquitin promoter (automated cell tracking)
  - Culture: DMEM complete media, 37 C, 5% CO2, no antibiotics
  - Reference: Tay et al. Nature 2010; Lee et al. Sci. Signal. 2009


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Chamber Coating
  Reagents  : Fibronectin, PBS wash
  Operation : Chamber perfusion coating (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Duration  : 5 min
  Purpose   : Promotes 3T3 fibroblast adhesion to PDMS chamber surface.
              Excess fibronectin removed with PBS wash.

Step 2 | Cell Seeding and Pre-culture
  Cell line : Mouse 3T3 p65-DsRed (p65^(-/-))
  Density   : 200 cells/chamber (seeding); ~100 cells/chamber at imaging
  Media     : DMEM complete (37 C, 5% CO2)
  Duration  : 24 h (= 1440 min; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  Target    : ~80% confluence before stimulation
  Notes     : Periodic media replenishment during pre-culture. Incubation
              chamber maintains 37 C and 5% CO2 on microscope stage.

Step 3 | Pre-stimulation Media Refresh
  Reagents  : DMEM complete (fresh, CO2-equilibrated)
  Duration  : 1 min
  Purpose   : Removes conditioned media; establishes NF-kB baseline before stimulus.

Step 4 | Combinatorial LPS x PAM Co-stimulation (9-condition 3x3 matrix)
  TLR4 agonist : Ultrapure LPS (Invivogen); TLR4-exclusive activation
                 Doses: 100, 33, 11 ng/mL
  TLR2 agonist : Pam3CSK4 (PAM, Invivogen); synthetic triacylated lipopeptide; TLR2 via endosome
                 Doses: 40, 13.3, 4.4 ng/mL
  Conditions   : 9 combinations (C1-C9); 2 duplicate chambers each; 18 chambers total
  Primary cond : C9 (LPS 11 ng/mL + PAM 4.4 ng/mL) -- most distinct LPS/PAM dynamics
                 used as representative condition for bagging classifier CFG gate
  Delivery     : Step increase via microfluidic media exchange; all vials pressured with
                 5% CO2 and kept on ice; delivered to parallel chambers on single chip
  Imaging      : Chambers sealed post-delivery; 5-6 min intervals for 480 min

  Dose matrix (ng/mL):
    LPS\PAM  |  40     |  13.3   |  4.4
    ---------+---------+---------+------
    100      |  C1     |  C2     |  C3
    33       |  C4     |  C5     |  C6
    11       |  C7     |  C8     |  C9*
    (* primary mechanistic condition)

Step 5 | NF-kB Live Imaging and Bagging Classifier Detection
  Microscope   : Leica DMI6000B widefield, 20x magnification
  Camera       : Retiga-SRV CCD (QImaging)
  Light source : Leica EL6000 mercury metal halide
  Channels     : DsRed (Y3 filter, NF-kB signal); GFP (L5 filter, H2B nuclear marker)
  Quantification: Mean nuclear DsRed / mean cytoplasm DsRed intensity ratio
  Tracking     : CellProfiler (automated) + custom MATLAB
  Peak analysis: MATLAB smooth + mspeaks; features: first peak intensity, max peak time
  Classifier   : Bagging classifier (N=50 decision trees, n=0.6 majority vote threshold)
                 Implemented via MATLAB fitensemble ('Bag','Tree','Classification')
                 Training: single-stimulus LPS and PAM trajectories at matched doses
                 Output: LPS-like / PAM-like / Uncertain (mixed) per cell
                 Accuracy: 89% overall; >=85% per condition (10-fold CV)
  Key results  : C9 (LPS 11 + PAM 4.4 ng/mL): ~40-50% LPS-like, ~40-50% PAM-like, ~15% mixed
                 C1 (LPS 100 + PAM 40 ng/mL): ~90% LPS-like
                 C7 (LPS 11 + PAM 40 ng/mL): ~90% PAM-like
  Gate         : classifySignal > 0 -> non-integrative (>80% LPS- or PAM-like) -> BB2 (pass)
                 classifySignal <= 0 -> integrative/mixed dominant -> BB3 (fail)

Step 6 | Sequential Stimulation Scheme A: LPS First, PAM at +2 hr
  Cell line     : Mouse 3T3 p65-DsRed (fresh chambers; parallel chip run)
  First stim    : LPS 11 ng/mL at t=0
  Interval      : 120 min incubation at 37 C, 5% CO2 (heat step in BioScript)
  Second stim   : PAM 13.3 ng/mL at t=120 min (delivered to same chamber)
  Imaging       : Continuous throughout (480 min total window)
  Detection     : nfkbLiveImagingDetection (480 min)
  Results (Fig 5C):
    53% cells responded to LPS only (LPS-induced IkB/A20/miR-146a blocked PAM response)
    30% cells responded to PAM only (LPS-refractory; caught by PAM at +2 hr)
    17% cells responded to both stimuli (incomplete negative feedback suppression)
  Interpretation: Rapid negative feedback induced by LPS sufficient to inhibit subsequent
                 PAM response in majority of pre-activated cells.

Step 7 | Sequential Stimulation Scheme B: PAM First, LPS at +4 hr
  Cell line     : Mouse 3T3 p65-DsRed (fresh chambers; parallel chip run)
  First stim    : PAM 13.3 ng/mL at t=0
  Interval      : 240 min incubation at 37 C, 5% CO2 (ensures miR-146a fully induced;
                  PAM onset ~2 hr; 240 min interval allows sustained expression to build)
  Second stim   : LPS 100 ng/mL at t=240 min (high dose to maximally challenge pre-activated cells)
  Imaging       : Continuous throughout (480 min total window)
  Detection     : nfkbLiveImagingDetection (480 min)
  Cross-tol gate: crossToleranceDetection on Scheme A signal (30 s detection)
                  crossTolSignal > 0 -> cross-tolerance confirmed -> BB5 (pass)
                  crossTolSignal <= 0 -> no cross-tolerance -> BB6 (fail)
  Results (Fig 5D):
    84% cells responded to PAM only (A20/miR-146a fully blocked high-dose LPS response)
    16% cells responded to both stimuli
  Interpretation: Moderate PAM stimulus activated all cells; sustained A20/miR-146a negative
                 feedback mediated cross-TLR tolerance, blocking even high-dose LPS at +4 hr.
                 Cross-tolerance operates via shared TRAF6 node downstream of both TLR2 and TLR4.

Step 8 | miR-146a TaqMan qPCR Validation
  Purpose       : Validate miR-146a as slow, sustained, ultrasensitive negative feedback
                  responsible for PAM response shutoff (Fig 2C) and cross-TLR tolerance
  Cell line     : Mouse 3T3 (bulk flasks; off-chip, not single-cell microfluidics)
  Stimuli       : LPS 10 ng/mL and PAM 10 ng/mL (separate flasks; not co-stimulation)
  Time course   : RNA harvested at 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 hr post-stimulation (480 min)
  Incubation    : 37 C, 5% CO2 (heat step in BioScript; 480 min per arm)
  RNA isolation : mirVana miRNA isolation kit (Ambion); TrizolReagent abstraction in BioScript
  cDNA synthesis: TaqMan microRNA reverse transcription kit (Applied Biosystems)
  qPCR assay    : TaqMan miRNA-specific assay hsa-miR-146a (cross-reactive with murine miR-146a)
  Normalisation : snoRNA234 snRNA endogenous control (Applied Biosystems)
  Thermocycler  : 95 C denaturation (15 s/cycle) + 60 C annealing/extension (60 s/cycle), 40 cycles
                  Total per arm: 2 x 50 min heat steps (BioScript; 95 C then 60 C)
  Detection     : miR146aExpressionDetection module; representative gate on LPS arm
                  miR146aSignal > 0 -> sustained induction confirmed -> BB8 (pass)
                  miR146aSignal <= 0 -> no induction -> BB9 (fail)
  Results (Fig 2C):
    LPS onset   : ~1 hr post-stimulation
    PAM onset   : ~2 hr post-stimulation
    Profile     : Sustained high expression for >6 hr (unlike IkB/A20 which return to baseline)
    Role        : Slow feedback via TRAF6 mRNA cleavage (also IRAK1/2); Hill coefficient 4
                  in ODE model (ultrasensitivity); explains rising-amplitude PAM oscillations
                  and abrupt shutoff at 300-400 min under low-dose PAM stimulation


MATHEMATICAL MODEL SUMMARY
--------------------------
Type         : ODE system; mass-action / Michaelis-Menten / Hill kinetics
Base         : Extended from Kellogg et al. eLife 2015 (LPS/TLR4 NF-kB model)
               and Tay et al. Nature 2010 (TNF NF-kB model)
Noise        : Receptor-level extrinsic noise only; TLR4 and TLR2 total counts are
               lognormally distributed (mu_R, sigma_R parameters)
Simulation   : 500 cells per condition; only active trajectories considered
Key features :
  - TLR4 (LPS): surface membrane signalling; rapid TRAF6a(LPS) accumulation
  - TLR2 (PAM): endosomal processing modelled as low binding (kf) + low unbinding (kr);
                 slow TRAF6a(PAM) accumulation; integrator-like PAM.TLR2 complex dynamics
  - Fast feedback : IkBa (principal fast feedback); A20
  - Slow feedback : miR-146a (Hill coefficient 4; ultrasensitive); targets TRAF6 mRNA
  - IKK activation: cooperative TRAF6 clustering (Hill term); switch-like NF-kB response
  - Non-integrative mechanism: LPS fires first (no endosomal delay); IkB/A20/miR-146a
    feedback prevents PAM response in TLR4-sensitive cells; TLR4-refractory cells receive
    PAM signal unimpeded. Switch-like activation polarises each cell to one outcome.
  - TRIF pathway excluded: inactive in 3T3 fibroblasts (A. Hoffmann, personal communication)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet On Tape: Protocol
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-on-tape-protocol-n2bvj9wzblk5/v1
DOI Link     : https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/protex.2017.017
Journal      : Nature Protocols Exchange, February 28, 2017
Platform     : Acoustic Droplet Ejection (ADE) onto Kapton conveyor belt (DOT system) for XFEL sample delivery
Associated   : Fuller et al., Nature Methods, 2017; DOI: 10.1038/nmeth.4195


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the Droplet On Tape (DOT) system, a flexible sample delivery platform
coupling Acoustic Droplet Ejection (ADE) with a moving Kapton conveyor belt for time-resolved
X-ray studies at X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs). DOT enables simultaneous X-ray Diffraction
(XRD) and X-ray Emission Spectroscopy (XES) from protein microcrystal slurry or protein
solution, along with ancillary signals (transmission, fluorescence). It supports multiple
reaction initiation schemes: laser flash photolysis (single-excitation free-space timing and
multi-step fiber excitation) and gas-phase activation (differential pumping of reactive gas).

The platform is designed for restricted-access beamline environments and is operated entirely
via remote control (EPICS framework). The DOT system is comprised of five main sub-systems:
the ADE injector, control systems, the conveyor belt, the sample environment (Helium enclosure),
and reaction initiation systems.

Typical beamline deployment: 5 days setup (3 people); 4-5 days data collection per experiment.
Custom fabrication of all components: ~1 month (machining) + ~1 month (assembly, 2 people).


SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Five integrated sub-systems:

Sub-system 1 | ADE Injector
  Transducer   : Olympus V319-SU, 1 inch spherical focus, 15 MHz resonance frequency
                 (developed for ultrasonic imaging applications)
  Waveform gen.: Agilent 33612A; tone-burst at 15 MHz, controllable amplitude and duration
  Amplifier    : Amplifier Research 500A250C RF amplifier; final driving voltage ~40 V
  Ejection     : Tone-burst <100 us ejects nano-liter droplet from sample-air interface
  Coupling     : BNC cable -> bi-directional coupler (30 dB) -> transducer
                 Bi-directional coupler samples forward and reverse signals
  Echo probe   : "probe" spike (few hundred ns) sent a few ms before ejection burst
                 Sonar principle: echo return at ~35 us delay (1 inch focal length transducer)
                 at correct focus; fluid level monitored with <50 um accuracy
                 Oscilloscope monitored remotely via remote desktop (critical at beamline hutch)
  Sample path  : Polymicro tubing (360 um O.D., 180-250 um I.D.) from Legato 130 syringe pump
                 to ADE reservoir; coupling water column isolates sample from transducer

Sub-system 2 | Control Systems
  Framework    : EPICS (Experimental Physics Industrial Control Software)
  Hardware     : Syringe pump (Legato 130), Waveform generator (Agilent 33612A),
                 Actuator motors (Newport XPS-Q8), Tape drive motor (Lexium M-Drive),
                 Cameras (Allied Vision Manta-style)
  Custom IOCs  : Syringe pump: https://github.com/fullerf/LEGATO130
                 Waveform generator: https://github.com/fullerf/Agilent33600A
  Dependencies : EPICS base, StreamDevice, Asyn
  Tape drive   : Lexium M-Drive connected via built-in serial terminal; telnet from Linux/Mac
                 Speed controlled via motor slew rate adjustments (infrequently needed after
                 initial calibration)

Sub-system 3 | Conveyor Belt System
  Belt type    : Seamless Kapton (polyimide, Kapton 100H, C22H10O2N5, DuPont)
                 0.063-0.125 inch width; 31-36 inch diameter; 50 micron thickness
                 Supplier: BPB Inc., Bay Area, CA (custom request)
  Why seamless : Ultrasonically welded belts skip at weld over rollers, disrupting XFEL
                 synchronisation. Seamless belts eliminate this problem.
  Alternative  : Mylar film (used early in development; inferior x-ray scattering vs Kapton)
  Consumable   : Yes; one belt lasts several shifts if XFEL beam does not directly hit it
  Surface tmt  : FAS (1H,1H,2H,2H-Perfluorodecyltriethoxysilane, 97%, Sigma-Aldrich) in
                 n-octane; WCA increased from ~60 deg to 100 +/- 5 deg (see protocol below)
  Tensioner    : Hanging weight on rotating arm; two crowned rollers; adjustable by adding or
                 removing weights; over-tension indicator: belt curls when tension released
  Rollers      : ABEC 5 low-friction ball bearings with CNC-machined crown cap (3 inch radius
                 of curvature); crown keeps belt centred during operation
  Electrostatic: Passive: steel anti-static brushes near drive mechanism
                 Active: Transforming Technologies IN3425 static gun (ionised air) near ADE
                 deposition point; both required to avoid disrupting ADE ejection
  Mounting     : Newport UTS-100 motorised stage; modified Thorlabs aluminium breadboards
  Drive motor  : Lexium M-Drive LMDCE423 micro-stepping stepper motor; direct drive to 1 inch
                 stainless steel shaft; <4 revolutions/s typical operating speed
                 (geared mechanism abandoned due to velocity error introduction)

Sub-system 4 | Sample Environment
  Enclosure    : Custom acrylic (0.5 inch) helium chamber; Professional Plastics Inc.
  Door         : Large inflatable door with wide aperture at X-ray interaction region
  Joints       : Solvent welded (where possible); rubber foam gaskets elsewhere
  Feed-through : 0.125 inch aluminium panel, water-jet cut; handles all electronic, gas,
                 water, and fibre connections into the chamber
  Helium path  : Thin inflatable polyethylene bags extend helium environment from sample to
                 detector; second bag between XES crystal spectrometer and main chamber;
                 minimises scatter from heavier atoms in air during XRD/XES

Sub-system 5 | Reaction Initiation Systems
  Laser (fiber): High-precision CNC-machined grid (tolerance 0.0005 inch); holds 3 excitation
                 fibre-coupled laser inputs and 2 IR gate fibres
                 IR gate separation: 60 mm; each gate 30 mm from nearest excitation point
                 Each excitation fibre: 5 degrees of freedom for coupling optimisation
                 Droplet arrival monitored via IR scatter onto photodiode
                 All 5 fibres monitored on remote-accessible oscilloscopes
  Laser (free) : Single-excitation; movable 1 m focal-length motorised lens upstream of XFEL
                 Max laser advance: 6 mm upstream of XFEL interaction
                 Time delay range: 20-100 ms (at 300-60 mm/s belt speed)
                 Spatial overlap: 100 um accuracy (laser spot: ~400 um diameter)
                 Temporal overlap: 200 us accuracy (camera exposure); ns via photodiode
  Gas reaction : Conveyor belt passes through limited-extent reactive gas region (O2 example)
                 Confinement: differential pumping via series of small orifices
                 Exposure time: L / v_tape; Dead time: L_xfel / v_tape
                 Sealing: vacuum grease on all openings except belt entry and exit holes


BELT SURFACE TREATMENT PROTOCOL
---------------------------------

Step 1 | Belt Cleaning
  Reagents  : Milli-Q water, isopropanol
  Action    : Sonicate in Milli-Q water for 10 min; then sonicate in isopropanol for 10 min
  Notes     : Removes surface contaminants before hydrophobicity treatment

Step 2 | Vacuum Drying (pre-FAS)
  Equipment : Precision vacuum oven, model 19
  Condition : 50 C, 1 hour
  Notes     : Belt must be fully dry before FAS treatment; moisture interferes with silane
              bonding chemistry

Step 3 | FAS Hydrophobicity Treatment
  Reagent   : 0.25% (w/v) FAS (1H,1H,2H,2H-Perfluorodecyltriethoxysilane, Sigma-Aldrich)
              in n-octane
  Action    : Reflux belt in FAS/n-octane solution for 2 hours
  Result    : Water contact angle (WCA) increases from ~60 deg to 100 +/- 5 deg
  Purpose   : Aqueous droplets bead up on belt surface and do not spread; critical for
              maintaining droplet integrity during transport to XFEL interaction region

Step 4 | Vacuum Drying (post-FAS)
  Equipment : Precision vacuum oven, model 19
  Condition : 150 C, 3 hours
  Notes     : Removes all residual unreacted FAS from belt surface


BELT CLEANING PROCEDURE (in-experiment)
-----------------------------------------
  Method    : Drive belt through 4 high-pressure water jets (200+ psi, 500 um I.D.)
  Drying    : 2 compressed Helium blow-off nozzles (top and bottom of belt)
  Gas supply: 3 x KNF Neuberger N145.1.2AN.18 gas-tight diaphragm pumps draw Helium from
              the Helium chamber and recirculate it to power the blow-off nozzles
  Residue QC: Run belt dry (no sample injected); probe XES signal; accumulated residue
              detected as XES background above baseline; performed periodically during beamtimes


FIBER EXCITATION TIMING (Multi-excitation, e.g. Photosystem II)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
  Principle : Space-time diagram representation; constant belt velocity -> trajectories are
              straight lines with slope = velocity; excitation positions fixed in space/time
  Two DOF   : (1) deposition delay (Delta_tau_dep): when droplet is ejected onto belt
              (2) laser delay (Delta_tau_laser): when each fibre excitation fires
  Setup     :
    1. Adjust deposition delay until droplet appears in XFEL crosshairs (stroboscopic monitor)
    2. Fine-adjust deposition delay until droplet observed to explode (camera synced to XFEL)
    3. Confirm via solvent scatter in forward detector or emission signal in XES detector
    4. Adjust belt velocity until IR gate signals coincide in time
       (confirms droplets simultaneously present on all excitation points)
    5. Laser delay must be time-coincident with IR gate signals
  Allowed speeds at 10 Hz rep rate: 30, 60, 150, 300 mm/s
  (droplet spacing must be integer multiple or divisor of both 30 mm and 60 mm)
  Note      : Deposition delay and belt speed are coupled; adjust both incrementally
