PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) and Droplet Digital PCR (ddPCR) Protocol
Authors      : Katie Jing Kay Lam, Olubankole Arogundade, Claire Clelland
Affiliations : Weill Institute for Neurosciences, University of California, San Francisco, USA
               Department of Neurology, University of California, San Francisco, CA, USA
Contact      : claire.clelland@ucsf.edu
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-digital-pcr-ddpcr-kqdg3244ev25/v1
DOI Link     : https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kqdg3244ev25/v1
Platform     : Benchtop PCR (Bio-Rad Thermal Cycler) + Droplet Digital PCR (Bio-Rad QX200 system)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol covers two sequential, complementary molecular biology workflows:

  1. Standard PCR: DNA amplification from cultured mammalian cells extracted with QuickExtract,
     followed by gel electrophoresis QC on a Bio-Rad Sub-Cell GT system and fluorescence imaging
     on a LI-COR Odyssey M imager.

  2. Droplet Digital PCR (ddPCR): absolute quantification of target DNA copy number using a
     Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Generator and Droplet Reader, with a two-channel FAM/HEX probe
     design (target gene + RPP30 reference). ddPCR partitions the PCR reaction into ~20,000
     nanodroplets (~0.85 nL each), enabling Poisson-statistics-based absolute counting of
     positive (target-containing) vs. negative (empty) droplets without a standard curve.

An optional gel extraction module (Qiagen MinElute, modified) is included for downstream
sequencing applications requiring a larger 50 uL PCR reaction.

The BioScript encoding covers both workflows in a single file with a linear-sequential
structure: DNA extraction → PCR → gel QC gate (BB1-BB4) → ddPCR → droplet readout gate
(BB4-BB7). A total of 7 basic blocks and 2 if/else QC gates are generated.


PROTOCOL 1: STANDARD PCR
-------------------------

Step 1 | DNA Preparation by QuickExtract (96-well plate)
  Reagents   : PBS, QuickExtract DNA Extraction Solution (Biosearch Technologies, 76081-768)
  Operations :
    1. Wash cells with 100 uL PBS per well; aspirate.
    2. Add 30 uL QuickExtract per well.
    3. Scrape well bottom with pipette tip to detach cells.
    4. Transfer cells to labelled PCR tubes.
    5. Vortex 15 s.
    6. Incubate at 65 C for 6 min.
    7. Vortex 15 s.
    8. Incubate at 98 C for 2 min.
    9. Store at -20 C.
  Output     : PCR-ready DNA template (direct lysis, no column purification required)

Step 2 | Primer Preparation
  Working stock : 10 uM (diluted from 100 uM IDT stock)
  Preparation   :
    - Resuspend IDT lyophilised primers in H2O to 100 uM (e.g. 20 nmol -> add 200 uL H2O).
    - Dilute to 10 uM working stock in new microcentrifuge tube (20 uL + 180 uL H2O).
    - Store at -20 C.
  Design guidelines (PCR primers):
    - Length: 18-30 bases (~20 optimal); GC content: 40-60%.
    - 3' end should be G or C; avoid >3 consecutive G/C repeats.
    - Tm: 50-65 C; primer pairs within 5 C of each other.
    - Product length: 200-1000 bp (up to 2-3 kb if needed).
    - Tools: Primer-BLAST (NCBI), Primer3web, OligoCalc (Properties Calculator).
    - Order from IDT as Custom DNA oligos.

Step 3 | PCR Reaction Setup (20 uL)
  Master Mix for one 20 uL reaction:
    BioMix Red (Meridian Life Sciences, C755F25)     10.0 uL
    DMSO (Sigma Aldrich, D8418)                       0.6 uL
    Forward primer (10 uM)                            1.0 uL
    Reverse primer (10 uM)                            1.0 uL
    RNase/DNase-free H2O                              6.4 uL
    ------------------------------------------------ -------
    Total Master Mix                                 19.0 uL
    + 1 uL DNA template per tube                  -> 20 uL

  Setup: prepare Master Mix for (number of reactions + 1) as extra.
  Load into Bio-Rad Thermal Cycler.

  PCR for sequencing (with gel extraction): use 50 uL reaction; 2.5 uL DNA + 47 uL Master Mix.
    BioMix Red 25 uL | DMSO 1.5 uL | Fwd primer 2.5 uL | Rev primer 2.5 uL | H2O 16 uL.

Step 4 | PCR Thermocycling (Bio-Rad Thermal Cycler)
  Step | Name                 | Temperature | Time
  -----+----------------------+-------------+----------
    1  | Enzyme Activation    | 94 C        | 3 min
    2  | Denaturation         | 94 C        | 30 s
    3  | Annealing            | 50-65 C*    | 30 s
    4  | Primary Extension    | 72 C        | 1 min/kb
    5  | Repeat steps 2-4     | --          | x34
    6  | Secondary Extension  | 72 C        | 5 min
    7  | Hold                 | 4 C         | infinity
  *Annealing temperature: 5-10 C below primer Tm.

  PCR for sequencing cycle (39 amplification cycles, 50 uL reaction):
    Enzyme Activation 94 C 3.5 min -> Denature 94 C 45 s -> Anneal 50-65 C 45 s ->
    Extend 72 C 1 min/kb -> x39 -> Secondary Extension 72 C 5 min -> Hold 4 C.

Step 5 | Gel Electrophoresis
  Buffer preparation:
    1X TAE: add 36 mL 50X TAE Buffer (Thermo Scientific, B49) to 2L bottle; add diH2O to 1800 mL.

  Gel preparation (1.5-2% agarose):
    - For 150 mL gel: weigh agarose (e.g. 2 g for 2% in 100 mL 1X TAE).
    - Heat in microwave until completely dissolved; let cool slightly.
    - Add 15 uL SYBR Safe DNA Gel Stain (Invitrogen, S33102) per 150 mL gel.
    - Pour onto tray; remove bubbles; place 15 or 20-well comb; let solidify.
    - NOTE: clean and rinse beaker after every use; do NOT discard excess gel in sink.

  Running the gel:
    - Place solidified gel in Bio-Rad Sub-Cell GT Cell; wells at negative (black) terminal.
    - Fill with 1X TAE buffer until gel is fully submerged.
    - Load ~12 uL Quick-Load Purple 1 kb Plus DNA Ladder (NEB, N0550S) and PCR products.
      Submerge pipette tip into well before dispensing; press only to first stop to avoid bubbles.
    - Set Bio-Rad PowerPac Power Supply to 100-140 V (Black to Black; Red to Red); START.
    - Run until bands resolved (~40 min typical).

  Gel imaging (LI-COR Odyssey M Imager):
    - Clean imager glass with EtOH and Kimwipe before and after each use.
    - Open LI-COR Acquisition Software.
    - Select: Scan -> Username: Clelland Lab -> Imager: Odyssey M -> Connect.
    - Select: Gel -> Connect -> Draw Scan Area -> Next.
    - Select: 488 / SYBR Safe -> Save -> Focus offset 2.00 mm -> Scan.
    - Wait for scan to finish; export image to desired destination.


PROTOCOL 2: DROPLET DIGITAL PCR (ddPCR)
-----------------------------------------
Instrument: Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Generator + Droplet Reader.
NOTE: Schedule equipment at CAT on iLab before proceeding.

Step 6 | 20X Target Primers/Probe Preparation
  Component                     Volume
  Forward primer (100 uM)       18 uL
  Reverse primer (100 uM)       18 uL
  Target probe (FAM)*            5 uL
  RNase/DNase-free H2O          59 uL
  Total                        100 uL
  *Light sensitive. Store all at -20 C.

  Design guidelines (ddPCR probes):
    - Between primer pair; no overlap with primers.
    - Length: <30 bases; Tm: 3-10 C above primers.
    - More Cs than Gs; no G at 5' end.
    - Product length: 50-250 bp (optimal 80-120 bp).
    - Order from IDT as PrimeTime qPCR Probes (5' FAM/ZEN/3' Iowa Black FQ).

Step 7 | ddPCR Master Mix Setup (22 uL per reaction)
  Component                                          Volume
  2X ddPCR Supermix for Probes (No dUTP, Bio-Rad)   11.0 uL
  20X target primers/probe (FAM)                      1.1 uL
  20X reference primers/probe (HEX/VIC) - RPP30       1.1 uL
  RNase/DNase-free H2O + DNA sample           up to 22.0 uL
  DNA input: up to 350 ng per reaction.

  Reference assay: ddPCR Copy Number Assay RPP30, Human, Homo sapiens
                   (Bio-Rad, dHsaCP1000485; HEX/VIC channel; Ch 2 Reference).
  Setup: thaw all components to room temperature; vortex at full speed 15 s when mixing.
  Prepare Master Mix for (number of reactions + 1).

Step 8 | Droplet Generation (Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Generator)
  1. Insert DG8 Cartridge (Bio-Rad, 1864008) into cartridge holder (Bio-Rad, 1863051).
  2. FIRST: load >20 uL sample into sample wells.
     - Empty wells: add 50:50 mix of Supermix and H2O. All 8 wells must be loaded.
     - No bubbles.
  3. THEN: load 70 uL Droplet Generation Oil for Probes (Bio-Rad, 1863005) into oil wells.
     - Oil is single-use; use within one day of opening.
  4. Apply DG8 Gasket (Bio-Rad, 1863009) on cartridge.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Parallel DNA Ligation for Recombinant DNA Cloning — Water-Oil Core-Shell Droplet Format with Multiple Insert Lengths

REAGENTS USED:
  - Vector DNA (linearized plasmid backbone droplets)
  - Insert DNA, 0.9 kb fragment
  - Insert DNA, 1.7 kb fragment
  - Insert DNA, 1.9 kb fragment
  - DNA Ligase Buffer (containing DNA ligase enzyme)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a vector DNA droplet and an insert DNA droplet (0.9 kb) from their respective reservoirs.
2. Merge and mix the vector and 0.9 kb insert droplets to pool them.
3. Dispense a droplet of DNA ligase buffer and merge/mix it with the pooled vector/insert droplet to initiate ligation.
4. Incubate the ligation reaction droplet at 16 C to allow the DNA ligase reaction to proceed, then discard the droplet.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 in parallel for the 1.7 kb insert: dispense fresh vector and 1.7 kb insert droplets, merge, add ligase buffer, incubate at 16 C, and discard.
6. Repeat steps 1-4 in parallel for the 1.9 kb insert: dispense fresh vector and 1.9 kb insert droplets, merge, add ligase buffer, incubate at 16 C, and discard.
7. Perform a fourth parallel reaction combining both the 0.9 kb and 1.9 kb inserts: dispense droplets of each insert, merge them together, then merge the combined-insert droplet with a fresh vector droplet, add ligase buffer, incubate at 16 C, and discard.

INTERPRETATION: Successful ligation is confirmed off-chip by transforming the resulting recombinant DNA into competent bacteria, culturing the transformed colonies, and confirming the presence of the correct insert fragment length by plasmid extraction and gel electrophoresis, with the four parallel on-chip reactions each yielding the expected vector-insert recombinant product corresponding to its designated insert length or combination.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Competitive ELISA for trace quantities of fentanyl and/or other metabolites in human urine, blood, or oral fluid. This version of the workflow has been adapted to run as a sequence of droplet operations on a digital microfluidic biochip (DMFB) instead of a standard 96-well plate.

REAGENTS USED:

* Sample (urine, blood, or oral fluid)
* Drug-enzyme conjugate (fentanyl labeled with horseradish peroxidase)
* Wash buffer (diluted 10X phosphate buffered saline with surfactant)
* K-Blue Substrate (stabilized 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine / TMB)
* Acid stop solution (1N H2SO4)

STEPS:

1. Combine 20 units of the sample with 100 units of the drug-enzyme conjugate. Mix for 60 seconds.
2. Incubate the combined mixture at 23C (room temperature) for 45 minutes. During this time, any free fentanyl in the sample competes with the enzyme-labeled conjugate for a limited number of antibody binding sites — this competition is the basis of the test.
3. Wash the reaction three times: each wash cycle combines 300 units of wash buffer with the reaction droplet, mixes for 45 seconds, and removes unbound material before moving to detection.
4. Add 100 units of K-Blue (TMB) substrate to the washed reaction and mix for 60 seconds. Incubate at 23C for 30 minutes to allow the color reaction to develop.
5. Add 100 units of acid stop solution and mix for 10 seconds to halt color development and shift the color from blue to yellow.
6. Measure the resulting absorbance signal to obtain the reading. Discard the sample afterward.

INTERPRETATION: This is a one-step competitive immunoassay. Free fentanyl in the sample and the enzyme-labeled conjugate compete for a fixed number of antibody binding sites on the plate. After washing away anything unbound, the remaining bound conjugate is revealed by the K-Blue (TMB) color reaction. Less color development means more drug was present in the sample (competing more successfully for binding sites); more color development means less or no drug was present. A result is typically called positive if the sample's absorbance reading is at or below the laboratory's designated cutoff calibrator, and negative if it is above.

---

## A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE

This is an exact numeric match to the cited Neogen protocol across every value: sample volume (20 units), conjugate volume (100 units), first incubation time (45 minutes), wash count and volume (3 times, 300 units), substrate volume (100 units), second incubation time (30 minutes), and stop solution volume (100 units) all match the source exactly.

An earlier version of this protocol's droplet program included a second, separate antibody/enzyme incubation-and-wash stage (resembling a two-step "sandwich" ELISA) and attempted to record the result using a "fluorescence" detect type. No real fentanyl or other small-molecule drug immunoassay kit was found using that structure: a two-step format requires the target molecule to be large enough for two antibodies to bind it simultaneously, which a small drug molecule (a "hapten") is not large enough to support. Every real urine drug-screening kit checked uses the one-step competitive format reflected in the steps above. Furthermore, TMB is a strictly colorimetric substrate requiring absorbance detection. The two-step fluorescent version is treated as a non-representative artifact of the original test file, while this corrected protocol represents the valid, biologically sound real-world assay.

ASSAY TYPE: Determination of Total Flavonoid Content (Aluminium Chloride Colorimetric Method)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Paper Microfluidics Goes Digital
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/paper%20DMF.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.201305168
Journal      : Advanced Materials, 2014, Vol. 26, pp. 2838-2843
Platform     : Paper DMF (digital microfluidics on inkjet-printed silver-on-paper substrates)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first demonstration of digital microfluidics (DMF) implemented on
paper-based substrates, combining the programmable drop manipulation of DMF with the low cost
and disposability of paper microfluidics. Devices are fabricated by inkjet printing silver
nanoparticle ink onto photo paper using a Dimatix DMP-2800 printer, followed by infrared
sintering (1500 W lamp, 10 s). The resulting paper DMF devices exhibit electrode resistances
500x lower than equivalent chromium-on-glass photolithography devices, and drop velocities
nearly identical to glass DMF devices at comparable actuation voltages.

Two complex, multistep assays are demonstrated:
  1. Homogeneous HRP chemiluminescence assay with on-chip serial dilution (Design A):
     63 discrete steps (27 dispense, 18 mix, 6 split, 12 measure) producing a four-point
     calibration curve in under 1 h; R^2 = 0.993. Represents a level of complexity
     difficult or impossible to achieve on capillary-driven paper devices.
  2. Proof-of-principle rubella IgG sandwich ELISA with magnetic bead separation (Design B):
     30 discrete steps per concentration; LOD = 0.15 IU/mL (well below the 10 IU/mL clinical
     threshold); R^2 = 0.988. First report of a rubella IgG assay on any microfluidic format.

Cost per device (Design A): less than $0.05 USD. Print time: approximately 1 minute.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication  : Inkjet printing of SunTronic U6503 silver nanoparticle ink onto optimized
               photo paper (custom substrate from Prof. M. Toivakka, Abo Akademi University,
               Finland; also tested on Epson Premium Photo Glossy and HP Premium Plus Photo
               Glossy). Dimatix Model Fluid 2 Waveform; printhead at 20-22 V; meniscus
               vacuum 4-5 inches H2O at room temperature.

Sintering    : 1500 W infrared lamp at ~1 cm distance for 10 s. Sintering >= 15 s causes
               paper browning (no effect on function). All devices sintered for 10 s.

Silver layer : <500 nm thick (vs 10-30 um for PCB-based DMF). Surface roughness Ra ~250 nm
               (bare silver on paper); Ra < 100 nm after Parylene-C + Teflon-AF deposition.
               Electrode gaps: 60-90 um. Minimum feature: 30 um.

Dielectric   : 6.2 um Parylene-C deposited by vapor deposition (Specialty Coating Systems).
Hydrophobic  : ~50 nm Teflon-AF 1600 (DuPont; 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40; 1000 rpm, 30 s;
               post-baked 160 C for 10 min).

Top plate    : ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd.) coated with 50 nm Teflon-AF.
               Teflon thread seal tape wrapped around contact pads before coating.

Assembly     : Top and bottom plates joined with two layers of double-sided tape (~80 um each).
               Drop volume: ~440 nL (Design A); ~750 nL (Design B).
               Reservoirs filled by pipetting adjacent to gap and applying potential to reservoir.

Design A     : 5 reservoir electrodes (4.17 x 4.17 mm); 19 driving electrodes (1.65 x 1.65 mm).
               Used for HRP assay and all non-immunoassay experiments.
               Also fabricated in chromium-on-glass format for performance comparison.

Design B     : 8 reservoir electrodes (5.6 x 5.6 mm); 38 driving electrodes (2.16 x 2.16 mm).
               Used for rubella IgG immunoassay; larger electrode array accommodates magnetic
               bead separation and reagent exchange steps.

Actuation    : ~100-125 V_rms, 15 kHz AC via solid-state relays.
Controller   : Open-source DropBot; with integrated magnetic control + PMT for immunoassay
               (ref [25]); without for HRP assay (ref [23]). Impedance-based feedback for
               velocity measurement.


ASSAY 1: HOMOGENEOUS HRP CHEMILUMINESCENCE (Design A)
------------------------------------------------------

Reagents:
  HRP standard          : 100 uU/mL horseradish peroxidase in DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64
  Wash/diluent buffer   : DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64
  Chemiluminescent sub  : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fischer Scientific, Rockford, IL);
                          two-component: stable H2O2 + Luminol-Enhancer; premixed before loading.
                          Supplemented with 0.025% v/v Pluronic L64.
  Detection instrument  : H10682-110 PMT (Hamamatsu Photonics K.K., Hamamatsu, Japan)
  Pluronic L64          : 0.05% v/v added to all reagent solutions (BASF Corp., Germany);
                          reduces protein adsorption and cross-contamination (ref [30]).

Protocol Steps:

Step A1 | Prepare diluent droplets
  Reagents  : PBS, PluronicL64
  Operation : Dispense + mix
  Duration  : 5 s per droplet
  Notes     : Three separate diluent droplets prepared (one per dilution level). Pluronic L64
              at 0.05% v/v in all PBS diluent drops.

Step A2 | Dispense HRP standard stock droplets
  Reagents  : HRP_Standard (100 uU/mL in DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64)
  Operation : Dispense x3 (one per dilution level)
  Volume    : ~440 nL per drop (1 unit, Design A)
  Notes     : Three stock drops dispensed from reservoir independently.

Step A3 | Generate on-chip serial dilution (1x, 2x, 4x)
  Operation : Dispense + merge
  Levels    :
    1x : 1 HRP unit + 1 diluent unit; effective ~50 uU/mL (1:2 dilution by volume)
    2x : 1 HRP unit + 1 diluent unit; effective ~50 uU/mL
    4x : 1 HRP unit + 3 diluent units; effective ~25 uU/mL (1:4 dilution by volume)
  BioScript note : No split-and-reuse construct available in lilott8/BioScript compiler.
                   All dilution levels encoded as explicit dispense+merge chains from fresh
                   manifest entries. 4x diluent (3 units) accumulated by chaining two

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Spatiotemporal NF-kB Dynamics Encodes the Position, Amplitude, and Duration of Local Immune Inputs
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/sciadv.abn6240
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abn6240
Journal      : Science Advances, 2022, Vol. 8, Article eabn6240
Authors      : Minjun Son, Tino Frank, Thomas Holst-Hansen, Andrew G. Wang, Michael Junkin,
               Sara S. Kashaf, Ala Trusina, Savas Tay
Platform     : Custom two-chamber PDMS diffusion microfluidic chip with pneumatic membrane valve


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic coculture platform designed to quantify spatiotemporal
NF-kB signaling dynamics in a model one-way immune communication channel: a signal-sending
macrophage (or soluble TNF source) to signal-receiving NIH 3T3 fibroblasts. The device consists
of two PDMS chambers separated by a pneumatically actuated membrane valve. Cytokine (TNF) is
loaded in the source chamber and released into a receiving chamber filled with fibroblasts by
opening the valve. A peristaltic sink channel continuously perfuses fresh medium at the far end
to simulate capillary clearance, establishing a stable diffusion gradient along the 2.5 mm
chamber axis.

Single-cell NF-kB nuclear translocation is tracked in p65-DsRed-expressing fibroblasts by
time-lapse fluorescence microscopy at 6 min intervals. After the imaging window, cells are
retrieved from three spatially resolved regions (near, mid, far from the TNF source) and
profiled by one-step RT-qPCR for early (A20/Tnfaip3) and late (Casp4, RANTES/Ccl5) NF-kB
target genes.

The BioScript file encodes the primary TNF diffusion experiment (100 ng/mL, 60 min release,
Fig. 3B primary arm) with downstream spatially resolved gene expression measurement (Fig. 6).
The macrophage coculture arm (Fig. 5) is documented in the manifest but not separately encoded.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication   : Standard soft lithography. PDMS (Momentive RTV-615, 10:1 polymer:catalyst)
                cast on SU-8 masters. Valve regions: positive photoresist MicroChemicals AZ40XT
                (20 um). Channel and control layers: negative photoresist SU-8 3025 (30 or 25 um).
                All photoresists exposed at 375 nm (Heidelberg MLA150 maskless aligner).
                PDMS layers cured overnight at 80 C. Oxygen plasma treatment (Harrick PDC-001,
                30 s) used to bond PDMS slab to clean glass slide.

Chambers      :
  Source chamber    : Cytokine (TNF) or single macrophage loaded here with valve closed.
  Diffusion chamber : Fibroblast receiving chamber, 2.5 mm along diffusion axis, coated
                      with 1:4 fibronectin (1 mg/mL in PBS) overnight before cell seeding.
  Sink channel      : Bottom channel; continuously washed with fresh medium at 0.33 Hz
                      (20 cycles/min) via on-chip peristaltic pumping to deplete cytokine
                      and simulate capillary clearance (bypass refreshed every 1-2 min).

Valve         : Pneumatic PDMS membrane separator; Festo 197334 solenoid valve; controlled by
                custom MATLAB interface (modified from Gomez-Sjoberg et al. Anal. Chem. 2007).
                Reagents delivered via Tygon ND-100-80 tubing + PEEK VICI TPK.505 tubing.

Microscope    : Nikon Eclipse Ti2; stage-top incubator box (Life Imaging Service, Basel);
                maintained at 37 C, 5% CO2, >98% humidity throughout all experiments.


CELL LINES
----------
- p65-/- NIH 3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (signal-receiving population):
    Reporters : p65-DsRed (NF-kB nuclear translocation marker)
                H2B-GFP (nucleus position and boundary marker)
    Medium    : Fluorobrite DMEM (Gibco A1896701) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific FB11)
                + 1% GlutaMax (Gibco) + 1x penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco)
    Passaging : Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco); 1:10 resuspension before 100% confluency

- p65-/- RAW 264.7 macrophages (signal-sending population; macrophage coculture arm only):
    Reporter  : p65-GFP
    Medium    : DMEM + 10% certified FBS (Gibco A3160401) + 1% GlutaMax + HEPES (Gibco 15630106)
    Passaging : Scraped and resuspended 1:10 before 100% confluency
    Stimulation: LPS 10 ng/mL (InvivoGen tlrl-3pelps) for 10 min; washed with fresh medium


PROTOCOL STEPS (BioScript-encoded TNF diffusion arm)
------------------------------------------------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Surface Coating of Diffusion Chamber
  Reagents    : Fibronectin (1 mg/mL) diluted 1:4 in PBS
  Operation   : Applied to PDMS diffusion chamber surface overnight at room temperature
  Duration    : 720m (overnight; = 43200 s in IR)
  Purpose     : Promotes fibroblast adhesion and uniform monolayer in diffusion chamber
  Wash        : Channels washed with fresh DMEM before fibroblast seeding
  Paper M&M   : "surface treated with 1:4 fibronectin (1 mg/ml) in PBS solution overnight
                 and washed with fresh medium"

Step 2 | NIH 3T3 Fibroblast Seeding and Attachment
  Cell line   : p65-/- NIH 3T3 (p65-DsRed + H2B-GFP)
  Confluency  : ~80% target seeding density
  Attachment  : 5 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 300m = 18000 s in IR); 1-2 medium feedings during window
  Side channel clearance: Non-adherent cells in side channels flushed out with trypsin
  Note        : `mix` in BioScript abstracts channel flow-through seeding, not DMF electrode
                actuation; no electrode-mediated mixing occurs in this device

Step 3 | TNF Loading into Source Chamber
  Reagent     : TNF (R&D Systems 410-MT); diluted to 100 ng/mL in Fluorobrite DMEM
  Operation   : Loaded into source chamber with pneumatic separator valve in closed position
  Conditions tested in paper: 10, 30, 100 ng/mL (Fig. 3A); this file encodes 100 ng/mL

Step 4 | Valve Opening - TNF Diffusion Initiation
  Operation   : MATLAB-controlled solenoid valve opened; TNF diffuses passively along 2.5 mm axis
  Release duration: 60 min (= 3600 s in IR); valve then closed to stop TNF source input
  Sink perfusion : 0.33 Hz peristaltic pumping (20 cycles/min); bypass washed every 1-2 min
  Diffusion profile (Fig. 1E, fig. S4):
    Near (0-0.4 mm) : Fast TNF rise, high peak concentration, ~0 min NF-kB delay
    Mid  (0.5-0.9 mm): Intermediate TNF kinetics, moderate delay
    Far  (1.0-1.5 mm): Slow TNF rise, low peak, ~25 min NF-kB activation delay;
                        extended NF-kB activation duration (Fig. 1I blue interval)
  Other durations tested: 15 min and 30 min (Fig. 3B)

Step 5 | NF-kB Fluorescence Imaging Window
  Duration    : 200 min total post-valve-open (= 12000 s in IR)
  Interval    : Fluorescence images every 6 min (automated acquisition, NIS Elements)
  Camera      : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2; p65-DsRed: 555 nm excitation, 0.3 s / 100% LED;
                H2B-GFP: 470 nm excitation, 40 ms / 100% LED; Nikon S plan Fluor ELWD 20x
  Stitching   : 4 FOVs per chamber stitched by custom MATLAB (detectSURFFeatures +
                estimateGeometricTransform)
  Analysis    : p65-DsRed nuclear intensity tracked per cell; basal level (pre-valve) used as
                reference; lowess smoothing applied; threshold = 2 SDs above mean basal per region
  Observations (100 ng/mL, 60 min):
    - Wave-like NF-kB propagation across entire 2.5 mm chamber (Fig. 1H, Movie S2)
    - Sharply defined activation zone: >75% to <25% activation within 0.4 mm (Fig. 1J)
    - 2-3 NF-kB oscillations within activation zone at 100 ng/mL
  QC criterion: >75% of near-region cells (0-0.4 mm) activate above 2 SD threshold

Step 6 | NF-kB Activation QC Gate
  Detection   : nfkbActivationDetection module; 30 s detect on imagingWindow
  Pass (BB2)  : nfkbSignal > 0 -> wave propagation confirmed; dispose(imagingWindow)
  Fail (BB3)  : nfkbSignal <= 0 -> device failure or TNF degradation; drain(imagingWindow)
  Join (BB4)  : dispose(nfkbSignal); proceed to gene expression arm

Step 7 | Continued Incubation to 8 h Time Point
  Duration    : 280m additional (= 16800 s in IR); 200m imaging elapsed; total 480m = 8 h
  Temperature : 37 C, 5% CO2
  Purpose     : Allow late NF-kB target gene expression to accumulate (Casp4, RANTES peak ~4-8 h)
  Timepoints  : Cells retrieved at 0, 2, 4, and 8 h post-TNF release (Fig. 6C)

Step 8 | Spatially Resolved Cell Retrieval
  Method      : Chip outlet PDMS cut with razor; purge medium carries detached cells onto
                glass slide as ~2 uL droplet; pipetted into 10 uL ice-cold lysis buffer
  Valve actuation: Separating valves divide chamber into three spatial zones:
    Near : 0-0.4 mm from TNF source
    Mid  : 0.5-0.9 mm from TNF source
    Far  : 1.0-1.5 mm from TNF source
  Detachment  : TrypLE Express (Gibco); 1-2 min per region (= 2m = 120 s in IR)
  Lysis buffer: 10 uL per region; 0.1% Triton X-100 + RNase inhibitor (Takara); ice-cold
  Storage     : -80 C until qPCR processing
  BioScript note: Three separate PBS + TrypLE + lysis buffer dispenses (one per region) used;
                  continuedIncub staged through chambNear/Mid/Far via distinct PBS dispenses
                  to comply with compiler single-consumption constraint

Step 9 | One-Step RT-qPCR Gene Expression Measurement
  Kit         : CellDirect One-Step RT-qPCR (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
  Targets     : Tnfaip3 (A20) -- early gene; Casp4 -- late gene; Ccl5 (RANTES) -- late gene
  Regions     : Near, Mid, Far (9 total reactions: 3 probes x 3 regions)
  Normalization: GAPDH; DeltaCT method; fold change = 2^(DeltaDeltaCT)
  RT step     : 50 C for 15 min (= 900 s in IR)
  PCR step    : 95 C for 42 min (2 min initial denaturation + 40 cycles; = 2520 s in IR)
  Expected spatial pattern (Fig. 6C):
    A20 (early) : Strongly induced near source at 2 h; drops sharply at mid/far by 8 h
    Casp4 (late): Upregulated across all three regions at 4-8 h (distance-insensitive)
    RANTES (late): Upregulated across all three regions at 4-8 h (distance-insensitive)
  BioScript note: Probes chained sequentially into each lysate to comply with compiler
                  single-consumption constraint: rxnNearA -> rxnNearAC -> rxnNearACR;
                  same chain applied to Mid and Far. Terminal ACR variable carries all
                  three probes and proceeds through RT/PCR heat steps and detect.

Step 10 | Gene Expression QC Gate
  Detection   : geneExpressionDetection module; 30 s detect on rxnNearACR
  QC criterion: A20 near-region signal must exceed 3 SDs above unstimulated baseline at 2 h
  Pass (BB5)  : geneExprSignal > 0 -> dispose(rxnNearACR, rxnMidACR, rxnFarACR)
  Fail (BB6)  : geneExprSignal <= 0 -> drain(rxnNearACR, rxnMidACR, rxnFarACR)
  Terminal (BB7): dispose(geneExprSignal); NOP


KEY FINDINGS
------------
Wave propagation  : TNF diffusion + intrinsic NF-kB network oscillations produce wave-like
                    NF-kB activity propagation; not paracrine amplification by fibroblasts
                    (fibroblasts do not secrete NF-kB-activating signals, fig. S5).

Activation zone   : Sharply defined for all source doses; transition from >75% to <25%
                    cell activation within 0.4 mm (<15% of chamber length) (Fig. 1J).

Dose controls range: Signaling range increases linearly with log(TNF dose);
                    y = 0.89*log(x) - 1.80 mm (Fig. 3C). Dose does not affect oscillation count.

Duration controls oscillations: Number of NF-kB oscillations correlates with stimulus
                    duration, not dose; y = 0.023*x + 1.40 oscillations per minute (Fig. 3C).
                    Duration does not affect signaling range.

Multidimensional decoding: First NF-kB peak height encodes dose; ratio of second to first
                    peak height encodes distance; oscillation count encodes duration -- all
                    decodable simultaneously from single-cell dynamics (Figs. 4D-E).

Single-cell accuracy: Binary decision tree cross-validation yields 0.69-0.94 accuracy
                    distinguishing dose and distance at single-cell level (Fig. 4F).

Gene expression zones: Early genes (A20) restricted near TNF source; late genes (Casp4,
                    RANTES) expressed broadly across all distances. IRF-family target genes
                    (IRF-1, -2, -7, -8, -9) show longer-range expression than NF-kB-family
                    target genes due to lower TNF activation threshold (Figs. 6-7).

Macrophage variability: Single macrophage secretion variability directly determines NF-kB
                    signaling range (0-2 mm) and oscillation count (0 to >3) across 35
                    independent coculture replicates (Fig. 5C).

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Nucleosome Immunoprecipitation (NuIP) with Fluorescent Detection on Functionalized Magnetic Beads (Digital Microfluidic Device)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Biotinylated Nucleosome Sample (purified human H3K4me2 nucleosomes)
  - Streptavidin-Coated Magnetic Beads
  - Primary Antibody (anti-H3K4me2, raised in rabbit)
  - Secondary Antibody (Alexa Fluor 405 Goat Anti-Rabbit, fluorescent-conjugated)
  - Wash Buffer

STEPS:
1. Capture: Mix the biotinylated H3K4me2 nucleosome sample with streptavidin-coated magnetic beads; incubate for 6 hours with agitation at 4 C.
2. Wash: Wash away unbound nucleosome species from the beads.
3. Detection Complex Preparation: Separately and simultaneously, under the same conditions (6 hours, 4 C, agitation), incubate the primary antibody (anti-H3K4me2) with the Alexa Fluor 405 Goat Anti-Rabbit secondary antibody to form the fluorescent detection complex.
4. Labeling: Add the detection complex to the washed, nucleosome-bound beads and incubate again.
5. Final Wash: Wash away unbound antibody species.
6. Detection: Re-suspend the beads and place a droplet on the digital microfluidic device; electrowet the droplet to the current wires to concentrate the beads magnetically, then image/detect via fluorescence (Alexa Fluor 405: ~395 nm excitation, ~421 nm emission, 420 nm longpass emission filter, CCD camera).

INTERPRETATION: Fluorescence signal on the concentrated magnetic beads confirms successful capture and antibody labeling of the target nucleosome modification (H3K4me2); a nucleosome-containing sample droplet shows clear fluorescence versus a negative control droplet, and fluorescence localizes to the beads (not the supernatant) when tested against an external magnet. In a semiquantitative dose-response series (0-20 uL of stock H3K4me2 nucleosomes), normalized pixel intensity (via ImageJ blue-channel analysis) increases with nucleosome volume, with a linear response observed between 0-10 uL, establishing this on-chip NuIP assay as a confirmatory checkpoint for antibody specificity/sensitivity prior to downstream analyses such as PCR, gel electrophoresis, or sequencing.

--------
This protocol describes a comprehensive saliva-based SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid testing pipeline
developed and validated at the University of Chicago Medical Center. It provides a complete
alternative to nasal or nasopharyngeal swab testing using two parallel molecular readouts:
real-time reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) and droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), both targeting
the nucleocapsid N1 and N2 genes and the RnaseP internal control.

Specimens were prospectively collected from 137 curbside outpatients (92 symptomatic, 45
asymptomatic pre-operative) and 29 COVID-19 inpatients, with paired nasal swab (NS) results
from the CLIA-certified clinical microbiology laboratory (CML) using the FDA-EUA Cepheid
Xpert Xpress system as the comparator gold standard.

The protocol is divided into three sequential phases:
  1. TRIzol-based RNA extraction (TRE method) from saliva specimens in a BSL3 facility
  2. RT-PCR assay (relative quantification; positive calling Ct < 40 for N1 or N2)
  3. ddPCR assay (absolute quantification; empirical threshold from 45 pre-op negatives)

Key outcomes:
  - RT-PCR saliva: 100% concordance with CML-positive cases (curbside and inpatient cohorts)
  - ddPCR saliva: 93.75% concordance (curbside); potential for higher sensitivity at low
    viral loads vs nasal swabs and RT-PCR (15 additional positives vs CML NS assay)
  - Viral load range: 10^6-fold across patients; saliva shows more uniform distribution
    than nasal swabs (less operator variability in volume collection)


COHORTS
-------
Curbside outpatients (N = 137):
  - Symptomatic (COVID-19 testing): N = 92
  - Asymptomatic (pre-operative screening, used as ddPCR threshold derivation cohort): N = 45
  - All SARS-CoV-2 negative by CML nasal swab (pre-op cohort)

Inpatients (N = 29):
  - All confirmed SARS-CoV-2 positive on hospital admission by CML
  - NS and saliva collected several days after admission (post-diagnosis)
  - CML identified 14/29 NS samples as positive at research collection timepoint


SPECIMEN COLLECTION
-------------------
Saliva:
  - Self-collection by drool technique (spitting into sterile tube to the 2 mL line)
  - 2 mL Zymo DNA/RNA Shield (ZymoR1100-50) added immediately at point of collection
  - Transported to BSL3 facility for RNA extraction

Nasal Swab (NS):
  - Anterior nares nasal swab collected by research team into 1 mL Amies transport solution
    (Thermo Scientific)
  - One NS sent to CML for standard-of-care analysis using FDA-EUA Cepheid Xpert Xpress
    (targets: N2 and envelope E gene; positive if Ct < 45 for either)
  - Second NS sent to BSL3 for research RT-PCR and ddPCR analysis alongside saliva

  Operation  : mix (30 s)

ASSAY TYPE: Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidic Protein Droplet Stamping for MALDI Mass Spectrometry (Oil-Encased Droplet Transport, Passive Stamping, and MALDI-TOF Analysis)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Protein Sample (bovine serum albumin (BSA) test solutions at 0.001-10 mg/mL, and the ABI 4700 proteomics analyzer calibration mixture containing des-Arg-Bradykinin, Angiotensin I, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B, ACTH (1-17), ACTH (18-39), and ACTH (7-38) in alpha-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid/acetonitrile/TFA matrix)
  - Silicone Oil (1 cSt filler/encasing medium that immerses droplets to prevent evaporation, minimize non-specific protein adsorption to the Teflon AF surface, and facilitate electrowetting transport)

STEPS:
1. Reservoir loading: Inject the protein sample into the on-chip reservoir, either from a well-plate via syringe-pump pressure (for water/low-viscosity samples) or by pipette (for protein solutions), with the reservoir and droplets immersed in silicone oil.
2. Droplet formation: Generate a unit droplet (~40 nL, electrode pitch L=750 um, spacer thickness H~75 um) from the reservoir using purely internal electrowetting forces, reliable up to 0.01 mg/mL BSA.
3. Transport: Actuate the oil-encased droplet across the electrode array toward the stamping hole; the silicone oil film isolates the droplet from the hydrophobic Teflon AF surface, minimizing irreversible protein adsorption and enabling transport of BSA concentrations up to 10 mg/mL.
4. Passive stamping: Route the droplet to the stamping hole (diameter >> spacer thickness) and vertically stamp it through the polycarbonate top plate onto the target substrate (hydrophobic glass slide with hydrophilic patch, or a standard MALDI target plate), where the larger hole diameter passively forces the droplet out without active pressure, leaving some liquid behind as dead volume.
5. MALDI-MS analysis: Analyze the stamped droplet(s) on a MALDI-TOF mass spectrometer (e.g. ABI 4700 MALDI-MS TOF system) to acquire the mass spectrum and confirm protein identity and relative intensity.
6. Cycle repeat: Repeat droplet formation, transport, and stamping for additional droplets to increase the total amount of protein deposited at the stamping site (e.g. 10 droplets dispensed, 6 stamped, 4 left as dead volume in one reported run).

INTERPRETATION: Successful protein stamping is confirmed by droplet transport being demonstrated for BSA concentrations up to 10 mg/mL (three orders of magnitude higher than prior electrowetting protein-handling reports) and reliable electrowetting-only droplet formation up to 0.01 mg/mL, by passive stamping depositing quantifiable protein amounts onto a target substrate (3.6 fmoles from 0.001 mg/mL and 16 fmoles from 0.01 mg/mL BSA solutions), and by MALDI-TOF mass spectra of the stamped ABI 4700 calibration mixture correctly identifying all constituent proteins (des-Arg-Bradykinin, Angiotensin I, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B, ACTH (1-17), ACTH (18-39)) after on-chip transport and stamping, establishing the feasibility of a compact, fast, moving-part-free electrowetting interface between well-plate sample formats and MALDI-MS target substrates.

ASSAY TYPE: Estimation of Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) Content in Plant Leaf Tissue

  - Potassium Iodide (KI)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Quantitative Multiparameter Measuring of Dynamic Single-Cell Immune Responses
Source Link  : https://q-bio.org/w/images/3/34/Quantitative_multiparameter_measuring_of_dynamic_single-cell_immune_responses.pdf
Paper DOI    : N/A
Journal      : IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Conference (EMBC), 2014
Platform     : Custom PDMS microfluidic device with single-cell trapping chambers,
               microfluidic valve-controlled dynamic stimulus delivery, and
               on-chip bead-based fluorescent sandwich immunoassay


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic platform for dynamic, multiparameter, non-destructive
measurement of immune cell responses at the single-cell level. The system isolates individual
macrophages in distinct trapping chambers, delivers arbitrary temporal stimulus profiles
(brief pulses in seconds to prolonged inputs spanning hours), and simultaneously measures
four functional parameters from the same single cell throughout the experiment:

  1. NF-kB nuclear translocation (real-time transcription factor activation via GFP fusion)
  2. Cytokine and protein secretion (on-chip bead-based fluorescent sandwich assay, multiplexed)
  3. Cell migration (centroid tracking from bright-field time-lapse)
  4. Cell morphology (area, circularity, aspect ratio from bright-field time-lapse)

All four measurements are non-destructive and conducted dynamically on the same single cells.
The resulting large, multiparameter dataset is used to construct predictive models of immune
input-output relationships governing internal and external cellular reactions during an
immune response.

Cell line: RAW264.7 macrophages expressing an NF-kB-GFP fusion reporter protein.
Stimuli:   LPS (brief pulse) and TNF (prolonged exposure), delivered sequentially
           via programmable upstream valve actuation to model physiological stimulus dynamics.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material      : PDMS (polydimethylsiloxane), soft-lithography fabricated
Configuration : Single-cell isolation chambers in a serpentine trapping channel
                integrated with an on-chip bead-based assay zone
Trapping      : Hydrodynamic single-cell trapping with custom trap geometry;
                trapping efficiency verified by bright-field imaging
Flow control  : Upstream microfluidic valves for programmable stimulus switching;
                arbitrary temporal input profiles (seconds to hours)
Imaging       : Inverted fluorescence microscope; time-lapse acquisition every 3-5 min

Measurement channels:
  - GFP (NF-kB reporter): excitation ~488 nm; emission ~510 nm (nuclear translocation)
  - Bead assay fluorescence: multiple spectrally distinct channels (multiplexed cytokines)
  - Bright-field: cell migration centroid tracking and morphology analysis


CELL LINE
---------
RAW264.7 macrophages (murine, ATCC TIB-71) stably expressing NF-kB-GFP fusion protein.
  Culture conditions : DMEM + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2
  Pre-loading prep   : Single-cell suspension in culture media, ~1e6 cells/mL
  NF-kB reporter     : GFP fused to NF-kB subunit (p65 or p50); cytoplasmic at rest,
                       nuclear upon activation; N/C ratio computed per frame per cell


STIMULI
-------
LPS (Lipopolysaccharide, E. coli):
  Type          : Pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP); TLR4 agonist
  Input profile : Brief pulse (~60 s representative; tunable from seconds to minutes)
  Delivery      : Upstream valve switched to LPS reservoir; flow carries LPS to chambers

TNF (Tumour Necrosis Factor):
  Type          : Pro-inflammatory cytokine; TNFR1/TNFR2 agonist
  Input profile : Prolonged sustained exposure (~60 min representative)
  Delivery      : Upstream valve switched to TNF reservoir after LPS pulse
  Purpose       : Models cytokine-driven NF-kB reactivation (second activation wave)

Sequential LPS -> TNF delivery allows independent characterisation of PAMP-triggered
and cytokine-triggered NF-kB dynamics in the same single cell without destruction.


PROTOCOL STEPS

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Dried Blood Spot Analysis by Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Nanoelectrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ac300305s?ref=article_openPDF
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac300305s
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2012, Vol. 84, pp. 3731-3738
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) coupled to nanoelectrospray ionization mass spectrometry (nESI-MS) on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated digital microfluidic (DMF) method for the extraction,
derivatization, and nanoelectrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (nESI-MS/MS)
quantification of succinylacetone (SA), a biomarker for hepatorenal tyrosinemia (HT,
tyrosinemia type 1), from 3.2 mm dried blood spot (DBS) punches on Whatman 903 filter paper.

The system integrates a standard two-plate DMF device (patterned chromium electrodes on glass
bottom plate + unpatterned ITO-coated glass top plate, both Teflon-AF coated) with a pulled-glass
capillary nanoESI emitter inserted between the two plates. This "sandwich" configuration
immobilizes the emitter without external seals or gaskets, and allows emitters to be exchanged
in seconds without disassembling the device.

A key innovation is an impedance-based automated feedback control system (RBBB Arduino
microcontroller) that detects droplet movement failures and automatically escalates driving
voltage (50 Vrms steps up to 350 Vrms) until movement succeeds -- achieving 100% droplet
movement success across DBS punches versus 60% without feedback.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. Sequential methanol pre-extraction (3 cycles) to remove non-SA analytes
  2. SA extraction and hydrazine derivatization (two-step: evaporate then re-dissolve)
  3. On-chip nESI-MS/MS quantification with internal standard normalization

An extended protocol (Fig. 6) additionally enables parallel amino acid (AA) analysis from
the methanol pre-extractate using a second capillary emitter and n-butanol HCl derivatization,
demonstrating compatibility with multi-analyte newborn screening panels.

The DMF method was validated against the gold-standard NSO technique (paired t-test,
p = 0.05, t = 0.8177) with no statistically significant difference at 95% CI, using
75 uL total reagent volume vs 200-310 uL conventionally.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass (photolithography + wet etching);
               22 square actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm), 7 reservoir electrodes (5 x 5 mm);
               interelectrode gaps 30 um; contact pads interface with 40-pin connector.
               Coated with 7 um Parylene-C (vapor deposition) + 50 nm Teflon-AF (spin-coated).

Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd.);
               37.5 x 25 mm; coated with 50 nm Teflon-AF.

Assembly     : 5 layers double-sided tape spacer (~450 um total gap).
               Gap > DBS punch thickness (~430 um including blood) to allow punch insertion.
               15 uL droplets span approximately two 2.2 x 2.2 mm electrodes.

nESI interface: Pulled-glass capillary emitter (New Objective Inc.); 360 um o.d., 50 um i.d.,
               30 um tip i.d., ~5 cm long; inserted ~2.7 cm between the two plates.
               Emitter tip positioned ~3 mm from LTQ MS orifice.
               Droplet fills capillary (~100 nL) by capillary action on contact.
               DC 1.7-2.2 kV applied to ITO top plate for nanoelectrospray generation.
               Spray stable >200 s, RSD = 7.3%, fluid consumption ~800 nL/min.
               Extended protocol uses two emitters (one per end of device, Fig. 6a).

Fabrication  : University of Toronto ECTI cleanroom facility.
               Photomask printed at Pacific Arts and Design (Markham, ON).


REAGENTS
--------
- MeOH (neat methanol):
    Pre-extraction solvent; 15 uL droplets x 3 cycles = 45 uL total.
    Extracts amino acids and acylcarnitines; SA remains in residual spot.

- HydrazineReagent (SA extraction/derivatization/MS solvent):
    6.5 mM hydrazine + 15 uM 13C5-SA in 80:20 acetonitrile:H2O + 0.1% v/v formic acid.
    15 uL droplets x 2 steps = 30 uL total.
    Derivatizes SA to hydrazone; 13C5-SA serves as internal standard.

- InternalStandard_13C5_SA (3,4,5,6,7-13C-succinylacetone):
    Supplier: Cambridge Isotope Laboratories (Andover, MA).
    Concentration: 15 uM. MS transition: m/z 160 -> 142.
    Co-formulated in HydrazineReagent (modelled separately in BioScript).

- AADerivatizationReagent (extended protocol only):
    3 N HCl in n-butanol; butyl ester derivatization at 75 C.

- AASolvent (extended protocol only):
    Acetonitrile:H2O 4:1 v/v; re-dissolution of dried AA derivatives.

- DBSPunch:
    3.2 mm diameter punch from Whatman 903 filter paper bearing dried blood.
    Toronto samples: male EDTA blood (Biochemed Services) spiked with SA (5-80 uM) and 13C5-SA.
    Ottawa samples: NSO standard technique; stored -20 C; pre-fortified with 13C5-SA before use.
    Note: DBSPunch is a solid-phase persistent object on the DMF bottom plate, not a liquid
    reagent. Declared as a BioScript manifest to allow mix step referencing.


ACTUATION AND FEEDBACK CONTROL
-------------------------------
Waveform     : Sine wave, 15 kHz, 150-350 Vrms
Source       : Function generator (Agilent Technologies) + amplifier
Contact pads : 40-pin connector; automated droplet control via C++ software / Arduino USB

Feedback control system (new, Table 1):
  - Buffered impedance measurement circuit managed by RBBB Arduino (Modern Device)
  - Digital potentiometer (1-10 kOhm) for automatic thresholding per liquid type
  - Actuation pulse: 505 ms (500 ms drive + 5 ms measure)
  - Failure response: step-up 50 Vrms per failed pulse (max 350 Vrms)
  - Relays: 80 AQV259H Panasonic solid-state relays, 2 per output (40 outputs)
  - Control software: custom C++ program via USB to Arduino
  - Result: 100% success rate (avg 4.8 +/- 1.3 pulses) vs 60% success (avg 25.6 +/- 4.8
    pulses) at constant 150 Vrms without feedback. First system with automated
    feedback-controlled variation of actuation potentials.


MS/MS DETECTION
---------------
Instrument   : LTQ linear ion trap mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific)
Ionization   : Nanoelectrospray (nESI), positive mode

SA quantification (MS/MS):
  Derivatization   : Hydrazine -> SA hydrazone (reaction: Sander et al. Clin. Chem. 2006)
  Parent ion scan  : 25% collision-induced dissociation (CID)
  Scan range       : m/z 100-300
  SA transition    : m/z 155 -> 137 (neutral loss H2O, -18 m/z)
  IS transition    : m/z 160 -> 142 (neutral loss H2O, -18 m/z; 13C5-SA)
  Averaging        : 50 acquisitions per spectrum; >=3 samples per condition
  Calibration      : SA/13C5-SA intensity ratio vs SA concentration (linear regression)
  R^2              : 0.9923
  LOD              : 4.95 uM (2.43 ng)
  Extraction efficiency: 85.2% (CV = 6.85%)
  Spray RSD        : 7.3% (TIC, Fig. 1d)
  HT clinical range: 16-150 uM (well above LOD)
  Tip washing      : 4-5 rinse droplets reduce SA signal to <LOD (Fig. 5)

AA analysis (extended protocol, MS1, Fig. 6b):
  Derivatization   : 3 N HCl in n-butanol, 75 C (butyl esters)
  AAs detected     : VAL, MET, TYR, HIS, GLN, PRO, PHE, ASP
  Mode             : Proof-of-concept, non-quantitative; primary MS (MS1)

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Platform for Multiplexed Fluorometric Enzyme Assays (Acid alpha-Glucosidase/GAA for Pompe Disease and Acid alpha-Galactosidase/GLA for Fabry Disease) in Dried Blood Spots for Newborn Lysosomal Storage Disease Screening

REAGENTS USED:
  - DBS Extract (single 3-mm dried-blood-spot punch extracted in 100 uL of 0.1% w/v Tween20 extraction buffer, 30 min at room temperature; one extract shared for both GAA and GLA assays)
  - GAA Reagent (2.5 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-glucoside substrate in sodium acetate, pH 3.8, with 6 umol/L acarbose inhibitor)
  - GLA Reagent (5 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-galactoside substrate in 40 mmol/L sodium acetate, pH 4.5, with 75 umol/L N-acetyl-D-galactosamine inhibitor)
  - Extraction Buffer (EXT: 0.1% w/v Tween20 in water)
  - Stop Buffer (STB: 0.2 mol/L NaHCO3, pH 10.0, 0.01% w/v Tween20)
  - Calibrant (known concentration of 4-methylumbelliferone, 4-MU, used for 2-point fluorescence calibration)

STEPS:
1. Two-point fluorescence calibration: dispense a calibrant droplet and read fluorescence (high calibrant value); dispense a stop-buffer-only droplet and read fluorescence (low calibrant/background value).
2. Substrate background (surrogate t=0): merge GAA reagent with extraction buffer (no DBS extract) plus stop buffer and read fluorescence as the GAA background; repeat the same merge/read for GLA reagent as the GLA background.
3. For each DBS extract loaded onto the cartridge (up to 11 samples per run): dispense one extract droplet and split it into two parallel reactions by merging separately with GAA reagent and GLA reagent.
4. t=0 measurement: immediately merge a droplet from each reaction with stop buffer and read fluorescence (GAA t=0 and GLA t=0), then discard these aliquots.
5. Incubate the remaining GAA and GLA reaction droplets at 37 C (1 h for the reduced-incubation protocol; 6 h in the original bench-comparison protocol).
6. Endpoint measurement: merge each incubated reaction droplet with stop buffer and read endpoint fluorescence (GAA endpoint and GLA endpoint), converting readings to enzyme activity via the calibration curve.
7. Screening interpretation: compare GAA and GLA endpoint activity against the normal/affected separation boundary established from control and disease samples; flag and discard reaction droplets whose activity falls at or below the cutoff as presumptively affected (Pompe or Fabry), otherwise report as normal.

OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This paper describes the ID2M (integrated droplet-digital microfluidic) device,
which merges single-plate digital microfluidics (co-planar ground/driving
electrodes) with droplet-in-channel microfluidics on the same multilayer chip.
The device performs five fluidic operations on the same substrate: droplet
generation (flow-focusing or on-demand T-junction), merging/mixing, trapping
and incubation (up to 24 h), optical detection, and n-ary (4-channel) sorting --
avoiding the droplet-transfer difficulties of separate droplet/digital platforms
used in prior work (e.g. the Mugele group's electrowetting-channel devices,
which were limited to binary sorting).

Two demonstrations are reported:

  (1) ON-CHIP FLUORESCEIN CALIBRATION (Protocol 1):
      A 1 mM fluorescein stock droplet is merged on-demand with diluent
      droplets to build a 2x/4x/8x dilution series. Each droplet is read by
      an optical-fibre fluorescence interface and sorted into one of four
      n-ary channels by threshold intensity. Sorting efficiency for
      positive vs. negative fluorescein droplets was measured at ~96%.
      Calibration curve: R^2 = 0.99 (N = 10); RSD 3.2-10.7% across dilutions.

  (2) YEAST / IONIC-LIQUID (IL) N-ARY SCREENING (Protocol 2):
      Wild-type S. cerevisiae BY4741 and two EMS-mutagenized IL-tolerant
      mutants (selected from a random mutant library on 50/75/100 mM IL
      agar plates) are Poisson-encapsulated as single cells, merged
      on-chip with a 200 mM ionic liquid droplet (final 100 mM IL),
      incubated 24 h at 30 C in on-chip traps, then sorted into 3 channels
      by absorbance (cell density). Mutant growth rates in 100 mM IL:
      ~2.2 and ~2.3 cells/h (mutant #1, #2) vs. ~0 cells/h (wild-type).
      This is reported as the first demonstration of culturing, mixing with
      ionic liquid, and n-ary (non-binary) sorting of microbes on one device.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Microfluidic Probe for Single-Cell Analysis in Adherent Tissue Culture
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms4421
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms4421
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2014, Vol. 5, Article 3421
Platform     : Three-layer PDMS microfluidic probe with hydrodynamic confinement lysis,
               pneumatic valve-controlled nanolitre reaction chambers, and fluorescence readout


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic probe that selectively lyses single adherent cells
from standard tissue culture using hydrodynamic confinement of a detergent-containing lysis
buffer, captures the resulting single-cell lysate, mixes it with assay reagents in nanolitre-
scale reaction chambers, and performs high-sensitivity fluorescence-based enzyme activity
assays. The platform is demonstrated by measuring Akt kinase activity and GAPDH housekeeping
enzyme activity simultaneously from single HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells in adherent
culture, revealing biological heterogeneity in Akt signalling that correlates with distinct
cell morphology subgroups -- not visible in bulk-level assays.

Hydrodynamic confinement is achieved by simultaneous outflow (Qout, central channel,
5 nL/min lysis buffer) and inflow (Qin, outer channels, 50 nL/min total) at the probe tip,
creating a confined lysis zone of tunable radius R (R/L set by Qin/Qout ratio, confirmed
by COMSOL Multiphysics simulation). The zone is set slightly smaller than the target cell
diameter (~15 um) so that only the targeted cell is lysed; neighbouring cells are unaffected
even in ~80% confluent cultures. The lysate is captured back into the device within ~20 s
and mixed with assay buffers at a 1:4 ratio (set by passive flow resistance ratio) before
pneumatic valves trap the assay mixture in 20 nL reaction chambers at 90 s post-lysis.

The integration of lysis, mixing, and assay in a single chip limits lysate dilution and
maintains sensitivity sufficient to measure enzyme activity from less than half a cell's
worth of total protein. The Akt assay LOD on the device is 0.32 pg active Akt -- approximately
1600x more sensitive than a standard plate reader (LOD 0.51 ng). The device can assay up to
four activities from a single cell (two to four chambers per lysate), and up to four cells
in parallel (one per chamber set), with sequential lysis per cell.

This is, to the authors' knowledge, the first use of hydrodynamic confinement to reclaim
cellular material from adherent culture for biochemical assay.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material     : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS, RTV615); three-layer monolithic construction.

Layer 1 (base)     : Bare glass slide; forms base of device except at probe tip region.
Layer 2 (membrane) : ~30 um thin PDMS; forms deformable base of tip (enables close approach
                     to adherent cells on tissue culture surface); contains pneumatic valve
                     lines V1-V4 (15 um SU-8 mould).
Layer 3 (flow)     : ~5 mm thick PDMS; contains all channels, reaction chambers, and
                     flow/control connection ports. Two channel heights:
                       5 um: tip channels + assay buffer mixing regions (tuned for 1:4 mixing
                             by flow resistance ratio)
                      30 um: reaction chambers (maximise fluorescence signal collection)

Fabrication:
  Mask design        : AutoCAD 2000; photoplot film or chrome mask.
  Flow layer 30 um   : AZ4620 photoresist on 6 inch silicon wafer.
  Flow layer 5 um    : SU-8 photoresist on 6 inch silicon wafer.
  Membrane layer     : SU-8 photoresist (15 um valve lines).
  Silanisation       : Heptadecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetra-hydrodecyl trimethoxysilane;
                       dessicator 1 min vent + 1 h vacuum before casting.
  Membrane PDMS      : RTV615 20:1; spin-coated at 1600 rpm.
  Flow layer PDMS    : RTV615 5:1; cast from Si mould, then plastic replica mould used.
  Partial cure       : 60 min at 65 C; aligned under stereo microscope; baked overnight
                       at 65 C for monolithic bond.
  Final assembly     : Plasma bonded to glass slide with tip protruding over straight edge;
                       baked 95 C 15 min; degassed >= 10 min before use.
  Tip shaping        : Cut with sharp microtome blade to pointed tip with flat front.

Probe tip:
  Channels             : 3 (1 central outflow, 2 outer inflows)
  Channel width (w)    : 100 um
  Channel separation (p): 50 um
  Characteristic length (L = w + 2p): 200 um
  Lysis buffer         : Qout = 5 nL/min (central channel)
  Lysate inflow        : Qin = 50 nL/min total (25 nL/min per outer channel)
  Qin/Qout ratio       : 10 (sets lysis zone R slightly smaller than cell, ~15 um)
  Zone confinement     : COMSOL simulated; detergent diffusivity 6e-11 m2/s; 1% v/v input;
                         R measured as distance from tip where detergent falls to 0.1%

Reaction chambers (AB1-AB4):
  Count            : 4 (AB1-AB4)
  Volume per chamber: ~20 nL
  Assay mix ratio  : lysate:assay buffer = 1:4 (passive flow resistance ratio)
  Travel time      : 90 s from tip to chamber
  Repeatability    : within 10% CV (mixing ratio and travel time)

Pneumatic valves (V1-V4):
  Actuation        : compressed air 30 psi via custom solenoid valve manifold
  Timing           : actuated at 90 s post-lysis (measured travel time)
  Function         : trap assay mixture in selected chamber; optionally split lysate
                     to multiple chambers for multiplexed assays from one cell

Multiplexed chamber assignment (this protocol):
  AB1  : Akt kinase Sox sensor assay
  AB2  : GAPDH NADH formation assay (loading control)
  AB3/4: available for additional activities or parallel cells


CELL LINES
----------
HepG2 (ATCC HB-8065):
  Application    : All enzyme activity assays (Akt, GAPDH, multiplexed); primary cell line.
  Culture medium : Eagle's MEM + 10% FBS (Hyclone, Fisher Scientific)
                   + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Invitrogen).
  Conditions     : 37 C, 5% CO2; tissue culture treated polystyrene.

MCF-7 (human breast cancer):
  Application    : Single-cell lysis characterisation only (Fig. 3a/b of paper).
  Dye            : Cell Tracker Green (ex 490 nm / em 526 nm).
  Notes          : Used to confirm lysis of target cell and unaffected neighbouring cells;
                   not used for enzyme activity assays. Not encoded in this .bs file.

-------------------
Two subpopulations of HepG2 cells identified under insulin stimulation:

'High Akt' cells:
  Akt activity     : Significantly increased upon insulin stimulation (p=3.2e-4, n=12)

  Morphology       : Smaller cell area; smaller minimum Feret diameter (caliper width)

'Low Akt' cells:
  Akt activity     : Not increased upon stimulation (p=0.35)
  GAPDH activity   : Also unaffected (p=0.50)
  Morphology       : Significantly larger cell area (p=0.037) and minimum Feret diameter
                     (p=0.0003); consistent with wider, flatter senescent morphology
  Putative identity: Cells in senescence (elevated SA-beta-gal activity confirmed under
                     sparse plating conditions; lower SMP-30 expression promotes lower Akt
                     in HepG2; consistent with literature on Akt in cardiac fibroblast
                     senescence and oncogene-induced senescence)

Key advantage: Morphological phenotype of 'low Akt' cells not observable in flow cytometry.
This probe allows selection of phenotypically distinct cells and direct signalling measurement
from the same individual cell in its adherent context -- connecting intracellular state to
phenotype in a way not achievable with existing suspension-based single-cell methods.
