PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : NF-kappaB Memory Coordinates Transcriptional Responses to Dynamic Inflammatory Stimuli
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/pdfExtended/S2211-1247(22)00968-8
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111159
Journal      : Cell Reports, 2022, Vol. 40, Article 111159
Platform     : Automated pressure-driven microfluidic live-cell imaging (channel-based PDMS/glass device,
               not DMF); 64-chamber device with 14 stimulus inputs; MATLAB-driven pneumatic valve control


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput microfluidic live-cell imaging approach to systematically
profile single-cell NF-kappaB responses to 24 non-repeating sequential combinations of four
inflammatory ligands (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, LPS, PAM2CSK4) at three dose levels (high, mid, low)
in RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts expressing a RelA-DsRed fusion protein. The core
finding is that NF-kappaB dynamics encode short-term memory of prior stimulus history through
ligand-dependent engagement of distinct negative feedback modules.

The protocol has four functional phases:
  1. Microfluidic device preparation, cell loading, and equilibration
  2. Sequential four-ligand stimulation (S1 -> S2 -> S3 -> S4, 2 h per interval) with continuous
     live-cell time-lapse imaging and nuclear/cytoplasmic RelA-DsRed quantification
  3. Information-theoretic analysis of NF-kappaB dynamics using channel capacity (CC) to quantify
     how accurately subsequent responses encode prior stimulus history
  4. Mechanistic dissection via IKK inhibition (PS1145), mathematical ODE modelling, and bulk
     RNA sequencing to identify ligand-dependent negative feedback modules

The complete 8 h imaging experiment profiles >10,000 single cells across 72 conditions
(24 sequences x 3 dose levels) in 2 independent biological replicates.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type      : Pressure-driven automated microfluidic cell culture device (channel-based; not DMF).
            No electrodes, no EWOD actuation. Reagent switching achieved by pneumatic valves.
Material  : PDMS (Momentive RTV-615, 10:1 monomer:catalyst) bonded to glass slide by oxygen plasma.
Layers    : Control layer: 66 g PDMS poured on silicon wafer master, cured 80 C overnight, ~2 cm thick.
            Flow layer: 15 g PDMS spun at 2200 rpm on silicon wafer master (50 um thick), cured 80 C 1 h.
            Both layers plasma-treated, aligned under custom stereomicroscope, baked 80 C overnight.
Chambers  : 64 independently controlled cell culture chambers, each 3.5 x 0.8 x 0.035 mm; >500 cells/chamber.
Inputs    : 14 unique stimulus inputs.
Coating   : 0.25 mg/mL human plasma fibronectin (Millipore FC010) in sterile PBS pH 7.4; overnight RT.
Control   : Pneumatic solenoid valves; electronic controller boxes; MATLAB scripts + custom GUI.
            Input pressure: 4 psi; reagent delivery via PEEK tubing (VICI, TPK.505).
Microscope: Nikon Ti2 enclosed in temperature-controlled incubator (Life Imaging Services); 37 C,
            100% humidity, 5% CO2 throughout all imaging steps.
Camera    : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2 sCMOS; 20X magnification; images every 6 min.
Channels  : RelA-DsRed (555 nm excitation, 0.5-1 s exposure; NF-kappaB nuclear translocation)
            H2B-GFP (485 nm, 50-100 ms; nuclear segmentation and cell tracking)
            JNK-KTR-mCerulean3 (440 nm, 100 ms; JNK kinase activity)
Design ref: Kellogg et al. 2014, Nat. Protoc. 9, 1713-1726; Son et al. 2021, Sci. Signal. 14, eaaz4382


CELL LINE
---------
RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 immortalized mouse embryonic fibroblasts (3T3s) stably expressing:
  - RelA-DsRed fusion protein (NF-kappaB nuclear translocation reporter)
  - JNK-KTR-mCerulean3 (JNK kinase activity reporter)
  - H2B-GFP (nuclear marker for segmentation and tracking)
Source    : Markus Covert laboratory (Stanford University)
Culture   : DMEM High Glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 1% GlutaMAX (Gibco)
            + 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco); 37 C, 5% CO2.
Imaging   : FluoroBrite DMEM (Gibco, A1896701) + same supplements; reduces autofluorescence.
Passage   : No more than 15 passages; passed before reaching 100% confluency.
MyD88 KO  : CRISPR-Cas9 knockout line generated using pX330 backbone (Addgene #42230) and
            guide RNA 5'-TCGCGCTTAACGTGGGAGTG-3'; confirmed by Sanger sequencing and western blot.
            Used to confirm MyD88-dependence of LPS, IL-1beta, and PAM signalling (Supp. Fig. 5).


LIGANDS AND DOSE LEVELS
------------------------
Four inflammatory ligands covering two receptor pathway groups:

  TNFR pathway (MyD88-independent):
    TNF-alpha : Recombinant Mouse TNF-alpha (R&D Systems, aa 80-235)
                Signals via TNFR -> TRADD/TRAF2 -> IKK -> NF-kappaB
                High: 90 ng/mL (>95% activated); Mid: 30 ng/mL (85-95%); Low: 3 ng/mL (50-70%)
                NOTE: maximal TNF-alpha activation ~90%; high dose activates slightly fewer cells than
                other ligands at high dose.

  MyD88-dependent pathway (shared IRAK1/4 -> IKK -> NF-kappaB):
    IL-1beta  : Recombinant Mouse IL-1 beta/IL-1F2 (R&D Systems, 401ML010CF); receptor IL-1R
                High: 3 ng/mL; Mid: 0.2 ng/mL; Low: 0.05 ng/mL
    LPS       : Ultrapure LPS E. coli 0111:B4 (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps); receptor TLR4
                High: 400 ng/mL; Mid: 100 ng/mL; Low: 12.5 ng/mL
                NOTE: LPS produces characteristically delayed NF-kappaB activation kinetics
                (linked to ligand-specific IKK cycling rates); TRIF/TRAM-independent in 3T3s.
    PAM       : PAM2CSK4 synthetic diacylated lipopeptide (InvivoGen, tlrl-pm2s-1); receptor TLR2/6
                High: 1 ng/mL; Mid: 0.2 ng/mL; Low: 0.01 ng/mL

All ligands diluted from -80 C stocks immediately before each stimulus, stored on ice during
the experiment. Delivered at 4 psi via PEEK tubing at each 2 h interval switch.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Fabrication and Surface Coating
  Reagents  : PDMS (RTV-615, 10:1), PBS (Gibco, pH 7.4), fibronectin 0.25 mg/mL
  Operation : Plasma-bond PDMS device to glass. Fill chambers with fibronectin/PBS solution.
  Duration  : Overnight at room temperature (fibronectin coating); flush with complete media before loading.
  Purpose   : Fibronectin coating promotes cell adhesion to PDMS chamber floor.

Step 2 | Cell Loading and Equilibration
  Cell line  : RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 (RelA-DsRed / JNK-KTR / H2B-GFP)
  Preparation: Harvest with trypsin; wash with complete medium; resuspend at 5e6 cells/mL
               in FluoroBrite DMEM + supplements.
  Loading    : Load at ~50% confluency to optimize single-cell tracking efficiency.
  Equilibration: 5 h (300 min) at 37 C, 5% CO2, 100% humidity before stimulus and imaging begin.
  Purpose    : Allow cells to adhere, spread, and return to baseline signalling state.

Step 3 | S1 Stimulus - Naive NF-kappaB Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): IL-1beta 0.2 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min (2 h interval)
  Delivery   : MATLAB valve script switches input from media to ligand at t=0 min; 4 psi, PEEK tubing.
  Imaging    : Time-lapse epifluorescence, 555 nm excitation, 0.5-1 s exposure, every 6 min.
               For time-resolved LPS-to-IL-1beta switching experiments: imaging every 3 min.
  Readout    : Nuclear/cytoplasmic RelA-DsRed ratio quantified by custom MATLAB image analysis.
               H2B-GFP used for nuclear segmentation; single-cell trajectories tracked over full
               experiment. Traces smoothed with lowess (span 3) to identify local maxima.
               Multiple local maxima allowed (min 5-frame = 30 min spacing between peaks).
               Cutoff: 95th percentile of maxima from unstimulated cells; sub-threshold values set to 0.
  Information: Nuclear NF-kappaB at 6 timepoints (20, 30, 40, 50, 70, 90 min post-stimulus)
               used as 6-dimensional input for channel capacity (CC) calculation (Fig. 3A).
  Result     : S1 response is naive baseline; used to normalize all S2-S4 responses for that ligand.

Step 4 | S1 QC Gate
  Condition  : s1Signal > 0 -> pass (valid naive response); proceed to S2.
               s1Signal <= 0 -> fail (no response: dead, unhealthy, or incorrectly loaded cell);
               dispose ligand variable; chamber excluded from downstream analysis.

Step 5 | S2 Stimulus - First History-Conditioned Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): LPS 100 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min; valve switches from IL-1beta to LPS at t=120 min.
  Key finding: Prior IL-1beta (S1, MyD88-dependent) induces IRAK1 auto-inhibitory phosphorylation,
               attenuating the subsequent LPS response in a dose-dependent manner (Fig. 4B/E).
               Asymmetry: prior LPS inhibits subsequent IL-1beta/PAM more strongly than vice versa
               at mid and low doses (Fig. 4E, red vs blue/green). Prior TNF-alpha (TNFR-dependent)
               only weakly attenuates MyD88-dependent signalling (Fig. 4D, blue).
  CC result  : Channel capacity increases from S1 to S2 despite response attenuation, indicating
               NF-kappaB dynamics encode prior history information (Fig. 3B).

Step 6 | S3 Stimulus - Two-Ligand History Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): PAM 0.2 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min; valve switches to PAM at t=240 min.
  Key finding: Cumulative MyD88-dependent history (IL-1beta + LPS, S1+S2) induces downstream
               NF-kappaB-dependent negative feedback proteins (A20/Tnfaip3, IkappaBepsilon/Nfkbie,
               Nfkbia). Channel capacity remains elevated at S3 vs S1 (Fig. 3B/C).

Step 7 | S4 Stimulus - Three-Ligand History Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): TNF-alpha 30 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min; valve switches to TNF-alpha at t=360 min.
  Key finding: TNF-alpha signals via TNFR (distinct receptor-associated intermediaries from MyD88);
               converges on IKK downstream of the accumulated IRAK1 auto-inhibition and
               NF-kappaB-dependent feedback induced at S1-S3. TNF-alpha response is only weakly
               attenuated regardless of prior MyD88-dependent history (Figs. 2B, 4B/D).

Step 8 | Cell Retrieval for Transcriptomics (S4 pass path only)
  Timing     : End of 8 h imaging window (t=480 min)
  Method     : TrypLE Express (Gibco); 1 min; detaches cells from fibronectin-coated surface.
               PBS wash; cells accumulate at outlet channel; removed in 2 uL droplet by pipette.
               Deposited in 10 uL ice-cold lysis buffer (0.1% Triton-X100 + RNase inhibitor, Takara).
               Stored at -80 C until processing. ~1500 cells per replicate per condition.
  Library prep: SMART-Seq2 pipeline. OligodT30VN annealing at 72 C. Reverse transcription
               (SuperScript III, Invitrogen) + TSO oligo (AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAAT[rG][rG][rG])
               at 42 C for 90 min + 10 cycles 50/42 C. 6-cycle KAPA HiFi preamplification.
               Ampure XP bead purification (1:1). Nextera XT library prep (Illumina, FC-131-1024).
  Sequencing : Illumina HiSEQ4000; single-end 50 bp; University of Chicago Genomics Facility.
  Analysis   : STAR alignment to GRCm38. featureCounts transcript quantification.
               edgeR + limma (R) differential expression. BH FDR < 0.01, log2FC > 1.
               3 biological replicates. Data deposited: GEO GSE193053.
  Conditions : LPS 100 ng/mL vs PAM 0.2 ng/mL vs IL-1beta 0.2 ng/mL vs untreated; 2 h stimulus.
  qPCR       : CellDirect One-Step RT-qPCR. Custom primers for Tnfaip3. IDT PrimeTime probes
               for Csf2, Csf3, Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Il23a, Gapdh. TaqMan probes for Nfkbia, Nfkbie.
               Ct normalized to Gapdh (deltaCt); fold change over unstimulated (deltadeltaCt).
               BH-adjusted two-tailed t-test. Data shown as mean +/- SEM, n=3 replicates.

Step 9 | IKK Inhibition Sub-Protocol (Fig. 5A, Supp. Fig. 6C/D)
  Purpose    : Determine whether NF-kappaB-mediated gene expression downstream of IKK is required
               for LPS-specific asymmetric attenuation of subsequent MyD88-dependent signalling.
  Reagent    : PS1145 dihydrochloride (Tocris, 4569); reversible IKK-beta inhibitor; 40 uM.
  Sub-steps  :
    9a. Load fresh RelA-DsRed 3T3 cells; equilibrate 5 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (as Step 2).
    9b. Pre-treat with PS1145 40 uM in complete media for 90 min at 37 C.
    9c. Stimulate with LPS (25-400 ng/mL) + PS1145 40 uM for 240 min at 37 C.
        (NF-kappaB translocation is significantly reduced during LPS due to IKK-beta inhibition;
        Supp. Fig. 6D confirms reduced activation vs untreated at all LPS doses tested.)
    9d. Wash out PS1145: 2 x 15 min washes with complete DMEM at 37 C.
    9e. Restimulate with IL-1beta 3 ng/mL (high dose) for 120 min at 37 C.
        Detect: nfkbTranslocationDetection; 90 s readout.
  Result     : PS1145-treated cells show significantly stronger NF-kappaB response to subsequent
               IL-1beta vs untreated cells (***p < 1e-4, Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon rank-sum;
               >120 cells per condition; 2 biological replicates; Fig. 5A).
  Conclusion : NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and NF-kappaB-mediated gene expression downstream
               of IKK are required for LPS-specific asymmetric attenuation, confirming that
               transcriptional induction of downstream negative feedback drives the asymmetry.


MATHEMATICAL MODEL
------------------
Type       : ODE network model; 14 differential equations; 20 parameters.
Base model : Krishna et al. 2006, PNAS 103:10840 (minimal 3-equation NF-kappaB oscillator).
Expansion  : Added receptors TNFR, IL-1R, TLR4; IRAK1/4 auto-inhibitory phosphorylation
             (Equations 6-9; nonlinear inactivation proportional to active IRAK^2);
             downstream NF-kappaB-dependent inhibitor (Equations 4-5; targets IKK activation;
             Hill coefficient 3 for cooperativity); IKK cycling (Equations 10-11).
LPS vs IL-1beta feedback: LPS-induced downstream inhibitor C parameter set 4x lower threshold
             than IL-1beta or TNF-alpha, modelling stronger transcriptional negative feedback.
Implementation: Python; scipy.integrate.odeint; Bokeh visualization.
Key result : Two-motif model (IRAK1 auto-inhibition + differential downstream feedback) is
             sufficient to reproduce all observed ligand- and dose-specific attenuation patterns
             without additional components (Fig. 5C-E, Supp. Fig. 7A).
Code       : https://github.com/tay-lab/Sequential_NF-kB_stim
Zenodo     : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6626195


KEY FINDINGS
------------
1. Sequential inflammatory stimuli broadly attenuate subsequent NF-kappaB responses (Fig. 2).
   LPS and PAM produce no response after first stimulus; TNF-alpha and IL-1beta show weak
   responses at S2-S4 depending on dose.

2. Variable attenuation encodes prior stimulus history. Channel capacity (CC) increases from
   S1 to S2 despite attenuation, and remains elevated at S3-S4 (Fig. 3B). NF-kappaB dynamics
   (multi-timepoint) carry substantially more information than peak amplitude alone (Fig. 3B/D).

3. TNF-alpha (TNFR) and MyD88-dependent ligands (IL-1beta, LPS, PAM) form two distinct
   history-encoding groups. Prior TNF-alpha weakly attenuates MyD88-dependent signalling
   and vice versa; prior MyD88-dependent signalling strongly attenuates subsequent
   MyD88-dependent signalling in a dose-dependent and asymmetric manner (Fig. 4D/E).

4. Asymmetry mechanism: at high dose, IRAK1 auto-inhibition produces symmetric cross-attenuation.
   At mid and low dose, differential downstream NF-kappaB-dependent gene expression (LPS induces
   2-4x more negative regulator expression than IL-1beta: Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nfkbie; Fig. 6C/E)
   produces asymmetric attenuation. This is IKK-dependent (PS1145 experiment; Fig. 5A).

5. LPS-specific prolonged NF-kappaB activation duration (not total AUC) explains differential
   downstream gene expression vs IL-1beta (Fig. 6E, Supp. Fig. 7F/G).

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Direct Competitive Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) for Opiate (Heroin) Detection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample (Urine)
  - Immobilized Capture Antigen (Heroin enzyme)
  - Drug-Enzyme Conjugate (Heroin conjugate)
  - Wash Buffer
  - TMB Substrate (K-Blue substrate)
  - Stop Solution

STEPS:
1. Primary Incubation: Add 10 units of the urine sample and mix with the immobilized heroin enzyme. Add 100 units of the heroin drug-enzyme conjugate and mix for 60 seconds. Incubate the mixture at 23°C (room temperature) for 45 minutes to allow free heroin/opiates in the sample to compete with the conjugate for antibody binding sites. Discard the supernatant droplet.
2. Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone three times to remove any unbound sample and unbound conjugate. For each wash cycle, add 300 units of wash buffer, mix with the retained enzyme for 45 seconds, and discard the wash supernatant.
3. Substrate Development: Add 100 units of K-Blue substrate to the retained enzyme. Mix and incubate at 23°C for 30 minutes to allow the colorimetric reaction to develop.
4. Stop Reaction and Detection: Add 100 units of stop solution and mix for 60 seconds to halt the enzymatic reaction. Measure the resulting optical signal (absorbance) of the final droplet. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of heroin/opiates in the sample. A lower signal indicates a higher presence of heroin, while a higher signal indicates little to no heroin (as more conjugate successfully bound to the antibodies).

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Non-Optical Multiplexed PCR Diagnostic Platform for Serotype-Specific Detection of Dengue Virus
Source Link  : https://academicweb.nd.edu/~changlab/documents/Yin2020.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.snb.2020.127854
Journal      : Sensors & Actuators B: Chemical, 2020, Vol. 310, Article 127854
Platform     : Integrated on-chip RT-PCR + ion-exchange membrane (IEM) sensor array on polycarbonate microfluidic chip


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a non-optical, multiplexed, point-of-care (POC) microfluidic platform for
simultaneous serotype-specific detection of all four dengue virus (DENV) serotypes from 1 mL of
human blood plasma in a single on-chip PCR reactor. The platform integrates three functional units:

  1. Off-chip RNA extraction using a chitosan-modified Fusion 5 filter paper dip-and-rinse technique
  2. On-chip multiplex RT-PCR amplification of all four DENV serotypes in a single 25 uL reactor
  3. Ion-exchange membrane (IEM) sensor array detection via current-voltage curve (CVC) measurement

By replacing optical (fluorescence/RT-qPCR) readout with ion-selective nanomembrane sensors, the
platform eliminates spectral overlap constraints and can be scaled to detect arbitrarily large numbers
of targets from a single sample. The IEM sensor's ion-depletion action increases the Debye length in
the detection zone (>30 nm), making it insensitive to pH variation, ionic strength, duplex conformation,
and non-specific amplification products -- the key failure modes of optical and electrochemical sensors.

Total assay time: ~90 min. Limit of detection: 100 copies/mL RNA in spiked human plasma (3x better
than any prior PCR-based DENV technology, Table 1).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Chip material  : Polycarbonate thermosoftening plastic (3 layers, each 0.3 mm thick)
Chip dimensions: 10 x 4 x 0.1 cm3 (l/w/t)
Fabrication    : Graphtec Pro FC 7000MK2-60 cutting plotter; thermal/pressure bonding

Sections:
  - On-chip PCR chip       : 25 uL reaction chamber; thermocouple plate for thermal cycling
  - AEM sensing chip       : Anion-exchange nanomembrane (AME) sensor array with input/output channels;
                             4 isolated reservoirs, one per DENV serotype sensor

AEM sensor composition:
  Material     : Polystyrene-divinylbenzene with strong basic quaternary ammonium groups;
                 polyethylene binder; polyamide/polyester textile fiber support (Mega a.s., Czech Republic)
  Dimensions   : 0.9 x 0.3 x 0.3 mm3 (l/w/t) per sensor piece; 1 or 4 pieces per sensor
  Functionalization: Serotype-specific oligoprobe attached via EDC coupling on the depletion side

Electrodes:
  Reference    : 2x Ag-AgCl (measure potential across nanomembrane sensor)
  Current      : 2x Platinum (apply current load 0-40 uA at 1 uA/s step rate)
  Potentiostat : Gamry 500 (Gamry Instruments, Warminster, PA); Gamry Framework software

Fluidics box:
  Dimensions   : 102 x 240 x 305 mm3 (l/w/t); contains fluidic pump and thermocouple heater


PATHOGENS AND SAMPLES
---------------------
- DENV-1  : WP-74 strain
- DENV-2  : OBS8041 strain
- DENV-3  : CH53489 strain
- DENV-4  : H241 strain
  (All DENV strains from Naval Medical Research Center, NMRC)
- ZIKV    : PRVABC59 strain (Emory University; used as non-specific negative control)
- Matrix  : Human blood plasma (ZenBio Inc., NC, USA); 1 mL per assay


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | TRIzol-Chloroform Lysis and Phase Separation
  Reagents     : HumanPlasma_DENV_RNA (1 mL), TRIzol_Reagent, Chloroform (0.2 mL)
  Operation    : Vortex with TRIzol 30 s; add chloroform, mix 60 s; centrifuge to separate phases
  Temperature  : 25 C (room temperature phase separation; 120 s)
  Output       : Aqueous supernatant containing DENV RNA (also contains PCR inhibitor
                 Guanidinium thiocyanate from TRIzol)
  BioScript    : Abstracted as mix(TRIzol, 30s) -> mix(Chloroform, 60s) -> heat(25C, 120s)
  Notes        : DENV RNA in plasma is predominantly encapsulated within virions; lysis step
                 is required to release internal RNA. TRIzol-chloroform emulsion aqueous phase
                 collected as supernatant for downstream filter paper extraction.

Step 2 | Chitosan Filter Paper Dip-and-Rinse RNA Extraction
  Reagents     : ChitosanFilterDisc (1 mm diameter), SDS_Wash (1% SDS), DI_Water
  Filter prep  : 5 cm Fusion 5 paper (Whatman); O2 plasma 2 min; overnight chitosan soak
                 (0.05% w/v in 0.1% acetic acid, pH 6.0); wash 3x DI water; vacuum dry;
                 cut to 1 mm discs; stored at room temperature
  Immersion    : Disc immersed in aqueous supernatant; incubate 5 min
  Wash         : 1% SDS (30 s) then DI water (30 s) to remove PCR inhibitors
  Mechanism    : Positively charged chitosan matrix electrostatically captures negatively
                 charged RNA molecules via physical entanglement and electrostatic adsorption
  Recovery     : Down to 50 copies/mL RNA; ~98% extraction efficiency (Liu et al. 2017)
  Duration     : ~10 min total (5 min incubation + 5 min wash)
  BioScript    : mix(disc, 5m) -> mix(SDS, 30s) -> mix(DI water, 30s)
  Notes        : No elution step; filter disc introduced directly into PCR mixture.
                 Chitosan also removes Guanidinium thiocyanate PCR inhibitor from TRIzol phase.

Step 3 | Multiplex RT-PCR Master Mix Assembly and On-Chip Loading

IEM SENSOR PHYSICS
------------------
Mechanism    : External concentration polarization across anion-exchange membrane (AEM)
               under applied electric field. Asymmetric ion migration creates a depletion
               zone (ion-free, high resistance) and enrichment zone on opposite sides.
Depletion zone: Forms at second critical voltage; Debye length >30 nm (vs ~1 nm at normal
               PCR buffer ionic strength). This large Debye length makes CVC shift insensitive
               to duplex conformation, pairing sequence location, and dangling tail lengths.
Limiting current: Differential resistance in depletion regime orders of magnitude higher than
               membrane resistance alone. Small number of charged targets produces large CVC shift.
Overlimiting : Electroconvective instability (vortices) above limiting voltage shears off
               non-specifically bound targets; further enhances selectivity.
Detection    : Probe-functionalized AEM depletion side. Hybridised target-probe duplexes
               suppress depletion action and shift CVC in overlimiting regime by several volts.
               Shift is 10-100x larger than electrochemical sensor signals.
Selectivity  : Hydrodynamic shear (4x PBS wash + flow) + electroconvective vortices remove
               non-specific PCR products, primer dimers, and cross-reactive ZIKV/DENV serotypes.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing of paraformaldehyde-fixed cells (FD-seq)
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-based-single-cell-rna-sequencing-of-parafo-n2bvj94k5lk5/v1
Paper DOI    : https://dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1604/v1
Journal      : Research Square (preprint), posted October 1, 2021
Authors      : Hoang Van Phan, Michiel van Gent, Nir Drayman, Anindita Basu,
               Michaela U. Gack, Savas Tay
Affiliation  : The University of Chicago; Cleveland Clinic
Platform     : Drop-seq microfluidic chip (Macosko et al., Cell 2015)
               Droplet Generation Microfluidic Chip (commercial or custom PDMS)


OVERVIEW
--------
FD-seq (Fixed Droplet RNA Sequencing) is a method for droplet-based single-cell RNA
sequencing (scRNA-seq) of paraformaldehyde (PFA)-fixed, stained, and sorted cells.
Standard high-throughput scRNA-seq methods such as Drop-seq are not compatible with
PFA-fixed cells due to RNA crosslinking. FD-seq resolves this by performing PFA
crosslink reversal inside intact droplets (56 C, 60 min) using heat and Proteinase K
before droplet breaking, thereby releasing intact mRNA for reverse transcription.

FD-seq is designed to work with existing Drop-seq experimental setups and does not
require additional specialized processing equipment. It enables scRNA-seq of cells that
require fixation prior to sequencing, e.g., for biosafety, intracellular staining,
or compatibility with FACS sorting workflows.

The protocol is divided into ten sequential phases:
  1.  Cell fixation (4% PFA, 15 min, RT)
  2.  Cell permeabilization (0.1% Triton X-100, 15 min, RT)
  3.  Pre-droplet preparation (0.01% BSA washes; lysis buffer + bead preparation)
  4.  Droplet generation (Drop-seq chip; co-encapsulation of cells and barcoded beads)
  5.  In-droplet crosslink reversal (56 C, 60 min; Proteinase K + heat)
  6.  Droplet breaking (Perfluorooctan-1-ol + 6X SSC)
  7.  Reverse transcription (Maxima H- RT; 25 C 30 min + 42 C 90 min)
  8.  Exonuclease I digestion (37 C, 45 min; removes unextended primers)
  9.  Whole transcriptome amplification (WTA PCR; Kapa HiFi; 14-cycle program)
  10. Tagmentation and library preparation (Nextera XT; NextSeq paired-end sequencing)


DEVICE AND PLATFORM
-------------------
Chip         : Drop-seq Droplet Generation Microfluidic Chip
               Commercial chip (Macosko 2015) or in-house PDMS fabrication.
               Hydrophobic treatment with Aquapel (cat 47100) required before use;
               chip rested overnight at RT after treatment.
Syringe pumps: Harvard Apparatus Pump 33 DDS and/or KD Scientific model 100.
Inlets       : Cell syringe (3 ml/h), Bead syringe (3 ml/h), Oil syringe (12 ml/h)
Oil          : Bio-Rad droplet generation oil (cat 1864006)
Droplets     : Nanoliter-scale water-in-oil emulsion; single cell + single bead
               co-encapsulated per droplet (stochastic, Poisson-limited).
Beads        : Drop-seq beads (ChemGenes Corp, cat Macosko-2011-10(V+));
               resuspended in TE-TW at 4 C after manufacturer wash.
               Loaded at 120,000 beads/ml in lysis buffer + 50 mM DTT + 800 U/ml Proteinase K.
Cells        : Loaded at 100,000 cells/ml in 0.01% BSA; filtered through cell strainer.
Collection   : ~20 min per sample into 50 ml centrifuge tube.

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Phase 1 | Cell Fixation
  Reagents    : PBS, 1% BSA wash buffer, 4% PFA in PBS
  Step 1      : Wash cells once with 1% BSA in PBS (400g, 5 min)
  Step 2      : Fix with 4% PFA in PBS at RT for 15 min
  Step 3      : Spin (400g, 5 min); discard PFA; wash once with wash buffer
  Storage     : Cells can be stored in wash buffer at 4 C overnight before proceeding
  BS variable : washedFixed (post-fixation, post-wash state)

Phase 2 | Cell Permeabilization
  Reagents    : 0.1% Triton X-100 in wash buffer, wash buffer
  Step 1      : Add 500 ul 0.1% Triton X-100 to cell pellet; incubate RT for 15 min
  Step 2      : Add 1 ml wash buffer; spin (400g, 5 min); discard supernatant
  Step 3      : Wash once more with 1 ml wash buffer
  Optional    : Blocking and intracellular staining can follow; reagents diluted in wash buffer
  BS variable : washed4 (post-permeabilization, post-wash state)

Phase 3 | Pre-Droplet Preparation
  Reagents    : 0.01% BSA, lysis buffer + DTT + Proteinase K, Drop-seq beads
  Cell prep   : Wash PFA-fixed cells 3x with 0.01% BSA (2 ml each); resuspend at
                100,000 cells/ml in 0.01% BSA; filter with appropriate cell strainer
  Bead prep   : Count beads with Fuchs-Rosenthal hemocytometer (20 ul beads + 20 ul 20% Ficoll)
                Resuspend beads at 120,000 beads/ml in lysis buffer (with DTT + ProtK); store on ice
  BS variable : cellsReady, beadsReady
  Compiler note: 3x 0.01% BSA washes unrolled explicitly (no loop construct in BioScript)

Phase 4 | Droplet Generation
  Chip        : Drop-seq Droplet Generation Microfluidic Chip (Aquapel-treated, rested overnight)
  Syringe setup:
    Cell syringe (BD 3 ml Luer-Lok): cells in 0.01% BSA; flow rate 3 ml/h
    Bead syringe (BD 3 ml Luer-Lok + magnetic disc VP 772DP-N42-5-2): beads in lysis buffer;
                  flow rate 3 ml/h; magnetic stirrer (VP710D2) to prevent bead settling
    Oil syringe (BD 10 ml Luer-Lok): Bio-Rad oil; flow rate 12 ml/h
  Start order : Cell pump first, then bead pump, then oil pump
  Collection  : ~20 min per sample into 50 ml centrifuge tube
  QC          : Inspect chip junction under microscope; stable generation = blur at junction
  BS variable : emulsion
  Compiler note: Syringe pump flow and chip geometry are not BioScript primitives;
                 cell/bead co-encapsulation modelled as sequential mix operations

Phase 5 | In-Droplet Crosslink Reversal
  Reagents    : Heat block
  Step 1      : Incubate 50 ml tube with droplets at 56 C for 60 min (heat block)
                KEY STEP: Proteinase K + heat reverses PFA crosslinks inside intact droplets
  Step 2      : Remove from heat block; leave at RT for 10 min
  Step 3      : Place on ice for 5 min
  QC check    : Pipette ~15 ul oil + 5 ul droplets onto Fuchs-Rosenthal hemocytometer;
                verify most droplets contain at most 1 bead
  BS variable : emulsion (in-place heat; heat is void in BioScript)
  Duration    : 56 C for 60m; 25 C for 10m; 4 C for 5m

Phase 6 | Droplet Breaking
  Reagents    : 6X SSC, Perfluorooctan-1-ol (in chemical hood)
  Step 1      : Remove as much oil as possible from 50 ml tube without disturbing droplets
  Step 2      : Add 30 ml 6X SSC + 1 ml Perfluorooctan-1-ol (chemical hood)
  Step 3      : Seal tube; shake vertically 4 times; spin at 1000g for 1 min
  Step 4      : Transfer ~30 ml supernatant (above oil interface) to new 50 ml tube
  Step 5      : Add 30 ml 6X SSC to original tube; wait 2-3 s; transfer 30 ml supernatant
                to second new 50 ml tube
  Step 6      : Spin both new tubes at 1000g for 3 min; pool beads into 1.5 ml DNA LoBind tube
  Step 7      : Wash beads: 2x with 1 ml 6X SSC, 1x with 300 ul 5X Maxima H- RT buffer
                (1000g, 1 min each); discard supernatant
  BS variable : beadWash2 (post-break, post-wash bead fraction)

Phase 7 | Reverse Transcription
  Reagents    : RT mix (200 ul; see Reagents section)
  Step 1      : Add 200 ul RT mix to beads; incubate RT for 30 min with rotation
                (primer annealing and RT initiation)
  Step 2      : Transfer to 42 C for 90 min with rotation (cDNA synthesis)
  Step 3      : Spin beads; discard supernatant
  Washes      : 1x TE-SDS (1 ml), 2x TE-TW (1 ml each), 1x 10 mM Tris pH 8.0
                (all at 1000g, 1 min; modelled as BSA_Wash_Buffer in BioScript)
  BS variable : rtWashed4
  Duration    : RT mix 30m; heat 25c for 30m; heat 42c for 90m
  Compiler note: 90 min = 90m (no h token); 4 wash steps unrolled explicitly

Phase 8 | Exonuclease I Digestion
  Reagents    : Exo I mix (200 ul; see Reagents section)
  Step 1      : Add 200 ul Exo I mix to beads; incubate 37 C for 45 min with rotation
                (removes unextended TSO_RNAhybrid primers from bead surface)
  Step 2      : Spin beads; discard supernatant

Title        : High-Throughput Microfluidic Single-Cell Analysis Pipeline for Studies of Signaling Dynamics
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2014.120
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2014.120
Journal      : Nature Protocols, Vol. 9, No. 7 (2014), pp. 1713-1726
Platform     : Valve-actuated multilayer PDMS microfluidic cell culture chip (continuous-flow; not DMF)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a complete end-to-end pipeline for microfluidics-based single-cell analysis,
combining live-cell imaging, automated image analysis, and downstream high-throughput gene expression
profiling. The system enables a single researcher to generate up to 1 million data points on single-cell
protein localization within one week, across 48 predesigned experimental conditions using different
signaling molecules, doses, timings, and combinations.

The pipeline comprises five major phases:
  1. Chip fabrication and system setup (Steps 1-15)
  2. Chip surface treatment and cell loading (Steps 16-33)
  3. Multiplexed cell stimulation and live-cell imaging (Steps 34-43)
  4. On-chip cell retrieval and high-throughput microfluidic qPCR (Steps 44-60)
  5. Automated image analysis and data extraction (Steps 59-66)

The chip described (Cell Culture Chip; Gomez-Sjoberg et al., Anal. Chem. 2007) contains 96
independently controllable 35-nL chambers. Each chamber can culture 1-1,000 mammalian cells.
Up to 16 reagent inputs are combined by an on-chip herringbone mixer and delivered to selected
chambers by an on-chip peristaltic pump (~0.35 nL per pump cycle). Programmable valve scripts
automate chamber surface treatment, cell loading, feeding, stimulation, staining, and retrieval
without researcher intervention.

Example applications demonstrated in the paper: NF-kB nuclear translocation dynamics in NIH3T3
mouse fibroblasts (p65-dsRed + H2B-GFP) and RAW264.7 mouse macrophages (p65-GFP + H2B-mCherry)
under TNF-alpha and LPS stimulation, with downstream 48-gene expression profiling at 30-min
intervals over 12 h using the Fluidigm BioMark 48.48 Dynamic Array (up to 9,216 simultaneous
qPCR measurements).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Chip design   : Two PDMS layers (multilayer soft lithography) bonded and mounted on
                PDMS-coated 50 x 75 mm glass slide.
Flow layer    : Contains cells and reagents; channels with rounded cross-section
                (positive photoresist, SU-8); positioned above control layer.
Control layer : Creates elastomeric membrane valves by deflecting thin PDMS membrane
                under pneumatic pressure; channels with rectangular cross-section
                (negative photoresist); spin-coated ~30 um thick at 2500 rpm.
Chambers      : 96 independent chambers; ~1 x 1 mm2 area, 35 um height, ~35 nL volume.
                Sieve valves at each chamber entrance and exit trap cells >20 um diameter.
                Four PDMS pillars inside each chamber prevent ceiling collapse.

Valve control : 48-valve system (six 8-valve solenoid manifolds); USB controller boxes;
                pressurized air at 20-30 psi. MATLAB or LabVIEW scripting for automation.
Peristaltic pump: 3-valve in-series sequence; ~0.35 nL per cycle; 30-60 nL/min at
                0.05-0.1 s valve delay.
Reagent inputs: Up to 16 vials; pressurized with 5% CO2 at 3-10 psi (200-700 mbar);
                PTFE tubing for reagents; PEEK tubing for cells.
Mixer         : On-chip herringbone mixer combines reagents before chamber delivery.
                InPurge PBS line clears manifold between inputs.

Microscope    : Inverted automated fluorescence (Leica DMI6000B or Nikon Ti-E);
                stage incubation at 37 C, 5% CO2, >95% humidity.
                Wide-field preferred (speed + low phototoxicity vs confocal).
                20x long-distance objective for nuclear-cytoplasm dynamics.
Software      : muManager (open-source) or manufacturer software for time-lapse control.


CELL LINES
----------
- NIH3T3 mouse fibroblasts (p65-dsRed + H2B-GFP): NF-kB translocation reporter line.
  Culture: DMEM + 10% v/v FBS; 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Loading target: ~150 cells per chamber (~80% confluence at experiment start).
- RAW264.7 mouse macrophages (p65-GFP + H2B-mCherry): LPS-responsive macrophage line.
  Culture: DMEM + 10% v/v FBS; 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Loading target: ~200-300 cells per chamber.

--------------

Step 1 | Chip Surface Treatment -- Pluronic Blocking (Steps 24-29)

  Analysis  : CellProfiler pipeline:

  Notes     : liveCellImagingDetection module abstracts the full CellProfiler/MATLAB

Title        : Multiplexed Proteomic Sample Preconcentration Device Using Surface-Patterned Ion-Selective Membrane
Source Link  : https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2394188/pdf/nihms46491.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/b717900f
Journal      : Lab Chip, 2008, Vol. 8, No. 4, pp. 596-601
Platform     : PDMS microfluidic chip with surface-patterned planar Nafion ion-selective membrane (PDMS/glass)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput proteomic sample preconcentration method in PDMS
microfluidic chip format using a surface-patterned submicron Nafion ion-selective membrane.
The key innovation is the direct printing of a Nafion permselective membrane onto a glass
substrate by micro-flow patterning, followed by single-step integration into the device via
standard O2 plasma bonding. This eliminates the need for complicated nanochannel fabrication
(as in prior silicon micro/nanofluidic devices) and cumbersome thin-film integration processes.

The preconcentration mechanism is electrokinetic trapping, exploiting the ion-selectivity of
the Nafion membrane to generate a depletion region in the sample microchannel. Charged
molecules (proteins, peptides, or any charged species regardless of size) are concentrated
in front of the depletion boundary by the combined action of a normal electric field (En)
across the membrane and a tangential electroosmotic flow (EOF) along the sample channel.

Key performance metrics:
  - Concentration factor: ~10^4 in 5 min from 400 pM starting concentration
  - Concentration factor: ~5x10^4 in 10 min from 40 pM starting concentration
  - Concentrated plug volume: ~200 pL per single unit
  - 12x faster than prior PDMS preconcentrator (junction gap breakdown method: ~10^4 in 1 h)
  - 350x larger concentrated volume vs. prior silicon nanochannel device (few pL)
  - 10-unit array: ~2 nL concentrated volume (3500x vs. silicon device); compatible with
    mass spectrometer interfacing via electrospray or droplet dispensing
  - Coefficient of variance: 11.5% across 3 devices (reasonable given pattern alignment inaccuracy)

The Nafion membrane is applicable to any charged molecule; the preconcentration platform is
general and not limited to specific biomarkers or antibody-antigen interactions.


SEPARATION PHYSICS
------------------
The device operates in two sequential electrical phases:

Phase 1 - Depletion mode (V1=50V, V2=50V, buffer GND):
  A voltage difference is applied between the sample channel and the flanking buffer channels
  through the planar Nafion membrane. The normal field component (En) perpendicular to the
  membrane depletes ions in the sample channel and drives charged molecules away from the
  membrane toward the V1 reservoir. A stable depletion region forms and grows with time.

Phase 2 - Concentration mode (V1=50V, V2=25V, buffer GND):
  V2 is reduced to 25V; Vdiff = V1-V2 = 25V (optimum). The tangential field component (Et)
  along the sample channel generates an electroosmotic flow (EOF) that injects molecules from
  the bulk toward the depletion boundary. Molecules stack in front of the depletion zone,
  forming a stable concentrated plug at equilibrium distance Y2 from the Nafion membrane.
  The balance of En (depletion force) and Et (electroosmotic injection) determines plug position.

Optimum Vdiff = 25V: at higher Vdiff, secondary nonlinear electrokinetics near the membrane
destabilize the concentrated zone. Preconcentration factor and depletion region size both
increase monotonically with Vdiff up to 25V (Fig. 5 of paper).

Ion selectivity mechanism: Nafion's cluster network reduces the effective pore size, while
sulfonate groups (-SO3H) provide high negative charge density, achieving permselectivity
superior to prior PDMS nanojunction approaches. No voltage breakdown limit applies (unlike
silicon oxide-gated nanochannels), allowing higher applied voltages and faster concentration.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material         : PDMS bonded to Nafion-patterned glass substrate (25 mm x 75 mm slides)
Overall size     : 20 mm x 25 mm
Channel geometry : All channels 50 um deep x 50 um wide
Layout           : Dual gate design

                   - Flanking left and right: two buffer channels (phosphate buffer; green in Fig. 4a)
                   - Nafion stripe printed on glass connects all three channels at channel bottom
                     as planar permselective junction
Nafion membrane  :
  Material       : Nafion perfluorinated ion-exchange resin (Sigma-Aldrich), 5 wt% in
                   lower aliphatic alcohols/H2O, 15-20% water content
  Target thickness: 191-400 nm; measured 191 nm by SEM (Fig. 4b/c)
  Critical limit : >400 nm causes PDMS sealing failure; leakage at membrane edges compromises
                   ion selectivity and preconcentration efficiency/reproducibility
Electrode config : Pt wire electrodes inserted into channel reservoirs via punched access holes

Array format (10-unit):
  10 single preconcentrators arranged radially around a common collection reservoir (center).
  Sample reservoirs S1-S10 each at V1=50V; common reservoir at V2=25V; individual ground
  reservoirs per buffer channel. Nafion patterned in half-circle shape per unit.
  Concentrated volume: ~2 nL (10 x ~200 pL); sufficient for pipette transfer or direct
  electrospray to mass spectrometer.

====================

Title        : Massively Parallel Concentration Device for Multiplexed Immunoassays
Source Link  : https://pubs.rsc.org/lc/article/11/7/1351/336806/Massively-parallel-concentration-device-for
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c0lc00349b
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2011, Vol. 11, pp. 1351-1358
Platform     : PDMS-glass nanofluidic concentration device with Nafion nanoporous junction


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a massively parallel nanofluidic concentration device for multiplexed
and high-throughput biomolecule detection. By integrating a Nafion nanoporous junction between
a main sample microchannel and a buffer microchannel, ion concentration polarization (ICP) is
generated under an applied dc voltage. This creates an ion depletion zone on the anodic side of
the nanojunction and strongly repels charged biomolecules (CRP, fluorescein) into a concentrated
plug within each microchannel. The key innovation is that a single-inlet/single-outlet reservoir
design allows the device to be massively parallelized: up to 128 individually controlled
concentration channels are operated simultaneously from a single applied voltage bias, without
scaling the number of fluidic connections.

The protocol is divided into two functional sub-protocols:

  1. Multiplexed preconcentration characterisation: up to 128 microchannels operated
     at the same ET (uniform concentration factor, ~4000x in 30 min at 50-100 V) or at
     graded ET values via varying inlet microchannel length (serial concentration, 100-4000x
     in a single 16-channel device). Fluorescein is used as the fluorescent tracer.

  2. Bead-based multiplexed immunoassay: streptavidin microsbeads functionalized with
     biotin-anti-CRP antibody are trapped in DRIE pillar arrays within each microchannel.
     Alexa-488-labeled CRP is loaded into the device and electrokinetically concentrated
     at the bead trap for 30 min (70 V). After buffer wash, fluorescence signal on the
     beads is measured. Serial concentration (ch#1 to ch#16, graded factors) generates
     16 distinct binding curves from a single inlet CRP concentration, extending the
     dynamic range from 44.66 to 2874.60 (ULD/LOD) and improving the LOD from
     162.2 ng/mL (reference) to 2.52 ng/mL (ch#16).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication:
  - Positive master mold: SU-8 photoresist patterned on silicon wafer; PDMS cast and cured
    at 65 C for 3 h; peeled from master.
  - Nanojunction: 20 wt% Nafion perflourinated ion-exchange resin (Sigma Aldrich) patterned
    by microflow patterning onto glass using a reversibly bonded PDMS channel
    (200 um wide x 50 um deep x 1 cm long); cured at 95 C for 5 min; PDMS removed.
  - Bonding: PDMS chip with concentration microchannels plasma-bonded onto the Nafion-
    patterned glass substrate.
  - Bead trap: DRIE (deep reactive-ion etching) fabricated pillar array for the bead-based
    immunoassay device (SU-8 resolution insufficient for pillar features).

Channel dimensions : 50 um wide x 15 um deep (sample microchannels)
Bead trap          : 100 um wide x 15 um deep; PDMS micro-pillar array
Nanojunction       : Nafion strip patterned perpendicular to microchannels
Electrodes         : Ag/AgCl (A-M Systems, Inc.)
Power supply       : Keithley 6487 dc power supply
Imaging            : Inverted fluorescence microscope (Olympus IX-51) + SensiCam CCD
                     (Cooke corp.); IPLab 3.6 image analysis (Scanalytics, Fairfax VA)

Multiplexing geometry:
  - Same-length channels (Fig. 2a): all microchannels have identical inlet length;
    same ET across all channels; uniform concentration factor.
  - Variable-length channels (Fig. 2b): inlet channels extended in zigzag pattern with
    different lengths; lower ET for longer channels; serial concentration factors 100-4000x
    across ch#1 (longest) to ch#16 (shortest).
  - Splitting/merging scheme at inlet/outlet matches hydraulic flow resistance.
  - Up to 128 channels demonstrated; single V_H and GND connection only.

--------------

Step 1 | Bead Functionalization (off-chip)
  Reagents      : Streptavidin beads (Applied Biosystems, 6-8 um, 35e6 beads/mL),
                  biotin-conjugated anti-CRP (Abcam ab86246)
  Operation     : Mix beads with antibody; stir 18 h at room temperature
  Duration      : 18 h (= 1080 min; encoded as 1080m; h token unsupported in compiler)
  Post-process  : Centrifuge to remove excess antibody; wash 3x with 1x PBS;
                  dilute tenfold before loading
  Notes         : Biotin-streptavidin conjugation links anti-CRP to bead surface.
                  Bead diameter 6-8 um provides optimal trap fit (1-2 beads vertically)
                  and avoids blocking sample flow or requiring sub-micron pillar geometry.

Step 2 | Device Blocking with BSA
  Reagents      : 1% BSA in buffer
  Operation     : Flush through microchannel for 10 min at room temperature
  Duration      : 10 min (600 s)
  Purpose       : Passivates PDMS channel walls; prevents nonspecific CRP adsorption
                  that would produce false-positive fluorescence signal on beads.

Step 3 | Pre-loading Buffer Wash (3x)
  Reagents      : 10 mM sodium phosphate dibasic buffer (pH 8.4)
  Operation     : Positive pressure applied 5 min per wash; 3 cycles
  Purpose       : Remove BSA from channel before bead loading; establish buffer baseline.

Step 4 | Bead Loading into Pillar-Array Traps
  Reagents      : Functionalized bead suspension (diluted tenfold), 10 mM buffer
  Loading       : Positive pressure at anodic reservoir; beads flow into pillar trap zone
  Trap geometry : DRIE pillar array, 100 um x 15 um; traps 6-8 um beads between pillars;
                  1-2 beads per trap stack vertically
  Post-loading wash : Positive pressure at cathodic reservoir; 3x wash to remove clogged

                  sodium phosphate dibasic buffer, pH 8.4
  Concentrations tested (5 independent runs):
    run1 : 1 ug/mL
    run2 : 100 ng/mL
    run3 : 10 ng/mL    [representative concentration encoded in BioScript]
    run4 : 1 ng/mL
    run5 : 100 pg/mL
  Operation     : Fill microchannels via positive pressure at anodic reservoir
  Notes         : Two independent channel-arm droplets dispensed in BioScript:

Step 6 | Electrokinetic Concentration - Channel 16 (ch16, ~4000x factor)
  Voltage       : 70 V dc (also tested at 50 V and 100 V; 70 V for immunoassay runs)
  Duration      : 30 min (1800 s)
  Mechanism     : Applied voltage across Ag/AgCl electrodes drives perm-selective ion
                  current through Nafion nanojunction; ion concentration polarization
                  depletes ions from anodic side, strongly repelling CRP toward anodic wall
                  and forming a concentrated CRP plug at the bead trap.
  Channel       : Ch16 has the shortest inlet microchannel; ET = deltaV / length is
                  maximised; ~4000x concentration factor achieved in 30 min.
  BioScript note: Encoded as `heat ... at 25c for 1800s`; standard abstraction for
                  voltage-driven concentration with no thermal component; 25c = ambient.

Step 7 | Electrokinetic Concentration - Channel 1 (ch1, ~100x factor)
  Voltage       : 70 V dc
  Duration      : 30 min (1800 s)
  Channel       : Ch1 has the longest inlet microchannel; lowest ET; ~100x concentration
                  factor. Represents the low-sensitivity end of the serial concentration
                  gradient and the low end of the extended dynamic range.
  Notes         : In the real device both arms concentrate simultaneously under the same
                  single applied voltage; serial modelling in BioScript reflects CFG
                  linearity constraint (no parallel execution primitives).

Step 8 | Post-Concentration Buffer Wash (3x per channel arm)
  Reagents      : 10 mM sodium phosphate dibasic buffer
  Operation     : Flush buffer through channel after concentration step
  Wash cycles   : 3 per arm (ch16 and ch1 washed independently in BioScript)
  Purpose       : Remove unbound bulk CRP from channel before fluorescence readout;
                  only bead-bound CRP signal is measured.
  Paper quote   : "the sample containing Alexa-488 labeled CRP was removed by flushing
                  sodium phosphate dibasic buffer solution through the device."

Step 9 | Fluorescence Detection of Bead-Bound CRP
  Instrument    : Inverted fluorescence microscope (Olympus IX-51) + SensiCam CCD;
                  IPLab 3.6 image analysis
  Fluorophore   : Alexa-488 (excitation ~490 nm, emission ~525 nm)
  Detection module : crpBindingDetection (BioScript)
  Detection duration : 30 s per channel arm
  Readout       : Fluorescent intensity on trapped beads; signal proportional to
                  amount of CRP bound to anti-CRP antibody on bead surface
  Background    : 40-50 AU (system baseline)
  Signal range  : 56-66 AU (run5, 100 pg/mL) to ~800 AU (run1, 1 ug/mL) at ch16
  QC gate (ch16): bindingSignal > 0 -> dispose; bindingSignal <= 0 -> drain
  QC gate (ch1) : ch1Signal > 0 -> dispose; ch1Signal <= 0 -> drain
  Notes         : Ch16 (shortest channel, ~4000x) gives highest signal and lowest LOD.
                  Ch1 (longest channel, ~100x) gives weakest signal; confirms low end

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Quantification of Extracellular Proteins, Protein Complexes and mRNAs in Single Cells by Proximity Sequencing
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-022-01684-z
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-022-01684-z
Journal      : Nature Methods, Vol. 19, December 2022, pp. 1578-1589
Platform     : Proximity Ligation Assay (PLA) combined with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq);
               plate-based (Smart-seq2 / 96-well) and droplet-based (Drop-seq / 10x Genomics Chromium) pipelines


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes Prox-seq (proximity sequencing), a method for simultaneous single-cell
measurement of extracellular proteins, pairwise protein complexes (up to n^2 per cell), and
whole-transcriptome mRNAs, using pairs of DNA-conjugated antibodies called Prox-seq probes. When
two probes bind proteins that are in physical proximity on the cell surface, their oligonucleotide
tails are ligated by T4 ligase via a universal connector region, producing a PLA product that
uniquely encodes the identities of both proteins. Only ligated products are captured and amplified
during downstream library preparation; unligated probes are automatically discarded. PLA products
are read out by next-generation sequencing alongside cDNA, enabling multimodal single-cell analysis.

The protocol is organised into three experimental arms that share probe design, ligation chemistry,
and sequencing infrastructure but differ in cell type, panel size, and library preparation platform:

  ARM 1 | Jurkat / Raji T cell / B cell validation (Drop-seq, 11-protein panel)
           Validates Prox-seq accuracy; confirms cell-type-specific PLA products; measures
           protein expression correlation with flow cytometry (Spearman rho = 0.88).

  ARM 2 | Human PBMC 38-marker panel (plate-based Smart-seq2 + 10x Genomics)
           Scales Prox-seq to 741 potential protein complexes; discovers the CD9-CD8 protein
           complex on naive CD8+ T cells as a novel interaction not previously described.

  ARM 3 | Primary human macrophage TLR signalling panel (plate-based, PFA-fixed cells)
           15 NF-kB pathway surface proteins (225 PLA products); LPS, PAM, or both stimulation
           at 5 min, 2 h, and 12 h; demonstrates additive signal integration, CD36 co-receptor
           activity, and identification of signalling inputs from receptor complex dynamics.

The complete Prox-seq workflow (probe incubation through sequencing library) takes approximately
1.5-3 hours of hands-on processing per sample batch depending on the arm.


PROBE DESIGN AND CHEMISTRY
---------------------------
Each protein target requires two Prox-seq probes: Probe A and Probe B, each consisting of a
monoclonal antibody conjugated to a single-stranded DNA oligomer.

Conjugation method:
  - Antibodies concentrated and buffer-exchanged into PBS using 50,000 MWCO concentrator (EMD Millipore)
  - Reacted with DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester (Sigma, 764019) in DMSO at 10:1 v/v DBCO:antibody solution
  - Incubated on ice for 1-2 h; purified through 50,000 MWCO concentrator
  - Antibody-to-DBCO ratio measured by UV-Vis (Nanodrop)
  - 1-2 ug DBCO-conjugated antibody (3-13 uM) combined with 80 uM azide-functionalized PLA
    oligomer (IDT) in PBS; allowed to react overnight at 4 C (click chemistry)
  - Long-term storage: reaction brought to 50% glycerol/PBS (Sigma Aldrich) at 4 C

PLA product structure (119 bp total):
  5' [PCR handle] -- [UMI] -- [Probe A barcode] -- [1st half connector] --
     [2nd half connector] -- [Probe B barcode] -- [Poly-A tail] 3'
  - 20 bases hybridise to connector oligomer to enable proximity ligation
  - UMI region corrects for PCR bias
  - Two barcode regions identify both proteins in each PLA product
  - 3' poly-A tail enables capture in poly-A-based scRNA-seq workflows
  - Universal connector region allows any Probe A to ligate with any Probe B

Physical range: 53.8-73.7 nm (estimated from ssDNA/dsDNA persistence length; spans typical
protein complex dimensions, ~10-50 nm)

Ligation solution (per reaction):
  - 50 mM HEPES pH 7.5
  - 10 mM MgCl2
  - 1 mM rATP (New England Biolabs)
  - 9.5 nM connector oligomer (IDT; sequence: TTTCACGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC)
  - 130 U/mL T4 ligase (NEB)
  - Volume: 100 uL (PBMC/macrophage arms); 300 uL (Jurkat/Raji arm)

Ligation efficiency: >90% of Prox-seq probes found ligated with other probes
(Extended Data Fig. 4b), explaining high concordance with flow cytometry.


CELL LINES AND PRIMARY CELLS
-----------------------------
- Jurkat (human T cell leukemia): model T cell line for ARM 1 validation.
  Cultured in RPMI + 10% FBS (Hyclone, Fisher Scientific), no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Gift from J. Huang (Pritzker School of Molecular Imaging, University of Chicago).

- Raji (human B cell lymphoma): model B cell line for ARM 1 validation.
  Cultured in RPMI + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Gift from J. Huang (Pritzker School of Molecular Imaging, University of Chicago).

- Human PBMCs (peripheral blood mononuclear cells): primary cells for ARM 2.
  Purchased from STEMCELL Technologies. Thawed at 37 C; washed 3x in 10 mL RPMI + 10% FBS
  (300g, 3 min); rested overnight at 37 C, 5% CO2 in RPMI + 10% FBS before use.

- Primary human macrophages: primary cells for ARM 3.
  Purchased from STEMCELL Technologies. Thawed, washed, and rested overnight in RPMI + 10% FBS.
  Plated in 10 wells of a non-tissue-culture-treated 24-well plate before stimulation.

ARM 1 | 11-protein panel (Jurkat / Raji; Drop-seq):
  Jurkat T cell markers : CD3, PD1, CD28, CD4, CD45RA, CD147, LFA1
  Raji B cell markers   : B7, ICAM1, HLA-DR, PDL1, CD147 (shared)

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Recovery of Phenotypically Sorted Cells Using Droplet-Digital Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://rscj.silverchair-cdn.com/rscj/content_public/journal/lc/25/17/10.1039_d5lc00415b/1/d5lc00415b.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/d5lc00415b
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2025, Vol. 25, pp. 4410-4421
Platform     : Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidics (flow-focusing droplet-in-channel + DMF electrode array)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a fully integrated Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidic platform for the
isolation and recovery of rare single cells and beads from individually processed droplets. The
system combines high-throughput fluorescence-activated droplet sorting (FADS) with on-demand
digital microfluidic (DMF) control at the collection site, enabling direct, precise, and automated
transfer of sorted single-cell-containing droplets into conventional 96-well culture plates.

The core innovation is the elimination of tubing at the collection step, replacing it with an
open-access semicircular outlet where a 3 uL recovery buffer droplet is pre-generated and
parked on-chip. After each sorting event, the sorted ~1 nL droplet is merged with the recovery
buffer via DMF electrode actuation (140 Vrms, 15 kHz, 3 x 500 ms), and the merged ~4 uL
volume is manually pipetted directly into a well. This approach removes the two primary failure
modes of conventional tubing collection: (i) droplet trapping in the PDMS-tubing arc and
(ii) droplet coalescence/cross-talk between adjacent sorted droplets in contact.

The protocol is divided into three experimental sub-protocols encoded sequentially in the
BioScript file, sharing the same D2 device (except Protocol 3 Step 1, which uses a separate
co-encapsulation chip for hybridoma-target cell pairing):

  1. Fluorescent bead recovery benchmark (pooled and single recovery vs tubing method)
  2. Low-input rare GFP HEK293 single-cell sorting, recovery, and 7-day viability
  3. Rare specific-antibody-secreting hybridoma cell screening and recovery
     (antibody discovery application; off-chip 2 h co-incubation + on-chip re-injection sort)

Key performance results:
  - Single bead recovery:    ~87% (D2) vs ~5% (tubing); p < 0.0001
  - Pooled bead recovery:    ~93.5% (D2) vs ~78.5% (tubing); SD 5.29% vs 26.1%
  - GFP HEK293 recovery:     >80% across all ratios (1:400, 1:1000) and cell inputs (1e4, 1e5)
  - Post-sort viability:     ~90% over 7 days; cells exhibit spreading by day 1
  - Hybridoma 1:400 ratio:   ~88% recovery
  - Hybridoma 1:1000 ratio:  ~78% recovery
  - Overall improvement:     18-fold over conventional methods


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium electrodes patterned on 50x75 mm glass slides (Telic, Valencia, CA).
            S1811 positive photoresist; UV exposure 7 s at 38-50 mW/cm2; developed MF-321;
            etched CR-4 chromium etchant; stripped AZ-300T photoresist stripper.
            Chromium contact pads covered with Scotch 3M tape during spin coating.

Layer ii  : PDMS dielectric, ~7 um thick. 1:10 w/w curing agent:prepolymer (DOW Silicones)
            spin-coated at 4500 rpm for 90 s; baked 90 C for 1 h.

Layer iii : PDMS channel layer. Two-layer SU-8 2075 master on 100 mm Si wafer (each layer
            ~100 um; spin: 10 s at 500 rpm, 30 s at 2000 rpm, 10 s at 500 rpm). Master
            silanised with chlorotrimethylsilane vapour 45 min. PDMS (1:10 w/w) poured and
            cured at room temperature >= 48 h to prevent shrinkage. Bonded to substrate after
            15 s O2 plasma treatment; baked 60 C for 30 min. Channels treated with Aquapel
            1 min, dried, baked 85 C for 20 min.

Device sections:
  - Flow-focusing droplet generator (two inlets: oil I1, aqueous cells/beads I2)
  - Fiber-optic PMT detection zone (200 um core multimode fiber, 0.49 NA, Thorlabs)
  - DMF binary sorting junction (patterned electrodes beneath channel)
  - Six pairs of arrest electrodes in sorting channel (hold sorted droplet in transit)
  - Two 200x200 um merging electrodes at channel-collection interface
  - Semicircular open-access collection outlet (3 mm biopsy punch + razor-excised semicircle)
  - Recovery buffer inlet (500 uL gastight syringe, 1/32-inch PEEK tubing)
  - Withdraw/waste channel (2.5 mL gastight syringe, -0.15 uL/s default)

Inlets  : I1 (2.5 mL gastight, HFE7500 + 2% surfactant, Tygon 0.06-inch OD),
          I2 (1 mL BD plastic, cells/beads, Tygon 0.06-inch OD),
          I3 (500 uL gastight, recovery buffer, 1/32-inch PEEK)
Outlets : O1 (waste/withdraw, 2.5 mL gastight, 1/32-inch PEEK),
          O2 (semicircular open-access collection site, direct pipette access)

Electrode actuation: 140 Vrms, 15 kHz AC, via optocoupler switches controlled by Teensy 4.1
                     microcontroller + port expander + Keysight 33210A function generator +

Pump system        : Cetoni neMESYS low-pressure syringe pump (automated flow control).

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

--- PROTOCOL 1: Fluorescent Bead Recovery ---

Step 1 | Device Priming and Baseline Flow
  Reagents  : HFE 7500 + 2% 008-fluoro-surfactant
  Operation : Inject oil at 0.15 uL/s via oil inlet; set waste syringe to -0.15 uL/s.
              All droplets routed to waste by default before any sorting event is triggered.
  Purpose   : Prime all channels; establish baseline flow direction.

Step 2 | Bead Suspension Preparation
  Reagents  : FluoSpheres 10 um blue-green, PBS, OptiPrep 16%
  Operation : Wash beads 3x PBS; dilute to 1e6 beads/mL; add 16% OptiPrep; load 1 mL BD syringe.
  Purpose   : OptiPrep prevents bead clumping and sedimentation during chip operation.

Step 3 | Bead Encapsulation in ~1 nL Droplets
  Flow rates : Oil 0.15 uL/s; aqueous bead phase 0.05 uL/s
  Droplet    : ~1 nL, monodisperse, ~50 Hz generation rate
  Sorting    : PMT threshold 7e3 to 2e4 photon counts; selects single-bead droplets.
               Below lower bound = empty droplet; above upper bound = multi-bead droplet.

Step 4 | PMT Detection, Sorting, and Recovery (Pooled or Single)
  Excitation : 470 nm (X-Cite XLED1); emission ~520 nm; detected by Hamamatsu H11890 PMT.
  Trigger    : Fluorescence peak within threshold window actuates sorting electrode.
  Recovery   : 3 uL PBS buffer generated at 1 uL/s; parked at semicircular outlet.
               7 s delay post-sort; 3x electrode actuation (140 Vrms, 15 kHz, 500 ms each).
               Merged ~4 uL transferred via P20 pipette (5 uL) to 96-well plate well
               pre-loaded with 100 uL PBS. Transfer time: ~10 s per well.
  Pooled     : 50 sorted droplets -> 1 well; then limiting dilution (1 bead/well).
  Single     : 1 sorted droplet -> 1 well (50 individual transfer operations).

  Results (pooled):  D2 ~93.5% vs tubing ~78.5%; D2 SD 5.29% vs tubing SD 26.1%.
  Results (single):  D2 ~87% vs tubing ~5%; p < 0.0001 (unpaired t-test).


--- PROTOCOL 2: Low-Input Rare GFP HEK293 Cell Recovery ---

Step 5 | Rare GFP Cell Mixture Preparation
  Cell lines : GFP-expressing HEK293 and WT HEK293; both at 1e6 cells/mL.
  Ratios     : 1:400 and 1:1000 (GFP:WT); total inputs 10,000 and 100,000 cells.
  Buffer     : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) + 80 uL OptiPrep per 400 uL suspension; gentle vortex.
  Syringe    : 480 uL loaded into 1 mL BD plastic syringe.

Step 6 | GFP Cell Encapsulation and Sorting
  Sorting threshold : 1e3 to 2.5e3 photon counts (lower than bead threshold; single GFP cell
                      fluorescence is weaker than bead signal).
  Detection         : singleCellGFPDetection module; 10 s detection window per droplet.
  Recovery          : Same D2 workflow as Step 4 but with 3 uL DMEM recovery buffer.
                      Well plate pre-loaded: 100 uL DMEM per well.

Step 7 | Post-Sort Conditioned Media Culture (First 24 h)
  Media      : 150 uL conditioned media per well (30% spent eGFP HEK supernatant,
               0.22 um filtered, + 70% fresh DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% P/S).
  Incubation : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 1440 min; IR: 86400 s).
  Purpose    : Conditioned media supports single-cell survival in the immediate post-sort period.

Step 8 | Viability Monitoring (SYTOX Blue, Days 1-7)
  Stain      : SYTOX Blue dead cell stain; 10 wells per time point per manufacturer protocol.
  Imaging    : EVOS M5000; every 24 h.
  Viability  : (non-blue wells) / (total stained wells) x 100.
  Detection  : viabilityDetection module; 60 s read.

Step 9 | 7-Day Clonal Expansion
  Media      : 50 uL fresh DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% P/S added every 48 h.
  Duration   : 6 remaining days after 24 h conditioned media phase = 8640 min (IR: 518400 s).
  Imaging    : EVOS M5000 bright-field + GFP fluorescence; every 24 h.
  Incubation : 37 C, 5% CO2.

  Results: >80% recovery across all ratios and cell inputs. ~90% viability over 7 days.
           Cells exhibit spreading by day 1 (positive viability indicator).
           Example: 1:1000 ratio, 6 GFP cells sorted and recovered in ~1 h operation.


--- PROTOCOL 3: Rare Antibody-Secreting Hybridoma Screening and Recovery ---

Step 10 | Hybridoma and Target Cell Preparation
  Hybridoma  : Specific (calcein-AM red, 1e6 cells/mL) + nonspecific (unstained) mixed at
               1:400 or 1:1000 in IMDM (no phenol red) + 10% FBS + IL-6 1 ng/mL + 11% OptiPrep.
  Target     : 3e6 cells/mL in IMDM (no phenol red) + 10% FBS + IL-6 1 ng/mL +
               Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse IgG 2.5 ug/mL + 11% OptiPrep. Stained CellTrace Blue.
  Prewash    : Both cell types washed 3x neat IMDM to remove FBS before experiment.
  Staining   : Calcein-AM red-orange (hybridoma); CellTrace Blue (target) per manufacturer protocol.

Step 11 | Co-Encapsulation (Separate Co-Encapsulation Chip)
  Chip       : Flow-focusing co-encapsulation chip (two cell inlets).
  Flow rates : Hybridoma 0.3 uL/s; target + secondary Ab 0.3 uL/s; oil 0.8 uL/s;
               withdrawal syringe (BD 1 mL plastic) at 1.4 uL/s.
  Occupancy  : 5-10% double-cell droplets (hybridoma + target) by Poisson statistics.
  Oil        : HFE 7500 + 2% 008-fluoro-surfactant (RAN Biotechnologies).

Step 12 | Off-Chip Droplet Incubation
  Duration   : 2 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 120 min; IR: 7200 s).
  Collection : Withdrawal syringe (BD 1 mL plastic) incubated in mammalian cell incubator.
  Mechanism  : Specific mAbs secreted by hybridoma cells bind surface antigen of co-encapsulated
               target cells. Pre-added Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibodies bind primary mAbs,
               generating sharp high-intensity green fluorescence (>18,000 counts) uniquely in
               specific-Ab + target cell doublet droplets.
  Signal logic:
    Specific-Ab producer + target cell  : >18,000 photon counts (Alexa Fluor 488 surface-bound)
    Non-specific hybridoma only          : medium fluorescence (free secondary Ab baseline)
    Target cell only or empty            : background fluorescence

Step 13 | Re-Injection into D2 Sorting Chip
  Flow rates : Droplet re-injection 0.02 uL/s; spacing oil 0.15 uL/s; waste -0.12 uL/s.
               Slower re-injection rate maintains droplet integrity post-off-chip incubation.
  Throughput : ~50 Hz sorting; ~1 nL monodisperse droplets.

Step 14 | Antibody-Binding Sort and Single-Pair Recovery
  Detection  : antibodyBindingDetection module; 488 nm excitation; 520 nm emission.
               Sorting threshold: 1.8e4 to 3e4 photon counts (green channel).
  Recovery   : 3 uL IMDM + 10% FBS + IL-6 1 ng/mL recovery buffer generated at 1 uL/s.
               7-9 s delay post-sort; 3x electrode actuation (140 Vrms, 15 kHz, 500 ms each).
               Merged contents pipetted (P20, 5 uL) to 96-well plate pre-loaded with 100 uL
               IMDM + 10% FBS + IL-6 1 ng/mL + 1% P/S. Plate to incubator immediately.
  Imaging    : EVOS M5000; confirm specific-Ab hybridoma by:
               calcein-AM red (hybridoma) + CellTrace Blue (target) + Alexa Fluor 488 green (bound Ab).

  Results: 1:400 ratio ~88% recovery; 1:1000 ratio ~78% recovery.
           Compared to ~30% conventional droplet recovery (Clausell-Tormos et al.).
