PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Proximity sequencing for the detection of mRNA, extracellular proteins and extracellular protein complexes in single cells
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01030-x
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-024-01030-x
Journal      : Nature Protocols, Volume 19, December 2024, pp. 3568-3589
Platform     : Proximity Ligation Assay (PLA) + 10x Chromium 3' V3.1 single-cell RNA sequencing


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq), a method for the simultaneous
measurement of extracellular proteins, mRNA, and hundreds of extracellular protein complexes
from single cells. Prox-seq combines a proximity ligation assay (PLA) with single-cell mRNA
sequencing, enabling characterisation of each individual cell across three analyte categories:
proteins, mRNA, and protein complexes. The method is compatible with Drop-seq, 10x Chromium
3' V3.1, and plate-based SMART-Seq2 single-cell isolation platforms. This BioScript file
encodes the 10x Chromium 3' arm of the protocol.

The core principle is that each targeted protein is labelled with two DNA-barcoded antibody
probes (probe A and probe B). When two probes from any two proteins are within 50-70 nm on
the cell surface, a short connector oligomer bridges their oligo tails and T4 ligase produces
a covalent PLA ligation product. This product carries the barcodes of both proteins, enabling
identification of which two proteins formed a complex. PLA products are co-captured with mRNA
during 10x GEM generation using an additional U_fwd primer in the amplification mix, then
separated from cDNA by SPRI size selection (0.6x ratio) and independently sequenced.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. Probe preparation: antibody buffer exchange, DBCO conjugation, click-chemistry
     oligo attachment (Steps 1-26; ~2 h work + overnight incubation)
  2. Sample processing (PLA): cell staining, PLA ligation, post-ligation washes (Steps 27-40; ~3 h)
  3. 10x Chromium single-cell isolation and library construction (Steps 87-102; ~8 h)
  4. Next-generation sequencing on Illumina NextSeq 500/550 (Steps 132-134; ~1-2 days)
  5. Computational analysis: cDNA alignment (Cell Ranger), PLA alignment (custom Java),
     protein abundance and protein complex quantification (Python; Steps 135-147)

The total wet-lab protocol requires approximately 16 h of work spread across several days.
Prox-seq is currently the only single-cell technology capable of measuring hundreds of protein
complexes simultaneously, with a reported throughput of 38 targets (741 protein pairs) and
an estimated maximum of ~100 targets (5,050 possible pairs) in a single experiment.


PROBE CHEMISTRY
---------------
Probe conjugation uses copper-free click chemistry (strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition):

Step 1 : Antibody buffer exchange into PBS using Amicon Ultra-0.5 concentrator (50,000 MWCO).
         CRITICAL: antibodies must be free of protein additives (BSA, gelatin) which react
         with DBCO NHS ester. Compatible formulations: azide, Tris, glycerol.

Step 2 : DBCO conjugation. Dissolve dibenzocyclooctyne-PEG4-N-hydroxysuccinimidyl ester
         (Sigma-Aldrich 764019) in DMSO; prepare 2 mM stock (molar extinction coefficient
         12,000 M-1 cm-1 at 309 nm). Mix with antibody at 1:10 DBCO:Ab volume ratio
         (0.5-2 mg/mL antibody; CRITICAL). Incubate on ice (0 C) for 60 min.

Step 3 : Purification and QC. Repeat concentrator wash to remove unconjugated DBCO.
         Measure absorbance at 280 nm (antibody; extinction coefficient 204,000 M-1 cm-1)
         and 309 nm (DBCO; extinction coefficient 12,000 M-1 cm-1) on Nanodrop.
         Target DBCO:Ab ratio: 1-10. Optimal input mass: 100 ug.
         Store aliquots at -20 C; avoid freeze-thaw.

Step 4 : Oligo conjugation (click chemistry). Combine 2 ug DBCO-Ab with equal volume of
         80 uM azide-functionalized DNA oligomers (IDT custom; Probe A and Probe B oligos
         carry unique barcodes; sequences from Vistain et al. Nat. Methods 2022).
         Incubate overnight at 4 C (16 h = 960 min; reaction can extend to 2 days).
         Store finished probes in 50% (wt/vol) glycerol/PBS at -20 C; stable >= 1 year.
         Probe binding buffer: PBS + 0.1% BSA + 0.1 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA + 6.7 nM/isotype.
         Final probe panel: 2.5 nM probe A + 2.5 nM probe B per target protein (5 nM total).


CELL LINES
----------
- PBMCs (peripheral blood mononuclear cells): primary cell line used in key experiments;
  Prox-seq discovered novel CD9-CD8 homodimer association specific to naive CD8 T cells.
- Jurkat T cells: positive control for CD147 homodimers (common, detectable as protein complex).
- NCI-H1299 or MCF-7 (user-defined): general model cell lines; any cell line accessible
  by anti-surface-protein antibodies is compatible.
- All cells cultured at 37 C, 5% CO2; resuspended in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) for protocol steps.
- 10x Chromium requires 20,000 viable cells input (>80% viability).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Antibody Buffer Exchange (Steps 1-12)
  Reagents : Antibody in storage buffer, PBS (GIBCO, cat. 20012027)
  Equipment : Amicon Ultra-0.5 concentrator, 50,000 MWCO (EMD Millipore, cat. UFC5050)
  Spin      : 14,000g, 4 C; three wash cycles (500 uL, 450 uL, 450 uL PBS)
  Duration  : 1 + 5 + 5 + 10 min spin cycles (BioScript: three mix steps of 5m, 5m, 10m)
  Purpose   : Remove protein additives from antibody storage buffer.

Step 2 | DBCO Stock Preparation and Antibody Conjugation (Steps 13-19)
  Reagents  : DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester (Sigma 764019), DMSO (Sigma D8418), PBS, concentrated Ab
  Operation : Dissolve DBCO in 10 uL DMSO; dilute 1:100 in PBS for 309 nm Nanodrop QC;
              prepare 2 mM stock. Combine with antibody at 1:10 volume ratio.
  Incubation: On ice (0 C), 60 min (extendable to 120 min). BioScript: heat at 0c for 60m.
  Critical  : Antibody concentration must be 0.5-2 mg/mL before conjugation.

Step 3 | DBCO-Antibody Purification and QC Gate (Steps 20-23)
  Reagents  : PBS, Nanodrop spectrophotometer
  Operation : Repeat concentrator wash (Steps 4-12); measure 280 nm and 309 nm absorbance.
  QC pass   : DBCO:Ab ratio 1-10 (dbcoSignal > 0) -> dispose dbcoReaction; proceed.
  QC fail   : Ratio out of range (dbcoSignal <= 0) -> drain; troubleshoot scale or DBCO ratio.

Step 4 | Azide-DNA Oligo Conjugation (Steps 24-26)
  Reagents  : DBCO-Ab (2 ug), Azide-DNA oligo A (80 uM), Azide-DNA oligo B (80 uM)
  Reaction  : Copper-free click chemistry; 4 C, 16 h (960 min). BioScript: heat at 4c for 960m.
  Output    : Prox-seq probe panel (2.5 nM each probe; 5 nM total per targeted protein).

Step 5 | Cell Pelleting, Fc Blocking, and BSA Wash (Steps 27-31)
  Reagents  : PBS, TruStain FcX (Biolegend, cat. 422302), 1% BSA/PBS
  Spin      : 300-500g, 4 C, 5 min
  Fc block  : 10 min; prevents non-specific antibody binding.
  Purpose   : Prepare cells for probe staining.

Step 6 | Prox-seq Probe Staining (Steps 32-34)
  Reagents  : Cell pellet, Prox-seq probe panel in probe binding buffer
  Volume    : 30 uL probe mixture per 100,000 cells
  Incubation: 37 C, 30-60 min (45 min modelled in BioScript as midpoint).
  Purpose   : Antibody-DNA probes bind target proteins on cell surface.

Step 7 | Post-Staining Washes (Step 35)
  Reagents  : 1% BSA/PBS, 1 mL per wash
  Washes    : 3x by centrifugation and resuspension (300-500g, 4 C, 5 min each).
  Note      : If overprocessing is a concern, reduce by at least one wash.

Step 8 | PLA Ligation (Steps 36-37)
  Reagents  : Ligation buffer (50 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM rATP,
              9.5 nM connector TTTCACGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC, 130 U/mL T4 ligase),
              RNase inhibitor (murine; NEB, cat. M0314L)
  Volume    : 100 uL ligation buffer per sample
  Incubation: 37 C, 30 min
  Mechanism : Connector oligo bridges probe A and probe B when within 50-70 nm;
              T4 ligase seals the nick -> covalent PLA ligation product.
  Optional  : Free oligo method (Step 38): add free oligos A and B with additional connector
              in two sequential 15-min steps to ensure all probes are measurable.
              Benefits minor for highly expressed target panels; increases overprocessing risk.

Step 9 | Post-Ligation Washes and Viability Check (Steps 39-40)
  Reagents  : 1% BSA/PBS (2 washes), PI (Invitrogen, cat. P1304MP),
              Dead cell removal kit (Miltenyi, cat. 130-090-101)
  Washes    : 2x post-ligation washes to remove excess connector and ligase.
  Viability : viableCells derived from postLigWash2 + Miltenyi kit (independently).
              stainedForSort derived from postLigWash2 + PI (independently).
              CRITICAL (BioScript): viableCells must NOT appear inside either gate branch
              to remain live at bsbbif_7_j. Only stainedForSort is disposed/drained in gate.
  QC pass   : viabilitySignal > 0 (>80% viable) -> dispose stainedForSort; proceed to 10x.
  QC fail   : viabilitySignal <= 0 -> drain stainedForSort; reduce washes or increase spin.

Step 10 | 10x Chromium GEM Generation (Steps 87-90)
  Reagents  : Viable cells (20,000), Chromium Next GEM Chip G (cat. 1000127),
              Chromium GEL beads v3.1 (cat. 1000268), partitioning oil,
              KAPA HiFi ReadyMix, dNTP mix, U_fwd primer (2 uM; CRITICAL)
  Filter    : 40 um cell strainer before loading to remove clumps (Step 88).
  Operation : 10x 3' single-cell isolation per manufacturer protocol until just before cDNA
              amplification; then add 1 uL of 2 uM U_fwd primer to amplification mix (Step 90).
  PCR       : 12 cycles (98 C 20s / 67 C 20s / 72 C 20s); U_fwd co-amplifies PLA products.
  Note      : Without U_fwd, PLA products are not amplified and are lost.

Step 11 | SPRI Size Selection: Separate cDNA from PLA Products (Steps 91-94)
  Reagents  : SPRIselect beads (Beckman Coulter, cat. B23317) x2 independent dispensations,
              Buffer EB (Qiagen, cat. 19086)
  cDNA path : 0.6x SPRI (cDNA ~1,000 bp binds beads; PLA ~100 bp stays in supernatant).
              Wash beads 2x 80% ethanol; elute cDNA into 35 uL Buffer EB.
  PLA path  : CRITICAL (Step 92): SAVE 75 uL supernatant containing PLA products.
              In standard 10x protocol this supernatant is DISCARDED; in Prox-seq it is retained.
  TapeStation QC: cDNA peak ~1,000 bp (Fig. 2c); PLA peak ~100 bp (Fig. 2d).
  BioScript SSA: Two independent SPRI dispensations (spriBeads_cDNA and spriBeads_PLA)
              produce spriMix_cDNA and spriMix_PLA as separate single-use variables.
              spriMix_cDNA consumed by elutedCDNA; spriMix_PLA flows through BB8/BB9 gate
              UNTOUCHED (not disposed or drained) and consumed at bsbbif_10_j by plaCleanup.
  QC pass   : librarySignal > 0 -> dispose(spriMix_cDNA); spriMix_PLA passes through.
  QC fail   : librarySignal <= 0 -> drain(spriMix_cDNA); check AMPure bead volume.

Step 12 | cDNA Gene Expression Library Construction (Step 95)
  Reagents  : Purified cDNA (10 uL), KAPA HiFi ReadyMix, 10x V3.1 library kit
  Protocol  : Standard 10x Genomics single-cell 3' V3.1 gene expression library protocol.
  Output    : GEX library (~500 bp; Fig. 2e); 1% vol/vol PhiX spike for sequencing.

Step 13 | PLA Product Library Construction (Steps 96-102)
  Reagents  : PLA supernatant (spriMix_PLA), SPRIselect beads (2.1x then 1.2x),
              Buffer EB, KAPA HiFi ReadyMix, 10x_SI_PCR primer (0.2 uM),
              P7_N70X_Custom2 primer (0.2 uM), nuclease-free water
  2.1x SPRI : Bind PLA products from supernatant; wash 2x 80% ethanol; elute 40 uL Buffer EB.
  PCR       : 12 cycles; 98 C 2 min initial denature; 98 C 20s / 60 C 30s / 72 C 20s;
              72 C 5 min; hold 4 C. (60 C anneal; lower than cDNA due to short amplicon.)
  1.2x SPRI : Final cleanup; elute into 40 uL Buffer EB.
  QC        : Qubit (concentration) + TapeStation (size distribution; target ~228 bp; Fig. 2f).
              Suboptimal example: no clear 228 bp peak (Fig. 2h) -> repeat 1.2x SPRI cleanup.
  Storage   : -20 C until sequencing.
  QC pass   : assaySignal > 0 -> proceed to sequencing.
  QC fail   : assaySignal <= 0 -> drain plaLibrary and gexLibrary; troubleshoot SPRI volumes.

Step 14 | Next-Generation Sequencing (Step 133)
  Platform  : Illumina NextSeq 500/550
  cDNA run  : High-output 150-cycle kit (cat. 20024907).
              Read 1: 28 cycles; i7 index: 10 cycles; i5 index: 10 cycles; Read 2: 90 cycles.
              PhiX: 1% vol/vol.
  PLA run   : Mid-output 150-cycle kit (cat. 20024904). Separate run from cDNA library.
              Read 1: 28 cycles; i7 index: 8 cycles; Read 2: 75 cycles.
              PhiX: 40% vol/vol (CRITICAL: low PLA library complexity requires high PhiX).
              Custom primers: DropPLA_Read2 (spiked into Illumina read 2 primer),
              DropPLA_i7Read (custom i7 read primer) prepared per Illumina instructions.

Step 15 | cDNA Alignment (Steps 135-138; computational)
  Software  : Cell Ranger v6.1.1+ (10x Genomics)
  Commands  : cellranger mkref (build reference genome index from NCBI/Ensembl files)
              cellranger count (alignment + gene-barcode + cell-barcode matrix output)
  Output    : Gene expression matrix; loadable in R with Read10x; Seurat/Scanpy compatible.

Step 16 | PLA Product Alignment (Steps 139-143; computational)
  Software  : PLA_alignment.jar (github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq/blob/master/PLA_alignment.jar)
  Commands  : ReadAlignment10x -> BulidCellBarcodes -> CellBarcodeCorrection (SUFFIX=-1 for 10x)
              -> UMIMerging -> DigitalCount
  Output    : Digital PLA product Expression (DPE) matrix (text file).
  Note      : Detailed alignment guidance: github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq/blob/master/alignment_manual.pdf

Step 17 | Protein Abundance and Complex Quantification (Steps 144-147; computational)
  Software  : Python scripts; github.com/tay-lab/NProt_data-src (Anaconda3/Python v3.8.8)
  Steps     : Import DPE matrix -> PLA object.
              calculateProteinCount -> protein_count dataframe.
              predictComplex (method='iterative' default; method='lr' for free oligo only)
              -> complex_count dataframe.
  Filtering : Double filter: (1) mRNA-based cell barcode correction; (2) filter cells with
              too few or too many PLA product UMIs.
  Output    : Three integrated count matrices (mRNA, protein, protein complex) for
              multimodal single-cell analysis in Seurat or Scanpy.
  Proximity noise: Random co-localisation of proteins within 50-70 nm without functional
              interaction; the iterative method accounts for this computationally.

ASSAY TYPE: Cell-Based Non-Invasive Diagnostic Testing Using the DISCO Platform -- Detergent Direct Capture (DDC) Reconstitution of the ABC Transporter MsbA in Peptidiscs and Malachite Green ATPase Activity Assay

REAGENTS USED:
  - MsbA-Enriched Membrane Extract (E. coli membrane fraction bearing His6-tagged MsbA)
  - DDM Detergent (n-dodecyl-beta-D-maltoside, 1% w/v solubilization solution)
  - Peptidisc Peptide (NSPr amphipathic peptide, molar excess)
  - Dilution Buffer (Buffer A: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 100 mM NaCl, 10% glycerol)
  - Wash Buffer (Buffer A, used for Ni-NTA resin washing)
  - Elution Buffer (Buffer A + 600 mM Imidazole)
  - ATP Reagent (2 mM ATP in reaction buffer: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2)
  - Malachite Green Reagent (Malachite green solution with 0.05% Triton X-100)

STEPS:
1. Solubilization: Solubilize the MsbA-enriched membrane extract with 1% DDM detergent for 30 min at 4 C to release MsbA from the native membrane.
2. Peptidisc reconstitution: Mix the clarified detergent extract with a molar excess of peptidisc peptide (NSPr) to initiate detergent-direct-capture reconstitution.
3. Dilution/concentration cycles: Rapidly dilute the mixture into fresh dilution buffer and concentrate over a filter; repeat this dilution/concentration cycle 3 times to progressively lower the detergent concentration to a calculated ~0.008% final level.
4. Resin binding and washing: Incubate the reconstituted mixture with Ni-NTA resin for 1 hour at 4 C, then wash the resin with wash buffer to remove unbound material.
5. Elution: Elute the peptidisc-reconstituted MsbA (DDC-MsbA) from the resin using elution buffer containing imidazole.
6. ATPase reaction: Combine the eluted peptidisc-MsbA with ATP reagent and incubate at 37 C for 10 min to allow ATP hydrolysis.
7. Colorimetric detection: Add Malachite green reagent to the reaction, incubate at room temperature for 10 min to allow color development, then measure light absorption at 660 nm to quantify the released inorganic phosphate and calculate the initial rate of ATP hydrolysis, then discard the analyzed reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: Successful peptidisc reconstitution and ATPase activity measurement is confirmed when the DDC-MsbA preparation shows comparable purity and yield to other reconstitution methods (SDS-PAGE), a distinct blue-native gel migration pattern reflecting captured endogenous lipid content, and an ATPase rate elevated 2- to 5-fold relative to detergent-solubilized MsbA (DDM-MsbA), consistent with the lipid-mediated increase in both thermal stability and ATPase activity described for peptidisc preparations with higher endogenous lipid content.

Title        : Measuring Droplet Volume in Home-Made Microfluidic Devices
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/measuring-droplet-volume-in-home-made-microfluidic-3byl46drgo5d/v1
DOI Link     : https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.mj5c4q6

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a bead-based volumetric calibration procedure for determining droplet
volume in home-made microfluidic devices. Monodisperse polystyrene beads suspended at a known
concentration are co-flowed with PBS through the device to generate droplets. The number of
beads per droplet (droplet occupancy) is measured by microscopy over several hundred droplets,
and the droplet volume is calculated from the occupancy and the known bead concentration in
the combined aqueous phase.

This is a device characterisation/calibration protocol, not a cell biology assay. It is
applicable to any home-made droplet microfluidic chip prior to biological experiments, providing
a ground-truth volume estimate without requiring dedicated optical volume sensors.


PRINCIPLE
---------
Beads (10 um carboxylated polystyrene) are resuspended in Drop-seq lysis buffer at
1000 beads/uL and loaded into the bead syringe. PBS is loaded into the cell-channel syringe.
When both syringes co-flow into the microfluidic device at equal rates, the combined aqueous
phase has an effective bead concentration of:

    1000 beads/uL (bead syringe) / 2 (co-flow dilution) = 500 beads/uL in droplet fluid

After generating droplets, beads inside droplets are counted under microscopy to compute:

    Droplet occupancy  = total beads counted / total droplets counted
    Droplet volume     = droplet occupancy / 500 beads/uL   [units: uL per droplet]

A minimum of several hundred droplets should be counted to obtain a statistically sound estimate.

PolyBeads_LysisBuffer:
  - Monodisperse carboxylated polystyrene beads, ~10 um diameter
  - Standard (non-fluorescent): Bangs Labs catalog PC06N-11355
  - Fluorescent (recommended): Bangs Labs catalog FC06F-10163
  - Suspension buffer: Drop-seq lysis buffer
  - Concentration: 1000 beads/uL
  - Loaded in syringe with magnetic mixer (as per standard barcoded-bead protocol)

PBS:
  - Phosphate-buffered saline (standard, no additives required)
  - Loaded into the syringe intended for cells (no cells present in calibration run)
  - Co-flow with bead syringe; halves bead concentration to 500 beads/uL in droplet fluid


PROTOCOL STEPS

Step 1 | Prepare Bead Suspension
  Reagent      : PolyBeads_LysisBuffer
  Operation    : dispense (BioScript abstraction for syringe loading)
  Details      : Wash and resuspend 10 um carboxylated polystyrene beads in Drop-seq lysis
                 buffer at 1000 beads/uL. Draw into syringe equipped with a magnetic mixer
                 to prevent bead settling during the run.

Step 2 | Load PBS into Cell-Channel Syringe
  Reagent      : PBS
  Operation    : dispense (BioScript abstraction for syringe loading)
  Details      : Load the syringe intended for cells with regular PBS. No cells are present
                 in this calibration run. The co-flow of bead suspension and PBS at equal
                 volumetric rates gives an effective bead concentration of 500 beads/uL
                 in the combined droplet fluid.

Step 3 | Co-Flow and Droplet Generation
  Inputs       : beadSuspension, pbsFlow
  Operation    : mix (BioScript abstraction for co-flow junction merging)
  Duration     : 30 s (stabilisation period before droplet collection begins)
  Details      : Connect all tubing to the appropriate channels in the microfluidic device.
                 Start both syringe pumps. The bead syringe and PBS syringe co-flow into the
                 aqueous inlet; the carrier oil generates droplets at the T-junction or
                 flow-focus nozzle.
  Note         : mix here models the co-flow merging of two aqueous streams at the chip inlet
                 junction, not a DMF electrode-merging event.

Step 4 | Bead Counting Detection (Droplet Occupancy Measurement)
  Input        : combinedFluid
  Operation    : detect (beadCountDetection module)
  Duration     : 60 s (image acquisition and counting window)
  Details      : Image several hundred droplets under microscopy (fluorescence channel if
                 fluorescent beads; brightfield otherwise). Count total beads inside all
                 imaged droplets and the number of droplets counted. Compute:
                   Droplet occupancy = total_beads / total_droplets
                   Droplet volume    = occupancy / 500 beads/uL

  QC Gate:

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based Pyrosequencing Using Digital Microfluidics (on-chip PCR amplification, magnetic-bead-based purification, and cyclic dNTP pyrosequencing with real-time luminescence detection)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Genomic DNA (C. parapsilosis genomic DNA purified from culture, PCR template)
  - Primer Mix (ITS1 forward primer 5'-Bio-tccgtaggtgaacctgcgg-3' and ITS2 reverse primer 5'-gctgcgttcttcatcgatgc-3', 0.24 uM each, amplifying a 229 bp fragment)
  - PCR Reagent (20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.4, 1.5 mM MgCl2, 50 mM KCl, 0.2 mM dNTPs, 1 U Platinum Taq polymerase)
  - Magnetic Beads (streptavidin-coated magnetic beads for capture of the biotinylated PCR product)
  - Wash Buffer (used in repeated merge-and-split wash cycles to purify bead-bound ssDNA)
  - Sequencing Primer (hybridizes to the bead-bound single-stranded template for pyrosequencing, e.g. P6/P6-1-style primer)
  - Enzyme Mix (ATP sulfurylase/luciferase/apyrase pyrosequencing enzyme cocktail with adenosine 5' phosphosulfate and luciferin)
  - dNTP Reagents (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP dispensed sequentially in a defined nucleotide addition order)

STEPS:
1. PCR setup: combine genomic DNA template with the ITS1/ITS2 primer mix and PCR reagent (Tris-HCl/MgCl2/KCl/dNTP/Taq polymerase buffer) to form the amplification reaction droplet.
2. Hot start: incubate the reaction at 95 C for 2 minutes.
3. Amplification: cycle 40 times through 95 C for 15 s (denaturation) and 60 C for 30 s (anneal/extend).
4. Final extension: incubate the reaction at 72 C for 1 minute.
5. Bead capture: merge the amplified, biotinylated PCR product droplet with a streptavidin magnetic bead droplet to capture the product.
6. Magnetic bead washing: repeatedly merge a fresh wash buffer droplet with the bead-bound droplet and split off the wash droplet, cycling to purify the captured single-stranded template (demonstrated over hundreds of wash cycles with no observable bead loss).
7. Primer annealing: merge the washed, bead-bound ssDNA with sequencing primer and incubate at 65 C to hybridize the sequencing primer.
8. Enzyme addition: merge the annealed template droplet with the ATP-sulfurylase/luciferase/apyrase enzyme mix to prepare the pyrosequencing reaction droplet.
9. Cyclic nucleotide dispensing and detection: in a defined dispensing order, sequentially merge each dNTP droplet (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP) with the reaction droplet and measure the real-time luminescence (photons/sec) generated by each addition; a rising signal indicates nucleotide incorporation into the growing strand, while a flat/background signal indicates a non-incorporating ("bkgd") addition, together revealing the template sequence.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Rapid Mixing Protocol on Digital Microfluidics via Reciprocating Droplet Motions - methodological protocol for high-efficiency droplet mixing using contact charge electrophoresis (CCEP) to overcome diffusion limitations during automated chemical reactions.

REAGENTS/MATERIALS USED:
  - Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) Aqueous Solution (0.4 wt%, 0.2 +/- 0.05 uL droplets, density 1.01 g/cm^3)
  - Phenolphthalein (PHP) Indicator Solution (ethanol:distilled water:PHP = 79:20:1 wt%, 0.2 +/- 0.05 uL droplets, density 0.78 g/cm^3; colorless, turns pink on reaction with base)
  - Silicone Oil (KF-96L, dynamic viscosity 28.6 mPa*s, density 0.95 g/cm^3), used as the dielectric suspending medium filling the chamber
  - Blue Dye Droplet and Yellow Dye Droplet (alternative colorant pair used to visually confirm mixing, merging to green when fully mixed)

STEPS:
1. Platform setup: Assemble a 3D digital microfluidic (DMF) platform with two parallel pin-header-socket electrode modules (2 mm pitch), a lower electrode module mounted in a U-shaped 3D-printed chamber with transparent acrylic walls, and an upper electrode module mounted on a translation stage (vertical spacing adjustable 2-4 mm). Fill the chamber with silicone oil as the dielectric suspending medium.
2. Horizontal droplet charging and transport: Dispense a droplet of NaOH solution so it contacts a ground electrode (becoming negatively charged) and a droplet of PHP indicator solution so it contacts a positively activated electrode (becoming positively charged); sequentially actuate neighboring electrodes to transport both droplets horizontally toward each other.
3. Electrocoalescence (horizontal case): When the oppositely charged NaOH and PHP droplets meet, they merge electrically via electrostatic interaction into a single droplet.
4. Horizontal reciprocating mixing: Actuate the merged droplet to shake horizontally back and forth between the positive and ground electrodes (CCEP actuation at 200 V, 300 V, or 400 V, 2 mm electrode pitch) until the PHP colorless-to-pink color change indicates mixing is complete, typically within about one minute (as fast as ~2 s to reach a 0.7-0.8 mixing index).
5. Horizontal/vertical droplet charging and transport (3D case): Dispense NaOH and PHP droplets so both contact positive electrodes (both positively charged); sequentially actuate neighboring electrodes to transport the droplets horizontally toward each other, then apply a ground signal to the upper electrode to transport them vertically.
6. Electrocoalescence (vertical case): As the droplets reciprocate vertically between upper and lower electrodes, they acquire opposite charges (due to differing reciprocation speeds from their density difference) and merge electrically when they touch.
7. Vertical reciprocating mixing: Actuate the merged droplet to shake vertically between the lower and upper electrodes (CCEP actuation at 400 V, electrode distance 2, 3, or 4 mm) until the PHP color change confirms complete mixing; the fastest full mixing (~2.4 s, mixing index 0.95) is achieved at 4 mm electrode distance and 400 V.
8. Mixing-index quantification: Record droplet motion/mixing at 120 fps (digital camera with macro lens) and internal flow patterns at 250-1000 fps (high-speed camera); crop and convert images to grayscale, identify the region of interest by edge detection, correct pixel intensity (grayscale minus green channel), and compute the standard deviation of corrected intensity per frame to calculate the temporal mixing index M(%) = (1 - (sigma - sigma_final)/sigma_final) x 100.
9. Repeat steps 2-4 (horizontal) or 5-7 (vertical) with a blue-dye/yellow-dye droplet pair in place of NaOH/PHP to visually confirm mixing (blue + yellow merging to green) and validate the CCEP-driven reciprocating-motion mixing procedure for general reagent pairs.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Droplet-Based Screen for Wavelength-Dependent Lipid Production in Algae
Source Link  : https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Steve-Shih/publication/262874413_A_droplet-based_screen_for_wavelength-dependent_lipid_production_in_algae/links/00b7d53909cf950ec1000000/A-droplet-based-screen-for-wavelength-dependent-lipid-production-in-algae.pdf?__cf_chl_f_tk=N2GSHFBauUsIm5B8xwZxkkXn_LuBAACs9pC5GteCtAg-1782901072-1.0.1.1-e0TB_oLJRbhpUUI8lmO01R0_1wpK5AF10F3ILeZ6Fv4
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c4ee01123f
Journal      : Energy & Environmental Science, 2014, DOI: 10.1039/c4ee01123f
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) on open electrode array with custom LED illumination


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first microfluidic method applied to discovery of algae culture
conditions favourable for generating high-energy lipids. The platform uses digital microfluidics
(DMF) — where droplets are manipulated on an open electrode array by application of electric
fields — to perform automated, multiplexed long-term culture and analysis of Cyclotella cryptica
(CCMP 332), a diatom widely used as a model organism for biofuel lipid research.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. Multicolour illumination screen: 7 LED wavelengths + dark control at two intensities,
     screening neutral lipid production and biomass accumulation simultaneously over 24 h.
  2. Blue/yellow cycling screen: 8 timed combinations of blue (~450 nm) and yellow (~580 nm)
     illumination at high intensity, identifying the optimal condition for biofuel production.
  3. ROS mechanistic assay: DCFDA fluorescence quantification of reactive oxygen species under
     yellow, blue, and ascorbate-treated conditions to elucidate the photooxidative stress
     mechanism underlying wavelength-dependent lipid accumulation.

The method reduces manual intervention from >600 pipette steps (conventional multiwell screen)
to fewer than 20, while generating equivalent or greater data density. Two pipette steps are
sufficient to run a single device for 24 h, producing 48 measurements (24 absorbance + 24
fluorescence) across 8 culture conditions at 3 time points.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Open-array DMF device; no pumps, valves, or mechanical mixers required.

Electrode layout (per device):
  - 2 four-electrode active reservoirs (algae suspension + LipidTOX dye)
  - 8 algae culture zone electrodes
  - 8 bussed dye dispensing electrodes
  - 8 absorbance detection electrodes (L-shaped, for daughter droplet routing)
  - 8 fluorescence detection electrodes
  - 8 waste reservoir electrodes with 1 mm-diameter through-holes

Dispensing: All dispenser electrode modules feature narrow central electrodes
  (>= 0.5:1 ratio relative to destination electrode) to facilitate necking during
  droplet formation; critical for reliable parallel dispensing on bussed electrodes.

Detection zones: 9 mm pitch; compatible with standard 384-well multiwell plate reader.
  Transparent windows for transmission (absorbance) and opaque-bottom wells for fluorescence.

Waste management: Spent reagents driven to waste electrodes; fluid wicks through 1 mm
  through-holes onto absorbent tissue below device after each measurement cycle.

Droplet volumes: 150 uL to 2 uL (wide range controlled by varying electrode sizes/shapes
  and bussed groupings).

Automation: Impedance sensing with feedback control over droplet position; programmed
  actuation sequences for culture, dispensing, detection, and waste routing.

Illumination: Custom LED arrays positioned below device; multicolour array (7 peak
  wavelengths: red ~625 nm, orange ~590 nm, yellow ~580 nm, green ~525 nm, blue ~450 nm,
  purple ~400 nm, white broadband) and blue/yellow dual-LED arrays for cycling experiments.
  Intensities: 50 and 250 umol/m2/s (low and high).


ORGANISM AND REAGENTS
---------------------
Organism    : Cyclotella cryptica (CCMP 332); purchased from National Center for Marine
              Algae and Microbiota (NCMA, East Boothbay, ME).
Culture     : f/2 medium (NCMA, Maine, NE) supplemented with biotin and cyanocobalamin
              (2 nM each, NCMA) and 0.02% w/v Pluronic F68; Pyrex media bottles (max 200 mL);
              20 C; 12 h white light / 12 h dark alternating cycle; weekly subculture 1:10.
              Inoculation density ~9.0e5 cells/mL (exponential phase).
On-chip     : 1.5e6 cells/mL in complete media; 150 uL loaded into algae active reservoir.
              LipidTOX working solution: 200x dilution in complete media; 120 uL loaded.

LipidTOX    : HCS LipidTOX Green neutral lipid stain (Life Technologies, Burlington, ON,
              Canada); fluorogenic reporter fluorescing in presence of neutral lipids (TAG);
              ex 488 nm / em 520 nm.

DCFDA       : DCFDA cellular reactive oxygen species detection assay kit (ab113851, Abcam,
              Cambridge, MA); reporter fluorescing in presence of ROS; ex 490 nm / em 526 nm.

Ascorbic    : 50 ug/mL ascorbic acid in complete media; antioxidant for ROS rescue arm.
acid


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Sterilisation and Algae Preparation (off-chip)
  Sterilise   : DMF devices incubated in 70% ethanol for 10 min prior to use.
  Algae prep  : Maintained by weekly subculture at 1:10 ratio; density confirmed by
                absorbance at 660 nm in 200 uL aliquots in clear-bottom 96-well plates
                using a plate reader. Exponential growth phase confirmed before loading.
  Absorbance  : 1 mL media aliquot (no cells) as reference; 1 mL culture aliquot measured
  spectrum    : by UV/Vis spectrophotometer (Eppendorf, Westbury, NY). C. cryptica
                absorbance maxima at blue (strong) and red (weak) wavelengths, consistent
                with primary photosynthetic pigment chlorophyll c.

Step 2 | Device Loading — Active Reservoir Initialisation
  Inputs      : Algae suspension (150 uL, 1.5e6 cells/mL) and LipidTOX solution (120 uL,
                200x stock dilution in complete media) pipetted into their respective
                active reservoirs.
  Pipette steps: 2 (only manual steps required for entire 24 h run).
  Circulation : Each active reservoir continuously circulates on its four electrodes in a
                circular mixing pattern to prevent cell settling and maintain homogeneous
                density before each dispense step. In BioScript, abstracted as a mix loop
                on the reservoir droplets prior to dispensing.

Step 3 | Culture Droplet Dispensing (Screening Step 2)
  Operation   : 8 culture droplets (12 uL each) dispensed from algae active reservoir to
                8 algae culture zone electrodes in series via bussed electrode actuation.
  Notes       : Representative single droplet lineage encoded in BioScript; hardware
                bussing handles 8 simultaneous culture droplets per device.

Step 4 | Label Droplet Dispensing (Screening Step 3)
  Operation   : ~15 uL source droplet dispensed from LipidTOX active reservoir to dye
                dispensing bus; 8 label droplets (2 uL each) formed simultaneously.
                If source volume insufficient, second source droplet dispensed from reservoir.

Step 5 | Absorbance Measurement — Cell Density (Screening Step 4)
  Operation   : 8 daughter culture droplets (2 uL each) dispensed from culture zones and
                actuated to L-shaped absorbance detection electrodes.
  Detection   : Device placed on transparent 384-well plate; PHERAstar plate reader
                (BMG Labtech, Durham, NC); 660 nm; scan matrix 15x15; scan width 3 mm;
                focal height 8.7 mm. Records cell density at each time point.
  Time points : t = 0 h (baseline), t = 6 h, t = 24 h.

Step 6 | Fluorescence Measurement — Neutral Lipid (Screening Step 5)
  Operation   : 8 daughter culture droplets merged 1:1 with 8 label droplets; incubated
                5 min for LipidTOX staining; mixed droplets driven to fluorescence
                detection electrodes.
  Detection   : Device placed on black 384-well plate; PHERAstar plate reader; 488 nm
                excitation / 520 nm emission; scan matrix 20x20; scan width 3 mm;
                focal height 8.7 mm; gain 550. Records neutral lipid content per droplet.
  Waste       : Mixed droplets driven to waste reservoirs after measurement; fluid wicks
                through 1 mm through-holes onto tissue below device.
  Time points : t = 0 h, t = 6 h, t = 24 h.
  Notes       : Screening Steps 3-5 (Steps 4-6 here) repeated after each illumination
                incubation phase (after 6 h and after 18 h additional incubation).

Step 7 | Multicolour Illumination Screen (Protocol 1)
  Conditions  : 7 LED wavelengths (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, white) +
                dark control; low (50 umol/m2/s) and high (250 umol/m2/s) intensity.
                All LEDs on continuously for 24 h; n=3 devices per condition.
  Schedule    : Load device (Step 2) → dispense and measure t=0 (Steps 3-6) →
                6 h illumination → repeat Steps 3-6 (t=6h) →
                18 h illumination → repeat Steps 3-6 (t=24h).
  Key finding : Yellow LEDs (~580 nm) produce the highest neutral lipid accumulation
                per cell (>2x vs. dark control) at high intensity (Fig. 3d/f).
                Blue LEDs (~450 nm) produce the highest biomass growth rate (Fig. 3b).
                First report of culture wavelength dependence of algal neutral lipid
                production; mechanism correlates with oxidative stress (see Step 9).
  QC gate     : absorbSignal1 > 0 → fluorescence measurement (BB2/pass);
                absorbSignal1 <= 0 → drain culture droplet (BB3/fail).

Step 8 | Blue/Yellow Cycling Screen (Protocol 2)
  Conditions  : 8 timed combinations of blue (~450 nm) and yellow (~580 nm) LEDs at
                high intensity (250 umol/m2/s), 24 h total; n=3 devices per condition.
                Combinations (h blue / h yellow): 24/0, 0/24, 1/23, 3/21, 6/18,
                12/12, 15/9, 20/4.
  Schedule    : Blue phase (900m = 15h) → measure t=15h → yellow phase (540m = 9h)
                → measure t=24h. Baseline t=0h measured before illumination.
  Optimal     : 15h blue / 9h yellow → ~4-fold lipid increase vs. dark control;
  condition   : ~2-fold vs. yellow or blue alone (Fig. 4b). Growth rates remain high
                (above any single colour other than blue) due to blue phase proliferation.
  Macroscale  : Best condition (15h blue / 9h yellow), 24h yellow, and 24h blue validated
  validation  : in 200 mL Pyrex flasks (n=5). Trends identical to DMF microscale (Fig. 4c/d).
                Confirms microfluidic screen hits translate to conventional-scale cultures.
  QC gate     : absorbSignal2 > 0 → fluorescence measurement (BB5/pass);
                absorbSignal2 <= 0 → drain culture droplet (BB6/fail).

Step 9 | ROS Mechanistic Assay (Protocol 3)
  Purpose     : Determine whether wavelength-dependent lipid accumulation correlates with
                reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, consistent with a photooxidative
                stress mechanism (analogous to nutrient-deprivation stress).
  Conditions  :
    Arm A     : Yellow illumination 24h — expected high ROS (positive arm).
    Arm B     : Blue illumination 24h — expected low ROS (negative control).
    Arm C     : Yellow illumination 24h + 50 ug/mL ascorbic acid — antioxidant rescue;
                expected ROS reversal to near-blue levels.
    Arm D     : Silicon deprivation (off-chip, macroscale positive control; known ROS
                inducer in C. cryptica via silicon-deficiency stress).
  DCFDA       : Algae grown at 5.0e6 cells/mL in 200 mL Pyrex flasks for >=1.5 weeks
  protocol    : under standard conditions (12h light/dark). Centrifuged 3000 rpm, 5 min;
                resuspended in 50 mL appropriate media variant. Illuminated 24h under
                assigned condition. Cells evaluated with DCFDA kit per manufacturer
                instructions: 5 mL aliquots centrifuged, washed 1x in buffer, resuspended
                in 500 uL DCFDA solution or complete media (control); incubated 37 C 30 min
                dark; centrifuged, washed, resuspended in 1x buffer. 150 uL aliquots placed
                in black-bottom 96-well plates; read at ex 490 nm / em 526 nm; n=5 per arm.
  Result      : Yellow light and silicon deprivation produce significantly higher ROS than
                blue light or normal conditions; ascorbate reverses the yellow-light ROS
                elevation (Fig. 5c). Supports hypothesis that yellow light causes
                photooxidative stress — when photosynthesis cannot keep pace with photon
                absorption, excited chlorophyll states (1Chl* and 3Chl*) form singlet-state
                oxygen (1O2*) and other ROS. Blue-light-specific antioxidant synthesis

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol encodes a high-throughput microfluidic cell culture experiment for quantitative
single-cell analysis of NF-kappaB nuclear localisation dynamics under TNF-alpha and LPS
stimulation. Using a fully automated microfluidic platform, more than 3000 NIH-3T3 cells
stably expressing a p65-GFP reporter are measured simultaneously under 8 doses of each
ligand spanning 4 orders of magnitude, with 6-minute temporal resolution over 12 hours.

The protocol addresses four key biological questions:

  A. Oscillation continuity: Are NF-kappaB nuclear localisation oscillations under TNF-alpha
     damped or continuous at the single-cell level? Extended 12-hour time-lapse confirms
     they are continuous (not damped).

  B. Dynamic range: How do response threshold, activation fraction, and response time
     scale with dose? Response time decreases from hundreds of minutes near threshold to
     <30 min at saturating doses. The standard NF-kappaB ODE model (Kearns/Hoffman 2009)
     was modified to explain this kinetic dose-response relationship.

  C. Stochastic switching and cell-to-cell variability: High-dose responses are
     stereotyped. Near-threshold doses produce stochastic switching driven by small
     fluctuations in key protein levels (IkBa, IKK), reproduced by the modified
     stochastic NF-kappaB model.

  D. Analog vs. digital signaling: TNF-alpha produces analog signaling (graded nuclear
     localisation intensity proportional to dose). LPS produces digital signaling (full
     all-or-nothing nuclear translocation even at the lowest doses). This distinction
     reflects the biological context: cell-cell communication (TNF-alpha) vs. bacterial
     infection detection (LPS).

Title        : A Versatile Microfluidic Device for Automating Synthetic Biology
Source Link  : https://escholarship.org/content/qt07q6b4f6/qt07q6b4f6.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.5b00062

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a hybrid microfluidic platform for automating the synthetic biology
build-and-test cycle. The device integrates a digital microfluidic (DMF) bottom plate (76
patterned gold/chromium electrodes on glass, 7 um SU-8 dielectric, Aquapel hydrophobic
coating) with a PDMS serpentine incubation channel and an on-chip electroporation region.
The three functional regions -- DNA assembly (DMF), queuing and incubation (channel), and
transformation (electroporation electrodes) -- are integrated on a single 75 x 25 mm chip.

Three DNA assembly methods are implemented and validated:
  1. Golden Gate assembly (25 C, 10 min; T4 DNA ligase; Type IIS BsaI restriction)
  2. Gibson assembly (50 C, 15 min; 2x Gibson master mix)
  3. Yeast/TAR cloning assembly (25 C, 10 min; no additional reagent; in vivo assembly)

For each method, 16 combinatorial plasmid variants (4 Promoter variants x 4 BCD-gfp variants)
are assembled, transferred into the incubation channel, and electroporated into E. coli DH5alpha
(or S. cerevisiae CEN.PK for yeast assembly) on-chip. Each step uses ~0.2 uL dispensed
subdroplets from 1.5 uL reservoir droplets (10x lower total volume than comparable platforms).

Cross-contamination between the 16 sequential reactions is prevented by Pluronic F-127
(0.05% w/v) surfactant additive in HFE 7500 oil -- the first application of this strategy
to on-chip DNA assembly -- eliminating the need for additional wash reservoirs or steps.

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Oil Phase Priming
  Reagents    : HFE 7500 + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127
  Operation   : 1 mL pipetted onto DMF surface
  Purpose     : Oil surrounds all aqueous droplets throughout protocol; Pluronic F-127
                prevents biofouling and cross-contamination without wash steps.
                First application of this strategy to on-chip DNA assembly.

Step 2 | Dispense Vector Backbone
  Reagent     : VectorBackbone (pFAB4876-based, BsaI + DpnI digested, gel-purified)
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed subdroplet
  Notes       : ~2100 bp band (Golden Gate). Reservoir refilled via SU-8 capillary
                between successive reactions (16 total per run).

Step 3 | Dispense Promoter1 Insert
  Reagent     : Promoter1 (pFAB4876, ~100 bp; DpnI + BsaI digested, gel-purified)
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed
  Notes       : Four variants used across 16 reactions: Prom1, Prom2, Prom9, Prom11.
                This .bs file encodes Prom1 as the representative variant.

Step 4 | Dispense BCD1-gfp Insert
  Reagent     : BCD1_gfp (pFAB4876, ~800 bp; DpnI + BsaI digested, gel-purified)
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed
  Notes       : Four variants: BCD1, BCD2, BCD20, BCD21 (all fused to sfGFP). GFP enables
                colony color screening: green = correct insert, white = self-ligation artifact.

Step 5 | Dispense T4 DNA Ligase
  Reagent     : T4 DNA ligase, 2.5 U/uL + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed
  Notes       : Reservoir maintained at room temperature while incubation zone is Peltier-
                heated. T4 ligase is heat-inactivated above 50 C; region-specific heating
                allows reagent storage on-chip without degradation. Gibson assembly substitutes
                2x Gibson master mix; Yeast assembly requires no additional reagent.

Step 6 | Mix Vector Backbone with Promoter1
  Inputs      : vectorDrop, promoterDrop
  Output      : dnaMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  Actuation   : ~100-120 V rms, 8 kHz; 2-3 circular mixing passes over mixing electrodes

Step 7 | Add BCD1-gfp to DNA Mix
  Inputs      : dnaMix, bcdDrop
  Output      : threePartMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  Volume      : ~0.6 uL (three-component droplet)

Step 8 | Add T4 Ligase to Complete Golden Gate Mix
  Inputs      : threePartMix, ligaseDrop
  Output      : assemblyMix
  Duration    : 10 s
  Total volume: ~0.8 uL
  Notes       : Paper Table 1: 0.8 uL total, 2 DNA fragment insertions, 16 plasmid
                combinations. Droplet circulates 2-3 times in circular fashion on
                digital-to-channel electrodes (1.75 x 1.75 mm) near D2D interface.

Step 9 | Digital-to-Droplet Transfer and Golden Gate Incubation
  Input       : assemblyMix
  Operation   : heat at 25 C for 10 min (600 s)
  Transfer    : Syringe-vacuum at 0.1 uL/s draws droplet from DMF; HFE 7500 at 5 uL/s
                drives droplet into serpentine incubation zone
  Incubation  : 25 C (room temperature), 10 min; BsaI-HF creates 4-bp overhangs;
                T4 ligase joins complementary sticky ends
  Peltier     : Region-specific; incubation zone at 25 C; reservoirs unheated
  Alternatives: Gibson: 50 C, 15 min. Yeast/TAR: 25 C, 10 min (no ligase).

Step 10 | Assembly QC Detection
  Input       : assemblyMix
  Output      : assemblySignal
  Module      : assemblyQC
  Duration    : 30 s
  Notes       : Abstracts GFP colony color screening after off-chip electroporation and
                plating. Expected pass rate: 95% Golden Gate (76/80), 100% Gibson (80/80),
                97.2% Yeast (70/72). QC branch gate decides proceed vs. discard.

  Branch BB2 (assemblySignal > 0)  : dispose(assemblyMix) -- proceed to transformation
  Branch BB3 (assemblySignal <= 0) : drain(assemblyMix)   -- ligation failed; discard

Step 11 | Dispose Assembly QC Signal [BB4 join]
  Operation   : dispose(assemblySignal)
  Notes       : Join block; transformation branch begins.

Step 12 | Dispense E. coli Cells
  Reagent     : CompetentEcoli (DH5alpha, NEB C2989K)
  Output      : cellDroplet
  Notes       : Dispensed from cell inlet via 4 microelectrodes at cell-inlet/channel
                intersection. Elastomeric microvalve (valve 5) closed to prevent
                cross-contamination with other assembled plasmid droplets in channel.

Step 13 | Dispense Incubated Plasmid (Channel Exit)
  Reagent     : AssembledPlasmid
  Output      : incubatedPlasmid
  Notes       : Models the assembled pProm1_BCD1-gfp droplet exiting the serpentine
                incubation channel and entering the electroporation zone, driven by
                HFE 7500 at 5 uL/s (all channel valves closed per Fig S2).
                BioScript ownership note: assemblyMix was consumed by detect(assemblyQC)
                in BB1; incubatedPlasmid is a new fluid object at this CFG location,
                representing the same physical droplet. This avoids the assemblyMix2
                phantom SSA index emitted by the compiler when a variable is re-used
                after detect has consumed it.

Step 14 | Mix Cells with Electroporation Media
  Inputs      : cellDroplet, electroporationMedia
  Output      : cellMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  EP media    : 8 mM Na2HPO4, 2 mM KH2PO4, 250 mM sucrose pH 7.4
  Notes       : Osmotically balanced buffer prevents cell lysis during pulse.

Step 15 | Merge Incubated Plasmid with Cell Mix
  Inputs      : incubatedPlasmid, cellMix
  Output      : preMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  Volume      : ~2 uL (merged droplet positioned over electroporation electrodes)

Step 16 | Electroporation
  Input       : preMix
  Operation   : heat at 37 C for 60 s (models post-pulse recovery temperature)
  Pulse params: 3 x 100 ms DC square pulses at 1800 V/cm (E. coli)
                Impedance feedback triggers pulse when Vsense > 0.15 V
                Oil phase (HFE 7500) > 10 GOhm impedance; prevents short when no droplet
  Efficiency  : 4.58e3 CFU/ng assembled DNA (110 +/- 8 colonies, N=3, microfluidic)
                4.46e3 CFU/ng (137 +/- 16 colonies, N=3, cuvette); not significantly different
  Notes       : Yeast (CEN.PK): 1200 V/cm; 1.90e3 CFU/ng (21 +/- 6 colonies, N=3).
                Higher fields (above optimum) decrease efficiency by killing cells.

Step 17 | Post-Electroporation Recovery
  Inputs      : preMix, LB_Recovery
  Output      : recoveredCells
  Mix         : 5 s
  Recovery    : 200 uL LB broth; 1 h at 37 C (3600 s)
  Notes       : Electroporated droplet driven to outlet by HFE 7500 (all valves closed).
                Plated on LB agar + kanamycin 50 ug/mL. ~100/110 colonies green (GFP+,
                correct insert); ~10 white (self-ligation). Yeast: collected in 200 uL
                deionized water; plated on CSM-agar delta-TRP.

Step 18 | Transformation QC Detection
  Input       : recoveredCells
  Output      : transformSignal
  Module      : transformationQC
  Duration    : 30 s
  Notes       : Abstracts off-chip colony counting (LB agar + kanamycin, 37 C overnight).
                Colony-PCR and Sanger sequencing (QB3284_fwd / QB3810_rev) confirm assembly.
                For yeast: 3 yeast colonies miniprepped; transformed into Turbo E. coli;
                5 green E. coli colonies sequenced per assembled plasmid (Genewiz).

  Branch BB5 (transformSignal > 0)  : dispose(recoveredCells) -- colonies confirmed
  Branch BB6 (transformSignal <= 0) : drain(recoveredCells)   -- no colonies; discard

Step 19 | Final Cleanup [BB7 terminal]
  Operations  : dispose(transformSignal), dispose(oilPhase)
  Notes       : Terminal block. In the actual protocol, Steps 1-19 are iterated 16 times
                in total (one reaction per plasmid combination) using the same electrode
                path, mixing channel, and incubation channel. Reservoir droplets refilled
                via SU-8 capillary channel between iterations.

Title        : Development of Digital Microfluidic Heterogeneous Immunoassays
Author       : Alphonsus Hon-Chung Ng

OVERVIEW
--------
This BioScript file encodes two protocols from the PhD thesis of Alphonsus H.C. Ng (University
of Toronto, 2015), which describes the development and validation of digital microfluidic (DMF)
methods for heterogeneous immunoassays. DMF electrostatically manipulates discrete droplets
(pL to uL) on a hydrophobic electrode array without the use of enclosed microchannels or
oil carrier fluid -- a key innovation of this work.

Protocol 1 (Chapter 2) introduces the first oil-free DMF particle-based immunoassay, using a
novel "supernatant separation" washing technique and demonstrating both non-competitive
(thyroid-stimulating hormone, TSH) and competitive (17beta-estradiol, E2) immunoassay modes.
Chapter 3 extends this with a fully automated platform (90 Pogo pin interface, integrated PMT,
magnetic lens) and DOE optimization. Chapter 4 applies the platform to infectious disease
diagnosis (rubella virus IgG and IgM), demonstrating 100% diagnostic sensitivity and specificity.

Protocol 2 (Chapter 5) introduces DISC (Digital Microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single-
Cells), which automates all sample preparation steps for in-situ adherent cell immunoassays with
<4 s temporal resolution. Using virtual microwells formed by passive dispensing over hydrophilic
lift-off spots, DISC enables single-cell phosphoprotein quantitation by laser scanning cytometry.

The BioScript encodes representative arms of both protocols and two QC gates per protocol,
yielding 13 basic blocks (BB1-BB13) and 4 if/else gates in the compiled IR/CFG.

PROTOCOL 1: DMF MAGNETIC PARTICLE IMMUNOASSAY (Chapter 2)
----------------------------------------------------------
Analytes       : Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH, non-competitive sandwich immunoassay)
                 17beta-estradiol (E2, competitive immunoassay)
Anti-fouling   : Pluronic L64 (BASF Corp.), 0.05% v/v in all on-chip reagents
                 Enables air-surrounded droplet movement; prevents protein adsorption

Reagents:
  TSH particles  : Mouse monoclonal Anti-beta TSH coated paramagnetic particles
                   (Abbott ARCHITECT kit 7K62); pre-processed: washed 2x DI water,
                   blocked with 3% NFDM/0.01% Tween-20 buffer pH 7.8 (1 h), washed 2x DI water,
                   resuspended at ~3.0e8 particles/mL in DMF-compatible particle diluent (pH 10:
                   Tris-base 6.1 g/L, NaCl 5.8 g/L, Sucrose 136 g/L, BSA 1% w/v,
                   Thimerosal 0.05% w/v, L64 0.05% v/v)
  E2 particles   : Rabbit monoclonal Anti-E2 coated particles (Abbott ARCHITECT kit 7K72);
                   same prep as TSH but no NFDM blocking step
  TSH conjugate  : Anti-TSH-HRP (goat polyclonal, Fitzgerald Industries), 2 ug/mL in conjugate
                   diluent (pH 7.4: Tris-Base 1.9 g/L, Tris-HCl 13.2 g/L, NaCl 17.5 g/L,
                   BSA 1% w/v, cold fish gelatin 0.1% w/v, Thimerosal 0.05% w/v, L64 0.05% v/v)
  E2 conjugate   : E2-HRP conjugated via 6-CMO (BiosPacific), 1 ug/mL in conjugate diluent
                   (optimal conc. determined empirically; higher conc. loses dynamic range)
  Substrate      : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fisher Scientific): H2O2 + luminol/enhancer
  Wash buffer    : pH 7.7; Tris-base 0.35 g/L, Tris-HCl 1.10 g/L, NaCl 8.367 g/L, L64 0.05% v/v

Supernatant Separation Washing (key innovation vs prior serial dilution method):
  Mechanism      : Magnet positions pellet on device surface; supernatant droplet actuated to waste;
                   magnet removed; fresh wash buffer droplet passed over pellet; circularly mixed
                   (4 electrodes) to resuspend particles
  Efficiency     : >98% unbound reagent removal by wash 2 (benchmark)
                   Serial dilution requires 6+ washes for same benchmark; 10-18 washes previously
  Minimum density: ~3.0e8 particles/mL for successful separation
  Magnetic force : ~470 uN (COMSOL FEA; pellet 7.75 mm from magnet bottom-edge origin)
  Residual liquid: ~5% of origin droplet retained by hydrophilic particles; resuspend immediately

Eight-step On-Chip Immunoassay Protocol:
  Step 1 | Particle dispense and separation
    Volume     : 800 nL unit droplet from reservoir
    Operation  : Supernatant separation (magnet on; diluent actuated to waste; magnet off)
  
  Step 2 | Sample incubation
    Volume     : 3 unit droplets (3 x 800 nL = 2.4 uL)
    Duration   : 6 min at room temperature with continuous circular mixing
    Notes      : 3 droplets chosen for optimal signal vs droplet reliability; evaporation <5%
                 over 30 min (measured by capacitance); TSH: analyte binds Anti-beta TSH particles;
                 E2: analyte competes with E2-HRP for Anti-E2 binding sites
  
  Step 3 | Wash x4 in wash buffer
    Volume     : 4 x 800 nL; supernatant separation each time
  
  Step 4 | Conjugate incubation
    Volume     : 800 nL
    Duration   : 2 min
    TSH        : Anti-TSH-HRP binds TSH captured on particles (non-competitive)
    E2         : E2-HRP binds Anti-E2 sites not occupied by analyte (competitive)
  
  Step 5 | Wash x4 in wash buffer + wash x2 in H2O2
    Notes      : 2x H2O2 wash developed in place of pre-mixing H2O2 + luminol off-chip;
                 pre-mixing caused high inter-assay variability
  
  Step 6 | H2O2 incubation
    Volume     : 800 nL; duration: 2 min
    Notes      : Particles moved to detection region (electrode array aligned to 96-well plate)
  
  Step 7 | Luminol/enhancer merge
    Volume     : 800 nL; on-chip mix (immediately before detection)
    Notes      : Activates HRP-catalyzed chemiluminescence
  
  Step 8 | Chemiluminescence detection
    Duration   : 1 min (signal saturates at 1 min; stable endpoint)
    Settings   : PHERAstar LUM module; focal height 8.6 mm; gain 3600;
                 device taped to 96-well Stripwell plate

  Source droplet translated across vacant lift-off spot (1.75 mm hydrophilic ITO on Teflon-AF top plate);

  Subsequent dispenses displace and replace microwell contents.

Eleven-step DISC protocol (representative arm: Akt phosphorylation at 50 ng/mL PDGF-BB):

  Step 1 | Cell seeding
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL passive dispenses (2.7 uL) per lift-off spot; VM = ~400 nL
    Incubate : 37 C, 5% CO2, 24 h in humidified chamber; device inverted for cell settling

  Step 2 | Serum starvation
    Reagent  : Starving media (0.5% CS/FBS + 0.05% F68 + pen/strep in DMEM)
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL; Incubate 37 C, 5% CO2, 24 h
    Purpose  : Synchronizes basal receptor/Akt activity

  Step 3 | Serum-free rinse
    Reagent  : Serum-free DMEM + 0.05% F68; Volume: 3 x 900 nL

  Step 4 | PDGF-BB stimulation
    Reagent  : PDGF-BB 50 ng/mL in serum-free DMEM; Volume: 2 x 900 nL (1.8 uL)
    Duration : 2 min (PDGFR) / 5 min (Akt); ~4 s reagent switch time to fixation
    Dose-response range: 0-200 ng/mL; EC50 ~12.5 ng/mL; Hill n=1.73 (Y857), 2.13 (Y1021)

    Reagent  : 4% paraformaldehyde + 0.05% F68 in DPBS; Volume: 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL)
    Incubate : 10 min, room temperature

  Step 6 | WB1 rinse
    Reagent  : WB1 (0.05% F68 in DPBS); Volume: 3 x 900 nL (5.4 uL total)

  Step 7 | Permeabilization
    Reagent  : 0.2% Tween-20 in DPBS; Volume: 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL)
    Incubate : 10 min, room temperature

  Step 8 | WB2 rinse
    Reagent  : WB2 (0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS); Volume: 4 x 900 nL (~8.1 uL)

  Step 9 | Blocking
    Reagent  : 1% bovine NFDM + 0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS; Volume: 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL)
    Incubate : 1 h, room temperature

  Step 10 | Primary antibody staining
    Reagents : pan Akt (Mouse mAb, 1:50, CST) + p-Akt S473 (Rabbit mAb, 1:200, CST) in BS
               OR PDGFR-beta (Mouse mAb, 1:50, CST) + p-PDGFR Y857/Y1021 (Rabbit pAb, 1:200, SCB) in BS
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL); Incubate: overnight (~12 h) at 4 C

  Step 11 | WB2 rinse (unbound primary antibody removal)
    Reagent  : WB2 (0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS); Volume: 3 x 900 nL (5.4 uL)

  Step 12 | Secondary antibody staining
    Reagents : Anti-Mouse IgG AF647 Fab2 1:500 + Anti-Rabbit IgG AF555 Fab2 1:500 in BS (CST)
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL); Incubate: 2 h, room temperature

  Step 13 | Off-chip detection (laser scanning cytometry)
    Post-process : Remove top plate; rinse in 10x DPBS/0.5% Tween-20 (30 s); rinse DI water (30 s); air dry
    Scanner      : Axon GenePix 4000B; 532 nm + 635 nm; 5 um resolution; 0 um focus; PMT 500 V
    Analysis     : CellProfiler; Otsu Global thresholding; 15-100 um objects; per-cell p-protein/total ratio
    Normalization: Per-cell ratio normalized to serum-free negative control mean on same device

  PDGFR Y857 max phosphorylation  : 75 s after 50 ng/mL PDGF-BB

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidics for Automated Proteomic Processing
Source Link  : https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157851/pdf/jove-33-1603.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.3791/1603
Journal      : Journal of Visualized Experiments (JoVE), 2009, Vol. 33
Platform     : Digital Microfluidics (DMF) -- two-plate EWOD configuration


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a digital microfluidics (DMF) based method for fully automated,
integrated proteomic sample processing on a single miniaturised device. The workflow covers
all major biochemical processing steps required in clinical proteomics prior to mass
spectrometric analysis: protein extraction by precipitation, resolubilization, reduction,
alkylation, and enzymatic (tryptic) digestion.

DMF is a microscale fluid-handling technique in which nanoliter-to-microliter droplets are
manipulated on an open surface coated with a dielectric layer and electrodes. Applying an
electrical potential to the droplet causes charges to accumulate on either side of the
dielectric, creating electrostatic handles that allow droplets to be dispensed, moved, merged,
mixed, and split. This makes DMF a natural fit for rapid, sequential, multistep, miniaturised
automated biochemical assays.

The paper demonstrates the method using bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a model protein,
achieving identification of 25 distinct peptides (99.9% confidence interval) with 44% sequence
coverage by nano-HPLC-MS/MS after on-chip processing. The approach eliminates the human error
inherent in conventional macroscale pipetting-based or robot-based proteomic sample handling
and enables precise duplication of conditions across laboratories.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate DMF device
Bottom plate  : Patterned chromium (Cr) electrodes (250 nm) on glass substrate.
                Dielectric: Parylene-C (2-5 um, chemical vapor deposition).
                Hydrophobic layer: Teflon-AF (50 nm, 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40,
                spin-coated at 2000 rpm for 60 s, post-baked at 160 C for 10 min).
Top plate     : Unpatterned indium tin oxide (ITO) glass (transparent contiguous electrode).
                Hydrophobic layer: Teflon-AF (50 nm, same conditions as bottom plate).
Gap           : 140 um total (set by two pieces of double-sided tape on bottom plate edges).
Actuation     : 100 V_rms / 18 kHz AC signals applied via 40-pin connectors.
Control       : LabView (National Instruments, Austin, TX) with in-house calibration program.
                Home-built control box: high-voltage relay array (NI DaqPad), function
                generator, and amplifier. Feedback control calibrated at startup.
Droplet vol.  : ~600 nL per dispensed droplet (defined by 1 mm square electrode dimensions,
                50 um gaps, 2.5 mm square reservoirs).

Fabrication (Part 1):
  1. Clean glass in Piranha solution (3:1 H2SO4:H2O2, 30%) for 10 min with agitation.
  2. Rinse in DI water, dry with N2, deposit 250 nm Cr by electron beam evaporation.
  3. Dehydrate Cr-coated substrate: rinse in isopropanol, bake 5 min at 115 C.
  4. Spin-coat HMDS (30 s, 3000 rpm) then Shipley S1811 photoresist (same parameters).
  5. Pre-bake (100 C, 2 min); expose to UV for 5 s through photomask.
  6. Develop in Shipley MF 321 developer (3 min); wash in DI water; post-bake 100 C, 1 min.
  7. Etch exposed Cr in Cr etchant (30 s); strip photoresist in AZ300T (10 min); rinse DI/N2.
  8. Deposit Parylene-C (2-5 um, CVD); spin-coat Teflon-AF 50 nm; post-bake 160 C, 10 min.
  9. Coat ITO glass top plate with Teflon-AF 50 nm; post-bake 160 C, 10 min.


RESERVOIR MAP (Figure 1b)
--------------------------
R-1  : Protein sample (serum or purified protein dissolved in working buffer WB)
R-2  : Precipitant -- 20% Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) in DI water
R-3  : Waste reservoir (receives supernatant after precipitation and wash eluates)
R-4  : Wash buffer -- 70/30 Chloroform/Acetonitrile (ACN)
R-5  : Resolubilizing buffer -- 100 mM Ammonium Bicarbonate pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
R-6  : Reductant -- 10 mM TCEP (tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine) in WB
R-7  : Alkylating agent -- 12 mM Iodoacetamide (IAM) in WB
R-8  : Trypsin -- dissolved in WB at 1/5 of total protein sample concentration


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Set-up (Part 2)
  - Remove polymer coatings from bottom substrate contact pads by scraping with scalpel.
  - Couple exposed pads to 40-pin connectors.
  - Power on LabView computer, control box, function generator, and amplifier.
  - Assemble device: position two pieces of double-sided tape (140 um total) on bottom
    substrate edges; complete with unpatterned ITO top plate (Teflon side facing down).
  - Attach ground connector to top substrate.
  - Run LabView calibration program to initialise feedback control.
  - Load sample and reagents into reservoirs R-1 through R-8.
  - Load and execute LabView actuation code to initiate droplet actuation.

Step 2 | Sample and Reagent Preparation (Part 3)
  Working buffer  : 100 mM TrisHCl pH 7.8, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v.
  R-1 (sample)    : Dissolve protein(s) in WB; pipette into R-1.
  R-2 (TCA)       : 20% TCA in DI water; pipette into R-2.
  R-4 (wash)      : 70/30 Chloroform/ACN; pipette into R-4.
  R-5 (resolub.)  : 100 mM AmBic pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127; pipette into R-5.
  R-6 (TCEP)      : 10 mM TCEP in WB; pipette into R-6.
  R-7 (IAM)       : 12 mM Iodoacetamide in WB; pipette into R-7.
  R-8 (trypsin)   : Trypsin in WB at 1/5 total protein concentration; pipette into R-8.

Step 3 | Protein Extraction by Precipitation (Part 4, Steps 2)
  Inputs     : ProteinSample (R-1), TrichloroaceticAcid (R-2)
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL protein droplet from R-1 and ~600 nL TCA droplet from R-2.
               Merge droplets on device surface (Figure 2, Frame 1).
               Incubate 5 min at room temperature; proteins precipitate onto surface
               (Figure 2, Frames 2-3).
               Actuate supernatant away to waste reservoir R-3 (Figure 2, Frame 4).
  Duration   : 5 min (300 s)
  Temperature: Room temperature (~25 C)

Step 4 | Precipitate Washing (Part 4, Step 3)
  Inputs     : WashBuffer (R-4) -- 70/30 Chloroform/ACN
  Operation  : Dispense 3 sequential ~600 nL wash buffer droplets from R-4.
               Drive each droplet across the precipitated protein to waste reservoir R-3
               (Figure 2, Frame 5).
  Wash cycles: 3 (unrolled as 3 independent dispense/drain operations in BioScript)
  Purpose    : Removes residual TCA, soluble contaminants, and lipids from precipitate.

Step 5 | Protein Resolubilization (Part 4, Step 4)
  Input      : ResolubilizingBuffer (R-5)
  Operation  : Allow precipitate to dry on device surface.
               Dispense ~600 nL resolubilizing buffer droplet from R-5 onto precipitate.
               Incubate 20 min until precipitate fully dissolves (Figure 2, Frame 6).
  Duration   : 20 min (1200 s)
  Temperature: Room temperature (~25 C)
  Notes      : AmBic buffer (pH 8.0) is trypsin-compatible. Pluronic F127 prevents biofouling.

Step 6 | Reduction (Part 4, Step 5)
  Inputs     : TCEP_Reductant (R-6), resolubilizedSample
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL TCEP droplet from R-6 and merge with sample droplet.
               Mix combined droplet by circular actuation across 6 electrodes.
               Incubate 1 h at room temperature in a humidified chamber (Figure 3, Frames 1-2).
  Duration   : 60 min (3600 s)
  Temperature: 25 C (room temperature, humidified chamber)
  Purpose    : TCEP reduces disulfide bonds between cysteine residues.

Step 7 | Alkylation (Part 4, Step 6)
  Inputs     : Iodoacetamide (R-7), reducedSample
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL IAM droplet from R-7 and merge with sample droplet.
               Mix combined droplet by circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as Step 6).
               Incubate 15 min at room temperature in a humidified chamber, protected from
               light (Figure 3, Frames 2-3).
  Duration   : 15 min (900 s)
  Temperature: 25 C (room temperature, humidified chamber, light-protected)
  Purpose    : IAM alkylates free thiols on cysteines to prevent re-oxidation of disulfides.

Step 8 | Tryptic Digestion (Part 4, Step 7)
  Inputs     : Trypsin (R-8), alkylatedSample
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL trypsin droplet from R-8 and merge with sample droplet.
               Mix combined droplet by circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as Step 6).
               Incubate 3 h at 37 C on a hot plate in a humidified chamber
               (Figure 3, Frames 3-4).
  Duration   : 180 min (10800 s)
  Temperature: 37 C (hot plate, humidified chamber)
  Purpose    : Trypsin cleaves at Lys-X and Arg-X peptide bonds.

Step 9 | Post-Processing Sample Preparation (Part 5, off-chip)
  1. Remove top substrate; quench digestion by adding 0.6 mL of 2.5% TFA in water.
  2. Purify quenched product using C18 ZipTips (Millipore, Billerica, MA) per manufacturer
     instructions.
  3. Dilute purified sample in DI water to a final volume of 100 mL.
  Notes      : TFA quenches trypsin enzymatic activity. C18 ZipTip SPE desalts and
               concentrates peptides for MS injection.

Step 10 | Mass Spectrometry Analysis (Part 6)
  HPLC system : Eksigent Technologies nano-HPLC
  Trap column : 3 mm dia. C18 beads, 150 um ID x 2.5 cm
  Sep. column : 3 um dia. C18 beads, 75 um ID x 15 cm (reversed-phase)
  MS          : LTQ (Thermo-Fisher Scientific)
  Emitter     : Nanoelectrospray emitter, 20 um ID tapered to 10 um ID (NewObjective)
  LC method   :
    Loading    -- 2 uL sample at 5 uL/min in 5% acetonitrile/water onto trap column
    Separation -- 0.5 uL/min; linear gradient 20% to 80% ACN over 25 min
    Hold       -- 80% ACN for additional 10 min
  DB search   : SEQUEST (Bioworks v3.01, Thermo-Fisher Scientific)
                Probability threshold: < 1.0E-03 (99.9% confidence interval)
                Sequence coverage threshold: >= 30%
  Results     : BSA model protein; 25 distinct peptides identified; 44% sequence coverage
                (Figure 4)

Title        : Attractive Design: An Elution Solvent Optimization Platform for
               Magnetic-Bead-based Fractionation Using Digital Microfluidics and
               Design of Experiments
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/attractive_design.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac504697r
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2015, Vol. 87, pp. 3902-3910
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with C18-functionalized magnetic beads on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a digital microfluidic (DMF) method for solid phase extraction (SPE)
using C18-functionalized magnetic beads manipulated within discrete droplets on an electrode
array. The approach replaces static porous polymer monolith (PPM) sorbents used in prior
DMF-SPE work with reconfigurable C18 magnetic beads, enabling on-the-fly tuning of sorbent
amount and removal of beads after extraction to maintain device reconfigurability.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Six-step C18 magnetic bead SPE (dispense, activate, wash, load, wash, elute)
  2. Loading capacity and equilibrium characterisation (fluorescein model analyte)
  3. Automated on-chip DOE-guided elution solvent optimisation for sitamaquine and angiotensin I
  4. Two-fraction sample fractionation and dried blood spot (DBS) extraction and cleanup

Total extraction time per sample is ~12 min. Throughput is 15 samples/h with 3 parallel
extractions on the current device implementation.

               Nanofabrication Centre, University of Toronto.

Assembly     : Top and bottom plates sandwiched with three layers of double-sided tape (3M,

Actuation    : 100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz, applied via automated control system with integrated
               moveable magnetic lens. Successive electrode actuation drives droplets.

Magnetic lens: Motorised vertical step-motor mounted beneath the DMF device.
               Engaged (close to device): immobilises C18 beads on device surface.
               Disengaged (moved away): beads freely suspended in droplet for active mixing.
               Originally developed for immunoassay workflows; repurposed here for SPE.
