PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Dispense C18 Magnetic Bead Bed
  Reagent    : C18 magnetic bead suspension, 5 mg/mL in water
  Volume     : 10 uL (~9e7 beads, ~9e-5 cm3 sorbent volume)
  Duration   : ~10 s
  Operation  : Bead suspension pipetted onto DMF device; magnetic lens engaged to form bed.
  Notes      : Sorbent volume tunable on-the-fly -- a key advantage over static PPM systems.
               Larger beds (12 uL) prevent saturation at high analyte concentrations (Fig. 2B).

Step 2 | Activate C18 Stationary Phase
  Reagent    : Acetonitrile (10 uL droplet)
  Duration   : ~30 s
  Operation  : (i) Droplet dispensed and driven to bead bed; beads engulfed.
               (ii) Magnetic lens disengaged; beads mixed via DMF actuation.
               (iii) Magnetic lens engaged; beads immobilised; supernatant driven away.
  Notes      : Solvent activation extends collapsed C18 chains into conformation capable of
               reversed-phase interaction with hydrophobic analytes (paper Fig. 1B).

Step 3 | Wash Beads with Water
  Reagent    : Deionized water (10 uL droplet)
  Duration   : ~30 s
  Operation  : Same three-operation sequence as Step 2.
  Notes      : Equilibrates activated C18 beads to aqueous phase before sample loading.

Step 4 | Load Sample and Incubate
  Reagent    : Analyte sample (10 uL droplet)
  Duration   : 5 min (300 s)
  Operation  : Droplet driven to beads; beads engulfed and actively mixed for 5 min;
               supernatant driven away. Mixing ensured by continuous DMF electrode actuation.
  Notes      : Analyte adsorbs onto C18 stationary phase during incubation.
               Loading equilibrium log K ~6 for sitamaquine (within typical SPE range).

Step 5 | Wash (x2)
  Reagent    : Deionized water (2 x 10 uL droplets)
  Duration   : ~60 s total (2 x 30 s)
  Operation  : Two sequential wash cycles using the three-operation sequence.
  Notes      : Removes unadsorbed matrix components while retaining adsorbed analyte on beads.

Step 6 | Elute
  Reagent    : Optimised elution solvent (10 uL, composed on-chip from unit droplets)
  Duration   : ~5 min (300 s)
  Operation  : Droplet driven to beads; beads engulfed and mixed for 5 min; eluate collected.
  Notes      : Solvent composition determined by DOE (see below). Unit droplets (2.5 uL) of
               neat water, methanol, and acetonitrile are dispensed from reservoirs and
               combined on-chip in the desired proportions to form the elution solvent.


LOADING CAPACITY CHARACTERISATION
----------------------------------
Model analyte : Fluorescein in 0.1% TFA (aqueous); concentrations 0.01-100000 ug/mL.
Measurement   : Fluorescence intensity of supernatant (post-extraction droplet) relative to
                stock solution. PheraStar plate reader (BMG Labtech, Durham, NC);
                ex 480 nm, em 520 nm. Triplicate experiments.

Results (Fig. 2A):
  - ~10% of sample remained unbound for 1-1000 ug/mL (no saturation).
  - At 10 mg/mL and above: saturation detected; >80% of sample remained unbound.

Sitamaquine equilibrium:
  - 1.45% unretained post-extraction at 1 ug/mL (by ESI-MS/MS).
  - Mobile phase volume: 10 uL; stationary phase volume: 6.03e-7 mL
    (shell model: uniform C18 thickness = octadecyl alkane chain length, 2.14 nm).
  - Equilibrium log K ~6; consistent with commonly reported SPE solute-sorbent equilibria.


DOE ELUTION SOLVENT OPTIMISATION
----------------------------------
Design software : JMP (SAS, Cary, NC); simplex-centroid design.
Solvents        : Acetonitrile (ACN), Methanol (MeOH), Deionized Water (H2O).
Combinations    : 7 points: neat ACN, neat MeOH, neat H2O, 1:1 ACN:MeOH, 1:1 ACN:H2O,
                  1:1 MeOH:H2O, 1:1:1 ACN:MeOH:H2O.

On-chip mixing  : Unit droplets (2.5 uL each) dispensed from reservoir electrodes containing
                  neat solvents, then combined and mixed in desired proportions.
                  DMF can automatically generate any composition from the ternary space.

Model           : Three-component special cubic (eq 2 in paper):
                  y_hat = sum(bi*xi) + sum(bij*xi*xj) + sum(bijk*xi*xj*xk)
                  where xi = solvent fraction; bi = linear, bij = binary, bijk = ternary coefficients.
                  Response surface plots generated for each analyte (Fig. 4A/B).

Solubility prediction: Abraham general solvation model (web calculator) used to predict
                  sitamaquine solubilities: MeOH > ACN > H2O; consistent with DOE results.

Results:
  Sitamaquine (1 ug/mL):
    - Optimal elution solvent: 100% Methanol (extraction efficiency ~45-55%; Fig. 4A).
    - General trend: increasing efficiency with increasing organic fraction.
    - MeOH outperforms ACN, consistent with Abraham solvation model prediction.

  Angiotensin I (50 ug/mL):
    - Optimal elution solvent: 1:1 ACN:H2O (extraction efficiency ~45-50%; Fig. 4B).
    - Consistent with common practice for reversed-phase peptide separations by HPLC.

Comparison with ZipTip (Fig. 5):
  - DMF C18 bead extraction comparable to C18 ZipTip (EMD Millipore) for both analytes.
  - Sitamaquine eluted in neat methanol; angiotensin I eluted in 1:1 ACN:H2O.


SAMPLE FRACTIONATION
---------------------
Mixture    : Sitamaquine (1 ug/mL) + angiotensin I (50 ug/mL), co-loaded on C18 beads.
Strategy   : Sequential elution with two solvents of differing polarity:

Elution 1 (Fraction 1) -- Neat methanol:
  Sitamaquine recovery : ~90-95%
  Angiotensin I carry-over : ~5-10%
  Result: Sitamaquine-enriched fraction.

Elution 2 (Fraction 2) -- 1:1 ACN:H2O:
  Angiotensin I recovery : ~85-90%
  Sitamaquine carry-over : ~10-15%
  Result: Angiotensin I-enriched fraction.

Coelution : <10% for both fractions (Fig. 6B).
Detection : ESI-MS/MS (344->271 m/z) for sitamaquine; ESI-MS (433 m/z, [M+3H]3+) for
            angiotensin I. IS: 2H10-sitamaquine (500 ng/mL) + bradykinin (531 m/z, [M+2H]2+).


DRIED BLOOD SPOT EXTRACTION AND CLEANUP
-----------------------------------------
Purpose    : Proof-of-principle for real-world complex matrix sample cleanup.
             Reduce ionisation suppression of sitamaquine in DBS extracts.

DBS preparation:
  - 15 uL human whole blood (BioChemed Services) spiked with sitamaquine (5 ug/mL).
  - Spotted onto PerkinElmer 226 Sample Collection Cards; allowed to dry.
  - 2 mm biopsy punch extracted into methanol (30 uL, 5 min).

On-chip procedure:
  1. Unit droplet (2.5 uL) of DBS extract split off for cleanup.
  2. Combined with water (22.5 uL) on-chip; total 25 uL at diluted aqueous matrix.
     (Aqueous dilution required for C18 reversed-phase compatibility.)
  3. C18 bead SPE cleanup following six-step protocol (elution: neat methanol, 10 uL).
  4. Off-chip: eluate diluted to 100 uL in 1:1 ACN:H2O + 0.5% formic acid.

Detection:
  - API 4000 Triple Quadrupole MS/MS (AB Sciex, Concord, Ontario).
  - Positive ion mode; direct infusion 2 uL/min; spray voltage 5 kV.
  - SRM transition: 344->271 m/z (sitamaquine); 12 scans averaged.

Results (Fig. 7):
  - Raw DBS extract: little signal for sitamaquine at 271 m/z (ionisation suppression).
  - Post C18 bead cleanup: sitamaquine signal (271 m/z) strongly enhanced.
  - Cleanup reduces matrix interferents (lipids, haem, proteins) that suppress ESI ionisation.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Liquid Biopsy and Therapeutic Response: Circulating Tumor Cell Cultures for Evaluation of Anticancer Treatment
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/pdf/10.1126/sciadv.1600274
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.1600274
Journal      : Science Advances, 2016, Vol. 2, Article e1600274
Platform     : Integrated three-layer PDMS microfluidic device (continuous-flow); tree-like gradient generator + channel barrier + tapered microwell array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an integrated microfluidic approach for short-term primary circulating tumor cell
(CTC) culture from patient whole blood and in situ anticancer drug screening. Blood samples from breast
cancer patients are collected via liquid biopsy, lysed to remove red blood cells, and the resulting
nucleated cell fraction (WBCs + CTCs) is seeded directly into a custom device incorporating arrays of
tapered elliptical microwells. No pre-enrichment of CTCs is required before culture.

Cells are cultured under hypoxic conditions (1% O2, mimicking the in vivo tumor microenvironment) for
11 days, during which CTC-containing clusters form in the tapered microwells. Culture positivity is
assessed on Day 11 by bright-field imaging. Positive samples (clusters in >=50% of microwells) proceed
to in situ drug screening: a tree-like serpentine gradient generator simultaneously delivers eight
different doxorubicin concentrations across eight parallel culture channels. After 72 hours of drug
exposure, cell viability is assessed by LIVE/DEAD fluorescence staining (calcein-AM / EtBr / CD45-APC),
and IC50 values are extracted by 4-parameter logistic curve fitting.

The complete procedure from blood collection to IC50 readout takes 14 days. Rapid IC50 feedback
enables immediate clinical intervention upon detection of drug resistance or tolerance.
Clinically validated with 73 blood samples from 55 breast cancer patients.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
The integrated device consists of three bonded PDMS layers assembled by oxygen plasma treatment:

Layer 1 (top)    : Tree-like serpentine gradient generator. Mixes two inlet flows (0% vehicle +
                   100% drug) to produce 8 output concentrations simultaneously at 100 uL/min.
                   Concentration gradient confirmed stable over 24 h (P < 0.05) and independent
                   of input dye concentration across 5 flow rates (25-200 uL/min).
                   Fabricated by standard photolithography on SU-8 2050 / SU-8 2000.5 silicon wafer.

Layer 2 (middle) : Channel barrier. Aluminum mold (Whits Technologies, Singapore). Defines 8
                   parallel culture channels; prevents cross-contamination between concentration zones.

Layer 3 (bottom) : Custom multimicrowell array. Each of the 8 channels contains ~1000 tapered
                   elliptical microwells (250 x 150 um footprint, 150 um depth, 4.7 mm pitch).
                   Fabricated by diffuser back-side lithography: laser direct writing on soda-lime
                   optical mask blank (Heidelberg DWL 66fs, Coherent I326C Ar laser), Cr etching,
                   SU-8 2100 resist (300 um thick, double spin-coat at 1500 rpm), UV exposure
                   through opal diffusing glass (Edmund Optics) at 12 mW/cm2, 365 nm, 9 s.
                   Dome-shaped SU-8 pillars (height 150 um) serve as PDMS casting template.

Microwell geometry: Tapered (dome-bottom) elliptical wells preferred over cylindrical wells because
   the inclined walls allow cells to settle to the center, forming a single dense cluster per well
   rather than multiple small aggregates. Tapered design retains 88 +/- 20% cell viability vs
   31.5 +/- 3% for cylindrical microwells.

Device integration: Assembled device placed in 150-mm dish filled with thin PBS film to limit
   evaporation; incubated in humidified chamber. Syringe pump (NE-1000, New Era Pump Systems)
   connected via BD Luer-Lok syringes for all infusion/withdrawal operations.


CELL SOURCE AND CLINICAL SAMPLES
---------------------------------
- Primary circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from breast cancer patients (n = 73 blood samples,
  55 patients; early-stage, newly diagnosed, locally advanced, or refractory metastatic).
- Study approved by DSRB (references 2012/00105, 2012/00979, 2010/00270, 2010/00691).
  All patients provided informed consent.
- Control validation: MCF-7 (HTB-22TM, ATCC) human breast adenocarcinoma cell line used
  to characterise and validate assay conditions before clinical sample evaluation.
  MCF-7 maintained in high-glucose DMEM (Invitrogen) + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep;
  37 C, 5% CO2, 80% confluence; subcultured twice weekly; 0.01% trypsin / 5.3 mM EDTA.
- Presence of cancer cells in clinical samples validated by fluorescence in situ hybridization
  (FISH) for breast cancer-associated markers TOP2A (Abbott) and CCND1 (Empire Genomics).

  Procedure   : Blood samples stored in EDTA vacutainer; lysed within 10 h of withdrawal.

Title        : One Cell, One Drop, One Click: Hybrid Microfluidics for Mammalian Single Cell Isolation
Source Link  : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_20644bba5a194fc0966d7bba24bbc451.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.202002400
Journal      : Small, 2020, Vol. 16, Article 2002400
Platform     : Hybrid DMF (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel microfluidics) on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a hybrid microfluidics method for deterministic single-cell isolation,
encapsulation, on-demand droplet manipulation, and isoclonal recovery for mammalian gene-editing
workflows. The device integrates a bottom digital microfluidic (DMF) layer (chromium co-planar
electrodes on glass + 7 um SU-8 5 dielectric) with a top PDMS channel layer (35 um height,
50-75 um width), enabling individual electrode-addressable control of droplets flowing inside
microfluidic channels -- a configuration referred to as "hybrid" microfluidics.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Hydrodynamic single-cell trapping in serpentine channel traps (8 um constrictions)
  2. In situ deterministic single-cell encapsulation by phase change (no Poisson statistics)
  3. On-demand droplet operations: forward/reverse release, keep, on-demand generation, and merge
  4. CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing pipeline: transfection, on-chip fluorescence screening,
     isoclone sorting, capillary recovery, and clonal expansion in a 96-well plate

The complete trap-to-recovery workflow takes approximately 45 minutes, compared to hours
or days required by standard FACS or limited dilution methods.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass (50 x 75 mm); electrode size ~100 um,
            area 0.06 mm2; co-planar ground and activated electrodes on same plate.
Layer ii  : SU-8 5 dielectric, 7 um thick; spin-coated and hard-baked to 180 C.
Layer iii : PDMS channel layer; channel height 35 um, main channel width 50 um,
            bypass channel width ~50 um; fabricated by soft lithography on SU-8 2035 master.

Device sections:
  - T-junction on-demand droplet generator (2 T-junctions, multiple sub-electrodes)
  - Serpentine single-cell trapping array: 12 traps total, 6 electrode-equipped;
    each trap has 4 co-planar electrodes (2 below main channel, 2 below trap)

Inlets  : I1 (oil + droplets), I2 (cells + priming), I3 (PBS/media for generator),
          I4 (HFE7500 for generator)
Outlets : O1 (waste), O2 (sample recovery / flow reversal), O3 (bridge to encapsulation)

Actuation: 15 kHz AC, 126 Vrms applied via optocoupler switches controlled through
           an in-house Python-based GUI automation framework.


CELL LINES
----------
- MCF-7 (human breast cancer): model cell line for trapping, encapsulation, and viability assays.
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- NCI-H1299 (human lung squamous cell carcinoma, eGFP+/Luciferase dual-labelled stable line):
  used for gene-editing, isoclone sorting, and expansion.
  Cultured in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronics F-127
  Mix      : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Duration : 5 min at 0.8-8 nL/s via inlet I1
  Purpose  : Reduces MCF-7 cell adhesion to PDMS channel walls.

Step 2 | Hydrodynamic Single-Cell Trapping
  Cell line      : MCF-7
  Concentration  : 1e5-1e6 cells/mL in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), stirred continuously in syringe
  Flow rate      : 1-4 nL/s (optimal); 5 nL/s tested at ~88.3% single-cell efficiency
  Trap design    : 8 um constriction (smaller than MCF-7 cell diameter); positioned at
                   curvature of serpentine channel so Qtrap > Qbypass when trap is empty.
                   Slanted overhang along main channel steers flow into trap.
  Multi-occupancy: >54 consecutive single-cell events confirmed; second cell does not enter
                   occupied trap (increased Rtrap reduces Qtrap).
  Filtering      : Cells passed through 40 um cell strainer before loading to remove clumps.

Step 3 | In Situ Deterministic Single-Cell Encapsulation
  Method         : Phase change from single-phase (aqueous) to two-phase (water-in-oil) flow.
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% w/v PEG fluoro-surfactant (Ran Biotechnologies), 4 nL/s
  Electrode      : 15 kHz, 126 Vrms; electric field density ~5x10^6 V/m between main channel
                   and trap; electrostatic force pulls aqueous phase into trap when oil shears.
  Droplet volume : 150.3 +/- 5.6 pL (N=11); monodisperse, no Poisson-based encapsulation.
  Frame sequence : Frame I: trap electrode activated, oil enters main channel.
                   Frame II: trap electrode active, other electrodes grounded; oil cuts aqueous
                             phase at both trap ends; cell remains inside.
                   Frame III: all potentials grounded; oil continues to next trap.

Step 4 | On-Demand Droplet Operations
  Forward release : Actuate electrodes below trap then main channel (15 kHz, 126 Vrms).
                    Flow rate <1 nL/s → >95% release probability.
                    Without actuation: droplet never released at any flow rate.
  Reverse release : Same actuation sequence under reverse oil flow.
                    Hydrodynamic only: >10.92 nL/s needed; with actuation: 100% at any rate.
  Keep            : 4 electrodes activated; field centred at trap opening.
                    Flow rates <45.4 nL/s → >95% keep probability (Ph < Felec).
                    Above 45.4 nL/s: Ph > Felec; droplet escapes.
  On-demand gen.  : T-junction; oil 2-2.5 nL/s, aqueous 0.6 nL/s; 15 kHz 126 Vrms.
                    Droplet volume 250.9 +/- 39 pL.
  Merge           : Incoming droplets merged with trapped droplets on demand; no stream
                    synchronisation required.

Step 5 | Cell Viability Assay
  Cells          : MCF-7 (fresh trap), PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Actuation      : 15 kHz, 126 Vrms for 30 s total (two top electrodes 10 s each,
                   ground electrode 10 s, two bottom electrodes 10 s)
  Stain          : FDA/PI 1X; 10 uL PI stock (2 ug/mL) + 2.5 uL FDA stock (5 ug/mL)
                   FDA: ex 490 nm / em 526 nm (live cells, green)
                   PI : ex 488 nm / em 617 nm (dead cells, red)
  Incubation     : 10 min on device in dark; imaged at 4x or 10x on inverted fluorescence
                   microscope (Olympus IX73)
  Results        : Control 87.5 +/- 7.2% viability; potentiated 82.5 +/- 8.1% viability
                   (p = 0.6687, unpaired t-test, N=3). No significant difference.
                   ~18% loss attributed to pre-processing handling outside culture environment.

Step 6 | Off-Chip CRISPR-Cas9 Transfection (eGFP KO arm)
  Cell line      : NCI-H1299 (eGFP+/Luciferase stable)
  Plasmid        : pCRISPR_eGFP_314 (Cas9 + mCherry reporter + eGFP sgRNA)
                   eGFP sgRNA sequence: GCAACTACAAGACCCGCGCCG
  Reagent        : Lipofectamine 3000, 5 ug DNA/well
  Format         : 24-well plate; Day 0: subculture; Day 1: transfect; Day 3: harvest
  Incubation     : 48 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 2880 min = 172800 s)
  Results        : ~25.3% transfection efficiency (mCherry+); ~4.95% KO efficiency (GCD assay)
  KO confirm     : Genomic Cleavage Detection assay (GeneArt GCD kit, Thermo Scientific);
                   ~500 bp PCR fragments re-annealed and cleaved; resolved on 2% LAB gel at 220 V.
  Note           : RAF1 KO is an independent parallel experiment (pCRISPR_RAF1_94;
                   RAF1 sgRNA: GCCGCCCGAGAGTCTTAATCG; 13.7% transfection, 8.3% KO efficiency).

Step 7 | On-Chip Isoclone Trapping, Screening, and Encapsulation
  Cells          : Transfected NCI-H1299, resuspended in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Trapping rate  : 4 nL/s
  Screening      : Fluorescence microscopy
                   mCherry (ex ~565 nm): positive = successful transfection
                   eGFP   (ex ~460 nm): loss of signal = eGFP knocked out
  Expected hits  : ~1 in 6 traps (~16.7%) contain a mCherry+ isoclone
  Re-trapping    : If trap contains no transfected clone, increase forward flow rate to
                   squeeze cell through trap and load a new cell iteratively.
  Encapsulation  : HFE7500 + 2% fluorosurfactant at 4 nL/s; 15 kHz, 126 Vrms
  Detection      : mCherryGFPDetection module; 30 s fluorescence read
  Sorting        : Positive clone released on-demand toward outlet (forward release)
  Total time     : ~45 min from trapping to release

Step 8 | Isoclone Recovery and Clonal Expansion
  Recovery method:
    1. Positive droplet forward-released on demand to outlet
    2. Loaded into glass capillary pre-filled with HFE7500 2% fluorosurfactant
    3. Capillary tip placed onto 20 uL conditioned media on hydrophobic PTFE membrane
       (0.22 um) on custom 3D-printed holder at 37 C
    4. Capillary flushed with 10 uL FC-40 oil; oil absorbs HFE7500, releasing aqueous droplet
    5. 1 min incubation; isoclone released into conditioned media droplet
    6. Transferred to 96-well plate with 50 uL conditioned media/well at 37 C

  Conditioned media: 50% RPMI-1640 10% FBS 1% pen/strep collected from 1-day 80%-confluent
                     H1299 cells + 50% fresh complete growth media; filter-sterilised; -80 C storage.
  Expansion        : 37 C, 5% CO2; 7 days (= 10080 min = 604800 s)
                     Day 1   : Single adherent clones visible
                     Day 2-3 : mCherry reporter lost (transient transfection, plasmid diluted)
                     Day 5   : Image eGFP-negative clones (460 nm channel)
                     Day 7   : Confirm clonal expansion; media changed with fresh complete media
  Format           : 96-well plate; expand to 50% confluency

Protocol details:

This is a competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for screening morphine in urine.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Urine Sample
  - Morphine Enzyme Conjugate
  - Distilled Water (Wash Buffer)
  - TMB Substrate
  - Stop Reagent

STEPS:
1. Sample Preparation: Add 20 units of the urine sample to the reaction zone. 
2. Conjugate Incubation: Add 100 units of morphine enzyme conjugate to the sample. Mix the solution for 60 seconds to allow competitive binding between free morphine in the sample and the conjugate.
3. Primary Incubation: Incubate the mixture at 23°C (room temperature) for 60 minutes to reach equilibrium. 
4. Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone six times to remove unbound conjugate. For each wash cycle, add 350 units of distilled water, mix for 45 seconds, and discard the wash supernatant.
5. Substrate Development: Add 100 units of TMB substrate to the retained mixture. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at 23°C for 30 minutes to allow the colorimetric reaction to develop.
6. Stop Reaction: Add 100 units of acid stop reagent. Mix with the developed substrate for 60 seconds to halt the enzymatic reaction and change the color from blue to yellow.
7. Detection: Measure the resulting optical signal (absorbance) over 1 minute to obtain the reading. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of morphine in the urine sample. A lower signal indicates a higher presence of morphine, while a higher signal indicates little to no morphine.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-Based High-Throughput Cultivation for Accurate Screening of
               Antibiotic Resistant Gut Microbes
Source Link  : https://elifesciences.org/articles/56998
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.56998
Journal      : eLife 2020, Vol. 9, Article e56998
Platform     : Anaerobic droplet microfluidics (flow-focusing generation +
               dielectrophoretic sorting) inside vinyl anaerobic chamber


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic platform for high-throughput anaerobic isolation,
cultivation, and sorting of human gut-associated bacteria in picoliter-scale droplets.
The system operates entirely within a vinyl anaerobic chamber, enabling cultivation of
strictly anaerobic organisms that are incompatible with standard aerobic bench workflows.

The protocol is divided into two functional phases:

  1. Rich-media droplet cultivation (Protocol 1)
     Fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) donor stool is stochastically encapsulated at
     single-cell density in picoliter droplets formed with three distinct rich growth
     media (BHIS, GMM, YCFA). Each droplet acts as an independent microreactor,
     eliminating inter-species competition and enabling slow-growing taxa to expand
     without being outcompeted. An image-based wavelet-OD sorting step selectively
     retains sparse (slow-growing) colony droplets to further enrich rare taxa.

  2. Antibiotic resistance screening (Protocol 2)
     The same donor stool is encapsulated in BHIS droplets supplemented individually
     with ampicillin (100 ug/mL), ciprofloxacin (5 ug/mL), or vancomycin (10 ug/mL).
     After 1-day incubation, optical density-based sorting removes non-viable droplets
     so only organisms that actively grew in the presence of antibiotic contribute to
     downstream 16S sequencing reads.

Key outcomes: richness increase over plate cultures of 15% (BHIS) to 410% (YCFA);
105 vs 57 low-abundance ASVs (<1% in stool) recovered by droplets vs plates; 21 unique
antibiotic-resistant organisms detected exclusively in droplets.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Enclosure   : Vinyl anaerobic chamber (Coy Laboratory Products)
Atmosphere  : 86% N2 / 10% CO2 / 4% H2; O2 <1 ppm; H2 maintained at 1.5-2.5%;
              monitored by Coy CAM-12. Coy H2S-reducing column inside chamber
              prevents corrosion of electronic components.

Components inside chamber:
  - Inverted microscope (Nikon Ts2R), 4x and 10x objectives
  - Microfluidic devices (droplet generation + droplet sorting)
  - High frame rate camera (Basler acA640-750um, 925 Hz, 672x360 px, 59 us exposure)
  - Syringe pumps (Harvard Apparatus Pump 11 Pico Plus Elite)
  - Incubator (37 C)
  - Electrodes

Components outside chamber (connected via sealed rubber ports):
  - Computer running custom LabView code
  - Voltage amplifier (TREK Model 2220, 200 V/V gain)
  - NI-DAQ 6211 (analog output -> amplifier)

Droplet generation device:
  - Architecture     : Flow-focusing junction
  - Channel height   : 50 um (SU-8 3050 on 4" silicon wafer)
  - Fabrication      : Soft lithography; PDMS (RTV 615) 10:1 A:B; cured 80 C >=1 h;
                       plasma bonded to glass slide
  - Hydrophobicity   : Aquapel coating followed by Fluorinert FC-40 flush
  - Oil phase        : Bio-Rad Droplet Generation Oil for EvaGreen
  - Droplet volume   : 65-115 pL
  - Emulsion volume  : 0.5-1 mL per run (~4-15 million droplets)
  - Generation time  : 20-60 min depending on device

Droplet sorting device:
  - Same fabrication as generation device; bonded to ITO-coated glass slide
    (Delta Technologies CG-811N-S207)
  - Electrodes       : Low-melting solder (51% In / 32.5% Bi / 16.5% Sn; Indium Corp.)
                       flowed into holes at 90 C
  - Sorting mechanism: Dielectrophoresis (DEP)
  - Actuation        : 10 kHz, 800 V p-p, 30% duty cycle, 10 ms pulse
  - Sorting rate     : ~30 Hz
  - Re-injection     : 20 uL/hr (droplets); 180 uL/hr (oil spacing)


WAVELET OD SORTING ALGORITHM
-----------------------------
Detection region : Interior of each droplet (~6080 pixels) between red-dot markers
                   at sorting junction; detected by edge-finding along channel centre.

Algorithm:
  - Discrete wavelet frame decomposition (LabView IMAQ Extract Texture Feature VI)
  - Wavelet type    : Biorthogonal 3.1
  - Subband         : Low-Low-High (LLH)
  - Window          : 15 x 15 pixels, step size 5 pixels
  - Co-occurrence   : 15 grey levels, 3 x 3 pixel displacement
  - Normalization   : Non-zero elements of wavelet feature vector normalized to 1

Threshold classification:
  - Wavelet OD < 0.3       : Empty droplet (waste)
  - Wavelet OD 0.3 to 0.7  : Sparse / slow-growing colony (KEEP)
  - Wavelet OD > 0.7       : Dense colony (waste)

False positive rate: <=8% (upper bound; actual rate likely lower as waste stream
                     slow-grower fraction was not counted)


STOOL SAMPLE PREPARATION
-------------------------
Donor         : Previously characterised FMT donor (Lee et al. 2017)
Ethics        : University of Chicago Ethics Committee and IRB (IRB 132-0212);
                written informed consent obtained from single donor
Preparation   : 50 mL stool diluted in 100 mL PBS; centrifuged; supernatant
                collected and stored at -80 C
Cell density  : Live ~1.5 +/- 1.0 x10^8 cells/mL; dead ~21 +/- 3 x10^8 cells/mL
                (Live/Dead BacLight kit, ThermoFisher; note: dye requires oxygenation,
                may introduce measurement artefact)
Plate control : 100 uL suspension spread at ~1 cell/500 um2 (bacterial lawn density)
                to ensure rare cells are represented
Droplet load  : 200x dilution; Poisson mean 2-12% of droplets contain one live cell
                (range accounts for cell density uncertainty and droplet volume variation)


GROWTH MEDIA
------------

BHIS (Brain Heart Infusion Supplemented):
  500 mL water + 18.5 g BHI Broth (Sigma) + 2.5 g yeast extract + 0.25 g L-cysteine
  + 7.5 g agar (plates only); autoclaved; add 0.5 mL 0.1% Vitamin K in 95% ethanol
  + 0.5 mL hemin solution (5 mg/mL in 0.1 M NaOH, filter-sterilised).
  BHIS-ASF variant: add 5% newborn calf serum + 5% sheep serum + 5% horse serum
  (Fisher Scientific) for ASF validation cultures.

GMM (Gut Microbiota Medium):
  Prepared per Goodman et al. 2011.

YCFA (Yeast Casitones Fatty Acid, modified DSMZ 1611):
  10 g casitone, 2.5 g yeast extract, 5 g D-glucose, 0.045 g MgSO4.7H2O,
  0.09 g CaCl2.2H2O, 0.45 g K2HPO4, 0.45 g KH2PO4, 0.9 g NaCl, 0.001 g resazurin,
  1.9 mL acetic acid, 0.7 mL propionic acid, 90 uL iso-butyric acid, 100 uL n-valeric
  acid, 100 uL iso-valeric acid, 500 mL DI water. Boil 10 min stirring; cool; add 4 g
  NaHCO3 + 0.5 g L-cysteine-HCl + 0.01 g hemin + 0.0025 g mucin + 15 g agar (plates).
  Adjust to 990 mL; pH 6.7-6.8; autoclave; +10 mL filter-sterilised vitamin solution.
  Vitamin solution (per litre): 2 mg biotin, 2 mg folic acid, 12 mg pyridoxine-HCl,
  4.5 mg thiamine-HCl, 5 mg riboflavin, 5 mg nicotinic acid, 5 mg D-Ca-pantothenate,
  0.1 mg vitamin B12, 5 mg p-aminobenzoic acid, 5 mg DL-thioctic acid.

Antibiotic-supplemented media (all in BHIS base):
  Ampicillin   : 100 ug/mL (commensurate with commercially available selection plates)
  Ciprofloxacin:   5 ug/mL
  Vancomycin   :  10 ug/mL


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fecal Cell Encapsulation in BHIS Droplets
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, BHIS_Medium, HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Operation     : Dispense cells + medium; mix (abstracts flow-focusing generation);
                  mix with oil phase (produces droplet emulsion)
  Poisson load  : 200x dilution; ~2-12% droplets encapsulate one live cell
  Droplet vol   : 65-115 pL; emulsion 0.5-1 mL; ~4-15 million droplets
  Storage       : 15 mL snap-cap culture tube (Fisherbrand 149569C) in 37 C incubator
  Notes         : Stochastic single-cell isolation in discrete droplets eliminates
                  competitive overgrowth of fast-growers over slow-growing taxa.
                  Quorum sensing signal accumulation is accelerated in small droplet
                  volumes (Boedicker et al. 2009), potentially benefiting certain organisms.

Step 2 | BHIS Droplet Incubation

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidic Multiplex Sorter for Strain Development
Source Link  : https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/admt.202401209
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/admt.202401209
Journal      : Advanced Materials Technologies, 2025, Vol. 10, Article 2401209
Platform     : Droplet-digital microfluidics with multiplex co-planar electrostatic sorting


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a droplet-digital high-throughput screening (HTS) workflow for strain
improvement of Saccharomyces cerevisiae var. diastaticus, a diastatic yeast used in beverage
fermentation for its ability to convert starch and dextrin into fermentable sugars via the
secreted glucoamylase enzyme encoded by the STA1 gene.

The core innovation is a multiplexed electrostatic droplet sorter capable of partitioning a
single genome-shuffled yeast library into two fitness sub-populations simultaneously:
  GT1 (high glucoamylase activity, SC1 channel, 95th fluorescence percentile)
  GT2 (mid glucoamylase activity, SC2 channel, 85th fluorescence percentile)

This avoids the non-uniform sampling bias of binary sorting (which would target only the
top-performing population) and reduces the post-analysis sample size by approximately 14-fold
compared to a binary approach at equivalent 95% confidence. The key finding is that mid-level
sorted strains (IDY1-M23, IDY2-M9) outperform high-level sorted strains in beverage
fermentation, an outcome only discoverable through multiplex screening.

The protocol consists of four sequential phases:
  1. Generation of a diversified genome-shuffled library (>10^7 variants) by self-mating
  2. Single-cell encapsulation in 30 pL droplets, off-chip incubation, and multiplex sorting
  3. Post-HTS colony recovery and maltodextrin growth screening
  4. Beverage fermentation evaluation of selected strains in synthetic media


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium co-planar electrodes patterned on 50 x 75 mm glass slide;
            ground and activated electrodes on same plane (<25 um gap).
Layer ii  : SU-8 5 dielectric, 7 um thick; spin-coated and hard-baked.
Layer iii : PDMS channel layer fabricated by soft lithography;
            channel height 75 um, 100 um width for 30 pL droplet sorting.
            Additional channel heights: 35 um (for 30 pL), 50 um (for 110 pL).

Sorter design:
  - Symmetrical co-planar electrode geometry with three outlets:
      SC1: sorting channel 1 (high-fitness, GT1, SE1 actuation)
      SC2: sorting channel 2 (mid-fitness, GT2, SE2 actuation)
      WC:  central waste channel (non-selected droplets)
  - Two sorting electrodes: SE1 (lateral deflection to SC1) and SE2 (lateral deflection to SC2)
  - No pressure rebalancing or device redesign required for droplet volumes 30-1000 pL
  - Droplet and plug morphologies both sortable (co-planar field intersects both)

Droplet generator: T-junction with 2% fluorosurfactant in HFE7500 oil

Actuation: 15 kHz AC sine wave, 105 Vrms, applied via in-house automation
           software and graphical user interface (Python-based, previously described)
           Software repository: https://bitbucket.org/shihmicrolab/f_ahmadi_2023_uflowcontrol


ORGANISMS
---------
- S. cerevisiae var. diastaticus IDY1: isolated from high-sugar, high-alcohol beverage
  industry setting. More robust and better suited for elevated sugar levels. Grows well
  in all droplet volumes (30, 110, 1000 pL). Peak glucoamylase fluorescence ~3 a.u. at 48 h.
- S. cerevisiae var. diastaticus IDY2: isolated from low-sugar, low-alcohol beverage
  setting. Less adaptable to high sugar; only 30 pL droplets show significant growth.
  Peak glucoamylase fluorescence ~1 a.u. at 48 h.
- IY1: non-diastatic S. cerevisiae (STA1-); negative control; does not secrete glucoamylase.
- IRY1: recombinant S. cerevisiae with heterologous glucoamylase gene; positive control.

Both strains sourced from Lallemand Inc. (Montreal, QC, Canada).


FLUORESCENT SUBSTRATE
---------------------
Substrate : 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-glucopyranoside (4-MUG-a)
            Validated using commercial Aspergillus niger glucoamylase at pH 7.5 and 11.
            Fluorescent signal distinguishable at neutral pH (pH 7.5) between IDY1/IDY2
            and negative control IY1.
            Previous substrate candidates 4-NPM (absorbance) and 4-NPG rejected:
              4-NPM requires pH >10 (reduces cell viability); absorbance less sensitive.
              4-NPG showed no distinguishable signal for diastatic strains.
Stock     : 4 mM in 0.1 M phosphate buffer pH 7.5
Final     : 2 mM per droplet (1:1 co-encapsulation with cell suspension)
Excitation: 360 nm (ex) / 450 nm (em); measured on CLARIOstar Plus (BMG LABTECH)
BSA       : 10% (w/w) bovine serum albumin added to cell suspension to reduce
            protein adsorption to droplet interface and PDMS walls


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Genome Shuffling Library Generation
  Strains        : IDY1 and IDY2 (independent libraries)
  Method         : Sporulation and self-mating (genome shuffling)
  Sporulation    : Inoculate saturated cultures into sporulation medium (1 g/L yeast
                   extract, 10 g/L KOAc, 0.5 g/L glucose); OD600 start = 0.3
                   Incubate 5 days at 23 C, 150 rpm
  Spore prep     : Ether-zymolyase ascospore technique
  Germination    : ~50 uL YPD 2% glucose, 30 C overnight; then 5 mL 2% YPD, 30 C overnight
  Library size   : >10^7 variants
  Freezer stocks : 25% glycerol (final) added to saturated YPD culture; multiple single-use vials
  Notes          : Non-GMO technique; compliant with agro-food regulatory requirements.
                   IDY2 starts with enhanced growth phenotype in maltodextrin relative to IDY1.

Step 2 | Cell Suspension Preparation
  Preculture     : Overnight YPD broth at 30 C, 200 rpm
  Wash           : Sonicate and wash 3x with PBS by centrifugation
  Resuspend      : 2x YPD broth buffered at pH 7.5
  Cell density   : Adjusted for Poisson lambda=0.3 per droplet size:
                     30 pL  -> 2x10^7 cells/mL
                     110 pL -> 5x10^6 cells/mL
                     1 nL   -> 6x10^5 cells/mL
  BSA            : 10% (w/w) added to cell solution before encapsulation

Step 3 | Single-Cell Encapsulation in 30 pL Droplets
  Generator      : T-junction droplet generator
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% PEG fluorosurfactant
  Encapsulation  : 1:1 cell suspension : substrate solution co-flow
  Droplet size   : 30 pL (D = 40 um channel)
  Collection     : PCR tube with 50 uL 2% fluorosurfactant in HFE7500
  Monitoring     : Droplet generation monitored by Fiji (ImageJ) for size verification

Step 4 | Off-Chip Incubation (48 h at 30 C)
  Temperature    : 30 C in the dark
  Duration       : 48 h (= 2880 min = 172800 s)
  Imaging        : Fluorescence + bright-field every 24 h
  Cell growth    : Counted by in-droplet cell counting (Fiji ROI)
  Fluorescence   : CTDF (corrected total droplet fluorescence) quantified per droplet:
                     CTDF = DF/(DA x Mean_BR) - DF_t0/(DA_t0 x Mean_BR_t0)
                     where DF = integrated density, DA = droplet area, BR = background reading
  Optimal volume : 30 pL selected for highest fluorescence and fastest throughput
  Results        : IDY1 peak ~3 a.u. at 48 h (30 pL); IDY2 peak ~1 a.u. at 48 h (30 pL)

Step 5 | Droplet Re-injection and Fluorescence Histogram Gating
  Re-injection   : 3 nL/s droplet flow rate; 300 nL/s spacer oil flow rate
  Tubing         : 1/32" OD, 0.381 mm ID PEEK (re-injection syringe)
  Throughput     : 160 Hz for 30 pL droplets
  Detection      : In-line optical fiber (ex: 470 nm LED, em: 450 nm bandpass filter)
                   Spectrometer: FLAME-S UV-VIS (Ocean Insight)
  Droplets screened: ~720,000 total
  Histogram      : Gaussian fluorescence distribution plotted; gates set as:
                     GT1 (gate-SC1): high fluorescence 95th percentile
                     GT2 (gate-SC2): mid fluorescence 85th percentile

Step 6 | Multiplex Electrostatic Sorting
  Mechanism      : Co-planar electrode actuation laterally deflects droplets into SC1 or SC2.
                   Without actuation: all droplets flow to WC (central waste channel).
  GT1 (SC1)      : SE1 actuated at 15 kHz, 105 Vrms -> high-fitness droplets deflect to SC1
  GT2 (SC2)      : SE2 actuated at 15 kHz, 105 Vrms -> mid-fitness droplets deflect to SC2
  WC (waste)     : Neither electrode actuated; droplet flows undeflected to central channel
  Sorting efficiency: >90.2% true positive; ~3% false negative; no significant difference
                      between SC1 and SC2 channels
  Multiplex efficiency at 30 pL:
    1 mM fluorescein: 100% (SC1), ~3% FN
    0.1 mM fluorescein: 98.6% (SC2), ~3% FN
  Droplets sorted : ~108,000 total (from ~720,000 screened)
  Sorted strains:
    IDY1 GT1 (high): H2, H3
    IDY1 GT2 (mid):  M2, M23
    IDY2 GT1 (high): H13, H23
    IDY2 GT2 (mid):  M9, M22

Step 7 | Colony Recovery and Plating
  Recovery       : Pipette top layer of oil emulsion from pipette tip at SC1 or SC2 outlet
  Aliquot        : 5 uL from sorted population diluted into 50 uL YPD broth
  Plating        : YPD agar plates; incubate 30 C for 48 h
  Colony count   : 24 single colonies picked per gate (GT1 and GT2)
  Glycerol stocks: Remaining emulsion pipetted into YPD broth; grow overnight;
                   add 25% glycerol (final); store at -80 C

Step 8 | Post-HTS Maltodextrin Growth Screening
  Preculture     : Colonies grown in YPD broth, 48 h at 30 C / 300 rpm
  Inoculation    : 5 uL into 1 mL maltodextrin media per well (96-well plate)
  Media          : 2 g/L yeast extract, 4 g/L bacto peptone, 20 g/L maltodextrin
  Incubation     : 30 C, 48 h; OD600 measured at 24 h and 48 h (Tecan Sunrise microplate reader)
  Metric         : Maltodextrin growth fold improvement = Mutant OD600 / Wild type OD600
  Results:
    IDY1 GT1 (high): only H2 showed significant improvement (~2.5x at 48 h)
    IDY1 GT2 (mid):  M2 ~1.4x improvement
    IDY2 GT1 (high): average 2.2x growth improvement vs WT
    IDY2 GT2 (mid):  average 1.7x growth improvement vs WT
  Notes          : IDY2 genome-shuffled populations show enhanced growth baseline vs IDY1
                   in maltodextrin due to starting phenotype advantage.

Step 9 | Enzyme Activity Measurement (parallel to maltodextrin screening)
  Preculture     : 48 h in YPD broth, 30 C, 300 rpm
  Substrate      : 4-MUG-a, 2 mM final concentration
  Protocol       : 20 uL culture + 150 uL YPD broth + 30 uL 4-MUG-a (2 mM);
                   incubate 30 C, 200 rpm; measure fluorescence every 1 h for 15 h
                   (CLARIOstar Plus, ex 360 nm / em 450 nm)
  End-point      : 96-well plate; 50 uL enzyme substrate (2 mM) + 50 uL supernatant;
                   incubate 30 C for 2 h; stop buffer pH 11; read fluorescence
  Metric         : Enzyme activity fold improvement = Mutant Activity (U/mL OD) / WT Activity (U/mL OD)
  Results:
    IDY1 GT1: ~3.7x fold improvement (average) vs WT; only H2 statistically significant (~3x)
    IDY1 GT2: ~1.2x fold improvement (average)
    IDY2 GT1: ~2x fold improvement (7 high strains showed improvement)
    IDY2 GT2: ~2x fold improvement (13 mid strains showed improvement at 24 h and 48 h)

Step 10 | Beverage Fermentation Evaluation
  Preculture     : YPD broth 48 h at 30 C, 300 rpm
  Inoculum       : 100 uL into 3 mL synthetic beverage media
  Synthetic media: 125 g/L maltose, 60 g/L maltodextrin, 1 mL ethanol,
                   1.25 mL 50% glycerol (in water), 3 mL 85% lactic acid,
                   2 g/L yeast extract, 6.4 g/L bactopeptone,
                   pH 5.9, 25 mg/mL chloramphenicol
  Vials          : 6 mL mini vials sealed with rubber caps; needles for gas exchange
  Mixing         : 180 rpm for 5 min; then without agitation
  Temperature    : Phase 1: 20 C for 22 h; Phase 2: 30 C until 72 h endpoint
  Weight loss    : Measured at 0, 18, 24, 42, 48, 66, 72 h (precision scale)
  Fermentation complete: 72 h (final mass loss point)
  Dry biomass    : Pellet cells; dry at 60 C overnight; weigh
  Metrics:
    CO2 released per mg dry biomass (mg CO2/mg yeast)
    Ethanol content normalised to dry biomass (mg ethanol/mL per mg yeast)
    Fermentation rate (mass loss rate h^-1)
  Statistical    : One-way ANOVA at 95% CI, N=3; p-values vs WT:
                   ns: p=0.1234, *: p=0.0332, **: p=0.0021, ***: p=0.0002, ****: p<0.0001
  Key results:
    IDY1-M23 (GT2/mid): highest CO2 mass loss ~7.8 mg CO2/mg biomass at 72 h
                         (vs ~5.01 mg CO2/mg biomass for WT IDY1)
                         Only IDY1 strain to show significant ethanol content improvement
    IDY2-M9  (GT2/mid): mass loss rate ~0.128 h^-1; highest CO2 and ethanol yield for IDY2
    IDY2-H13 (GT1/high): mass loss rate ~0.105 h^-1; second best for IDY2
    Top ethanol producers: IDY1-M23, IDY2-M9 (both mid-level sorted)
  Key finding    : Mid-level sorted strains outperform high-level sorted strains in fermentation.
                   Hypothesised mechanism: high-level strains incur increased metabolic burden
                   from elevated glucoamylase expression (higher ATP demand, amino acid
                   consumption for protein synthesis, diversion from fermentation).
                   Mid-level strains balance enzyme secretion with metabolic load, maintaining
                   fermentation efficiency. This is consistent with metabolic burden literature
                   in heterologous protein production.

  - Methanol/DI water (50:50 dilution solvent for HPLC injection)

STEPS:
1. Setup: Position a tissue sample and a PPM disc on a DMF device bottom plate; pipette a 25 uL droplet of lysing solvent (DCM:acetone 80:20) onto the sample and allow it to evaporate (~30 s); assemble the device with a top plate.
2. Extraction: Load 25 uL of extraction solvent (mixture B, containing deuterated internal standards) into a reservoir and drive it onto the tissue sample; actuate the droplet in a clockwise circular motion across the tissue for 5 min, then incubate statically for 10 min.
3. PPM Activation: Dispense a droplet of methanol onto the PPM disc, incubate for 5 min, then drive the remaining methanol to waste.
4. Cleanup (SPE): Drive the sample-extract droplet back and forth across the activated PPM disc for 2 min, then drive it away to a collection reservoir.
5. Repeat: Repeat the extraction (Step 2) and cleanup (Steps 3-4) cycle a total of four times, pooling the four resulting extract droplets; allow the pooled extract to dry at room temperature (~30 min).
6. Derivatization: Reconstitute the dried pooled extract in 25 uL of a 1:1 mixture of 1 mg/mL dansyl chloride in acetone and 100 mM sodium bicarbonate (pH 10.7); incubate in a 60 C water bath for 5 min.

8. Detection: Analyze by HPLC-MS/MS (electrospray ionization, positive mode, multiple reaction monitoring) using a 22 min gradient run, quantifying estradiol, androstenedione, testosterone, and progesterone from the analyte/internal-standard peak-area ratio against a calibration curve.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Synchronized Synthesis of Peptide-Based Macrocycles by Digital Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/macrocycle_synthesis.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.201001604
Journal      : Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 2010, Vol. 49, pp. 8625-8629
Platform     : Two-plate digital microfluidics (DMF) on EWOD/electrode array
Authors      : Mais J. Jebrail, Alphonsus H. C. Ng, Vishal Rai, Ryan Hili,
               Andrei K. Yudin, Aaron R. Wheeler
Affiliation  : Department of Chemistry and Institute of Biomaterials and Biomedical
               Engineering, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON M5S 3H6, Canada


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first two-plate digital microfluidic platform for parallel
multi-component, multi-step chemical synthesis. It implements synchronized on-chip
synthesis of five peptide-based macrocycles (PMs) from three components -- amino acids,
amphoteric aziridine aldehydes, and tert-butyl isocyanide (tBuNC) -- in a one-step
Ugi-type macrocyclization reaction. Products contain aziridine sites that are primed for
late-stage nucleophilic modification.

Downstream processing converts the PMs into macrocyclic peptide thioesters (ring-opened
products, ROPs) by reacting with thiobenzoic acid (PhCOSH). As a further demonstration,
a nine-membered macrocycle is synthesized from a Pro-Leu dipeptide substrate -- a ring
size associated with considerable synthetic difficulty in conventional cyclic peptide
synthesis.

The platform is fully automated, hardware-free (no pumps, tubing, or valves), compatible
with a wide range of organic solvents and corrosive chemicals, and supports critical
steps -- solvent removal and re-dissolution of solids -- that are problematic in
microchannel-based systems. Five products are formed in 30 total processing steps
(6 steps per parallel reaction), verified by ESI-MS and 1H-NMR against macroscale
reference syntheses.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate DMF
Top plate     : Transparent ITO (indium tin oxide) glass; removable for product isolation
Bottom plate  : Electrode array coated with Teflon-based hydrophobic insulator
Reservoirs    : 10 reagent supply reservoirs
Electrodes    : 88 actuation electrodes dedicated to dispensing, merging, and mixing
Droplet volume: 900 nL per unit droplet
Actuation     : Electrical potentials applied to electrode array (EWOD principle);
                discrete nL-to-uL droplets controlled in parallel with no cross-contamination
Surface       : Chemically inert Teflon; compatible with TFE, organic solvents, corrosive
                chemicals -- diversifies reagent scope beyond PDMS-based microchannel systems

Key advantages over microchannel platforms:
  - No pumps, tubing, valves, or 3D channel networks required
  - Individual reagent addressing with no complex microvalve networks
  - Supports solvent removal by evaporation and re-dissolution of solid products
  - Easy off-chip product access (remove top plate; recover by pipette)
  - Scalable: proposed future systems capable of tens to hundreds of simultaneous products


REAGENTS
--------
Amino acids (five tracks):
  Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro -- 0.1 M in deionized water; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)

Aziridine aldehyde:
  Amphoteric aziridine aldehyde -- 0.05 M in TFE; 45 nmol per droplet (900 nL)
  Role: electrophilic macrocyclization partner; aziridine ring in product is site for
  late-stage modification by nucleophilic ring-opening

tert-Butyl isocyanide (tBuNC):
  0.1 M in TFE; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)
  Role: isocyanide component of Ugi-type three-component cyclization

Thiobenzoic acid (PhCOSH):
  0.1 M in TFE; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)
  Role: nucleophile for aziridine ring-opening; yields macrocyclic peptide thioesters
  (ROPs); thioesters are precursors to native chemical ligation (S-to-N acyl transfer)

Trifluoroethanol (TFE):
  Re-dissolution solvent; 4 x 900 nL droplets (~3.5 uL) driven to each dried PM spot
  by electrode actuation before ring-opening

Pro-Leu dipeptide (nine-membered macrocycle synthesis):
  0.1 M in TFE; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)

Off-chip analysis solvents:
  MS  : 100 uL MeOH + 0.1% formic acid (ESI-MS)
  NMR : 250 uL CD3OD (1H-NMR)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Phase 1 | Peptide Macrocycle (PM) Synthesis -- Five Parallel Tracks

Step 1 | Amino Acid + Aziridine Aldehyde Merge
  Tracks    : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro (5 simultaneous reactions)
  Inputs    : AminoAcid_X (900 nL, 0.1 M, 90 nmol) + AziridineAldehyde (900 nL, 0.05 M, 45 nmol)
  Operation : Dispense from respective reservoirs; electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Duration  : 20 s (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)
  Purpose   : Imine formation between amino acid and aziridine aldehyde

Step 2 | tBuNC Addition and Macrocyclization
  Tracks    : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Inputs    : AA+AzAld merged droplet + tBuNC (900 nL, 0.1 M, 90 nmol)
  Operation : Dispense tBuNC; electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Duration  : 20 s (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)
  Purpose   : Completes three-component Ugi-type macrocyclization

Step 3 | Macrocyclization Incubation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 1 h (60 min; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Enclosure   : Parafilm-sealed Petri dish to minimize evaporation
  Kinetics    : ~70% depletion of initial reagent within 1 h by DMF;
                ~90% by macroscale; anticipated improvement with continuous rapid mixing

Step 4 | PM Isolation by TFE Evaporation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Method      : ITO top plate removed; TFE evaporated at RT (25 C) for 15 min
  Result      : Solid PM precipitates on electrode; accessible by pipette after re-dissolution
                in 100 uL MeOH/0.1% formic acid (MS) or 250 uL CD3OD (NMR)

Phase 1 QC Gate | PM Verification (BB1 -> BB2/BB3)
  Representative track : Met
  Detection module     : macrocycleQC (abstracts off-chip ESI-MS + 1H-NMR)
  Detection duration   : 30 s
  MS verification      : m/z 342 (PM-Met; Fig 4b); other PMs in Supporting Information Figs S1-S4
  NMR verification     : 1H-NMR in CD3OD; chemical shifts correlated with macroscale product
                         (Supporting Information Fig S6)
  Pass (BB2)           : macrocycleSignal > 0 -> dispose(rxnMixMet); proceed to Phase 2
  Fail (BB3)           : macrocycleSignal <= 0 -> drain(rxnMixMet)
  Join (BB4)           : dispose(macrocycleSignal); Phase 2 begins


Phase 2 | Aziridine Ring-Opening (ROP) -- Five Parallel Tracks

Step 5 | PM Re-Dissolution in TFE
  Tracks    : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Inputs    : 4 x TFE droplets (4 x 900 nL = ~3.5 uL) per dried PM spot
  Operation : Four sequential TFE dispenses chained via electrode-actuated mixing;
              combined droplet driven to dried solid spot by electrode actuation
  Purpose   : Re-dissolve solid PM for ring-opening reaction
  Notes     : Volume of TFE is not constrained (unlike microchannel platforms);
              flexibility is a key DMF advantage highlighted in Fig 3 frames 1-2

Step 6 | PhCOSH Merge and Ring-Opening Incubation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Inputs      : pmSolnX (~3.5 uL) + PhCOSH (900 nL, 0.1 M, 90 nmol)
  Operation   : Dispense PhCOSH; electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Mixing      : 20 s (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)
  Incubation  : 1 h at 25 C (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); parafilm-sealed Petri dish
  Purpose     : Nucleophilic opening of aziridine by PhCOSH yields macrocyclic
                peptide thioester at defined position

Step 7 | ROP Isolation by TFE Evaporation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Method      : TFE evaporated at RT (25 C) for 15 min (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  Result      : Precipitated macrocyclic peptide thioesters (ROPs) at defined electrode
                positions; spatially resolved on-chip

Phase 2 QC Gate | ROP Verification (BB4 -> BB5/BB6)
  Representative track : Met
  Detection module     : ringOpeningQC (abstracts off-chip ESI-MS + 1H-NMR)
  Detection duration   : 30 s
  MS verification      : m/z 150 (unreacted Met), 342 (PM-Met), 480 (ROP-Met; Fig 4c)
  NMR verification     : 1H-NMR in CD3OD; chemical shifts correlated with macroscale
                         (Supporting Information Fig S7)
  Pass (BB5)           : ringOpeningSignal > 0 -> dispose all 5 ROP droplets
  Fail (BB6)           : ringOpeningSignal <= 0 -> drain all 5 ROP droplets
  Terminal (BB7)       : dispose(ringOpeningSignal); 9-mer sub-protocol follows


Supplementary Protocol | Nine-Membered Macrocycle Synthesis (Fig 5, paper)

Step 8 | Pro-Leu Dipeptide + AziridineAldehyde + tBuNC Merge
  Substrate   : Pro-Leu dipeptide (0.1 M in TFE, 900 nL, 90 nmol)
  Inputs      : Pro-Leu dipeptide + AziridineAldehyde (900 nL, 0.05 M) + tBuNC (900 nL, 0.1 M)
  Operation   : Dispense all three components; sequential electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Mixing      : 20 s per merge (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)

Step 9 | Nine-Membered Macrocycle Incubation
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 3 h (180 min; IR: 10800.0 SECOND)

                linear tripeptide cyclization (Failli et al., Can. J. Chem. 1979, 57, 3257)

  Method      : TFE evaporated at 25 C for 15 min (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  Product     : Compound 8; ESI-MS m/z 421 (Fig 5b, paper)
  Significance: Demonstrates reaction selectivity and scope extension to larger ring sizes

                anticipated native chemical ligation applications

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Continuous-Flow Biomolecule and Cell Concentrator by Ion Concentration Polarization
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/ancham/article-pdf/83/19/7348/15036094/ac2012619.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac2012619
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2011, Vol. 83, pp. 7348-7355
Platform     : Nanofluidic PDMS microfluidic chip with Nafion nanojunction (cation-selective membrane)
               coupled to syringe pump and high-voltage DC supply


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a continuous-flow nanofluidic concentrator for charged biomolecules
and cells, operating on the principle of ion concentration polarization (ICP) at a Nafion
cation-selective nanojunction. Unlike batch-type preconcentrators that trap analytes in a
stationary plug, this system achieves a steady-state concentrated stream that can be
delivered continuously to downstream sensors or reservoirs.

The device consists of a PDMS microchannel bonded to a Nafion-patterned glass substrate.
The main channel bifurcates into a narrow concentrated channel and a wider filtered channel.
A Nafion line is patterned at 30 degrees along the concentrated channel. When a voltage is
applied across the Nafion (V+) combined with Poiseuille flow (delta-P from a syringe pump),
an ICP depletion zone forms near the nanojunction. Charged biomolecules and cells are
blocked electrostatically by this depletion zone and guided hydrodynamically into the
concentrated channel, while the filtered channel carries essentially target-free buffer.

Concentration factors from 1 to ~200 are achievable by tuning the channel geometry:
  w' = (w1+w2)/w1  (width ratio; tested: 10, 20, 50, 100)
  l' = L1/L2       (length ratio; tested: 0.3, 0.7, 2)
  r  = 1 + R1/R2   (theoretical concentration factor from hydrodynamic resistance ratio)

The protocol is divided into three experimental arms, encoded sequentially in the BioScript:
  1. Fluorescein sodium salt / rGFP continuous-flow concentration demonstration
  2. FITC-lectin polarity assay (negatively charged at pH 8.7; positively charged at pH 7.4)
  3. Red blood cell (RBC) and E. coli co-concentration demonstration


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate    : Clean glass slide; Nafion perfluorinated ion-exchange resin (20 wt%, Sigma-Aldrich)
               patterned using PDMS line mold (width 100 um, height 50 um).
PDMS layer   : Bonded to Nafion-patterned glass by plasma treatment.
               Fabricated by standard photolithography (SU-8 master) and soft lithography.

Channel dimensions (fluorescein/rGFP/cell experiments):
  Main channel width        : 200, 400, 1000, or 2000 um (varied across devices)
  Main channel height       : 15 um
  Inlet length              : 1 cm (inlet to bifurcated point)
  Concentrated channel width: 20 um (fixed; 10 um for FITC-lectin high-factor tests)
  Filtered channel width    : Determined by width ratio w' = (w1+w2)/w1

Channel dimensions (FITC-lectin experiments):
  Concentrated channel width: 10 um
  Concentrated channel height: 15 um
  Main channel width         : 200 or 500 um
  Channel lengths            : 5-10 mm (outlet reservoir location controls length)

Nafion junction angle        : 30 degrees to main channel axis
  Purpose: Generates a straight (not curved) ICP boundary along the junction,
           enabling predictable ICP boundary position and concentrated plug shape.

Voltage application:
  Inlet of main channel (0-150 V) to buffer channel (electrical ground) across Nafion junction.
  Concentrated channel and filtered channel outlets are electrically floated.
  Maximum voltage: 150 V (= 150 V/cm; ~1000x below PDMS breakdown voltage of ~25 V/um).
  Voltage/flow rate values adjusted to balance depletion force and hydrodynamic force.

Flow control:
  Syringe pump: Harvard Apparatus PHD 2200
  Flow rate range: 0-5 uL/min

COMPARISON: BATCH-TYPE vs CONTINUOUS-FLOW
------------------------------------------
Batch-type preconcentrator:
  Max factor       : ~1e6-fold (Wang et al., 2005)
  Limitation       : Low throughput; unstable after concentration stops; diffusive dispersion
                     makes plug delivery to downstream sensors difficult.

This continuous-flow system:
  Max factor       : ~200-fold (experimental)
  Advantages       : Steady-state concentrated stream maintained continuously in downstream
                     channel or reservoir; no dispersion loss; seamless sensor integration;
                     target-independent (concentration factor set only by channel geometry);
                     sample flow rate ~few uL/min without downstream limitation.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Enhancing Protease Activity Assay in Droplet-Based Microfluidics Using a Biomolecule Concentrator
Source Link  : https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3165005/pdf/nihms305699.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ja2036628
Journal      : J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2011, Vol. 133, No. 27, pp. 10368-10371
Platform     : Integrated nanofluidic ICP biomolecule concentrator + flow-focusing droplet generator (PDMS chip)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an integrated microfluidic platform that combines a nanofluidic
biomolecule concentrator based on ion concentration polarization (ICP) with a flow-focusing
microdroplet generator on a single PDMS chip. The concentrator pre-concentrates low-abundance
enzyme molecules from a diluted physiological sample into a pL-scale plug before encapsulating
them into water-in-oil droplet microreactors. This addresses two fundamental limitations of
droplet-based enzyme assays: low assay sensitivity from low-abundance analytes, and long
reaction times required to turn over sufficient substrate for detection.

The platform was validated on:
  1. beta-galactosidase (platform characterisation)
  2. Kinase MK2 (platform characterisation)
  3. Recombinant MMP-9 at 0.2-3.2 nM (primary assay; kinetics determination)
  4. MMP activity in MEF cellular supernatant -- stimulated vs. untreated conditions

Key achievements vs. conventional droplet assays:
  - ~10-fold reduction in assay reaction time
  - ~100-fold reduction in sample volume (<25 uL total for up to 10 conditions)
  - ~100-fold concentration enhancement in the ICP plug (~20-fold at encapsulation)
  - kcat/Km = 7.81e4 M^-1 s^-1 for MMP-9, consistent with plate-reader and prior literature
  - Stimulated vs. untreated MEF differentiation in 5 min (concentrated) vs. >50 min
    (unconcentrated)


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication  : PDMS chip bonded to PDMS-coated glass slide; standard soft lithography.
               Three syringe pumps (Harvard PHD2000) drive fluid flow.

Concentrator section:
  - Polymeric nanoporous ion-selective junctions flanking the main sample channel
  - Buffer side channels on either side of the junction for voltage application
  - Applied voltage: ~50 V (main channel at +50 V, buffer channels at GND)
  - Sample flow rate: 0.03 uL/min (middle channel, pressure-driven)
  - Mechanism: electrokinetic force opposes pressure-driven flow; negatively charged
    molecules accumulate at depletion boundary into a continuously growing pL-scale plug
  - Enhancement: ~100-fold in plug; reduces to ~20-fold at encapsulation due to Gaussian
    diffusion during ~200 um transport to droplet generator
  - Enhancement factor tunable by adjusting accumulation time and flow rate

Mixing zone:
  - Released plug merges 1:1 with substrate from two flanking side channels
  - Enzyme:substrate ratio controlled by balancing three aqueous stream flow rates

Droplet generator section:
  - Flow-focusing geometry; hydrophobic PDMS surfaces cause aqueous phase to lift off
    into oil and encapsulate
  - Carrier fluid: HFE7500 fluorocarbon oil at 1.0 uL/min
  - Surfactant: biocompatible perfluorinated surfactant (synthesised in-house) in oil phase
  - Droplet volume: ~40 pL; generation rate: ~2.5 kHz; monodisperse W/O emulsion
  - Gaussian plug divided into train of droplets with graded enzyme concentrations
    (0.2-3.2 nM from tail to centre) enabling parallel kinetics screening in one run

Channels:
  - Middle channel   : Sample stream (enzyme + Alexa Fluor-546 tracer)
  - Side channels    : Substrate streams (two flanking); converge at mixing zone
  - Buffer channels  : PBS flanking main channel on either side of ion-selective membrane


REAGENTS
--------
Tracer dye       : Alexa Fluor-546 phalloidin; ex 561 nm / em 572 nm
                   Co-loaded with enzyme; monitors plug in real time; intensity ratio
                   vs. enzyme-free droplet infers local enzyme concentration per droplet.
Carrier oil      : 3M Novec HFE7500 fluorocarbon oil
Surfactant       : Synthesised biocompatible perfluorinated surfactant in oil phase
Priming agent    : Pluronics F-127 (2% in PBS)
MMP buffer       : Standard MMP assay buffer
Enzyme (recomb.) : MMP-9 (recombinant); 0.2 nM in MMP buffer; screened 0.2-3.2 nM
Substrate        : FRET-based polypeptide MMP substrate; 5 uM; fluoresces upon cleavage
Cellular samples : Mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) conditioned media;
                   0.5x dilution in MMP buffer; stimulated (cytokine-treated) and untreated;
                   <25 uL total consumed across both conditions

  Volume    : <25 uL total across both conditions
  Notes     : Both conditions run in sequence on same chip platform.

  Operation : Electrokinetic trapping; same conditions as Step 4
              Modelled as heat at 25 C for 10 min in BioScript
  Output    : ~10-20x enhancement at encapsulation
  Notes     : Concentration step amplifies activity difference between stimulated and
              untreated ~10-fold relative to unconcentrated samples. Enables detection
              of biologically relevant MMP activity differences from physiological samples.

Step 10 | Cellular Assay Droplet Encapsulation
  Operation  : mix concentrated plugs with FRET substrate + carrier oil phase
  Substrate  : FRET MMP substrate (5 uM)
  Carrier    : HFE7500 + fluorocarbon surfactant
  Notes      : Same flow-focusing geometry as Step 6. Stimulated and untreated samples

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidics with Impedance Sensing for Integrated Cell Culture and Analysis
Source Link  : https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0956566312007105
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bios.2012.10.035
Journal      : Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2013, Vol. 42, pp. 314-320
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with integrated label-free impedance sensing on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first digital microfluidic system capable of impedance-based sensing
of mammalian cells, integrating cell seeding, long-term culture, and multiplexed label-free analysis
on a single DMF device. The approach repurposes the feedback-control impedance circuit already used
for high-fidelity droplet position sensing (Vsense loop) to simultaneously measure cell density
as a function of impedance -- eliminating the need for fluorescent dyes, enzymatic stripping,
fixatives, or imaging for routine cell population analysis.

Three assays are validated in sequence on the same device platform:
  1. Calibration -- impedance vs. surface density regression for three cell lines
  2. Proliferation -- 4-day growth curve monitoring by periodic impedance measurement
  3. Serum screening -- 5-plex on-chip FCS dilution series with 4-day growth readout

The system achieves approximately 1000-fold reduction in reagent use compared to commercial
multiwell-plate impedance systems (e.g. Applied Biophysics ECIS: 1.5-4 mL per assay vs.
1-10 uL per assay in DMF format). Automated media exchange without intervention enables
uninterrupted long-term culture and analysis.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : 66 electrodes on glass substrate; coated with Parylene-C dielectric + Teflon-AF
               hydrophobic layer. Electrode types: reservoir, driving, active dispensing,
               and cell-sensor (ITO, patterned). Device dimensions: 50 x 100 mm.
Top plate    : ITO-coated glass with Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating; 6 hydrophilic cell-culture
               sites (1 mm diameter, exposed ITO) patterned for cell attachment and virtual
               microwell formation.

Droplet volumes:
  Unit droplet    : ~1 uL (covers area over single driving electrode)
  Virtual microwell: ~0.2 uL (sub-droplet spontaneously formed when unit droplet is translated
                     across hydrophilic ITO culture site; passive dispensing, S1-S3 program)

Reagent exchange (E1-E3 program): three-droplet sequential wash sequence replaces virtual
microwell contents (e.g. cell media -> sucrose buffer) without disturbing the adherent cell
monolayer on the hydrophilic ITO surface.

Feedback control: Vsense loop (Fig S1) repeatedly measures droplet impedance to enable
high-fidelity automated droplet movement (104 movements per full protocol run).
Same hardware repurposed for cell density measurement by detecting Vsense as a function
of cell surface density in low-conductivity sucrose medium.


IMPEDANCE SENSING SYSTEM
-------------------------

Title        : Integrating Machine Learning and Digital Microfluidics for Screening Experimental Conditions
Source Link  : https://rscj.silverchair-cdn.com/rscj/content_public/journal/lc/23/1/10.1039_d2lc00764a/2/d2lc00764a.pdf

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a new method for assay optimization on a digital microfluidic (DMF) device,
combining one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experimental design with machine learning (ML) predictive
modeling to optimize the synthesis yield of [18F]FDG (fluorodeoxyglucose) radiotracers. The method
is demonstrated on a seven-parameter radiosynthesis assay and is generalizable to any biological or
chemical assay on DMF that involves many parameters and levels.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Base-case [18F]FDG synthesis to establish the reference fluorination efficiency (61.27%)
  2. OFAT variable experiments: seven synthesis runs each changing exactly one parameter,
     compared against the base by one-tailed one-sample t-test (P < 0.05 significance cutoff)
  3. ML modeling: linear regression (Ridge) and neural network (Keras) trained on a 55-experiment
     database to predict optimal conditions and generate a predictive model for synthesis yield
  4. On-chip neutral alumina disc purification of the optimized [18F]FDG product (~93% purity)

The OFAT approach reduced the required experiment count from 3^7 = 2187 (full factorial, no
replicates) to 8 experiments (1 base + 7 variable; 24 with 3 biological replicates). The OFAT
optimal fluorination efficiency was 70.82 +/- 1.54% (n=6). ML modeling further improved the
total crude radiochemical yield to 79.13% (vs 66.64% from OFAT alone), with a synthesis time
of ~19 +/- 2 min.

--------------------------
Database     : 55 experiments; initial conditions from literature (Keng 2012, Chen 2014),

Split        : 80% training (44 experiments), 20% test (11 experiments).
Normalization: Standardization (subtract mean, divide by SD, eqn (1) in paper).
Oversampling : Rare-condition datapoints (those with at least one infrequent parameter level)
               replicated in training set to balance distribution and reduce model bias

Models:
  (i)  Single-input linear (7 models, one per parameter):
       RMSE train range: 13.89 +/- 1.1 to 15.53 +/- 1.3.
       Does not capture parameter interactions; insufficient for prediction.

  (ii) Multiple-input linear regression (Ridge, scikit-learn):
       All 7 variables as inputs. RMSE train: 11.47 +/- 1.0; RMSE test: 11.71.
       Regularization: L2 (Ridge); optimum regularization factor via GridSearchCV.

        Architecture: input (7 neurons) -> hidden dense layer (4 neurons, ReLU, L2 reg) ->
        output (1 node; predicted FDG incorporation yield).
        RMSE train: 11.54 +/- 1.2; RMSE test: 13.26.
        Similar accuracy to linear model (limited by N=55 database size).
        Adam optimizer; learning rate 1; regularization factor 0.5; GridSearchCV tuned.

OVERVIEW
--------
Sprox-seq (Spatial Proximity Sequencing) is a multi-omic method that simultaneously profiles
three molecular modalities from intact tissue sections on a single 10x Visium slide:
  (1) mRNA transcriptome  -- poly(A) capture on spatial barcodes; standard Visium readout
  (2) Surface protein abundance -- PLA UMI counts from Probe A + Probe B per target protein
  (3) Protein complexes (interactome) -- proximity ligation products between co-localised
      protein pairs within 50-70 nm; quantified by Fisher's Exact Test + fractional overlap

The method combines a 32-plex antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) cocktail with the
standard 10x Visium library preparation workflow, modified at two key steps: (i) Probe B
carries 6 terminal UTP residues cleaved by USER enzyme post-ligation to expose a poly(A)
tail, enabling co-capture of PLA products alongside mRNA; (ii) a U-Fwd primer is added
during reverse transcription and second-strand synthesis to enhance PLA amplification.

The method was applied to fresh-frozen human palatine tonsil tissue sections from two donors
(three biological replicates: samples A1, B1 from donor 1; D1 from donor 2), revealing:
  - Spatial maps of 32 proteins, 528 pairwise interactions, and thousands of mRNAs per section
  - Protein interaction network complexity positively associated with B cell maturation state
  - A protein-interaction-based B cell developmental trajectory (Non-GC follicles -> Dark zone
    -> Light zone) distinct from that inferred by RNA expression alone
  - Direct in situ capture of VLA-4 (ITGA4-CD29) -- VCAM1 mediated B cell-FDC interactions
    enriched in the Light zone of Germinal Centers across all three biological replicates

The BioScript file encodes sample A1 (representative replicate). Samples B1 and D1
follow an identical workflow and should be encoded as separate .bs files.

PROTOCOL: triDrop Digital Microfluidic Electroporation for CAR-T Cell Therapy
================================================================================

SOURCE LINK : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_07554e20c82e469c9608111c6af47aa0.pdf
PAPER DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.4c06911
JOURNAL     : Analytical Chemistry, 2025, Vol. 97, pp. 11026-11034
PLATFORM    : Digital Microfluidic (DMF) -- triDrop system
TARGET CELL : Primary Human T Cells
APPLICATION : CAR-T cell therapy production and functional immune cell engineering

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The triDrop system is a three-droplet digital microfluidic electroporation
platform designed to transfect primary human T cells while minimizing cellular
harm. It achieves:

  - Transfection efficiency : >95% (mRNA delivery)
  - Cell viability (18h)    : 80-85% post-EP (vs ~65% for Neon/Nucleofector)
  - Payload requirement     : 50 ng mRNA per reaction (10x less than Nucleofector)
  - Cell input              : 0.5 x 10^5 cells per reaction
  - Cost reduction          : up to 20-fold vs gold standard methods
  - CAR-T killing efficacy  : up to 2-fold improvement vs conventional EP systems
  - Gene dysregulation      : only 32 genes dysregulated (vs 105 Neon, 89 NF)

The key advantage of triDrop is its three-droplet geometry: a cell+payload
droplet is flanked by buffer droplets, physically separating cells from the
anode and cathode. This limits exposure to Joule heating, pH changes, metal
ion contamination, and electrolytic byproducts that cause cell death and
transcriptomic dysregulation in conventional EP systems.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ID                    DESCRIPTION                         QUANTITY / SPEC
  --------------------  ----------------------------------  ----------------------
  tCells                Primary human T cells               0.5 x 10^5 per rxn
  electroporationBuffer Electroporation buffer              1 unit per rxn
  mrnaPayload           mRNA payload                        50 ng per rxn
                        (alt: Cas9 RNP for CRISPR KO/KI)  (alt: 2.5 pmol RNP)
                        (alt: CAR construct for CAR-T)
  recoveryBuffer        Recovery buffer                     1 unit per rxn
  il2Media              Culture media with IL-2             400 IU/mL; 1 unit
  rajiCells             Raji cells (CD19-positive target)   1 unit per rxn
  mcf7Cells             MCF-7 cells (CD19-negative ctrl)    1 unit per rxn

  NOTE: T cells must be electroporated within 24h after removal of activation
  beads. Cells must remain in EP buffer for no more than 15 min before
  transfer to recovery buffer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  electroporationAssay  : Handles the electroporation procedure on DMF chip
  cytokineDetection     : Handles IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha ELISA detection

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Pulse count    : 3 pulses
  Voltage        : 1600 V_DC
  Pulse duration : 10 ms each                [FIX: was incorrectly 10s in old file]
  Temperature    : 37 degrees C

  NOTE: These parameters correspond to Neon-equivalent settings used in the

    cellPayloadMix = mix cellsInBuffer with payloadDrop for 5s
    triDropMerged  = mix cellPayloadMix with bufferFlank for 3s
  Notes:

    - It physically separates the cell+payload volume from electrode surfaces
    - Limits Joule heating and electrolytic byproduct (pH, metal ions, gas
