PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Magnetic Separation for Particle-Based Immunoassays
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/estrogen%20and%20TSH%20immunoassay.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac3020627
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2012, Vol. 84, pp. 8805-8812
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF), air-matrix (oil-free), EWOD electrode array with movable permanent magnet


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first particle-based immunoassay implemented on digital microfluidics
(DMF) without the aid of an oil carrier fluid (i.e., droplets surrounded by air). The air-matrix
format enabled a novel on-chip magnetic particle separation and resuspension method -- the
"supernatant separation" method -- capable of removing greater than 90% of unbound reagents in
a single step. Using this approach, two immunoassays were developed:

  1. Competitive immunoassay for 17beta-estradiol (E2), a small-molecule steroid (272.38 Da).
     This is the first competitive immunoassay implemented on any DMF platform.
  2. Noncompetitive (sandwich) immunoassay for Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), the most
     commonly performed immunoassay in clinical laboratories.

Compared to conventional well-plate ELISA:
  - 100-fold reduction in reagent volume (11.2 uL vs. 1.2 mL total per assay)
  - 10-fold reduction in analysis time (6 min sample incubation vs. 60 min)
  - Analytical performance retained at a level suitable for clinical screening

The technique has potential for use in fast, low-waste, inexpensive instruments for quantitative
analysis of proteins and small molecules in low sample volumes.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Actuation electrodes : 96
Reservoirs           : 10
Assay regions        : 4 (independent assays per device)
Detection region     : 1 (shared; electrodes rinsed with H2O2 between assays)
Unit droplet volume  : ~800 nL
Droplet environment  : Air (no oil carrier fluid; Pluronic L64 enables oil-free actuation)

Magnet system:
  - Neodymium permanent magnet, N48 grade, 5/8 in diameter x 1/4 in thick, 15.3 lb pull force
  - Positioned in Stripwell microplate manifold (selected wells removed as guides) below device
  - Controlled manually via metal clip; horizontal movement adjusts magnetic force on particles
  - Estimated magnetic force on particle pellet: ~470 uN
  - Minimum particle density for supernatant separation: ~3.0 x 10^8 particles/mL

Detection instrument:
  - Pherastar plate reader (BMG Labtech, Cary, NC)
  - Module: LUM (chemiluminescence); Gain: 3600; Focal height: 8.6 mm
  - Device affixed with tape to empty 96-well Stripwell plate; each droplet aligned to a well
  - Endpoint: 1 min (chemiluminescence signal saturates at 1 min)


IMMUNOASSAY MODES
-----------------
Competitive (E2):
  Exogenous E2-HRP conjugate (labeled antigen) competes with unlabeled E2 in sample for
  binding sites on anti-E2 capture antibodies immobilised on paramagnetic particle surfaces.
  Signal (chemiluminescence, RLU) is INVERSELY proportional to E2 concentration.
  Calibration: 10-1000 pg/mL. Curve fit: 4-parameter logistic equation.

Noncompetitive / Sandwich (TSH):
  Anti-TSH-HRP detection antibody and anti-beta-TSH capture antibody bind TSH at different
  epitopes, forming an antibody-antigen-antibody sandwich complex on the particle surface.
  Signal (chemiluminescence, RLU) is DIRECTLY proportional to TSH concentration.
  Calibration: 0.4-20 uIU/mL. Curve fit: linear equation.


REAGENTS
--------
Fouling mitigation:
  Pluronic L64 (BASF Corp., Germany), donated by Brenntag Canada, at 0.05% (v/v) in all
  solutions. Enables oil-free droplet actuation. Not found to interfere with specific binding
  in well-plate or DMF immunoassays. Custom DMF-compatible particle diluent, conjugate diluent,
  and wash buffer formulated with L64 as sole surfactant (ARCHITECT native surfactants
  cross-reacted with added L64 and prevented reliable droplet movement).

TSH-specific blocking:
  TSH paramagnetic particles blocked with nonfat dried milk prior to use. Required because
  initial TSH immunoassay experiments showed high background noise (nonspecific adsorption of
  anti-TSH-HRP on particle surfaces) preventing differentiation between 0 and 0.4 uIU/mL.
  Blocking significantly reduced background without affecting droplet actuation.

E2 conjugate optimisation:
  E2-HRP (E2 antigen labeled with HRP) at 1 ug/mL optimal concentration. At higher
  concentrations the dynamic range collapses: 50 pg/mL and 500 pg/mL produce similar signals.

Substrates:
  H2O2 (oxidising co-substrate for HRP) + luminol/enhancer solution. Mixed on-chip immediately
  before measurement. Two H2O2 pre-rinse cycles remove residual wash buffer before substrate
  delivery, preventing interference with the chemiluminescent reaction.

ELISA kits:
  Calbiotech (Spring Valley, CA) E2 and TSH kits for well-plate comparison experiments and
  wash-test TMB assays.


WASHING METHODS
---------------

Serial dilution (prior art; NOT used in this protocol):
  Particles immobilised by magnet. Droplet diluted by merging with wash buffer droplet.
  DMF splits pooled droplet; excess removed. Repeated until sufficient dilution.
  Requires >=6 washes (1:1 wash/initial ratio) for 98% unbound reagent removal.
  Drawbacks: slow dilution over many cycles; magnet immobilises particles throughout,
  trapping unbound material between particles.

Supernatant separation (THIS PROTOCOL):
  Magnet focuses particles into pellet on device surface. Supernatant droplet actuated
  away to waste with magnet in place. Magnet removed. Fresh droplet passed over pellet
  and shuttled in circular motion across 4 electrodes to resuspend.
  Achieves 98% unbound reagent removal within 2 wash cycles.
  Requirements:
    (1) Sufficient magnetic force: pellet force (~470 uN) must exceed interfacial force
        pulling particles into droplet. Satisfied for pellets of >=3.0x10^8 particles/mL.
    (2) Adjustable magnetic force: magnet moved horizontally for resuspension.
    (3) Stable particle suspension: ~5% residual liquid retained; particles resuspended
        immediately to prevent aggregation or drying.
  Not compatible with oil-immersed DMF devices.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Particle Separation from Diluent
  Operation  : Dispense 1 unit (800 nL) antibody-coated paramagnetic particle suspension.
               Pluronic L64 pre-mixed to 0.05% (v/v).
  Magnet     : Positioned to immobilise particles as pellet; diluent supernatant actuated to waste.
  Notes      : ~5% residual liquid retained by hydrophilic particles in pellet.
               Performed identically for both E2 and TSH assays (different particles dispensed).

Step 2 | Sample Incubation (3 unit droplets, 6 min)
  Operation  : Three 800 nL sample droplets (2.4 uL total) sequentially dispensed and
               delivered to particle pellet for resuspension and incubation.
  Duration   : 6 min (sufficient to saturate analyte binding; droplets show <5% volume loss
               at >=30 min, so evaporation is not a concern at 6 min).
  E2 (competitive)      : Unlabeled E2 competes for anti-E2 binding sites on particle surface.
  TSH (noncompetitive)  : TSH antigen captured by anti-beta-TSH antibody on particle surface.
  Notes      : 3 unit droplets chosen to improve signal over 1 droplet while remaining
               easily manipulated by DMF (volumes much larger than 1 unit are less reliable).

Step 3 | Post-Sample Wash x4 (Supernatant Separation)
  Operation  : 4 supernatant separation wash cycles with 800 nL wash buffer each.
               Each cycle: magnet immobilises pellet; supernatant to waste; fresh wash buffer
               reconstitutes particles via 4-electrode circular motion.
  Purpose    : Removes unbound sample matrix, excess analyte, and nonspecifically bound proteins.

Step 4 | Conjugate Incubation (2 min)
  Operation  : 1 unit (800 nL) conjugate droplet delivered to washed particles for
               resuspension and incubation.
  Duration   : 2 min
  E2         : E2-HRP (1 ug/mL) competes with sample E2 for remaining anti-E2 binding sites.
  TSH        : Anti-TSH-HRP detection antibody binds TSH at a second epitope, completing
               the antibody-antigen-antibody sandwich complex on the particle.

Step 5 | Post-Conjugate Wash x4 (Supernatant Separation)
  Operation  : 4 supernatant separation wash cycles (same as Step 3).
  Purpose    : Removes unbound HRP-labeled conjugate.

Step 6 | H2O2 Pre-Rinse x2 (Supernatant Separation)
  Operation  : 2 supernatant separation wash cycles with 800 nL H2O2 each.
  Purpose    : Removes residual wash buffer prior to substrate delivery. Prevents dilution
               or quenching of the H2O2/luminol chemiluminescent reaction.
               Replaces manufacturer-recommended H2O2/luminol pre-mix, which caused
               high inter-assay variability.

Step 7 | H2O2 Substrate Incubation (2 min)
  Operation  : Particles delivered to shared detection region. 1 unit (800 nL) H2O2 droplet
               reconstitutes particle pellet and incubates for 2 min.
  Purpose    : H2O2 serves as the oxidising co-substrate for HRP enzyme activity.
  Notes      : Detection region pre-rinsed with H2O2 between successive assays.

Step 8 | Chemiluminescence Activation and Detection
  Operation  : 1 unit (800 nL) luminol/enhancer droplet merged on-chip with the
               H2O2/particle droplet. Incubated 1 min (signal saturates at 1 min endpoint).
  Detection  : Pherastar plate reader, LUM module, gain=3600, focal height=8.6 mm.
               Device taped to empty 96-well Stripwell plate, detection zone per-well aligned.
  E2 signal  : Inversely proportional to E2 concentration (competitive assay).
  TSH signal : Directly proportional to TSH concentration (noncompetitive assay).
  QC gate    : Signal > 0 -> dispose assay droplet (pass). Signal <= 0 -> drain (fail).

-----------

  Dynamic range     : ~2 orders of magnitude

  Sample       : 2.4 uL vs. 50 uL    (E2) / 25 uL (E2) well-plate

3. Equilibration: Dispense a fresh 5 uL droplet of equilibration solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 1 min, then actuate the droplet away to waste.
4. Sample Loading: Dispense a 1 uL sample droplet, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 2 min (optimized loading time), then actuate the droplet away to waste.
5. Monolith Washing: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of wash solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to waste; repeat this wash cycle a second time (2 x 5 uL total).
6. Elution: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of elution solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to a collection spot; repeat this elution cycle a second time so that two eluate droplets are pooled (optimized elution volume).

This protocol describes a just-in-time solvent replenishment strategy for managing droplet evaporation

edge of the thermal zone and pre-heated for 5 s before merging, minimising the temperature perturbation

automated concentration or volume sensing with feedback control).

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform for Chemiluminescent Detection of Rubella Virus (RV) IgG and IgM by Indirect ELISA

REAGENTS USED:
  - RV-Coated Paramagnetic Particle Suspension (virus-immobilized magnetic microparticles for antigen capture, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - Patient Sample (serum or plasma, pre-diluted, containing RV IgG and/or RV IgM, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (1.8 uL droplets, used in 4x wash cycles after each binding step)
  - HRP-Conjugated Goat Anti-Human IgG (detection conjugate for the RV IgG assay, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - HRP-Conjugated Goat Anti-Human IgM (detection conjugate for the RV IgM assay, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - Goat Anti-Human IgG Pretreatment Reagent (blocks endogenous RV IgG/rheumatoid-factor IgM interference before the IgM assay, 0.9 uL droplets)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide, H2O2 (chemiluminescent substrate component, 0.9 uL droplets)
  - Luminol-Enhancer Solution (chemiluminescent substrate component, 0.9 uL droplets)

STEPS:

RV IgG Immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA):
1. Dispense a droplet of RV-coated paramagnetic particle suspension (1.8 uL) and separate the particles from the storage diluent.
2. Dispense a sample droplet (1.8 uL), deliver it to the particles, mix for 3 min, then magnetically separate particles from the supernatant.
3. Wash the particles in 4 successive 1.8 uL wash-buffer droplets, mixing and then separating from the supernatant each time.
4. Dispense a droplet of HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG (1.8 uL), deliver to the particles, and mix for 2 min.
5. Repeat the 4x wash cycle from step 3.
6. Dispense one droplet each of H2O2 (0.9 uL) and luminol-enhancer solution (0.9 uL), merge them with the particles, and mix for 2 min.
7. Measure the mean chemiluminescent signal over 10 s with the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT).

RV IgM Immunoassay (identical 7-step assay, preceded by an IgG-blocking pretreatment):
0. Pretreatment: Mix a 1.8 uL sample droplet with a 0.9 uL droplet of goat anti-human IgG pretreatment reagent for 7 min to block endogenous RV IgG and rheumatoid-factor IgM before analysis.
1-7. Repeat the same capture -> 4x wash -> conjugate (HRP-anti-human IgM in place of anti-IgG) -> 4x wash -> substrate -> PMT-detect sequence described above.

INTERPRETATION: Results are reported as a signal-to-cutoff (s/co) ratio, calculated by normalizing the mean chemiluminescent signal of each assay to the mean signal of the corresponding cutoff control (a 10 IU/mL RV IgG calibrator for the IgG assay; the RV IgM cutoff Cal 1 reagent for the IgM assay). An s/co >= 1 is interpreted as positive; an s/co in the gray zone (0.69-0.99 for IgG, 0.75-0.99 for IgM) is interpreted as equivocal; an s/co below the gray zone is interpreted as negative. Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of 100%/100% for both RV IgG and RV IgM were obtained against a commercial mixed-titer performance panel referenced against an Abbott EIA platform, supporting use of the method as a portable, decentralized alternative to central-laboratory rubella serology for identifying pregnant women at risk of transmitting rubella to their offspring.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic qPCR Cartridge Protocol for Viral Detection (SARS-CoV-2)

REAGENTS USED:
  - cDNA template of the SARS-CoV-2 N gene (SARS-CoV-2 RUO plasmid control, ten-fold serial dilutions from 10,000 to 1 copy/uL)
  - N1 primer-probe mix (U.S. CDC-referenced, IDT)
  - N2 primer-probe mix (U.S. CDC-referenced, IDT)
  - RNase P (RP) primer-probe mix (human internal control gene)
  - TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix (2X, Applied Biosystems)
  - Nuclease-free water (diluent, and NTC substitute for template)
  - Positive control template
  - Hexadecane (environmental oil filling the cartridge to prevent droplet evaporation and reduce friction)
  - Tween-20 surfactant (0.1% final concentration in aqueous reagents, reduces surface tension/biofouling)

STEPS:
1. Reaction assembly: On the DMF cartridge, generate a 1.5 uL droplet-scale reaction for each of five parallel tracks/reservoirs (N1, N2, RP, positive control, NTC) by combining 1 uL cDNA template (or nuclease-free water for the NTC), 1.5 uL primer-probe mix, 10 uL TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix, and 7.5 uL nuclease-free water (20 uL bulk reaction mix, scaled down on-chip).
2. Enzyme activation: Heat each reaction droplet at 95 C for 2 min (1 cycle) to activate the polymerase.
3. Thermal cycling (40 cycles): For each cycle, denature at 95 C for 1 s, then anneal/extend at 60 C for 20 s, with droplets electrowetting-actuated between the two on-chip temperature zones (~1.75 C/s ramp rate, ~42 min total for 40 cycles).
4. Real-time fluorescence detection: After every thermal cycle, capture the FAM fluorescence intensity of each droplet using the optical module (camera, fluorescence filter cube, LED) to build real-time amplification curves.
5. Data analysis / dispose: Subtract baseline intensity to obtain delta fluorescence intensity (dFI), determine threshold cycle (Ct) values via LinRegPCR, and evaluate qPCR efficiency from the Ct-vs-log(concentration) standard curve; discard analyzed droplets once data collection is complete.

INTERPRETATION: Successful SARS-CoV-2 N gene detection is confirmed by sigmoidal amplification curves resembling standard benchtop qPCR, a limit of detection down to 10 copies/uL (15 copies/droplet) for both N1 and N2 target regions, and standard-curve qPCR efficiencies within the acceptable 90-110% range (92.8% for N1, 101.2% for N2), supporting use of the DMF cartridge as a point-of-care NAAT platform for COVID-19 diagnosis.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : On-chip Integration of Droplet Microfluidics and Nanostructure-Initiator
               Mass Spectrometry for Enzyme Screening
Source Link  : https://ipo.lbl.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2017/05/2016-049_pub.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c6lc01182a
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2016 (Royal Society of Chemistry)
Authors      : Joshua Heinemann, Kai Deng, Steve C. C. Shih, Jian Gao, Paul D. Adams,
               Anup K. Singh, Trent R. Northen
Platform     : uNIMS (digital droplet microfluidics + NIMS array, EWOD-actuated)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the uNIMS platform -- a first-of-its-kind integration of droplet
microfluidics with nanostructure-initiator mass spectrometry (NIMS) for label-free,
time-resolved enzyme kinetics screening at the 150 nL droplet scale. The system couples
a digital microfluidics (DMF) chip (electrowetting-on-dielectric, EWOD) with a patterned
silicon NIMS array (640 pads, 5x5 cm wafer), enabling programmable droplet deposition
onto discrete NIMS elements for subsequent mass spectrometry (MS) imaging.

The protocol is divided into two functional parts:
  PART 1: Dextromethorphan (DXM) standard validation -- confirms droplet actuation
          onto NIMS pads and analyte sorption at m/z 272.
  PART 2: CelE-CBM3a enzyme kinetics -- two independent pH conditions:
    2A: pH 6.0 (phosphate buffer, 50 mM) -- parallel droplet loading, 5 time points
        (10, 20, 30, 40, 50 min), G4 substrate degraded to G3, G2, G1.
    2B: pH 5.0 (acetate buffer, 100 mM) -- continuous series loading, 3 time points
        (10, 20, 40 min), similar product distribution to pH 6 demonstrating CelE
        robustness to process conditions.

Key advantages over conventional NIMS screening:
  - 150 nL droplets vs 20 uL dead volume from 384-well acoustic printing (~133x reagent
    reduction)
  - Programmable time resolution for kinetics (droplets deposited and removed at defined
    intervals via EWOD)
  - Fluorous probe and products remain adsorbed on NIMS surface after droplet removal,
    enabling off-line MS imaging
  - Scalable: demonstrated 20 assays per NIMS array; protocol modification enables 620
    individual assays (1 pad per enzyme); theoretical maximum >100,000 pads per 5 cm2
    at 50 um grid resolution


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
The uNIMS stack consists of five layers held together in a 3D-printed chassis:

Layer i   : 3D-printed PLA top cover (Ultimaker 2, 215 C, Blender.org design)
Layer ii  : PDMS mounting gasket for PEEK tubing interfacing (upper gasket)
Layer iii : DMF chip -- glass substrate; 128 chrome electrodes (5 cm L x 500 um W x
            375 um H); 5 um SU-8-5 dielectric; PDMS fluidics channel (500 um W x 225 um H);
            31 digital arrayers for droplet actuation over NIMS pads;
            1 T-junction for pressure-driven droplet generation (~150 nL droplets)
Layer iv  : NIMS array chip -- 5 x 5 cm silicon wafer; 640 patterned NIMS pads
            (photopatternable PDMS protective gasket, laser-cut wafer, ICP-RIE etching)
Layer v   : 3D-printed PETG bottom piece with Dropbot PCB adapter (pogo pins)

Seal      : Reversible PDMS compression seal between DMF chip (layer iii) and NIMS array
            (layer iv) -- allows NIMS array removal and mounting in mass spectrometer
            after experiment, without disturbing adsorbed analytes.

DMF chip fabrication:
  - Photolithography on chrome Telic wafers (AZ1500 positive resist, OAI Series 200 aligner,
    16 mW/cm2, 15 s exposure; MF-321 developer ~1 min)
  - Chrome etch: CR-4 chromium etchant, 5 min agitation
  - Post-bake: 120 C, 10 min
  - Plasma treatment: 20% O2, 20 W RF, 5 min
  - Dielectric: 5 um SU-8-5 (Microchem protocol)
  - Channel layer: SU-8-2075 master mold (140 um height); PDMS (20:1, cured 100 C 1 h);
    sealed against glass slide with 100 uL Picoglide, rinsed with Novec HFE-7500

NIMS array fabrication:
  - Photopatternable PDMS (10:1 ratio, 3% benzophenone, degassed by centrifugation)
  - Spin-coat on silicon wafer: 2500 rpm, 30 s
  - UV exposure: <365 nm, 10 min; photomask ~100 um above substrate
  - Post-exposure bake: 120 C, 2.5 min (vacuum oven)
  - Development: toluene, 10 s; rinse IPA and H2O
  - ICP-RIE etching (PlasmaLab 100, Oxford Instrument):
      Gas: SF6/O2 at 30/20 ratio; pressure: 6 mTorr; temperature: -80 C (cryogenic)
      Etching chamber power: 5 W; plasma generator power: 1000 W
  - Result: silicon nanostructures for NIMS-based laser desorption/ionisation

Dropbot control:
  - Hold voltage: 20 V (maintains droplet position during flow halt)
  - Actuation: 90 V, 10 kHz, 250 ms bursts (moves droplets in/out of NIMS pad pockets)
  - Impedance detection: used to detect actuation failure
  - Software: Dropbot + microdrop GUI; monitoring and validation visual (limitation noted)


REAGENTS
--------

Carrier oil      : Novec HFE-7500 (3M, US); 100 uL Picoglide (Dolomite Microfluidics, UK)
                   pumped through channel for 30 min for surface preparation.
                   Flow rates: 0.05 uL/s reaction cocktail, 0.2 uL/s HFE-7500 oil.

Enzyme           : CelE-CBM3a (CelE); chimeric endoglucanase; GH family 5 (GH5) domain
                   from Clostridium thermocellum (Cthe_0797) fused to carbohydrate binding
                   module CBM3a. Deconstructs plant hemicellulose via beta-1,4 glycosidic
                   bond cleavage. Concentration: 240 ug/mL. (Ref: Deng et al., ACS Chem.
                   Biol. 2014, 9(7), 1470-1479)

Substrate probe  : 1,4-beta-D-cellotetraose-probe (G4). Fluorous-tagged (perfluorocarbon)
                   for NIMS surface affinity. MW 1515.48; formula C55H78F17N5O24.
                   Detected at m/z 1516.43 (H+). Volume: 1 uL per reaction.

Degradation      :
products           G3 (cellotriose-probe)  -- MW 1353.42; C49H68F17N5O19; m/z 1354.37 (H+)
                   G2 (cellobiose-probe)   -- MW 1191.37; C43H58F17N5O14; m/z 1192.32 (H+)
                   G1 (glucose-probe)      -- MW 1029.32; C37H48F17N5O9;  m/z 1030.28 (H+)

Buffers          : pH 6: Phosphate buffer, 50 mM, pH 6.0 (4 uL per 6 uL reaction)
                   pH 5: Acetate buffer, 100 mM, pH 5.0 (4 uL per 6 uL reaction)

Validation std   : Dextromethorphan (DXM); 1 mg/mL in H2O; detected at m/z 272 (H+);
                   matrix-free ionisation; no signal on non-NIMS surrounding structures.

MALDI matrix     : Universal MALDI matrix; 20 mg/mL in MeOH; applied to NIMS array after
                   removal from uNIMS system prior to MS imaging.

General reagents : SU-8-5, SU-8-2075, SU-8 Developer (Microchem, Newton, MA); gold and
                   chromium-coated glass slides (Telic, Valencia, CA); ITO-coated glass slides
                   and silicon wafers (Delta Technologies, Stillwater, MN); Aquapel (TCP Global,
                   San Diego, CA); MF-321 developer (Rohm and Haas); CR-4 chromium etchant
                   (OM Group); AZ-300 T photoresist stripper (AZ Electronic Materials);
                   Sylgard 184 PDMS (Dow Corning); benzophenone and mixed xylenes (Sigma);
                   TPS (Trichloro(1H,1H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane) for master mold silanisation.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

-- PART 1: DXM STANDARD VALIDATION --

Step 1 | Device Surface Preparation and Oil Phase Loading
  Reagent  : Novec HFE-7500 (with 100 uL Picoglide surfactant)
  Operation: Dispense oilPhase; pump through PDMS channel for 30 min
  Purpose  : Coats channel surfaces; stabilises droplets at T-junction; enables EWOD
             actuation; primes reversible PDMS seal interface with NIMS array.

Step 2 | Dextromethorphan Standard Preparation
  Reagent  : DXM, 1 mg/mL in H2O; 5 uL plug prefilled into syringe tubing
  Operation: Dispense dxmDroplet (1 unit = ~150 nL droplet abstraction)
  Purpose  : Validates microfluidic droplet actuation and NIMS pad analyte sorption before
             enzymatic assay. DXM detected at m/z 272 (H+); matrix-free ionisation.

Step 3 | DXM Droplet Generation at T-Junction
  Inputs   : dxmDroplet + oilPhase
  Operation: mix for 5 s (abstracts T-junction droplet generation)
  Flow rate: 0.05 uL/s reaction cocktail; 0.2 uL/s HFE-7500 oil
  Result   : ~150 nL DXM droplets in HFE-7500 oil train; synchronised with electrode
             actuation for uniform spacing along central fluidics chamber.

Step 4 | DXM Droplet Loading and Incubation on NIMS Pads
  Input    : dxmDropletInOil

Method   : Fractional conversion (internal normalisation)
Formula  : [Gx] / ([G4] + [G3] + [G2] + [G1]) for each product Gx at each time point

           (device maintains +/-10% SD in droplet size; turbulent mixing at t-junction
           causes initially larger droplets). Less sensitive to concentration measurement
           errors than direct quantification approaches.
Software : OpenMSI spot set analysis tools (Rubel et al., Anal. Chem. 2013, 85(21),
           10354-10361)

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Colorimetric enzyme test strip reaction for measuring glucose concentration in a fluid sample, run as a series of small droplet reactions on a lab-on-a-chip device.

REAGENTS USED:
  - glucose sample: the fluid being tested; five separate portions are used, one per trial, so a small calibration-style series of readings can be built up
  - enzyme reagent: a ready-mixed reagent containing glucose oxidase and peroxidase along with a color-forming dye; it reacts with glucose to produce a colored product, with more color developing as more glucose is present
  - distilled water: used in a side reaction alongside the reagent, prepared and set aside for each trial but not measured

STEPS:
1. Place a small portion of the glucose sample on the chip.
2. Add a small portion of the enzyme reagent next to it.
3. Bring the two together and mix them for about 10 seconds so the reaction can begin.
4. Hold the combined droplet in place and measure the color/light signal it gives off for 30 seconds. This reading reflects how much glucose was in the sample.
5. Separately, combine a portion of distilled water with a portion of the enzyme reagent, mix for 30 seconds, and discard it.
6. Repeat steps 1-5 four more times, for a total of five trials. In each trial the amount of glucose sample stays the same, but the amount of enzyme reagent added is changed (first a small amount, then twice as much, then twice as much again, then twice as much again, before returning to the original small amount for the fifth trial).
7. After all five trials are complete, discard the reacted droplets from each trial.

INTERPRETATION: Each of the five trials produces a signal reading whose strength corresponds to how much glucose was present in that sample. Comparing the five readings against each other (or against known glucose standards run the same way) lets a technician build a calibration curve and estimate the glucose concentration of an unknown sample. A stronger signal generally means more glucose reacted with the reagent.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The cited paper (Srinivasan, Pamula & Fair, 2004) describes an electrowetting droplet-chip glucose assay using a colorimetric enzyme-kinetic method (Trinder's reaction): a glucose oxidase/peroxidase/dye reagent droplet is merged with a sample droplet, mixed for about 15 seconds, and the color signal is read continuously for at least 30 seconds. That final step - a mix, then a 30-second optical read whose strength scales with glucose concentration - matches this .bs file's five detect steps exactly on timing (30s) and closely on mixing time (10s in the code vs. 15s in the paper).

Two things differ and are worth being upfront about:

1. In the real protocol, the five (or more) calibration points are made by varying the GLUCOSE CONCENTRATION of the sample while keeping the reagent-to-sample ratio fixed. In this .bs file, the glucose amount is held constant across all five trials and it is instead the REAGENT amount that is varied (10, 20, 40, 80, then back to 10 units). This is a different way of generating a multi-point series, and it does not exactly reproduce the paper's dilution method, though the end goal (multiple readings to compare against each other) is the same. This is a benchmark-authoring choice, not something we changed.

2. The paper explicitly states that this kinetic method "does not require a blank reading." This .bs file nonetheless prepares a water+reagent droplet in every trial and discards it without ever reading it. It does not affect the final glucose readings (it is disposed of and never feeds into any detect step), but it is an extra, scientifically unnecessary step relative to the cited source. We are documenting it rather than silently removing it, since it is part of the original benchmark code.

No structural/dependency bugs were found in this file - each of the five glucose+reagent reaction droplets is read via detect before being discarded, so every reported reading is genuinely derived from its corresponding glucose sample. The .bs file also declares a "Sample" material that is never dispensed or used anywhere in the code; this appears to be a leftover/unused declaration from the original benchmark authoring and has no effect on execution.

Overall: the reaction chemistry, the fixed 30-second read, and the multi-trial calibration-style structure all point to this being an adaptation of the Srinivasan et al. 2004 droplet glucose assay for the BioScript benchmark suite, with the two documented differences above (what is varied per trial, and the extra unread blank step).

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-based Single-cell Joint Profiling of Histone Modification and Transcriptome (Droplet Paired-Tag)
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-based-single-cell-joint-profiling-of-histo-eq2ly6kergx9/v1
Paper DOI    : https://dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2310/v1
Journal      : Research Square (Method Article preprint), 2023
Authors      : Yang Xie, Chenxu Zhu, Zhaoning Wang, Melodi Tastemel, Lei Chang, Yang Eric Li, Bing Ren
Affiliation  : Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, University of California San Diego;
               Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, La Jolla; Center for Epigenomics, UCSD
Platform     : 10x Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome (ATAC + Gene Expression) with pA-Tn5 tagmentation


OVERVIEW
--------
Droplet Paired-Tag is a rapid multiomic technique for joint single-cell profiling of histone
modifications and gene expression simultaneously at scale. The method adapts the original
combinatorial indexing-based Paired-Tag protocol by incorporating nuclei barcoding on the
commercially available 10x Chromium Single Cell Multiome platform and simplifying the library
preparation process.

Compared to conventional Paired-Tag, Droplet Paired-Tag delivers a higher signal-to-noise ratio
for histone modification data and generates joint modality data with the same efficiency as
single-modality methods such as scRNA-seq and scCUT&Tag. The protocol has been validated on
both cultured mammalian cells (mouse embryonic stem cells, mESC) and primary mouse brain tissue,
where it accurately reconstructs cell type-specific active (H3K27ac) and repressive (H3K27me3)
gene regulatory networks.

The core innovation is a bridged Protein A-Tn5 (pA-Tn5) transposome that carries 10x Genomics-
compatible adapter sequences. Nuclei are first incubated overnight with an anti-histone antibody
bound to pA-Tn5. Tagmentation is then activated by Mg2+, inserting sequencing adapters at histone-
marked genomic loci. Tagmented nuclei are loaded onto the Chromium chip, where each nucleus is
co-encapsulated with a gel bead (GEM) barcoding both the CUT&Tag DNA fragments and the nuclear
mRNA in the same droplet, enabling paired epigenomic and transcriptomic readout per cell.

The three-day protocol produces two independently sequenced libraries per sample:
  - DNA library: histone modification CUT&Tag (200-1000 bp; nucleosome ladder pattern)
  - RNA library: single-nucleus gene expression cDNA (400-500 bp peak, narrow)


DEVICE / PLATFORM
-----------------
Microfluidics : 10x Chromium Next GEM platform (ChromiumX controller)
Chip          : Chromium Next GEM Chip J Single Cell Kit (Cat#1000234)
Encapsulation : Gel-bead-in-emulsion (GEM) droplet generation; each GEM contains one nucleus
                + one gel bead; barcoded RT primer on bead captures both cDNA and tagmented DNA
Sequencing    : Illumina NextSeq 2000
  DNA library : 200-cycle kit (#20046812); cycle config 100+8+24+100
                (Read1 + Index1 + Index2 [cellular barcodes] + Read2)
  RNA library : 100-cycle kit (#20046811); cycle config 28+10+10+72
                (Read1 [cellular barcodes] + Index1 + Index2 + Read2)
Demultiplexing: cellranger-arc mkfastq (10X Genomics); downstream analysis with in-house pipeline

  OMNI Lysis Buffer : ATAC-RSB 693.75 uL + Digitonin 2% 3.75 uL + IGEPAL-CA630 10% 7.5 uL +

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

DAY 1

Step 1 | OMNI Nuclei Lysis Buffer Preparation
  Combine all components (see Reagents above) in order on ice; mix gently.
  Use immediately; do not pre-make. Keep on ice throughout.

Step 2 | Antibody + pA-Tn5 Conjugation
  Mix  : 1 ug rabbit polyclonal anti-histone antibody + 1 uL assembled pA-Tn5 (0.4 mg/mL)
         in 50 uL MED1 buffer per PCR tube.
  Incubation : Rotate 60 min at room temperature (25 C).
  IR duration: 3600.0 SECOND
  Storage : Conjugate can be stored at -20 C if not used immediately.

Step 3 | Nuclei Preparation (Cultured Cells)
  Input    : 250,000 - 1,000,000 cells
  a) Disassociate cells per culture protocol. Spin at 300 RCF / 5 min.
     Wash once with PBS; spin at 300 RCF / 5 min (4 C). [IR: 300.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  b) Resuspend in 750 uL OMNI buffer (<5 million cells/mL); sit on ice 5 min.
     [IR: mix @ 300.0 SECOND]
  c) Spin at 1,000 RCF / 10 min at 4 C. [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  d) Resuspend nuclei in 100 uL MED1 buffer. Count using cell counter.

Step 4 | Epitope Targeting (Overnight)
  Input    : 250,000 - 500,000 nuclei
  a) Aliquot nuclei into Maximum Recovery tubes. Spin at 1,000 RCF / 10 min at 4 C.
     [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  b) Resuspend in 25 uL MED1. Add conjugated antibody-pA-Tn5 (in MED1).
  c) Incubate overnight at 4 C with rotation (~12 h).
     [IR: 43200.0 SECOND @ 4 C; BioScript: 720m]


DAY 2

Step 5 | MED Buffer 2 Preparation (prepare 3 fresh working volumes)
  Prepare three independent 1 mL batches of MED2 (composition in Reagents section above).
  Instance 1 (med2BufferWash1): first MED2 wash
  Instance 2 (med2BufferWash2): second MED2 wash
  Instance 3 (med2BufferTag)  : tagmentation resuspension
  Note: Three fresh builds required; BioScript cannot re-dispense from computed variables.

Step 6 | PBS + RI Wash Buffer and 1X Nuclei Buffer Preparation
  Prepare PBS + RNase Inhibitor wash buffer and 1X Nuclei Buffer (see Reagents above).
  Use within 1 h; do not pre-make the day before.

Step 7 | Nuclei Washing (x2) and Tn5 Tagmentation
  a) Spin nuclei at 300 RCF / 10 min at 4 C. Wash with 50 uL MED2. [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  b) Repeat wash: add 50 uL MED2; spin 300 RCF / 10 min at 4 C. [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  c) Resuspend in 50 uL MED2. Add 2 uL MgCl2 (250 mM) to activate Tn5.
  d) Rotate in ThermoMixer at 550 rpm, 37 C, 60 min. [IR: 3600.0 SECOND @ 37 C]
     Note: Thaw 10X Multiome gel beads and barcoding reagents at room temperature during this step.

Step 8 | Stop Tagmentation and Post-Tagmentation Wash
  a) Add 50 uL 2X Stop Solution; mix well.
  b) Spin at 500 RCF / 6 min at 4 C. [IR: 360.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  c) Wash with PBS + RI buffer.
  d) Spin at 500 RCF / 6 min at 4 C. [IR: 360.0 SECOND @ 4 C]

Step 9 | Nuclei Resuspension and Chromium Chip Loading Preparation
  a) Resuspend in 20 uL 1X Nuclei Buffer. Count nuclei using cell counter.
  b) Aliquot 10,000-16,000 nuclei in 8 uL into PCR tube.
  c) Add 7 uL ATAC Buffer B (PN-2000193). Total volume: 15 uL.
  d) Proceed immediately to droplet generation.

Step 10 | RT Master Mix Preparation and GEM Droplet Generation
  Prepare RT master mix:
    Barcoding Reagent Mix (PN-2000267) : 49.5 uL
    Template Switch Oligo (PN-3000228) :  1.1 uL
    Reducing Agent B (PN-2000087)      :  1.9 uL
    Barcoding Enzyme Mix (PN-2000266)  :  7.5 uL
    Total                              : 60.0 uL
  Add 60 uL master mix to 15 uL nuclei mixture. Load onto Chip J.
  Proceed to droplet generation on ChromiumX per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338.
  Aspirate 100 uL emulsion into new PCR tube after generation.
  Note: `mix` in BioScript abstracts the microfluidic GEM encapsulation event.

Step 11 | Reverse Transcription and Cell Barcoding in Droplets
  Incubate emulsion in Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler (lid at 50 C):
    Stage 1 : 37 C for 45 min  -- reverse transcription (cDNA synthesis)
              [IR: 2700.0 SECOND @ 37 C]
    Stage 2 : 25 C for 30 min  -- template switching and cell barcoding
              [IR: 1800.0 SECOND @ 25 C]
    Hold    : 4 C
  Note: Both cell barcoding and cDNA synthesis complete during this incubation.

Step 12 | Quench and Products Cleanup
  a) Add 5 uL Quenching Agent (PN-2000269). Pipette mix gently.
  b) Proceed to Dynabeads + SPRI bead cleanup per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338.
     Dynabeads cleanup: 5 min mix [IR: 300.0 SECOND]
     SPRI bead cleanup: 5 min mix [IR: 300.0 SECOND]


DAY 3

Step 13 | Pre-amplification
  Protocol : Per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338 with one modification:
             Elute in 80 uL after SPRI cleanup (instead of standard 160 uL).
  Rationale: Concentrates tagmented fragments; scCUT&Tag library complexity is lower than ATAC;
             higher input increases DNA library complexity.
  Extension: 72 C / 5 min [IR: 300.0 SECOND @ 72 C]

---------------
Low nuclei yield before chip loading:

  - Check for nuclei clumping during CUT&Tag; fragile nuclei may lyse and aggregate in high-salt buffer.

Low library complexity (DNA):
  - scCUT&Tag library complexity is overall lower than snATAC-seq.
  - Increase indexing PCR cycles (13 for H3K27ac, 12 for H3K27me3 as baseline).
  - Confirm elution volume at pre-amplification step is 80 uL (not 160 uL).

Unexpected fragment size distribution:
  - Verify Tn5 activation: ensure MgCl2 was added and tagmentation ran at 37 C / 60 min.
  - Check stop solution was added immediately after tagmentation.
  - Verify antibody specificity and pA-Tn5 assembly quality.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Quantification of Proteins and mRNA in Single Mammalian Cells
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/molecular-cell/pdfExtended/S1097-2765(16)00174-X
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.molcel.2016.02.030
Journal      : Molecular Cell, 2016, Vol. 61, pp. 914-924
Platform     : Digital PLA (proximity ligation assay + droplet digital PCR) combined with
               two-step RT-ddPCR; bench-top Bio-Rad QX100 microfluidic droplet system


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a practical, commercially available workflow for the absolute and
simultaneous quantification of both protein and mRNA copy numbers from the same single
mammalian cell. The method combines proximity ligation assay (PLA) with droplet digital PCR
(ddPCR) to achieve femtomolar sensitivity for protein detection (digital PLA), and integrates
a two-step reverse transcription ddPCR (RT-ddPCR) for absolute mRNA quantification from the
same single-cell lysate.

The protocol is divided into two parallel arms operating on split lysate from one cell:
  1. Digital PLA arm (protein): proximity probes bind target protein -> connector
     oligonucleotide hybridises -> ligation forms dsDNA -> protease digestion ->
     ddPCR in 20,000 droplets -> absolute protein copy number via calibration curve.
  2. RT-ddPCR arm (mRNA): two-step GoScript RT (42 C, 60 min) -> ddPCR (40 cycles,
     60 C annealing, TaqMan Probe 2) -> mRNA copy number corrected for 87.6% RT recovery.

The joint dataset was used to construct and validate a stochastic two-state model of CD147
transcription and translation in single HEK293T cells. Key findings: CD147 mRNA and protein
are poorly correlated at the single-cell level (Spearman R = 0.10); approximately 1,000
proteins are produced per mRNA molecule; transcription occurs in bursts of ~40 mRNAs at
a rate of 3.78 bursts/day.

The entire assay uses commercially available reagents and equipment; no genetic manipulation
of host cells or custom microfluidic device fabrication is required. A single researcher can
process 100 single-cell samples in one day.


ASSAY SPECIFICATIONS
--------------------
Digital PLA:
  Target proteins   : CD147 (endogenous, HEK293T), GFP-p65 (exogenous, RAW264.7), ICAM-1
  LOD (CD147)       : 0.14 fM assay / 16.2 fM sample / 86 proteins per uL ddPCR solution
  LOD (single cell) : 29,300 CD147 molecules per cell (from 2 uL lysate fraction)
  Sensitivity       : 70 proteins per DNA count (CD147); 95 (GFP); 565 (ICAM-1)
  Dynamic range     : 2-3 orders of magnitude (linear)
  Calibration curve : CD147: y = 0.0142x + 12.4, R2 = 0.9997
                      GFP  : y = 0.0094x + 10.6, R2 = 0.9982
                      ICAM-1: y = 0.00177x + 1.30, R2 = 0.9993
  Droplets          : ~20,000 per reaction at ~0.85 nL each (limiting dilution; 0 or 1 dsDNA)
  Concentration eq. : C = (1000/Vd) * ln(1 - P/R)

RT-ddPCR:
  Target            : CD147 mRNA (NM_198589.2)
  Primer/probe      : TaqMan Gene Expression Assay Hs00174305_m1 (Probe 2; FAM/MGB)
                      Exon-exon junction spanning; excludes genomic DNA signal
  PCR cycles        : 40; fluorescence threshold 3200 RFU
  RT recovery rate  : 87.6% (validated against T7 in-vitro transcribed CD147 mRNA standard)
  LOD               : 52.5 copies/cell (87 aM); corrected for RT recovery
  Expected output   : Mean 188.2 +/- 90 CD147 mRNA copies per HEK293T cell

  University of Tokyo): primary cell line for joint CD147 protein and mRNA measurements.
  Media: high-glucose DMEM (Gibco 41965-039) + 10% FCS (Gibco 26010-066) + 100 U/mL
  penicillin G + 100 ug/mL streptomycin (Gibco 15070063).

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Single-Cell FACS Sort and Lysis
  Cell line      : HEK293T (Tlr4-GFP stable)
  Buffer         : 0.1X TM lysis buffer (3 uL per well)
  Operation      : Single viable cell sorted by FACS (R4 gate) directly into well containing
                   3 uL 0.1X TM lysis buffer; cell contacts buffer and lyses immediately.
  Duration       : 5 min mixing (BioScript abstraction: mix for 5m; IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Notes          : 0.1X TM buffer confirmed compatible with both PLA and RT-ddPCR (Fig S4G-H).
                   Cell strainer (40 um) used before loading to remove clumps. DRAQ7 excludes
                   dead cells. Tlr4-GFP expression used as sort marker.

Step 2 | Lysate Split: Protein Fraction (2 uL) and mRNA Fraction (1 uL)
  Total lysate   : 3 uL
  Protein arm    : 2 uL (2/3 of lysate) -> digital PLA workflow
  mRNA arm       : 1 uL (1/3 of lysate) -> RT-ddPCR workflow
  Notes          : Physical 1:2 ratio split; no BioScript native split operator; modelled as
                   two independent dispense+mix variables (proteinLysate, mRNALysate).
                   LOD for CD147 protein in the 2 uL fraction: 29,300 molecules/cell.

Step 3 | Proximity Probe Adsorption  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : 2 uL protein lysate + 2 uL assay probe solution (200 pM each probe final)
  Temperature    : 37 C
  Duration       : 60 min
                   (BioScript: heat at 37c for 60m; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Mechanism      : Both anti-CD147 antibody-oligonucleotide probes bind distinct epitopes on
                   the same CD147 molecule; tethered oligonucleotides come into ~40 nm
                   proximity enabling connector hybridisation in the next step.
  Notes          : Probe specificity confirmed: human CD147 probes show no signal with mouse
                   3T3 bulk lysate (Fig S3A). GFP-negative cell lysate background comparable
                   to PBS buffer (Fig S3C).

Step 4 | Connector Oligonucleotide Hybridisation and Ligation  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : Probe-bound sample + 96 uL ligation solution (25-fold dilution)
  Temperature    : 37 C
  Duration       : 10 min
                   (BioScript: heat at 37c for 10m; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Mechanism      : Connector oligonucleotide hybridises to both paired probe oligonucleotides;
                   T4 DNA ligase seals nicks; three-oligonucleotide complex becomes a dsDNA

Step 5 | Protease Digestion and Inactivation  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : Ligated sample + 2 uL diluted protease solution

Step 6 | ddPCR Droplet Generation and Amplification  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]

DOWNSTREAM ANALYSIS
-------------------

mRNA-Protein Correlation
  Method         : Spearman rank correlation
  Result         : R = 0.10 (n=131 HEK293T cells; Fig 4B)
  Interpretation : Poor single-cell correlation; bulk analyses (Pearson R = 0.41-0.59) overestimate
                   correlation due to noise averaging. mRNA abundance is a poor surrogate for
                   protein copy number in single mammalian cells.

Distribution Fitting
  Software       : R v3.1.0; fitdist / fitdistcens (fitdistrplus package; Delignette-Muller 2015)
  mRNA           : Gamma pdf fit; p=0.65 (chi-squared); bins of 40 copies/cell.
                   Inconsistent with Poisson (one-step birth-death process).
  Protein        : Gamma pdf fit; p=0.24; bins of 65,000 copies/cell.
  Conclusion     : Both distributions consistent with two-state stochastic gene expression.

Stochastic Two-State Model
  Model          : Promoter stochastically switches between Off and On states.
                   mRNA transcribed only from On state; translated into protein.
                   Six kinetic parameters (c1-c6) + extrinsic noise parameter.
  Inference      : Moment-based MCMC (Zechner et al. 2012); fitted to E[M], E[P],
                   E[M^2], E[P^2] at steady state. Five independent MCMC runs per dataset.
  Validation     : E[M(t)P(t)] (mRNA-protein covariance) computed from model parameters
                   and compared against experimentally measured correlation (not used in fit).
                   4 of 5 experimental repeats: predicted and measured E[M(t)P(t)] agree.
  mRNA half-life : 20.97 hr (from Schwanhausser et al. 2011; mouse fibroblasts)
  Protein half-life: 33.48 hr (from Schwanhausser et al. 2011)
  Parameters     : See Table S1 in paper for posterior MCMC estimates.

1. Load the CNB tissue homogenate onto the bottom plate and affix the top plate bearing the hydrophilic anchor.
2-3. Dispense a 4.8 uL methanol extraction-solvent droplet, deliver it to the CNB tissue sample, and extract by moving the droplet in a circular pattern around the tissue for 5 min.
4. Drive the sample-extract droplet away from the tissue to the hydrophilic anchor and evaporate at room temperature for 5 min.
5-6. Repeat steps 2-4 once more (second extraction/evaporation cycle onto the anchor).
7. Redissolve the dried analyte on the anchor: dispense a 4.8 uL droplet of immunoassay reconstitution buffer onto the anchor and actuate for 30 s.
8. Dispense a 1.6 uL droplet of anti-E2 paramagnetic microparticles and engage the magnet to separate the particles from the diluent.
9. Deliver the 4.8 uL reconstituted sample extract to the immobilized particles for resuspension.
10. Actively mix the particles with the sample for 6 min, then engage the magnet and drive the supernatant to waste.
11-13. Wash cycle: dispense a 1.6 uL wash-buffer droplet, deliver it to the particles, resuspend/mix for 10 s, engage the magnet, and drive the supernatant to waste; repeat this cycle a total of 4 times.
14. Dispense a 1.6 uL droplet of E2-HRP conjugate and deliver it to the immobilized particles for resuspension.
15. Actively mix for 2 min.
16-18. Repeat the wash cycle (steps 11-13) a total of 4 times.
19. Dispense a 0.8 uL droplet of H2O2 and deliver it to the immobilized particles.
20. Dispense a 0.8 uL droplet of luminol/enhancer solution and deliver it to the immobilized particles, combining with the H2O2 droplet.
21. Actively mix the combined droplet for 10 min and measure chemiluminescence using the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT); then discard the droplet.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Signaling Decouples Activation Probability and Population Heterogeneity
Source Link  : https://elifesciences.org/articles/8931
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.7554/eLife.08931
Journal      : eLife 2015, Vol. 4, Article e08931
Authors      : Ryan A Kellogg, Chengzhe Tian, Tomasz Lipniacki, Stephen R Quake, Savas Tay
Platform     : Automated microfluidic cell culture (PDMS chip, Gomez-Sjoberg et al. 2007) +
               widefield fluorescence live-cell microscopy + 96-well bulk RT-qPCR


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol studies how the NF-kB transcription factor system encodes and decodes temporal
information in inflammatory input signals. Using a combination of mathematical modeling and
microfluidic single-cell experiments, the paper demonstrates that NF-kB activates in a
digital (all-or-none) fashion in response to both LPS (pathogen signal) and TNF (host immune
signal), and that this digital switch enables two-dimensional control over population-level
and single-cell-level responses:

  1. Stimulus AREA (concentration x duration) controls the FRACTION of cells that activate
     NF-kB in the population -- the "Area Rule."
  2. Stimulus TEMPORAL PROFILE (shape: short-strong vs. long-low) controls NF-kB DYNAMICS
     and gene expression phenotype in the responding cells.

These two axes are independently tunable: a brief high-dose (SS) stimulus and a sustained
low-dose (LL) stimulus with the same area activate the same responding fraction, but produce
distinct NF-kB dynamics (rapid/uniform vs. delayed/heterogeneous) and therefore distinct
downstream gene expression profiles.

Three experimental protocols are encoded in the BioScript file in sequence:

  Protocol 1 : LPS Dose-Modulation (LL Signal, on-chip microfluidics)
  Protocol 2 : LPS Duration-Modulation (SS Signal, on-chip microfluidics)
  Protocol 3 : NF-kB-Dependent Gene Expression Assay (off-chip, 96-well RT-qPCR)


CELL LINE
---------
p65-knockout NIH 3T3 fibroblasts modified via lentiviral vectors to express:
  - p65-DsRed under the endogenous p65 promoter (NF-kB nuclear translocation reporter)
  - H2B-GFP (nuclear position reporter for cell tracking)
Clonally derived to express p65-DsRed at the lowest detectable level to preserve
near-endogenous expression. (Lee et al., 2009; Tay et al., 2010)


DEVICE AND IMAGING
------------------
Microfluidic chip: PDMS-based automated cell culture system (Gomez-Sjoberg et al. 2007;
  Kellogg et al. 2014 Nat. Protoc. 9:1713). Chamber dimensions: 1.12 mm x 0.9 mm x 0.040 mm.
  ~200 cells/chamber; all LPS doses tested in parallel on a single chip in duplicate chambers.

Microscope  : Leica DMI6000B widefield, 20x magnification
Camera      : Retiga-SRV CCD (QImaging)
Filters     : Leica L5 (GFP channel, H2B-GFP nuclear reporter)
              Leica Y3 (DsRed channel, p65-DsRed NF-kB reporter)
Light source: Leica EL6000 mercury metal halide
Imaging interval: 5-6 min over ~250 min post-stimulation

NF-kB quantification: Mean nuclear DsRed fluorescence / mean cytoplasm DsRed fluorescence.
  Cell tracking: CellProfiler + custom Matlab. Peak detection: Matlab smooth() + mspeaks().
  Peak area integration: Matlab trapz() (baseline-corrected, LPS onset to first minimum).
  Statistics: Unpaired two-sample T-test (Matlab ttest2()). Mitotic cells excluded.


MATHEMATICAL MODEL
------------------
Base model: IKK-NF-kB regulatory module from Tay et al. 2010 (Nature 466:267).
LPS extensions: TLR4 receptor species; TRAF6 activation; cooperative IKK activation
  via Hill kinetics (n=4) to model Myddosome/TRAF6 lattice clustering.
Cell-to-cell variability: TLR4 receptor number drawn from lognormal distribution
  (mu=8.0, sigma=0.8; expected 4.1e3 receptors/cell; median 3.0e3; mode 1.6e3).
Simplifications: CD14 removed (assumed in excess; LPS binds TLR4 directly).
  TLR4-TRIF-dependent branch removed (LPS.TLR4 complexes do not internalize in model).
  Only TLR4-MyD88 (early response) branch modeled.
Parameter estimation: Iterative automatic (L2-norm error on activation fractions,
  log-scale parameter sampling) + manual; 200 simulations per parameter set.
LPS concentration conversion: 1 ng/mL LPS = 2.4e4 molecules/cell
  (MW ~10 kDa; chamber volume 1.12x0.9x0.040 mm; ~100 cells/chamber).

Area Rule (Appendix 1, Equation 2): For high-dose inputs where ligand-receptor
  backward reaction is negligible:
    P([AB] >= [AB]_th) = P(B0 >= [AB]_th / (1 - exp(-k+ * S)))
  where S = integral(concentration dt) = stimulus area, B0 = receptor number (lognormal),
  k+ = forward binding rate. Fraction of activation depends ONLY on input area S.
  Caveat: at sub-threshold doses, the maximal activatable fraction saturates and
  further increases in duration cannot exceed that ceiling.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Indirect Competitive Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ci-ELISA) for Ciprofloxacin Detection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample (e.g., extracted animal tissue or fluid)
  - Primary Antibody (Monoclonal antibody against Ciprofloxacin)
  - Wash Buffer (PBST)
  - Secondary Conjugate (HRP-conjugated goat anti-mouse serum)
  - TMB Substrate
  - Stop Solution (2M H2SO4)

STEPS:
1. Primary Incubation: Add 50 units of the sample and 50 units of the primary antibody to the reaction zone. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at 37°C for 60 minutes. During this time, free ciprofloxacin in the sample competes with the immobilized plate antigen for the primary antibody.
2. First Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone three times to remove unbound ciprofloxacin and unbound primary antibody. For each wash, add 300 units of wash buffer, mix for 45 seconds, and discard the wash supernatant.
3. Secondary Incubation: Add 100 units of the secondary conjugate (enzyme-linked antibody) to the well. Mix for 60 seconds and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes to allow it to bind to the retained primary antibodies.
4. Second Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone three times with 300 units of wash buffer (mixing for 45 seconds each time) to remove any unbound secondary conjugate.
5. Substrate Development: Add 100 units of TMB substrate to the retained mixture. Mix for 60 seconds and incubate at 23°C for 10 minutes to allow the colorimetric reaction to develop.
6. Stop Reaction and Detection: Add 50 units of acid stop solution and mix for 10 seconds to halt the enzymatic reaction. Measure the resulting optical signal (absorbance) over 1 minute. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of ciprofloxacin in the sample. A lower signal indicates a higher presence of ciprofloxacin, while a higher signal indicates little to no ciprofloxacin.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Automated Digital Microfluidic Magnetic-Particle-Based Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH), DOE-Optimized Protocol

REAGENTS USED:
  - Antibody-Coated Paramagnetic Microparticles (Abbott Laboratories; ~3.0 x 10^8 particles/mL in DMF-compatible particle diluent, pH 10, 5 um diameter, magnetic susceptibility 1.05)
  - TSH Standards (0, 0.4, and 4 uIU/mL, supplemented with 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64)
  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (custom-prepared, used for post-capture and post-conjugate particle washing)
  - HRP-Conjugated Anti-TSH Detection Antibody (mouse monoclonal, 2 ug/mL working solution in conjugate diluent)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide / Stable Peroxide Substrate Component (SuperSignal ELISA Femto, supplemented with 0.025% v/v Pluronic L64)
  - Luminol-Enhancer Solution (SuperSignal ELISA Femto chemiluminescent substrate, second component)

STEPS (Optimized Immunoassay protocol, as validated against the pilot/DOE-derived parameters):
1. Particle Capture: Dispense antibody-coated paramagnetic particles from a reservoir and separate from the particle diluent using the magnetic lens; deliver five pooled sample droplets (~4 uL) of TSH standard to the immobilized particles and mix for 3 min (the DOE-optimized incubation time).
2. First Wash: Wash the particles four times in wash buffer, separating particles from the supernatant after each wash using the magnetic lens.
3. Conjugate Binding: Dispense HRP-conjugated anti-TSH detection antibody, deliver to the immobilized particles, and mix for 2 min.
4. Second Wash: Wash the particles four times in wash buffer, separating from the supernatant; unlike the pilot protocol, the chemiluminescent reaction is initiated immediately after the final wash rather than queuing particles in wash buffer, to avoid signal loss from unequal wait times.
5. Chemiluminescent Reaction: Resuspend the washed particles in one droplet of H2O2 substrate component, merge with one droplet of luminol-enhancer solution, and mix for 4 min until the chemiluminescent signal saturates.
6. Detection: Using the integrated, motorized photomultiplier tube (PMT), collect the chemiluminescent signal ~10 s after the substrate mixing step, for each of the four replicate measurements per concentration.
7. Endpoint: Average the four replicate measurements at each TSH concentration and fit to a linear equation; the limit of detection (LOD) is defined as the concentration corresponding to the blank (0 uIU/mL) signal plus 3 standard deviations of the blank measurements. Dispose of the reacted droplet after measurement.

INTERPRETATION: A successful, correctly optimized assay is confirmed by a chemiluminescent signal that increases monotonically with TSH concentration (0, 0.4, 4 uIU/mL) with low inter-replicate variability (CV 6-10%), yielding a linear calibration curve with an LOD of ~0.15 uIU/mL -- sufficiently low to screen for hyperthyroidism (TSH < 0.3 uIU/mL) -- and reduced sample incubation time (3 min) relative to the non-optimized prototype protocol (6 min), demonstrating that the DOE-derived parameters (five sample droplets, 3 min capture incubation) improve both sensitivity and speed relative to previous non-automated work.

The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's "Optimized Immunoassays" procedure (Experimental Section, p. 9641), which itself modifies the seven-step pilot protocol described immediately prior in the same section. It captures the particle-capture incubation (3 min, five pooled droplets), the two four-cycle wash stages bracketing conjugate addition, the HRP-conjugate incubation (2 min), the H2O2/luminol-enhancer chemiluminescent reaction (4 min mix), and the ~10 s PMT signal-collection window, using the optimized (not pilot) timing values throughout. Because BioScript's grammar has no primitive for magnetic separation, particle pelleting/supernatant removal is folded implicitly into each wash-loop's dispense-mix-dispose cycle (mirroring the wash-loop pattern used in the ciprofloxacin reference script) rather than being modeled as a distinct operation. Because BioScript does not support explicit droplet-count or merged-volume parameters, the paper's "five pooled unit droplets (~4 uL)" sample delivery is represented as a single nominal "dispense 20 units of tsh_standard" rather than five discrete droplet-merge operations; the "20 units" figure is an arbitrary placeholder volume, not a value sourced from the paper. The two four-times wash loops are modeled with BioScript's repeat construct rather than as four explicit unrolled dispense/mix/dispose steps. A "heat f at 25c for 10s" instruction was added immediately before detection as a scripting convenience to explicitly stage the substrate at a nominal bench-top temperature prior to signal collection; this step is a modeling addition and is not described in the paper, which specifies only mixing followed directly by PMT measurement with no explicit thermal-control step at this point. The detect operation is declared using BioScript's only available detection primitive, "fluorescence," even though the physical readout in the paper is a chemiluminescent (non-excitation-based) signal, since the compiler/grammar exposes no distinct "chemiluminescence" detect module. The paper's 3^3 full-factorial DOE analysis (varying analyte concentration, incubation time, and sample volume across 108 discrete experiments), the coefficient/ANOVA modeling used to derive the optimized parameters, the magnetic-lens finite-element force modeling, the integrated-PMT-vs-well-plate-reader HRP calibration comparison, and the pilot (non-optimized) protocol's queuing artifact are physically distinct sub-analyses/validation experiments used to justify and derive the optimized protocol rather than part of the optimized assay execution itself, and are intentionally not modeled; only the final validated Optimized Immunoassay procedure (Table 1) is captured here.

Protocol Details:

Title: A Tri-Droplet Liquid Structure for Highly Efficient Intracellular Delivery in Primary Mammalian Cells Using Digital Microfluidics (triDrop Transfection)

Overview:
The triDrop protocol uses digital microfluidics (DMF) to electroporate mammalian cells with biological payloads (dextran, plasmids, mRNA, or Cas9 ribonucleoproteins) using a three-droplet liquid structure. Two outer "liquid electrode" droplets of high-conductivity buffer flank a central sample droplet of low-conductivity buffer containing cells and payload. Applying voltage to the outer droplets generates a focused, homogeneous electric field through the central droplet, enabling efficient electroporation while protecting cells from electrochemical damage and excessive current.

1. Reagents and Materials
- High conductivity buffer (liquid electrode): PBS with 0.05% Pluronics F-68, conductivity ~16 mS/cm (immortalized cells) or ~32 mS/cm custom buffer (primary T cells in RPMI)
- Low conductivity buffer (sample/electroporation buffer): Type T electroporation buffer with 0.05% Pluronics F-68, conductivity ~8 mS/cm
- Cell types: HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat cells, and primary human CD4+ T cells
- Payloads: FITC-tagged dextran (70, 250, 2000 kDa), eGFP plasmid (~5 kb), eGFP mRNA (~1 kb), Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) with gRNA
- DMF device: bottom plate with chromium driving/reservoir electrodes, dielectric (SU-8 5) and hydrophobic (Teflon-AF) coating; top plate with gold electroporation electrodes and grounding plane

2. Cell Preparation
- Resuspend cells in low-conductivity electroporation buffer containing the desired payload
- Target concentration: at least 2 x 10^7 cells/mL
- Cell number per reaction: 20,000-40,000 cells (low-cell-number workflow)
- For plasmid/mRNA experiments: resuspend at 4 x 10^7 cells/mL with payload at 1.275 pg/cell (plasmid) or 2 pg/cell (mRNA)
- For CRISPR experiments: form Cas9 RNP by combining sgRNA (100 pmol per 1 million cells) with Cas9 protein (50 pmol per 1 million cells), incubate 10 min at room temperature before adding to cells

3. Reservoir Loading
- Load three reservoirs on the DMF device:
  - Two outer reservoirs: high-conductivity buffer (6 microliters each)
  - Middle reservoir: cells + payload in low-conductivity buffer (6 microliters)
- Reservoirs filled by pipetting fluid onto the bottom plate edge and applying driving potentials to draw fluid in

4. Droplet Dispensing and Actuation
- Dispense three ~1 microliter droplets (one from each reservoir) via pulling/necking
- Actuate the cell-containing droplet to the center of the electroporation site
- Actuate the two high-conductivity droplets to the outer edges of the electroporation site
- Actuation achieved via AC potentials of 300-400 V RMS at 15 kHz

5. triDrop Formation (Merging)
- Merge the three droplets into a continuous tri-droplet chain by actuating the high-conductivity droplets toward the central sample droplet
- Mixing between droplets is limited to diffusion; three discrete regions remain distinguishable for over 30 seconds post-merge

6. Electroporation Pulse
- Immediately upon merging, apply high-voltage DC square-wave pulses to the gold electrodes in contact with the flanking droplets
- Standard conditions (immortalized cell lines, e.g., HEK293/HeLa): 3 pulses, 200 VDC, 10 ms duration; effective field range 0.5-0.63 kV/cm
- Jurkat/HeLa optimized range: 0.75-0.90 kV/cm
- Primary T cells: 3 pulses, 450 V, reduced pulse duration of 1-3 ms (shorter durations improve viability)
- Electroporation pulse circuit: 8-pin optocoupler, DC power source, Arduino Uno-controlled pulse generator (100-450 VDC, 1-10 ms duration range)
- Total electroporation process completes within 5 seconds of droplet merging
- Total time from reservoir loading to electroporation: ~3 minutes for three triDrop structures

7. Off-Chip Transfer
- Remove the top plate immediately after electroporation
- Pipette the total tri-droplet volume (~3 microliters) off-chip into a well plate pre-loaded with warmed culture media
- Maximum cell exposure time in electroporation buffer: 20 minutes (to preserve viability)
- HEK293/HeLa cells: recovered in flat-bottom 48-well plates
- Jurkat/primary T cells: recovered in U-bottom 96-well plates

8. Post-Electroporation Recovery and Culture
- Incubate cells for recovery for more than 24 hours at 37 C in a humidified chamber with 5% CO2
- Primary T cells monitored daily for up to 7 days post-electroporation; viability becomes comparable to non-electroporated controls by day 5
- For CRISPR knockout experiments, cells are cultured for 72-96 hours post-electroporation prior to analysis

9. Analysis and Validation
- Flow cytometry (e.g., BD FACS Melody) to measure:
  - Viability ratio (VR): ratio of viable (DAPI-negative) electroporated cells to non-electroporated control
  - Transfection efficiency (TE): percentage of fluorescent living cells above threshold relative to total living cells
  - Mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) fold-change: ratio of MFI in transfected cells to non-transfected control
  - Knockout efficiency: percentage of living cells below a fluorescence threshold (for gene knockout assays)
- Fluorescence microscopy (bright-field and fluorescent imaging) for morphology and expression confirmation
- For CRISPR knockout validation (e.g., beta-2-microglobulin or TRAC locus): stain with FITC-tagged antibody and analyze fluorescence shift via flow cytometry

10. Key Reported Outcomes
- Transfection efficiency: greater than 95% with greater than 95% viability for dextran delivery in immortalized cells (HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat)
- Plasmid delivery: TE 71% / VR 90% (HEK293); TE 60% / VR 99% (HeLa)
- mRNA delivery in Jurkat: TE 95%, VR 98%, MFI fold-change greater than 500, using only 2 pg mRNA/cell
- Primary CD4+ T cells: plasmid TE >38%, VR 81%; mRNA TE 89%, VR 90% (using high-conductivity culture media flanks)
- CRISPR knockout efficiency: 35% average (beta2M, Jurkat); 70% average, up to 80% peak per introduction (beta2M, primary T cells); average 30-67% (TRAC locus, 10-condition arrayed primary T-cell experiment using fewer than 1,000,000 total cells)
- Comparable performance to Neon, Lonza, and Celetrix benchtop electroporation systems, while requiring substantially fewer cells (20,000-40,000 vs. 200,000-1,000,000+)

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Oil-Free Homogeneous Enzyme Kinetics Assay — Alkaline Phosphatase (AP) Activity and Inorganic-Phosphate Product Inhibition, Monitored via Fluorescein Diphosphate (FDP) Fluorogenic Substrate

REAGENTS USED:
  - Alkaline Phosphatase (AP) enzyme droplets
  - Fluorescein Diphosphate (FDP) fluorogenic substrate droplets
  - Inorganic Phosphate solution (product-inhibition titrant)
  - Distilled Water (dilution/quench droplets)

STEPS:
1. Dispense an AP droplet and an FDP droplet on an oil-free DMF device.
2. Merge and actively mix the AP and FDP droplets to initiate the enzymatic reaction, converting FDP into fluorescent fluorescein.
3. Incubate the merged droplet at room temperature to allow the reaction to proceed.
4. Measure the baseline fluorescence intensity of the fluorescein product to establish uninhibited AP reaction kinetics.
5. Titrate inorganic phosphate into the reaction droplet across a series of points to assess product inhibition: for each point, dispense a fresh phosphate droplet, merge/mix it with the reaction droplet, incubate, and re-measure fluorescence intensity.
6. Repeat the phosphate titration/measurement cycle across multiple points to build a dose-response inhibition curve.
7. Dilute/quench the final reaction droplet with distilled water and discard it.

INTERPRETATION: Successful assay performance is confirmed by AP enzyme kinetic constants (e.g., Km, Vmax) that are consistent with values reported in the literature for conventional macroscale assays, and by a phosphate-concentration-dependent decrease in fluorescence signal consistent with competitive product inhibition — demonstrating that an oil-free DMF platform supports quantitative homogeneous enzyme kinetics studies without partitioning of hydrophobic reagents into a carrier-oil phase.

    heat rxn at 25c for 5m
    inhibition_reading = detect fluorescence on rxn for 30s

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Sperm-seq wet lab protocol: sperm preparation and droplet-based sequencing library generation
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/sperm-seq-wet-lab-protocol-sperm-preparation-and-d-j8nlk9q81v5r/v1
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-823/v1
Journal      : Research Square (preprint), posted June 3rd, 2020
Authors      : Avery Davis Bell, Curtis J. Mello, Steven A. McCarroll
Affiliations : Department of Genetics, Harvard Medical School;
               Program in Medical and Population Genetics, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
Platform     : Droplet-based single-sperm sequencing (10X Genomics GemCode, Option 1)


OVERVIEW
--------
Sperm-seq is a high-throughput, droplet-based single-sperm sequencing technology capable of
generating thousands of cell-barcoded single-sperm sequencing libraries in a single run. This
protocol encodes the complete wet-lab workflow: sperm preparation (decondensation), fluorescence-
based cell quantification, and 10X Genomics GemCode droplet library generation.

The protocol is divided into three phases:
  1. Sperm preparation (~3.5 h): PBS washes, Buffer SMT freeze-thaw cycling, chromatin
     decondensation in Buffer DB (heparin + BME), and heparinase treatment to remove PCR inhibitor
  2. Sperm quantification (~15 min): SYBR Green I fluorescent staining (1:100 dilution),
     hemocytometer counting, and concentration-based QC gate
  3. Library generation (1-3 days): dilution to target cell number, GemCode master mix assembly,
     droplet generation on chip, GEM barcoding incubation, and library QC

Sequencing output is processed using the Bell et al. Nature 2020 pipeline (31,228 human sperm
genomes; "Insights about variation in meiosis from 31,228 human sperm genomes").


REAGENTS
--------

Buffer SMT (freeze-thaw buffer; adapted from Montag et al. 1992; Samocha-Bone et al. 1998):
  250 mM sucrose (from 1 M sucrose, Sigma S7903)
  5 mM MgCl2 (from 1 M MgCl2, Sigma M8266)
  10 mM Tris pH 7.5 (from 1 M Tris pH 7.5, ThermoFisher Scientific 15567027)
  Example 10 mL recipe: 2500 uL sucrose + 50 uL MgCl2 + 100 uL Tris pH 7.5 + 7350 uL ultrapure water

Buffer DB (salt decondensation buffer; adapted from Montag et al. 1992; Samocha-Bone et al. 1998):
  113 mM KCl (from 1 M KCl, Sigma P5405)
  12.5 mM KH2PO4 (from 1 M KH2PO4, Sigma P9791)
  2.5 mM Na2HPO4 (from 1 M Na2HPO4, Sigma S3264)
  2.5 mM MgCl2 (from 1 M MgCl2, Sigma M8266)
  20 mM Tris pH 7.5 (from 1 M Tris pH 7.5, ThermoFisher Scientific 15567027)
  Freshly added per 100 uL (4 samples): 1.5 uL 10 mM heparin + 2 uL 100 mM BME + 96.5 uL Buffer DB base

Other reagents:
  1X PBS pH 7.4 (Life Technologies 10010023)
  10 mM heparin (Heparin Sodium Salt from Porcine, Sigma H3393; diluted in ultrapure water)
  100 mM beta-mercaptoethanol / BME (diluted from 14.3 M, Sigma M6250; used in fume hood)
  0.1 units/uL Heparinase 1 (Sigma H2519; diluted in ultrapure water; stored at -20 C)
  10X SYBR Green I (diluted from 10000X, ThermoFisher Scientific S7563)

10X GemCode reagents (Option 1):
  GemCode Gel-Bead Kit
  GemCode Chip Kit
  GemCode Library Kit
  Master mix per sample (60 uL total): 32.5 uL GemCode reagent mix + 1.5 uL primer release agent
    + 9.2 uL GemCode polymerase + 16.8 uL ultrapure water
  Beads: vortex full speed 25 s; dilute 1:11 in ultrapure water (>=90 uL per sample)
  Chip loading: 60 uL sample / 85 uL diluted beads / 150 uL droplet generation oil


EQUIPMENT
---------
  Nonstick 1.5 mL microfuge tubes (ThermoFisher Scientific AM12450)
  Fuchs-Rosenthal C-chip hemocytometer (VitaScientific NANC07005)
  10X GemCode controller and accessories (per GemCode User Guide Rev C)
  Centrifuge capable of 400g at 4C
  Fluorescence microscope (green channel for SYBR Green I counting)
  Liquid nitrogen (for freeze-thaw cycles)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Thaw and Transfer Sperm Aliquot
  Input    : SpermAliquot (>=250,000 cells; typically 10 uL)
  Procedure: Thaw at room temperature. Quick spin. Transfer to nonstick 1.5 mL tube.
  Notes    : Nonstick tubes minimise cell loss during subsequent centrifugation steps.

Step 2 | First PBS Wash
  Inputs   : spermRaw, PBS
  Procedure: Spin 400g, 4C, 10 min. Remove supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 10 uL PBS.
  BioScript: heat at 4c for 10m abstracts cold centrifugation (in-place, no variable assignment).

Step 3 | Second PBS Wash
  Inputs   : spermPellet1, PBS
  Procedure: Spin 400g, 4C, 10 min. Remove supernatant.
  BioScript: heat at 4c for 10m.

Step 4 | Resuspend in Buffer SMT
  Inputs   : spermPellet2, BufferSMT
  Volume   : 2.5 uL Buffer SMT
  Purpose  : Osmotic protection of sperm membrane during freeze-thaw cycles.

Step 5 | Freeze-Thaw Cycles x3
  Input    : spermInSMT
  Procedure: Submerge tube in liquid nitrogen 5-10 s. Uncap to de-pressurise.
             Hold in fist until thawed. Repeat for a total of 3 cycles.
  Purpose  : Mechanical disruption of sperm membrane to aid chromatin release.
  BioScript: 3 cycles unrolled as 6 sequential heat calls (no loop constructs):
             heat at 4c for 10s (freeze) / heat at 37c for 30s (thaw) x3.

Step 6 | Prepare Buffer DB with Heparin and BME
  Inputs   : BufferDB_Base, Heparin_10mM, BME_100mM
  Recipe   : 1.5 uL 10 mM heparin + 2 uL 100 mM BME + 96.5 uL Buffer DB base per 100 uL (4 samples)
  Notes    : Prepare fresh immediately before use. BME handled in fume hood.
  BioScript: Two sequential mix steps (heparin into DB base, then BME).

Step 7 | Chromatin Decondensation in Buffer DB
  Inputs   : spermInSMT, bufferDBReady
  Volume   : 22.5 uL Buffer DB per sample
  Incubation: 37C for 45 min
  Purpose  : BME reduces protamine disulfide crosslinks; heparin prevents chromatin aggregation.
  BioScript: heat at 37c for 45m (in-place on spermDecondensing).

Step 8 | Heparinase Treatment
  Inputs   : spermDecondensing, Heparinase (0.1 units/uL)
  Volume   : 5 uL freshly-thawed heparinase per sample
  Thaw     : On ice during last half of 37C incubation (Step 7)
  Incubation: Room temperature, 2 h (120 min)
  Purpose  : Removes heparin to eliminate PCR inhibition in downstream library amplification.
  BioScript: heat at 25c for 120m abstracts RT incubation.
  Dataflow : spermDecondensed is the terminal output of the full prep chain; consumed at Step 11.

Step 9 | SYBR Green I Staining for Cell Counting
  Inputs   : SpermCountAliquot_Decondensed (1 uL sub-sample), SYBRGreenI_10X, PBS
  Dilution : 1:100 (1 uL sperm + 10 uL 10X SYBR Green I + 89 uL PBS)
  Incubation: 5-10 min in dark at room temperature (with or without gentle rotation)
  Morphology: Decondensed sperm appear as large bright fluorescent circles under green light;
              non-decondensed sperm appear as compact dots.
  BioScript abstraction note: BioScript has no split operation. The 1 uL counting sub-sample is
    physically pipetted from the post-heparinase decondensed tube before the bulk stock is used
    for library prep. In BioScript this sub-sample is modelled as a single dispense of
    SpermCountAliquot_Decondensed -- a manifest explicitly named to identify its physical source.
    The bulk stock (spermDecondensed) flows unbroken into Step 11 to preserve end-to-end dataflow.

Step 10 | Hemocytometer Cell Count
  Input    : stainedSperm
